富士山是日本最高的山。: Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan.
冬天，山顶因为下雪而变白。: In winter, the top of the mountain turns white with snow.
夏天，很多人会来爬这座山。: In summer, many people climb this mountain.
山上夏天也很冷，所以穿上暖和的衣服去爬吧。: It's cold at the top of the mountain even in summer, so let's wear warm clothes when we climb.
天气好的日子，从东京也能看到富士山。: On days when the weather is good, you can see Mount Fuji even from Tokyo.
我也想明年夏天和朋友一起去爬。: I want to climb it with my friends next summer, too.
攀登，爬（山）: to climb, to go up (a mountain)
他每周日都和朋友在公园打棒球。: Every Sunday, he plays baseball with his friends in the park.
在日本，棒球是非常受欢迎的运动。: In Japan, baseball is a very popular sport.
有很多人喜欢棒球。: There are a lot of people who like baseball.
夏天，我和哥哥一起在电视上看高中生的棒球比赛。: In summer, I watch high school baseball on TV with my brother.
哥哥棒球打得很好，可是我还打得不好。: My brother is good at baseball, but I'm still not very good.
所以，我现在每天都练习一会儿。: So right now, I'm practicing a little every day.
明年我也想和哥哥一起打棒球。: Next year, I want to play baseball with my brother, too.
优太：“妈妈，今天老师说‘优太是班上最安静的’。”: Yuta: "Mom, today the teacher said, 'Yuta is the quietest one in the class.'"
妈妈：“上课的时候你在做什么呢？在看书吗？”: Mom: "What were you doing during class? Were you reading a book?"
妈妈：“那么，是在听老师讲话吗？”: Mom: "Then were you listening to the teacher?"
优太：“不是。从早上到中午，我都在教室里睡觉。”: Yuta: "No. I was sleeping in the classroom from morning until noon."
在日本，一月一日是新年。: In Japan, January 1 is the New Year (Oshogatsu).
新年的时候，学校和公司都放假。: At New Year's, both schools and companies are closed.
全家人一起吃年菜。: The whole family eats osechi ryori (traditional New Year's dishes) together.
年菜颜色漂亮，非常好吃。: Osechi dishes are beautifully colorful and very delicious.
然后去神社或寺庙。: After that, people go to a shrine or a temple.
在那里许下新一年的愿望。: There, they make a wish for the year.
孩子们会从大人那里收到压岁钱。: Children receive otoshidama (New Year's money) from adults.
然后去买自己喜欢的东西。: Then they go out to buy things they like.
我的奶奶住在乡下。: My grandma lives in the countryside.
她每个月都会给我写信。: She sends me a letter every month.
奶奶总是写：“你好吗？要多吃饭哦。”: Grandma always writes, "How are you? Be sure to eat plenty, okay?"
一读那封信，我心里就暖暖的。: When I read her letters, my heart feels warm.
我也给奶奶写信。: I write letters to Grandma, too.
我会写很多学校学习和朋友的事。: I write a lot about my schoolwork and my friends.
暑假我要去看奶奶。: During summer vacation, I'm going to go see Grandma.
然后，我想吃奶奶做的好吃的菜。: And I want to eat Grandma's delicious cooking.
有一天放学回家的时候，下起了大雨。: One day, on my way home from school, it rained hard.
这时，一位不认识的老爷爷走过来说：“请用这把伞吧。”: Just then, an old man I didn't know came up and said, "Please use this umbrella."
老爷爷说：“我家就在那边，没关系的。”: "My house is just over there, so I'll be fine," the old man said.
我借了那把伞回了家。: I borrowed the umbrella and went home.
第二天，我去老爷爷家还伞。: The next day, I went to the old man's house to return the umbrella.
然后对他说了声“谢谢您”。: And I said, "Thank you very much."
知道，认识: to know, to be acquainted with
拉面是日本人非常喜欢的食物。: Ramen is a food that Japanese people love.
有酱油、味噌、盐等各种口味。: There are many flavors, such as soy sauce, miso, and salt.
北海道的札幌以味噌拉面闻名。: Sapporo, in Hokkaido, is famous for miso ramen.
街上有很多拉面店。: There are many ramen shops in town.
因为又便宜又好吃，学生也常常去吃。: Because it's cheap and delicious, students often go out to eat it, too.
在日本，吃拉面时发出声音也没关系。: In Japan, it's okay to make noise when you eat ramen.
我喜欢在寒冷的日子里吃热腾腾的拉面。: I like eating hot ramen on cold days.
上周我和家人去京都旅行了。: Last week, I went on a trip to Kyoto with my family.
我们在东京站坐上了新干线。: We took the shinkansen from Tokyo Station.
新干线非常快，到京都只用了两个小时左右。: The shinkansen was very fast, and it took about two hours to get to Kyoto.
我们在车上吃了车站便当。: We ate ekiben on the train.
车站便当是在车站卖的便当，非常好吃。: Ekiben are bento boxes sold at train stations, and they were very tasty.
在京都，我们参观了许多古老的寺庙。: In Kyoto, we saw many old temples.
还拍了很多照片。: We also took lots of pictures.
这次旅行非常愉快，所以我还想再去。: It was a really fun trip, so I want to go again.
因为是春天，樱花开得很多，非常漂亮。: It's spring, so lots of cherry blossoms are in bloom, and it's very beautiful.
在学校里，学生们每天自己打扫教室。: At school, the students clean their classrooms themselves every day.
在小学，午饭是在教室里和班上的同学们一起吃的。: In elementary school, students eat lunch in the classroom together with everyone in their class.
夏天有很长的假期。: In summer, there is a long vacation.
暑假大约从七月底放到八月底。: Summer vacation runs from around the end of July to the end of August.
相扑是日本古老的运动。: Sumo is an old Japanese sport.
从事这项运动的人叫做“力士”。: People who do this sport are called 「力士」 (rikishi).
力士身体非常高大，而且很强壮。: Rikishi are very big and strong.
他们每天大量练习，饭也吃得很多。: They practice hard every day and eat a lot, too.
两名力士进入圆形的土俵（比赛台）。: The two rikishi step into the round dohyo (ring).
不可以出到土俵外面。: They must not go outside the dohyo.
先出到外面的人就输了。: The one who goes out first loses.
大型比赛一年举行六次。: There are six big tournaments a year.
出去，出来: to go out, to come out
一起去泡温泉吧: Let's go to a hot spring
山里有，海边也有。: There are some in the mountains and some near the sea.
寒冷的冬天，泡温泉最好了。: In the cold winter, a hot spring is the best.
泡之前，请先把身体好好洗干净。: Before you get in, please wash your body well.
毛巾不可以放进温泉水里。: You must not put your towel in the water.
泡完温泉后喝的冰牛奶非常好喝。: The cold milk you drink after a hot spring bath is very delicious.
你要不要也一起去呢？: Why don't you come along with us?
秋天的夜晚，月亮非常美丽。: On autumn nights, the moon is very beautiful.
日本人在秋天会“赏月”。: In autumn, Japanese people enjoy 「お月見」 (moon viewing).
赏月的晚上，人们会吃白白圆圆的团子。: On the night of moon viewing, people eat white, round dango (dumplings).
我和家人一起从窗口看了月亮。: I looked at the moon from the window with my family.
月亮又大又明亮。: The moon was very big and bright.
住在远方城市的朋友，现在大概也正看着同一轮月亮吧。: My friend who lives in a faraway town is probably looking at the same moon right now, too.
钱有纸币和圆圆的硬币。: Money comes in paper bills and round coins.
硬币一共有六种。: There are six kinds of coins.
分别是一日元、五日元、十日元、五十日元、一百日元和五百日元。: They are 1 yen, 5 yen, 10 yen, 50 yen, 100 yen, and 500 yen.
颜色、大小和重量各不相同。: They are all different in color, size, and weight.
五日元和五十日元的硬币中间有一个小洞。: The 5-yen and 50-yen coins have a small hole in the middle.
一日元硬币最小，非常轻。: The 1-yen coin is the smallest and very light.
把它轻轻地放在水面上，有时它都不会沉下去。: If you place it gently on water, sometimes it doesn't even sink.
纳豆是用大豆做的日本食物。: Natto is a Japanese food made from soybeans.
它气味很重，而且黏糊糊的。: It has a strong smell and is sticky.
日本人常在早饭时吃纳豆。: Japanese people often eat natto for breakfast.
先用筷子好好搅拌，再放到米饭上面。: You mix it well with chopsticks and then put it on top of rice.
第一次吃的时候，我不太喜欢。: When I first ate it, I didn't like it very much.
不过每天早上吃一点，现在已经喜欢上了。: But I ate a little every morning, and now I've come to like it.
它对身体也很好哦。: It's good for your health, too.
学校的营养午餐里也经常有咖喱。: Curry is often served for school lunch, too.
我家每周五晚上都做咖喱。: At my house, we make curry every Friday night.
爸爸切土豆和胡萝卜。: My father cuts the potatoes and carrots.
我切洋葱，可是总会流眼泪。: I cut the onions, but tears always come to my eyes.
妈妈说：“咖喱第二天更好吃哦。”: My mother says, "Curry tastes better the next day."
所以，周六早上我们也吃咖喱。: So we eat curry on Saturday morning, too.
奈良公园里有很多鹿。: There are many deer in Nara Park.
鹿在路上散步，或者在寺庙前睡觉。: The deer walk along the paths and sleep in front of temples.
公园里有卖“鹿仙贝”。: In the park, they sell 「鹿せんべい」 (shika senbei, deer crackers).
我拿起仙贝的时候，很多鹿都过来了。: When I held a cracker, lots of deer came over.
一头小鹿向我鞠了个躬。: A small deer bowed to me.
会鞠躬的奈良鹿非常有名。: Nara's bowing deer are very famous.
不过，鹿有时会突然跑起来，所以请多加小心。: But deer sometimes suddenly start running, so please be careful.
走，步行: to walk, to go on foot
小心，注意: to be careful, to pay attention
冲绳位于日本的南部。: Okinawa is in the southern part of Japan.
一月，我和家人去冲绳旅行了。: In January, I took a trip to Okinawa with my family.
东京非常冷，但冲绳很暖和。: Tokyo was very cold, but Okinawa was warm.
冲绳的海又蓝又美。: The sea in Okinawa was blue and very beautiful.
因为是冬天，我们没有游泳，但在海边散了步。: Since it was winter, we didn't swim, but we took a walk near the sea.
下次想夏天来，在海里游泳。: Next time, I want to come in summer and swim in the sea.
折纸是把纸折成各种形状的游戏。: Origami is a kind of play in which you fold paper to make various shapes.
既不用剪刀也不用胶水。: You use neither scissors nor glue.
在折纸中，最有名的是“纸鹤”。: The most famous origami is the 「つる」 (crane).
我跟爷爷学了纸鹤的折法。: I learned how to fold a crane from my grandpa.
一开始很难，但练习了很多次以后就熟练了。: At first it was difficult, but I practiced many times and got good at it.
在日本，人们有时会送很多纸鹤给生病的人。: In Japan, people sometimes give many cranes to someone who is sick.
用线把许多纸鹤串起来的东西叫做“千纸鹤”。: Many cranes strung together with thread are called 「千羽づる」 (senbazuru, "a thousand cranes").
日本人用筷子吃饭。: Japanese people eat their meals with chopsticks.
用筷子的时候，有些事是不可以做的。: There are things you must not do when using chopsticks.
首先，不能把筷子竖着插在米饭里。: First, you must not stand your chopsticks upright in rice.
还有，不能用筷子把食物递到别人的筷子上。: Also, you must not pass food from chopsticks to chopsticks.
不吃的时候，把筷子放在“筷架”上。: When you are not eating, you put your chopsticks on a 「はし置き」 (chopstick rest).
在餐厅里，也有装在纸袋里的筷子。: At restaurants, some chopsticks come in paper wrappers.
也有人把那个纸袋折一折，做成筷架哦。: Some people even fold the wrapper to make a chopstick rest.
今天早上，我和弟弟在家门前堆了雪人。: This morning, my little brother and I made a snowman in front of our house.
日本的雪人是由一大一小两个球组成的。: Japanese snowmen are made of two balls, a big one and a small one.
外国的雪人大多是三个球。: Snowmen in other countries often have three balls.
我们用树枝做了手。: We made hands out of tree branches.
弟弟把自己的红帽子戴在了雪人头上。: My brother put his own red hat on the snowman's head.
可是下午天气变好了，雪人就变小了。: But in the afternoon, the weather cleared up, and the snowman got smaller.
在日本，很多小学都有游泳池。: In Japan, many elementary schools have a swimming pool.
炎热的夏天，学校有游泳课，大家一起游泳。: In the hot summer, there are pool lessons at school, and everyone swims together.
大家穿一样的泳衣，戴有颜色的泳帽。: Everyone wears the same swimsuit and a colored cap.
一年级的时候，我还不会游泳。: When I was in first grade, I couldn't swim.
我很怕水，每天都会哭一点。: I was afraid of the water and cried a little every day.
但是，老师每周都在游泳池里耐心地慢慢教我。: But every week, my teacher took the time to teach me in the pool.
柔道是诞生于日本的运动。: Judo is a sport that was born in Japan.
现在，世界上许多国家的人都在练。: Now people from many countries around the world do it.
它也是奥运会的项目之一。: It is also one of the Olympic sports.
我也从上个月开始在镇上的教室学习。: I have also been taking lessons at a class in my town since last month.
穿上白色的衣服，系上白色的腰带。: I wear white clothes and tie a white belt.
练习前后总是要鞠躬。: We always bow before and after practice.
我家附近有一家小面包店。: There is a small bakery near my house.
面包店的田中先生每天早上三点起床。: Tanaka, the baker, gets up at three every morning.
从四点开始做面包。: He starts making bread at four.
早上，很多去上学和上班的人来买面包。: In the morning, lots of people on their way to school or work buy bread.
最受欢迎的是咖喱面包。: The most popular item is curry bread.
田中先生说：“大家说‘好吃’，我就很开心。”: Tanaka says, "It makes me happy when everyone says 'delicious.'"
起床: to get up, to wake up
开（门）: to open (of a door or shop)
我姐姐在镇上的图书馆工作。: My older sister works at the town library.
姐姐的工作不只是借书给别人。: My sister's job isn't just lending out books.
要把还回来的书摆回书架上。: She arranges returned books on the shelves.
买新书也是姐姐的工作。: Buying new books is also part of her job.
星期六下午，她给孩子们读绘本。: On Saturday afternoons, she reads picture books to children.
孩子们安静地听姐姐讲故事。: The children listen quietly to my sister's stories.
姐姐说：“喜欢书的孩子多起来，我就很高兴。”: My sister says, "It makes me happy when more children come to like books."
日本的马桶上有很多按钮。: Japanese toilets have lots of buttons.
第一次看到的时候，我非常吃惊。: When I first saw one, I was really surprised.
有用水冲洗屁股的按钮，还有发出声音的按钮。: There are buttons that wash your bottom with water and buttons that make sounds.
冬天，坐的地方是暖暖的。: In winter, the seat is warm.
还有人一来，盖子就会自己打开的马桶。: Some toilets even open their lids by themselves when someone comes in.
现在，在我的国家，用这种马桶的家庭也越来越多了。: Now, more and more homes in my country are using these toilets, too.
一张卡就能坐电车: Riding the train with just one card
在日本的车站，很多人使用IC卡。: At train stations in Japan, many people use IC cards.
有了它，就不需要车票。: If you have one, you don't need a ticket.
只要在车站入口“嘀”地碰一下就行。: You just tap it at the station entrance, and it goes "beep."
用它还可以在便利店买东西。: You can also use it to shop at convenience stores.
钱变少的时候，就在车站充值。: When the money on it runs low, you top it up at the station.
因为非常方便，所以我每天都在用。: It's very convenient, so I use it every day.
弟弟出生的那天: The day my little brother was born
去年五月，我有了一个弟弟。: Last May, my little brother was born.
我在医院第一次见到了弟弟。: I saw my brother for the first time at the hospital.
弟弟非常小，总是在睡觉。: He was very small and was always sleeping.
我伸出手指，弟弟就用小手紧紧地握住了。: When I held out my finger, he grabbed it tightly with his tiny hand.
那时我心想：“从今天起我就是哥哥了。”: At that moment, I thought, "From today on, I'm a big brother."
现在，弟弟每天常常哭，但也常常笑。: Now my brother cries a lot every day, but he laughs a lot, too.
我希望他快点长大，和我一起好好地玩。: I want him to grow up fast so we can play together a lot.
我住的公寓隔壁，住着一位独居的老奶奶。: An old woman lives by herself next door to me in my apartment building.
每天早上碰到，她都会对我说：“早上好，路上小心。”: Every morning when we meet, she says to me, "Good morning. Have a good day."
秋天，老奶奶送给我她家树上结的柿子。: In autumn, she gave me persimmons from the tree at her house.
非常甜，非常好吃。: They were very sweet and delicious.
上周，老奶奶感冒了，没什么精神。: Last week, she had a cold and wasn't feeling well.
我去超市买了东西，给她送了过去。: I did some shopping at the supermarket and took it over to her.
老奶奶笑着说：“谢谢你，你就像我的家人一样啊。”: She smiled and said, "Thank you. You're just like family."
老师：“太郎，有五个苹果，吃了三个，还有几个？”: Teacher: "Taro, there are five apples. You ate three. How many are there?"
只要说“吃饭啦”，它马上就跑过来。: When I say "Food's ready!", it comes running right away.
说“零食”，它也马上就来。: When I say "Treats," it comes right away, too.
可是，一说“我们去洗澡吧”……: But when I say "Let's take a bath"...
小三花就哪儿也找不到了。: Mike is nowhere to be found.
果然是一只很懂日语的猫。: Just as I thought, it's a cat that understands Japanese very well.
上个月，我在车站把钱包弄丢了。: Last month, I lost my wallet at the station.
里面装着钱、卡，还有家人的照片。: Inside were money, cards, and a photo of my family.
我非常难过，马上去了车站附近的派出所。: I was very upset, and I went straight to the police box near the station.
第二天，派出所的人打来了电话。: The next day, I got a call from someone at the police box.
原来是一个高中生捡到了我的钱包，送到了派出所。: A high school student had found my wallet and brought it to the police box.
钱、卡和照片都一样不少。: The money, the cards, and the photo were all there.
我给那位高中生写了一封感谢信。: I wrote a thank-you letter to that high school student.
红绿灯的颜色有红色、黄色，还有一种是什么颜色呢？: A traffic light's colors are red, yellow, and what is the third color?
可是仔细一看，那是接近绿色的颜色。: But if you look closely, it's a color close to green.
在日语里，自古以来绿色的东西有时也叫“青”。: Since long ago, Japanese has sometimes used 「青」 for green things.
例如，绿色的蔬菜也叫“青い野菜”。: For example, green vegetables are also called 「青い野菜」 ("blue vegetables").
所以，信号灯的颜色也叫“青”。: That's why the color of the traffic light is also 「青」.
在玄关脱鞋: Taking off your shoes at the genkan
日本的房子都有“玄关”。: Japanese homes have a 「玄関」 (genkan, entryway).
进屋的时候，要在玄关脱鞋。: When you enter a house, you take off your shoes in the genkan.
脱下的鞋要摆整齐。: You line up the shoes you took off neatly.
然后穿上拖鞋，走进房间。: Then you put on slippers and go into the room.
不过，进榻榻米房间时，拖鞋也要脱掉。: But you take off your slippers, too, before entering a tatami room.
学校里也有换鞋的地方。: Schools also have a place where you change your shoes.
屋子里总是干干净净的，让人心情舒畅。: The inside of the house is always clean, which feels nice.
穿（鞋、裤子）: to put on, to wear (shoes, pants)
东京晴空塔是位于东京的一座非常高的塔。: Tokyo Skytree is a very tall tower in Tokyo.
它高634米，是日本最高的塔。: It is 634 meters tall and is the tallest tower in Japan.
星期天，我和朋友上到了塔上。: On Sunday, I went up to the top with a friend.
从上面看下去，东京的房子和大楼都非常小。: Seen from the top, Tokyo's houses and big buildings were all very small.
因为天气很好，还看到了远处的富士山。: The weather was good, so we could even see Mount Fuji in the distance.
在火车上吃的铁路便当: Ekiben to eat on the train
在车站卖的便当叫做“铁路便当（駅弁）”。: Bento sold at train stations are called 「駅弁」 (ekiben).
不同的地方有各种各样的铁路便当。: Different towns have different kinds of ekiben.
在靠海的城市，鱼和螃蟹的便当比较多。: In towns near the sea, many ekiben have fish or crab.
在山区的城市，有肉和山野菜的便当。: In mountain towns, there are ekiben with meat and mountain vegetables.
我坐新干线的时候，总会买铁路便当。: Whenever I ride the shinkansen, I always buy an ekiben.
一边看着窗外一边吃的便当，特别好吃。: Ekiben eaten while looking out the window taste wonderful.
下次吃哪种便当呢，我总是很期待。: I always look forward to finding out which ekiben I'll eat next.

我一听到歌声，就马上拿着钱跑到外面。: When I hear the song, I grab some money and go straight outside.
烤红薯又烫又甜，非常好吃。: Baked sweet potatoes are hot, sweet, and very delicious.
在冬天回家的路上吃一个，身体和心里都暖暖的。: Eating a baked sweet potato on the way home in winter warms both your body and your heart.
新干线于1964年开始在东京和新大阪之间运行。: The shinkansen began running between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka in 1964.
那是在东京奥运会开幕前不久。: That was shortly before the Tokyo Olympics began.
现在，最快的新干线时速可达320公里。: Today, the fastest shinkansen runs at 320 kilometers per hour.
因为比特快和快车快得多，所以赶往远处的城市时很方便。: It is much faster than limited express and express trains, so it is convenient when you need to hurry to a distant city.
另外，新干线以几乎不晚点而闻名。: The shinkansen is also famous for almost never being late.
在东京站，清洁人员大约7分钟就能把车厢打扫干净。: At Tokyo Station, cleaning crews clean the inside of a shinkansen in about seven minutes.
在乘客下车到下一批乘客上车的短短时间里，把座位也全部弄干净。: In the short time between when passengers get off and the next passengers get on, they clean every seat, too.
因为这项工作非常出色，据说还有人从国外来参观。: Their work is so impressive that some people reportedly come from abroad to see it.
下次有机会去日本旅行的话，请一定要坐一坐。: Next time you have a chance to travel to Japan, be sure to try riding it.
迟；晚点: to be late; to be delayed

先出土俵的人，或者脚底以外的部位着地的人就输了。: The one who goes out of the dohyo first, or who touches the ground with any part of the body other than the soles of the feet, loses.

最强的力士被称为“横纲”。: The strongest rikishi are called 「横綱」 (yokozuna).
在现场观看的话，你一定会被力士庞大的身体吓一跳哦。: If you watch at the venue, you'll surely be surprised at how big the wrestlers are.
有机会的话，请一定去看看吧。: If you get the chance, be sure to go and see it.

“诶？什么从什么时候开始？”: "Huh? Since when has what been happening?"
茶道是一种重视沏茶、饮茶的日本文化。: The tea ceremony is a part of Japanese culture that values the making and drinking of tea.
茶道中使用一种叫“抹茶”的绿色茶。: In the tea ceremony, a green tea called matcha is used.
喝茶之前，先吃甜甜的点心。: Before drinking the tea, you first have a sweet.

沏茶的人和喝茶的人都会郑重地行礼问候。: Both the person making the tea and the person drinking it exchange polite greetings.
对第一次接触的人来说也许有点复杂，但应该很快就会习惯。: It may be a little complicated for first-timers, but you should get used to it quickly.
在安静的房间里喝茶，心情会变得平静。: Drinking tea in a quiet room calms your mind.
吃；喝；领受（谦让语）: to eat; to drink; to receive (humble)

下次回家的时候，我打算对妈妈说一声“谢谢”。: Next time I go home, I plan to say "thank you" to my mother.
一直等待的八公: Hachi, the dog who kept waiting

八公每天都去涩谷站接它的主人上野老师。: Every day, Hachi went to Shibuya Station to meet his owner, Professor Ueno.
可是有一天，老师在工作途中突然去世了。: However, one day, the professor suddenly died while he was at work.
即便如此，八公仍然每天去车站，一直等着老师回来。: Even so, Hachi kept going to the station every day and waiting for the professor to come home.
不管是下雨天还是寒冷的日子，它从不间断。: On rainy days and cold days alike, he never missed a day.
据说八公在同一个地方等了将近十年。: It is said that Hachi waited in the same place for nearly ten years.
路过车站的人们看到这样的八公，心里都很难过。: People passing through the station felt sad when they saw Hachi like that.
如今，涩谷站前立着八公的雕像。: Today, a statue of Hachi stands in front of Shibuya Station.
许多人都在那座雕像前和朋友约好见面。: Many people meet up with their friends in front of the statue.
来往；定期去: to go back and forth; to go regularly
拉面是日本人非常喜爱的食物之一。: Ramen is one of the foods Japanese people really love.
不同的地方，汤的味道也不一样。: The flavor of the soup varies by region.

寻找味道少见的拉面也是旅行的乐趣。: Looking for ramen with unusual flavors is also one of the pleasures of travel.
下次去旅行的时候，要不要尝尝当地的拉面？: Next time you travel, why not try the local ramen?

一开始有点不好意思，但很快就习惯了。: At first I was a little embarrassed, but I soon got used to it.

泡完温泉后喝的冰牛奶也棒极了。: The cold milk I drank after the hot spring was the best, too.
因为心情变得非常舒畅，我想再去住一次。: I felt so good that I'm thinking of going back to stay again.

其实，富士山是一座至今仍在活动的火山。: In fact, Mount Fuji is a volcano that is still active today.
2013年，富士山成为了世界文化遗产。: In 2013, it became a World Cultural Heritage site.
能攀登富士山的时间大约是七月到九月初。: You can climb Mount Fuji roughly from July to early September.
除了这个季节以外，因为有雪和大风，很危险。: Outside that season, it is dangerous because of snow and strong winds.
也有人中途会觉得不舒服，所以登山之前要好好做准备。: Some people feel sick partway up, so be sure to prepare well before you climb.
在天气晴朗的冬日，从东京也能看到富士山。: On clear winter days, you can see Mount Fuji even from Tokyo.

飘来诱人的香味，光是走一走就让人开心。: Delicious smells fill the air, and just walking around makes you happy.

新干线第一次开始运营是在1964年10月1日。: The shinkansen first began operating on October 1, 1964.
那仅仅是东京奥运会开幕前的9天。: That was just nine days before the Tokyo Olympics began.
最早的线路是连接东京和新大阪的东海道新干线。: The first line was the Tokaido Shinkansen, connecting Tokyo and Shin-Osaka.
当时的最高时速是210公里，作为世界上最快的列车受到了全世界的关注。: Its top speed at the time was 210 kilometers per hour, and it drew attention from all over the world as the fastest train in the world.
后来，多亏了技术的进步，现在也有了时速超过300公里的车辆。: Since then, thanks to advances in technology, some trains now run at over 300 kilometers per hour.
新干线不仅速度快，还以发车和到站时刻准确而闻名。: The shinkansen is not only fast but also known for its punctual departure and arrival times.

他们出色的工作表现被称为“7分钟奇迹”，在海外也有过报道，成为了话题。: Their remarkable work has been called the "7-minute miracle," and it has been featured overseas and become a talking point.
对很多乘客来说，新干线已经成为安全、舒适又值得信赖的出行方式。: For many passengers, the shinkansen has become a safe, comfortable, and reliable means of travel.
相扑被称为日本的国技，作为一项历史悠久的传统运动而为人所知。: Sumo, also called Japan's national sport, is known as a traditional sport with a long history.
力士们在被称为“土俵”的圆形场地上一对一地比赛。: Rikishi fight one-on-one in a round area called the 「土俵」 (dohyo).
规则很简单：只要把对手推出土俵，或者让对方脚底以外的身体部位触地，就算获胜。: The rules are simple: you win if you push your opponent out of the dohyo or make them touch the ground with any part of the body other than the soles of their feet.
据说力士赛前撒盐是为了净化土俵。: It is said that rikishi throw salt before a bout to purify the dohyo.
职业的大型比赛叫做“本场所”，规定一年举行6次。: The major professional tournaments are called 「本場所」 (honbasho), and they are held six times a year.
一个本场所持续15天，力士每天进行一场比赛。: Each honbasho lasts 15 days, and each rikishi fights one bout a day.
力士有叫做“番付”的排名，最高的地位是“横纲”。: Rikishi are ranked in a system called banzuke, and the highest rank is 「横綱」 (yokozuna).
每当小个子力士打倒大个子力士时，会场里就会响起观众热烈的掌声。: Every time a small rikishi defeats a big one, the arena fills with loud applause from the crowd.
即使是觉得它好像很难懂的人，实际看了之后也一定会入迷。: Even people who have the impression that it seems hard to understand are sure to be hooked once they actually see it.
请一定要去现场亲身感受一次那种震撼。: Be sure to go to the arena at least once and experience its power firsthand.
有一天，小学老师在上课的时候向班上的学生们提了一个问题。: One day, in the middle of class, an elementary school teacher asked the children in the class a question.

孩子们齐声回答：“不对！”: The children answered in unison, "It's not right!"
老师满意地微微一笑，说：“说得对。老师也觉得那样不公平。”: The teacher smiled with satisfaction and said, "That's right. I think that would be unfair, too."

老师一脸疑惑地问：“为什么呢？请说明一下理由。”: The teacher looked puzzled and asked, "Why is that? Please explain your reason."
太郎充满自信，理所当然似的回答：: Taro answered confidently, as if it were obvious:
“因为昨天的作业我一点儿也没做！”: "I didn't do any of yesterday's homework!"
茶道之心: The spirit of the tea ceremony
茶道是点茶招待客人的日本传统文化。: The tea ceremony is a traditional Japanese practice of preparing tea and hosting guests.
据说是16世纪的千利休完善了它的形式。: It is said that Sen no Rikyu perfected its form in the 16th century.
在茶道中，要把抹茶放进茶碗，倒入热水，再用茶筅充分搅拌。: In the tea ceremony, you put matcha in a tea bowl, pour in hot water, and mix it well with a bamboo whisk (chasen).
客人接过茶碗后，要按照规定的礼法稍微转一下再喝。: When guests receive the tea bowl, they turn it slightly, following set etiquette, before drinking.
这是为了通过避开茶碗最漂亮的正面，来表达对主人的敬意。: This is to show respect to the host by avoiding the front of the bowl, which is its most beautiful side.
茶道中有一句很重要的话，叫做“一期一会”。: In the tea ceremony, there is an important phrase: 「一期一会」 (ichigo ichie).
意思是要把今天这段时光看作一生只有一次，用心款待对方。: It means thinking of this time today as something that happens only once in a lifetime, and hosting your guest with all your heart.
也就是说，茶道并不仅仅是品茶而已。: In other words, the tea ceremony is not simply about tasting tea.
如今这句话不仅用于茶道，也被广泛用来表达珍惜日常的每一次相遇。: Today, this phrase is widely used not only in the tea ceremony but also as an expression of cherishing everyday encounters.
倒入、注入: to pour in, to pour into

奶奶捡起一片通红的叶子告诉我：“这种颜色，是忍耐过夏天炎热之后的颜色哦。”: My grandmother picked up a bright red leaf and told me, "This is the color of a leaf that endured the summer heat."
当时的我，完全无法理解这句话的意思。: Back then, I couldn't understand what those words meant at all.
后来我长大成人参加了工作，在工作中失败、烦恼的事情越来越多。: Eventually I grew up and got a job, and I found myself failing and struggling at work more and more often.
就在那时，奶奶的话忽然浮现在我的脑海里。: At times like that, my grandmother's words suddenly came to mind.
也许正因为经历过艰难的时期，人才能变成美丽的颜色。: Perhaps it is precisely because they go through hard times that people, too, can take on beautiful colors.
奶奶已经去世了，但那句话至今仍支撑着我的心。: My grandmother has already passed away, but those words still support me today.
有时我也会觉得遗憾，要是当初多听她讲讲各种事情就好了。: Sometimes I feel regret, wishing I had listened to more of her stories.
今年秋天，我决定时隔多年再去那座山看看。: This autumn, I've decided to visit that mountain for the first time in a long while.

因为早上天还晴着，她没带伞就出了门。: Because it had been sunny in the morning, she had left home without an umbrella.
这时，一位陌生的老爷爷突然递过来一把蓝色的伞，对她说：“用这个吧。”: Then an old man she didn't know suddenly held out a blue umbrella and said to her, "Use this."
由衣正想拒绝，说：“可是您会被淋湿的。”老爷爷却笑着说：“我家就在那边。”然后冒: When Yui tried to refuse, saying, "But you'll get wet," the old man laughed, said, "My house is just over there," and ran off into the pouring rain.
从第二天起，由衣为了表达感谢并把伞还回去，每天都在同一时刻到车站等。: From the next day on, Yui waited at the station at the same time every day to thank him and return the umbrella.
可是，一个星期过去了，老爷爷也没有出现。: But even after a week, the old man didn't show up.
有一天，她把这件事告诉了站务员，站务员露出了惊讶的表情。: One day, when she told a station employee what had happened, the employee looked surprised.
“那位老先生啊，每次在下雨天看到没伞为难的人，都会把自己的伞借给别人呢。”: "Oh, that gentleman? Whenever he sees someone stuck without an umbrella on a rainy day, he lends them his own."
由衣听了很感动，心想自己也要像他那样帮助别人。: Yui was moved by this and felt that she, too, wanted to help others in the same way.
从那以后，由衣的包里总会多放一把伞，用来借给需要的人。: Ever since then, Yui always carries an extra umbrella in her bag to lend to someone.
据说拉面原本是从中国传来的料理。: Ramen is said to have originally come to Japan from China.
但如今，它受欢迎到被称为日本的国民美食。: But today, it has become so popular that it is called Japan's national dish.
很有意思的是，不同地区的汤的味道和面的特点完全不同。: What's interesting is that the flavor of the soup and the characteristics of the noodles are completely different from region to region.
比如，北海道札幌的味噌拉面、福冈博多的豚骨拉面都很有名。: For example, Sapporo in Hokkaido is famous for miso ramen, and Hakata in Fukuoka for tonkotsu ramen.
也有像福岛县喜多方那样，以酱油拉面作为旅游的中心来振兴城镇的地方。: Some places, like Kitakata in Fukushima Prefecture, are revitalizing their towns by making soy sauce ramen the centerpiece of tourism.
另外，1958年安藤百福发明了方便面。: Also, in 1958, Momofuku Ando invented instant ramen.
这种只要倒入热水就能吃的方便商品，后来逐渐传遍了全世界。: This convenient product, which you can eat just by pouring hot water over it, eventually spread around the world.
在日本，吃拉面的时候即使吸面发出声音，也并不失礼。: In Japan, it isn't rude to slurp noisily while eating ramen.
出去旅行的时候，请一定要尝尝当地的拉面，比较一下。: When you travel, be sure to try the local ramen and compare.
传入: to be introduced (from elsewhere), to be passed on
这个暑假，我去大分县的别府旅行了。: This summer vacation, I took a trip to Beppu in Oita Prefecture.
别府的温泉源数量是日本第一，镇上到处都升腾着白色的热气。: Beppu has the largest number of hot spring sources in Japan, and white steam rises from all over town.
这次旅行我最期待的是“地狱巡游”。: What I was looking forward to most on this trip was the 「地獄めぐり」 (jigoku meguri, the "hell tour").
虽然叫“地狱”，但并不是什么可怕的地方，而是指滚烫的热水涌出的地方。: Although they are called 「地獄」 ("hells"), they are not frightening places; the word refers to spots where hot water gushes up from the ground.
“海地狱”是像大海一样的蓝色，非常美丽。: The 「海地獄」 ("Sea Hell") was blue, just like the ocean, and extremely beautiful.
另一方面，“血池地狱”正如其名，一片通红，让我不由得吃了一惊。: Meanwhile, the 「血の池地獄」 ("Blood Pond Hell") was bright red, just as its name suggests, and it took me by surprise.
晚上我泡在旅馆的露天浴池里，一边眺望星星一边悠闲地度过。: At night, I soaked in the ryokan's outdoor bath and relaxed while gazing at the stars.
多亏如此，旅途的疲劳完全消除了。: Thanks to that, all my travel fatigue melted away.
在温泉里，为了不给其他客人添麻烦，进浴池之前先洗身体是基本的礼仪。: At hot springs, basic etiquette is to wash your body before getting into the bath so as not to bother other guests.
下次我想在严寒的冬天再来一次。: Next time, I'd like to come again in the bitter cold of winter.
眺望: to gaze at, to look out over
在日本，2月22日被定为“猫之日”。: In Japan, February 22 is designated as 「猫の日」 ("Cat Day").
这是因为猫叫声“喵（nyan）”和数字“2（ni）”的发音相似。: This is because a cat's meow, 「ニャン」 (nyan), sounds similar to the pronunciation of "2" (ni).
这个纪念日是1987年定下的，如今很多商店都会在这天出售各种各样和猫有关的商品。: This day was established in 1987, and today many stores sell all kinds of cat-related products.
你在商店门口见过举着一只爪子的猫摆件吗？: Have you ever seen a cat figurine with one paw raised at a shop entrance?
这叫“招财猫”，人们相信它能招来好运。: This is called a 「招き猫」 (maneki-neko, "beckoning cat"), and it is believed to bring good luck.
一般来说，举右手的猫招财，举左手的猫招客。: Generally, a cat raising its right paw is said to beckon money, and one raising its left paw to beckon customers.
也有举起双手的招财猫，不过据说也有人觉得它“太贪心了”。: There are also maneki-neko with both paws raised, but apparently some people feel they are "too greedy."
最近，猫的照片和视频在网上成为话题的情况也越来越多了。: Recently, cat photos and videos have increasingly become hot topics on the internet.
猫自古以来就是日本人身边重要的存在。: Since long ago, cats have been a familiar and important presence for Japanese people.
对日本的高中生来说，甲子园是一个特别的地方。: For Japanese high school students, Koshien is a special place.
甲子园是位于兵库县西宫市的棒球场，每年夏天都会在这里举办全国高中棒球大赛。: Koshien is a baseball stadium in Nishinomiya, Hyogo Prefecture, where the National High School Baseball Championship is held every summer.
在全国几千所学校中，只有在地区大赛中胜出的代表队才能在这里比赛。: Out of several thousand schools nationwide, only the teams that win their regional tournaments and go on as representatives get to play here.
比赛会通过电视向全国转播，很多人都会为选手们加油。: The games are broadcast nationwide on TV, and many people cheer for the players.
甲子园有一个习惯：输掉比赛的队员会把球场的土装进袋子里带回家。: At Koshien, there is a custom in which players on losing teams put soil from the field into bags and take it home.
每年，队员们流着眼泪收集泥土的身影都会让很多人感动。: Every year, the sight of players gathering soil in tears moves many people.
那些土会成为他们和伙伴一起拼命努力过的夏天的珍贵回忆。: That soil becomes a precious memory of the summer they worked so hard with their teammates.
即使输了比赛，反复练习积累下来的经验也绝不会白费。: Even if they lose, the experience of practicing over and over is never wasted.
无论输赢，坚持到最后全力以赴的高中生们的身影，我觉得真的很美。: Win or lose, I think the sight of high school students playing with all their might to the very end is truly beautiful.
田中先生在公司总是夸耀自己的狗。: At work, Tanaka is always bragging about his dog.
那天他又在同事们面前得意地讲起了狗的事。: That day, too, he began proudly talking about his dog in front of his coworkers.
“每天早上，它都会把送到门口的报纸给我叼过来。”: "Every morning, he brings me the newspaper that's been delivered to the front door."
同事山田先生很佩服，说：“那可真了不起啊。”: His coworker Yamada was impressed and said, "That's amazing."
“不过，要把它训练到那种程度，一定费了不少功夫吧。”: "But training him to do that must have taken a lot of work."
“请一定告诉我你是用什么方法教的，让我参考一下。”: "Please tell me what method you used to teach him, so I can learn from it."
田中先生一脸不解地歪着头回答：: Tanaka tilted his head, looking puzzled, and answered:
“不，我一次都没训练过它。”: "No, I've never trained him even once."
“而且，其实还有件事让我有点头疼。”: "Besides, there's actually something that's been bothering me a little."
“我家根本就没有订报纸啊。”: "We don't even subscribe to a newspaper."
日本有一个在秋夜观赏月亮的传统习俗，叫做“赏月”。: Japan has a traditional custom called 「お月見」 (tsukimi, moon viewing), in which people enjoy gazing at the moon on autumn nights.
尤其是农历八月十五夜晚的月亮，被称为“十五夜”或“中秋名月”。: In particular, the moon on the night of the 15th day of the 8th month of the old lunar calendar is called 「十五夜」 (jugoya) or 「中秋の名月」 (the harvest moon of mid-autumn).
这一天，人们会摆上芒草，供上圆圆的团子来赏月。: On this day, people decorate with susuki (Japanese pampas grass), offer round dango, and gaze at the moon.
据说芒草是作为秋天收获的稻穗的替代品来摆放的。: Susuki is said to be displayed in place of the rice plants harvested in autumn.
也就是说，赏月也包含着感谢秋天丰收的意思。: In other words, moon viewing also carries the meaning of giving thanks for the autumn harvest.
另外，在日本，人们自古就说月亮表面的图案看起来像“兔子在捣年糕”。: Also, in Japan, people have long said that the patterns on the moon's surface look like "a rabbit pounding mochi."
中国也有月亮上住着兔子的传说，不过据中国的传说，兔子是在捣药。: China also has a story about a rabbit living on the moon, but according to the Chinese story, the rabbit is making medicine.
同一个月亮，不同国家的人看法却略有不同，真是有意思啊。: It's really interesting how the same moon is seen a little differently depending on the country.
今年的十五之夜，请一定抬头望望天空，亲眼确认一下月亮上的图案。: On this year's jugoya, be sure to look up at the sky and check the moon's patterns with your own eyes.

地址从大到小写: Addresses are written from largest to smallest
在日本寄信时，对在信封上填写地址的顺序感到吃惊的外国人出乎意料地多。: Surprisingly many foreigners are taken aback by the order in which the address is written on the envelope when they send a letter in Japan.
日本的地址是按照都道府县、市区町村、町名这样，从大的范围依次往下写。: Japanese addresses are written starting from the largest area, in the order of prefecture, then city, ward, town, or village, then the name of the neighborhood.
后面接着写“丁目”“番地”“号”，最后加上建筑物的名字和房间号。: After that come the 「丁目」 (chome), 「番地」 (banchi), and 「号」 (go), and finally the name of the building and the room number are added.
英语地址是从小的范围开始写，所以顺序正好相反。: English addresses are written starting from the smallest area, so the order is exactly the opposite.
还有一点出人意料，就是很多道路没有名字。: Another surprising thing is that many roads do not have names.
日本的番地不是按道路编的，而是编给被道路分隔开的一个个街区。: In Japan, block numbers are assigned not to streets but to each of the blocks that the streets divide the land into.
因此，只靠地址找到要去的房子并不容易，实际上连日本人有时也会费一番功夫。: Because of this, finding the house you are looking for with only the address to go on is not easy, and in fact even Japanese people sometimes have trouble.
迷路的时候，不要勉强，可以去附近的派出所问一问。: If you get lost, don't push yourself; it's a good idea to ask at a nearby koban (police box).
十二种动物与纪年: The twelve animals and how years are counted
在日本，每一年都有一种固定的动物，这叫做“干支”。: In Japan, each year has its own set animal, and these are called 「干支」 (eto).
一共有鼠、牛、虎、兔、龙、蛇、马、羊、猴、鸡、狗、野猪这十二种。: There are twelve of them: the rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, sheep, monkey, rooster, dog, and wild boar.
因为十二年转一圈，所以轮到自己出生那年的动物时，这个人就被称为“年男”“年女”。: Because they go around in a twelve-year cycle, when the animal of the year you were born comes around again, you are called a 「年男」 (toshiotoko) or 「年女」 (toshionna).
贺年卡上常常画着当年的动物。: New Year's cards often have a picture of that year's animal on them.
它和中国的十二生肖几乎相同，但在日本最后一个动物不是猪，而是野猪。: They are almost the same as the Chinese zodiac, but in Japan the last animal is the wild boar instead of the pig.
另外，自古还流传着解释猫为什么没有进入十二生肖的故事。: There is also a story, handed down since long ago, that explains why the cat is not one of the twelve zodiac animals.
故事说，都怪老鼠告诉了猫一个错误的日子，猫才没有赶上聚会。: The story goes that because the rat told the cat the wrong date, the cat didn't make it to the gathering in time.
据说大人会讲给孩子们听：所以直到现在猫还在追老鼠。: It is said that adults tell children, "That's why cats still chase rats to this day."
东西不同的电: Electricity that differs between east and west
你知道日本的电在东边和西边有不同之处吗？: Did you know that electricity in Japan differs between the east and the west?
东日本的电是50赫兹，而西日本的电是60赫兹，频率不一样。: Electricity in eastern Japan is 50 hertz, while in western Japan it is 60 hertz; the frequency is different.
据说分界线大约在静冈县的富士川和新潟县的糸鱼川一带。: The boundary is said to run around the Fuji River in Shizuoka Prefecture and Itoigawa in Niigata Prefecture.
像这样一个国家内部存在两种频率，这在世界上也很少见。: Having two frequencies within one country like this is rare even by world standards.
其实，这要一直追溯到明治时代。: In fact, its origins go all the way back to the Meiji era.
当时，东京的公司从德国、大阪的公司从美国进口了发电机。: At that time, a company in Tokyo imported generators from Germany, and a company in Osaka imported them from the United States.
因为两国的机器频率不同，这种差异就这样一直保留到了现在。: The machines from the two countries had different frequencies, and so that difference has simply remained to this day.
最近的电器大多在哪个地区都能用，不过搬家前先确认一下会更放心。: Most electrical appliances these days can be used in either region, but it is reassuring to check once before you move.
正月的1月2日和3日，许多家庭的电视上都在播放大学生的接力长跑。: On January 2 and 3, during the New Year holidays, a university ekiden (long-distance relay race) is on TV in many homes.
那就是往返于东京和神奈川县箱根之间的箱根驿传。: It is the Hakone Ekiden, which goes from Tokyo to Hakone in Kanagawa Prefecture and back.
10名选手依次跑，把一条叫做“绶带”的布交给下一位选手。: Ten runners take turns running, each passing a cloth called a 「たすき」 (tasuki, sash) on to the next runner.
其中，不停歇地一路爬上箱根山的那一段，以非常艰苦而闻名。: Among the sections, the one that climbs the mountains of Hakone without a break is known for being extremely grueling.
在驿传中，绶带是寄托着全队心意的重要之物。: In an ekiden, the tasuki is a precious thing filled with the feelings of everyone on the team.
但是，如果前一位选手落后太多，下一位选手就必须不等队友到达直接出发。: However, if the previous runner falls too far behind, the next runner has to set off without waiting for their teammate to arrive.
这叫做“提前出发”，这种情况下要用另一条绶带。: This is called a 「繰り上げスタート」 (kuriage start, early start), and in that case a different tasuki is used.
看到差一点没赶上的选手流泪的样子，加油的人们也会感到心头一热。: When people cheering see runners in tears after missing the handoff by just a little, their hearts are deeply moved too.
映出；显示: to be reflected; to be shown (on a screen)
剑道是使用竹子做的“竹刀”进行比赛的日本武道。: Kendo is a Japanese martial art in which people fight using a 「竹刀」 (shinai), a sword made of bamboo.
选手穿戴“护具”，击打头部、手腕、腹部等规定的部位。: Competitors wear 「防具」 (bogu, protective gear) and strike set target areas such as the head, wrists, and stomach.
击打时必须大声喊出“面！”“小手！”。: When striking, they must shout 「メン！」 (men, head) or 「コテ！」 (kote, wrist) in a loud voice.
只是打中并不能得分，声音、身体和竹刀的动作协调一致才是关键。: Simply landing a hit does not score a point; what really matters is that the voice, the body, and the movement of the shinai all come together as one.
剑道里有一句话叫“始于礼，终于礼”，非常重视礼仪。: In kendo there is a saying, 「礼に始まり、礼に終わる」 ("It begins with courtesy and ends with courtesy"), and etiquette is highly valued.
比赛前后，要面向对手认真鞠躬。: Before and after a match, competitors face their opponents and bow politely.
据说如果赢了之后高兴得举起手来，会被视为失礼的态度，得分甚至可能会被取消。: Apparently, if you raise your hands in joy when you win, it can be seen as disrespectful behavior, and the point may even be taken away.
培养尊重对手的精神，也是剑道的重要目的。: Developing a spirit of respect for one's opponent is also an important aim of kendo.
有一天，小学生健太带着比平时开朗的表情从学校回来了。: One day, Kenta, an elementary school student, came home from school looking happier than usual.
“妈妈，你听我说。今天老师表扬我了。”: "Mom, listen. The teacher praised me today."
儿子平时很少被表扬，所以妈妈掩饰不住惊讶地问道：: Her son rarely got praised, so his mother asked, unable to hide her surprise.
“哇，真厉害呀。是因为什么被表扬的？”: "Wow, that's great! What were you praised for?"
健太挺起胸膛，得意地回答：“说我上课时是全班最安静的。”: Kenta puffed out his chest and answered proudly, "The teacher said I was the quietest one in the class during the lesson."
妈妈越发高兴，不由得露出了笑容。: His mother grew even happier and couldn't help breaking into a smile.
“你真努力呀。你一直在专心、认真地听老师讲课吧。”: "You did a great job. You must have been concentrating and listening carefully to what the teacher said."
健太想了一会儿，摇了摇头。: Kenta thought for a moment, then shook his head.
“不是。其实，我从上课开始到结束一直在打瞌睡。”: "No. Actually, I was dozing the whole time, from the beginning of the lesson to the end."
体检结果不太好的爸爸，在全家人面前明确宣布：“从今天开始减肥。”: After getting not-so-good results from his health checkup, my dad clearly announced in front of the whole family, "I'm starting a diet today."
“为了减轻体重，从今以后我每天午饭都吃沙拉。”: "To lose weight, from now on I'll have salad for lunch every day."
爸爸平时净吃肉，所以家人都怀疑他是否真能坚持下去。: Since Dad usually eats nothing but meat, the family doubted whether he would really keep it up.
一周后，妈妈正要洗衣服时，从爸爸外套的口袋里掉出了一张收据。: A week later, when Mom was about to do the laundry, a receipt came out of the pocket of Dad's jacket.
上面写着“拉面大份”。: Written on it was 「ラーメン大盛り」 (large ramen).
妈妈把收据拿给他看，爸爸却一点也不慌，冷静地回答说：: When Mom showed him the receipt, Dad didn't panic in the least and answered calmly.
“我确实吃了沙拉啊。我是遵守约定的。”: "I did eat salad. I'm keeping my promise."
“这张收据上哪儿有沙拉呀？”妈妈生气了。: "Where on this receipt is there any salad?" Mom said angrily.
于是爸爸一脸自信地说：: Then Dad said with a confident look:
“拉面上面放了好多豆芽呢。蔬菜的量够多了吧？”: "There were lots of bean sprouts on top of the ramen. That's plenty of vegetables, isn't it?"
一个大雨的傍晚，田中先生浑身湿透地站在车站前。: One evening when the rain was pouring down, Tanaka was standing in front of the station, soaked from head to toe.
仔细一看，他手里紧紧握着一把新伞。: Looking closely, you could see he was gripping a new umbrella tightly in his hand.
恰好路过的朋友觉得他的样子很奇怪，就上前搭话。: A friend who happened to pass by found this strange and called out to him.
“田中，你明明拿着伞，为什么不打呢？这样下去会感冒的。”: "Tanaka, you have an umbrella, so why aren't you putting it up? You'll catch a cold like that."
田中先生像宝贝一样把伞抱在胸前，一脸认真地说：: Tanaka held the umbrella against his chest as if it were precious and said with a serious face:
“这可是我今天刚买的、很贵的伞呀。”: "This is a very expensive umbrella that I just bought today, you know."
朋友完全无法理解田中的想法，说道：: His friend couldn't understand Tanaka's thinking at all and said:
“既然是贵的伞，那就更应该用了啊。”: "If it's an expensive umbrella, shouldn't you use it all the more?"
“不不，这样的雨天用的话，好不容易买的新伞不就淋湿了嘛。”: "Oh no, if I used it on a rainy day like this, my nice new umbrella would get wet!"
抱: to hold (in one's arms), to hug
风吕敷是用来包裹和搬运东西的方形布。: A furoshiki is a square cloth for wrapping and carrying things.
名字里含有“风吕（澡堂）”这个词，据说是因为江户时代人们在澡堂里使用它。: The reason its name contains the word 「風呂」 (furo, bath) is said to be that it was used at public bathhouses in the Edo period.
据说当时的人们用布包起脱下的衣服，或者站在布上换衣服。: People back then reportedly wrapped the clothes they had taken off in the cloth or changed clothes on top of it.
后来，它逐渐被用在旅行、购物等各种场合。: Eventually, it came to be used in all kinds of situations, such as traveling and shopping.
风吕敷的优点是不挑所包东西的形状。: What makes the furoshiki so good is that it can wrap things of any shape.
盒子、瓶子自不必说，就连西瓜那样的圆东西，只要换个系法也能包得很漂亮。: Not only boxes and bottles, but even round things like watermelons can be wrapped neatly if you change the way you tie it.
用完后可以叠得小小的，放进包里。: After using it, you can fold it up small and keep it in your bag.
因为能反复使用，最近用它代替环保袋的人也越来越多了。: Because it can be used again and again, more and more people these days are using it in place of a reusable shopping bag.
无法重写的一笔: A line that can't be rewritten
书道是用毛笔和墨把字写得优美的日本传统文化。: Shodo (calligraphy) is a traditional Japanese art of writing characters beautifully with a brush and ink.
日本的小学有“习字”课，所以很多孩子都至少接触过一次毛笔。: Japanese elementary schools have 「習字」 (shuji, calligraphy) classes, so many children have held a brush at least once.
另外，新年时还有一个叫做“新春试笔”的习惯，会写下新一年的目标等。: There is also a New Year's custom called 「書き初め」 (kakizome), in which people write things such as their goals for the new year.
书道的难处在于，写过的笔画无法修改。: The difficulty of calligraphy lies in the fact that a line, once written, cannot be corrected.
用铅笔写的字可以用橡皮擦掉，但墨写的线是再也擦不掉的。: Letters written in pencil can be erased with an eraser, but a line of ink can never be erased.
所以写之前要慢慢吸一口气，让心静下来，在脑海中想象纸上字的样子。: So before writing, you breathe in slowly, calm your mind, and picture in your head the shape the character will take on the paper.
不过，即使线条稍微弯曲，也并不会被当作失败而遭到嫌弃。: However, even if a line bends a little, that does not mean it is frowned upon as a failure.
反而会被当作体现书写者性格的独特韵味来欣赏。: Rather, it is enjoyed as a unique touch that clearly shows the writer's personality.
每一张字里都能看到书写者的样子，这正是书道的魅力所在吧。: It is fair to say that the appeal of calligraphy lies precisely in being able to see the writer in each and every sheet of characters.
上大学那年春天，爷爷送给我一块旧手表。: In the spring I started university, my grandfather gave me an old wristwatch.
据说那是爷爷年轻时用第一份工资买的表。: Apparently, it was a watch he had bought with his first paycheck when he was young.
说实话，我当时觉得只要有手机就能知道时间，根本用不着手表。: To be honest, I thought I didn't need a wristwatch, since I could tell the time as long as I had my smartphone.
不过我不想让爷爷失望，就说了声“谢谢”，戴到手腕上给他看。: Still, I didn't want to disappoint my grandfather, so I said, "Thank you," and put it on my wrist to show him.
求职面试那天，一边等着轮到自己一边非常紧张的我，不经意间看了看手腕上的表。: On the day of a job interview, as I waited for my turn feeling terribly nervous, I happened to glance at the watch on my wrist.
秒针就像爷爷平和的说话方式一样，慢慢地、准确地走着。: The second hand was moving slowly and precisely, just like my grandfather's gentle way of speaking.
我仿佛听到它在说“不用慌”，紧张感奇妙地消失了。: I felt as if it were telling me, "There's no need to panic," and strangely enough, my nervousness melted away.
从那以后，每逢重要的日子，我一定会戴上这块表出门。: Ever since, I have made a point of always wearing this watch when I go out on important days.
消除、解开: to melt away, to come undone
搬家那天留下的信: The note left on moving day
工作定下来后，我要离开生我养我的小镇，去东京一个人生活。: Once I had found a job, it was decided that I would leave the town where I was born and raised and live on my own in Tokyo.
搬家那天早上，妈妈带着和平时一样的表情做了早饭，并没有特别说什么。: On the morning of the move, my mother made breakfast with the same expression as always and didn't say anything in particular.
我也觉得不好意思，几乎一言不发，只说了句“那我走了”就出了家门。: I felt awkward too, so I left the house almost without a word, saying only, "Well, I'm off."
在新房间里打开纸箱，行李的最上面放着一个白色信封。: When I opened a cardboard box in my new room, there was a white envelope right on top of my things.
里面是妈妈的字迹，写着一段简短的留言。: Inside was a short message in my mother's handwriting.
“饭一定要好好吃。累了的话，随时回来。”: "Make sure you eat properly. If things get hard, come home anytime."
在连家具都还没有的房间里，我心里满满的。: In that room without even any furniture yet, my heart was full.
我握着信，好一会儿都没能从那里挪动。: With the letter still in my hand, I couldn't move from that spot for a while.
直到现在，那封信还珍藏在我书桌抽屉的深处。: Even now, I keep that letter carefully tucked away at the back of my desk drawer.
离开: to leave, to be away from
挂在栅栏上的手套: The glove left on the fence
住在多雪地区的由衣，在一个冬天的早上，在上学路上弄丢了一只红手套。: One winter morning, Yui, who lives in a snowy region, dropped one of her red gloves on her way to school.
那是妈妈给她织的珍贵手套，所以她回家路上拼命找，结果还是没有找到。: It was a precious glove her mother had knitted for her, so she searched desperately on her way home, but in the end she couldn't find it.
第二天早上，公园的栅栏上，静静地放着那只红手套。: The next morning, that red glove was sitting neatly on top of the fence in the park.
为了不被雪打湿，它被装在一个塑料袋里。: It had been put in a plastic bag so that it wouldn't get wet in the snow.
袋子上贴着一张小便条，上面写着：“这是失物。天这么冷，希望能早点被找到。”: A small note was attached to the bag, which said, "Lost item. It's cold, so I hope it gets found soon."
到底是谁写的，至今仍不得而知。: Who wrote it is still unknown to this day.
但是，由衣被那位不知名的人的温暖心意深深感动了。: But Yui was deeply moved by the warm kindness of that stranger.
从那以后，由衣每次在路上看到失物，都会把它轻轻放到显眼的地方。: Since then, whenever Yui finds something someone has dropped on the street, she makes a point of gently placing it somewhere easy to see.
上学: going to school, commuting to school
放上: to put on, to place on top of
末班车的司机: The driver of the last bus
高中时，我总是在补习班下课后坐末班车回家。: When I was in high school, I always took the last bus home from cram school.
一个下雨的晚上，补习班的课比预定的拖了堂，我到车站时已经过了发车时间。: One rainy night, my cram school class ran longer than scheduled, and by the time I got to the bus stop, the departure time had already passed.
正当我想“只能走回去了”而准备放弃时，看到前面不远处的路上停着一辆公交车。: Just as I was about to give up, thinking, "I'll just have to walk home," I saw a bus stopped on the road a little way ahead.
我急忙上车，司机微笑着说：“平时那个孩子没来，所以稍微等了一下。”: When I hurried aboard, the driver gave me a big smile and said, "The usual kid hadn't shown up, so I waited just a bit."
原来他一直清楚地记得每晚同一时间上车的我的脸。: He had actually remembered my face, since I got on at the same time every night.
多亏了他，我没有淋雨，平安地回到了家。: Thanks to him, I was able to get home safely without getting wet in the rain.
那天晚上的车厢里，感觉比平时温暖得多。: Inside the bus that night, it felt much warmer than on other days.
考上大学那天，我把感谢之情写成信，亲手交给了那位司机。: On the day I found out I had been accepted to university, I wrote a letter expressing my gratitude and handed it to the driver in person.
归还图书里的便条: The note in a returned book
在镇图书馆工作的山本女士，每天早上都从整理还书箱里的书开始一天的工作。: Yamamoto, who works at the town library, starts each day by sorting the books that have been dropped in the return box.
有一天，从一本菜谱中间掉出了一张小便条。: One day, a small note came out from between the pages of a cookbook.
“多亏了这本书，我才能给住院的妻子做她喜欢的粥。谢谢。”: "Thanks to this book, I was able to make my wife, who is in the hospital, the rice porridge she loves. Thank you."
上面用有些颤抖的字迹这样写着。: That is what was written, in shaky handwriting.
山本女士得到许可后，把那张便条贴在了图书馆的公告栏上。: After getting permission, Yamamoto put the note up on the library's bulletin board.
于是，其他读者也陆续寄来了“这本书帮了我”的信。: Then letters from other library users saying, "This book helped me," began arriving one after another.
如今，公告栏的一角贴满了对书的温暖的感谢之语。: Now one corner of the bulletin board is filled with warm words of gratitude toward books.
山本女士觉得，书不仅支撑着读它的人，甚至还支撑着那个人所珍视的人。: Yamamoto believes that books support not only the people who read them but even the people who are dear to those readers.
寿司店里听到的词: Words you hear at a sushi restaurant
坐在寿司店的吧台前，会听到一些日常生活中很少听到的独特词语。: When you sit at the counter of a sushi restaurant, you hear distinctive words that you rarely come across in everyday life.
比如，寿司的米饭叫“shari”，用甜醋腌的姜叫“gari”。: For example, sushi rice is called 「シャリ」 (shari), and ginger pickled in sweet vinegar is called 「ガリ」 (gari).
据说“gari”这个名字来自于咀嚼时发出的嘎吱嘎吱的声音。: The name 「ガリ」 reportedly comes from the crunching sound, 「ガリガリ」 (gari-gari), that it makes when you chew it.
另外，用餐最后上的热茶好像叫“agari”，酱油叫“murasaki”。: Also, the hot tea served at the end of the meal is apparently called 「あがり」 (agari), and soy sauce 「むらさき」 (murasaki).
不过，其实这些原本主要是在店里工作的人之间使用的词。: In fact, however, these were originally words used mainly among the people working in the restaurant.
因此，不少寿司店的人觉得，客人用这些词会给人一种有点装模作样的印象。: For that reason, quite a few sushi restaurant staff feel that when customers use these words, it gives the impression that they are showing off a little.
尤其是结账时说的“oaiso”，是店家一方使用的说法，所以作为客人使用时需要注意: In particular, 「おあいそ」 (oaiso), used when settling the bill, is an expression for the restaurant's side, so you need to be careful about using it as a customer.
对客人来说，只要简单地说一句“麻烦结账”就足够了。: For customers, simply saying 「お会計をお願いします」 ("The check, please") is all it takes.
不知道该怎么说的时候，记住这个说法就放心了，因为在哪家店都能听懂。: If you're unsure what to say, remembering this phrase will put your mind at ease, because it will be understood at any restaurant.
茶泡饭是在米饭上放上配料，再倒入热茶或高汤的料理。: Ochazuke is a dish in which toppings are placed on rice and hot tea or dashi is poured over it.
配料的种类多种多样，常用梅干、烤鲑鱼、海苔、芥末等。: There are many kinds of toppings, and umeboshi (pickled plums), grilled salmon, nori, and wasabi are commonly used.
因为做起来不费工夫，所以很多人会在深夜肚子饿的时候或者聚会喝酒之后吃。: Because it takes little effort to make, many people eat it when they get hungry late at night or after a drinking party.
能呼噜呼噜地吃下去，而且对胃温和，这也是它受欢迎的原因之一。: Another reason for its popularity is that, on top of being easy to slurp down, it is gentle on the stomach.
京都流传着一个关于茶泡饭的耐人寻味的说法。: In Kyoto, there is an interesting story about ochazuke that has been passed down.
在京都，有时把茶泡饭叫做“bubu渍”。: In Kyoto, ochazuke is sometimes called 「ぶぶ漬け」 (bubuzuke).
据说去别人家拜访时被问“要不要来碗茶泡饭”，意思其实是“您差不多该回去了”。: It is said that if you are visiting someone's home and are asked, 「ぶぶ漬けでもどうですか」 ("How about some bubuzuke?"), it actually means "It's about time you went home."
虽然不清楚是不是事实，但它常被当作一种很有京都特色的、不直接说出口而向对方传达心: Whether this is true is unclear, but it is often presented as an example of a typically Kyoto expression that gets one's feelings across without saying them directly.
对方: the other person, the other party
立在海中的鸟居: The torii gate standing in the sea
广岛县的宫岛上，有一座立在海中的红色大鸟居。: On Miyajima in Hiroshima Prefecture, there is a large red torii gate that stands in the sea.
这是严岛神社的鸟居，宫岛自古以来就作为“日本三景”之一而闻名。: This is the torii of Itsukushima Shrine, and Miyajima has long been known as one of the 「日本三景」 (Nihon Sankei, the Three Views of Japan).
涨潮的时候，鸟居和神社看起来就像浮在海面上一样。: When the tide is in, the torii and the shrine look as if they are floating on the sea.
退潮后会露出沙滩，就能一直走到鸟居的正下方。: When the tide goes out, a sandy beach appears, and you can walk right up to the foot of the torii.
令人惊讶的是，这座鸟居的柱子并没有深埋在土里。: Surprisingly, the pillars of this torii are not buried deep in the ground.
是古人想了很多办法，让鸟居仅靠自身的重量支撑整体，不倒地站立着。: People long ago put a great deal of thought into building it so that the torii could support itself with its own weight alone and stay standing without toppling over.
岛上的鹿悠闲地走来走去，会走到游客身边。: On the island, deer wander leisurely here and there and come right up close to the tourists.
先确认好潮汐时间再去，就能欣赏到两种不同的景色哦。: If you check the tide times before you go, you can enjoy two different views.
涨满: to fill up, to come in (tide)
最近，巡游寺庙和神社收集“御朱印”的人越来越多。: Recently, more and more people have been making the rounds of temples and shrines to collect 「御朱印」 (goshuin).
御朱印是参拜后作为凭证，在寺庙或神社求得的印章。: Goshuin are seals you receive at temples and shrines as proof that you have visited to pray.
上面盖着红色的印章，再用墨写上寺庙的名字和日期。: A red seal is stamped, and on top of it the name of the temple and the date are written in ink.
因为是一张张手写的，所以即使是同一个地方，字的感觉也会因书写的人而稍有不同。: Because each one is written by hand, even at the same place the feel of the writing differs slightly depending on who writes it.
御朱印要盖在叫做“御朱印帐”的、专门用来收集御朱印的本子上。: You receive goshuin in a 「御朱印帳」 (goshuincho), a book made especially for collecting them.
不过，它和景点的纪念章不一样，所以按礼节要先参拜完。: However, they are not like the souvenir stamps at tourist spots, so good manners call for finishing your prayers first.
还有随季节变换图案的御朱印，以及只有当天才能求到的御朱印。: There are also goshuin whose pictures change with each season, and goshuin you can only get on a particular day.
每多一个御朱印，一本小册子就渐渐变成串起旅行回忆的日记。: Each time you add a goshuin, the book gradually becomes like a diary that links together your travel memories.
坐夜班大巴抵达清晨的城市: To a morning town by night bus
夜班大巴是晚上出发、早上抵达目的地的长途汽车。: A night bus is a long-distance bus that departs at night and arrives at its destination in the morning.
因为可以在睡觉期间移动，所以很受想节省住宿费和时间的学生欢迎。: Because you can travel while you sleep, night buses are popular with students who want to save on hotel costs and time.
最近，座位之间装有帘子的大巴，以及设有女性专用座位的大巴也越来越多了。: Recently, there have also been more and more buses with curtains between the seats and buses with seats that only women can sit in.
为了舒适地度过，最好在出发前稍微做些准备。: To have a comfortable trip, it's a good idea to do a little preparation before you leave.
带上围在脖子上的枕头、眼罩和耳塞，会更容易入睡。: If you have a pillow that wraps around your neck, an eye mask, and earplugs, it becomes much easier to sleep.
另外，在车内打电话或大声交谈会打扰周围正在睡觉的乘客，应该避免。: Also, phone calls and loud conversations on the bus disturb the sleeping passengers around you, so you should avoid them.
清晨到达后，在还很安静的城市里散散步也不错。: When you arrive early in the morning, it might be nice to take a walk around the town while it's still quiet.
这正是只有夜班大巴才能体验到的乐趣。: That is exactly the kind of pleasure you can only experience on a night bus.
在日本的住宅区，有时“传阅板”会一家一家地传过来。: In Japanese residential areas, a "kairanban" (circulating notice board) sometimes makes its way from house to house.
传阅板是附着町内会通知的板子或夹子。: A kairanban is a board or folder with notices from the neighborhood association attached to it.
上面写着垃圾投放方式的变更、祭典和防灾演练的日期等。: It contains information such as changes to the rules for putting out garbage and the dates of festivals and disaster drills.
读完后，在自己名字旁边盖章或签字，再送到邻居家。: When you finish reading it, you stamp your seal or sign next to your name and take it to the house next door.
在互联网时代，也许有人觉得用纸传阅很过时。: Some people may feel that passing paper around in the age of the internet is old-fashioned.
但是，每次送传阅板的时候，都会和邻居产生简短的交谈。: However, every time you deliver the kairanban, a short conversation with a neighbor begins.
它还能成为察觉老人情况的机会，比如“最近没见到他，不知道还好吗”。: It also becomes a chance to notice how elderly neighbors are doing, as in "I haven't seen them lately. I wonder if they're all right."
不过，如果一直放在家里，下一家会很为难，所以要尽量早点传下去。: However, if you leave it sitting in your house, the next household will be inconvenienced, so try to pass it on promptly.
每当老家寄来满满一纸箱蔬菜，妈妈总会分一点送到邻居家。: Every time a cardboard box full of vegetables arrives from her parents' home, my mother divides them up and takes a little to each of our neighbors.
像这样把得到的东西分给周围的人，叫做“分享（osusowake）”。: Sharing things you have received with the people around you like this is called "osusowake."
“suso”指和服的下摆，据说其中体现了“只是一点点心意”的意思。: "Suso" means the bottom edge of a kimono, and the word is said to carry the feeling of "it's only a tiny bit, but..."
收到分享的人家，之后大多会回送些什么。: Households that receive osusowake often give something back later.
归还容器的时候，也有人不是空着还，而是放些点心再还回去。: When returning the container, some people don't give it back empty but put sweets or something in it.
这样，感谢的心意就随着东西在彼此的家之间来来往往。: In this way, feelings of gratitude travel back and forth between the households along with the things themselves.
而且，即使是一家人吃不完的大量蔬菜，分出去就不会浪费。: Also, even if there are more vegetables than one household can eat, sharing them keeps them from going to waste.
从这一点来看，分享也可以说是个好习惯。: In that respect, too, osusowake can be called a good custom.
扶梯站哪边？: Which side of the escalator do you stand on?
在东京的车站坐扶梯，会发现很多人站在左侧。: When you ride an escalator at a station in Tokyo, you notice that many people stand on the left side.
右侧是空出来给赶时间的人走上去的。: The right side is kept open so that people in a hurry can walk up.
然而在大阪正好相反，很多人站在右侧，空出左侧。: In Osaka, however, it's the opposite: many people stand on the right and leave the left side open.
因为不同地方习惯不同，旅行时最好仔细观察一下周围的人。: Customs differ from region to region, so when you travel, it's a good idea to watch closely what the people around you are doing.
不过，最近“请不要在扶梯上行走”的呼吁越来越多了。: Recently, though, there have been more and more requests saying, "Please do not walk on the escalator."
因为在扶梯上行走，有撞到人或摔倒的危险。: This is because walking on an escalator carries the risk of bumping into people or falling.
另外，也有人因为受伤或生病，只能用一只手扶扶手。: Also, some people can only hold the handrail with one hand because of an injury or illness.
其实，排成两列站着不动地乘坐，才是安全的乘坐方式。: In fact, the safe way to ride is to line up in two rows and stand still.
撞上: to bump into, to collide with
在河滩围坐的山形芋煮会: A Yamagata imonikai on the riverbank
一到秋天，山形县的河滩上就会聚集起围着大锅的人们。: When fall comes, people gather around big pots on the riverbanks of Yamagata Prefecture.
这就是被称为“芋煮会”的东北地区秋天的乐趣之一。: This is called an "imonikai" (taro stew party), one of the pleasures of fall in the Tohoku region.
和家人、朋友、公司同事一起在户外做加了大量芋头的火锅来吃。: People cook and eat a hot-pot dish packed with taro outdoors together with family, friends, and coworkers.
山形的芋煮一般用牛肉和酱油来调味。: Yamagata's imoni is generally flavored with beef and soy sauce.
然而，不同地区用料不同，据说在邻近的宫城县，多用猪肉和味噌。: However, the ingredients differ from area to area, and in neighboring Miyagi Prefecture, pork and miso are reportedly used more often.
因此，有时人们会为了哪边的芋煮更好吃而聊得热火朝天。: Because of this, people sometimes get completely caught up in arguing about which imoni tastes better.
在山形，还有用超大的锅煮大量芋煮、并用工程机械搅拌的节日活动。: Yamagata even has a festival where a huge amount of imoni is made in an enormous pot and stirred with construction machinery.
在红叶黄叶下吃热乎乎的芋煮，不仅暖身，也暖心。: Hot imoni eaten under trees turned red and yellow warms not only your body but your heart as well.
兵库县明石市靠近大海，是以盛产章鱼而广为人知的城市。: Akashi City in Hyogo Prefecture is close to the sea and is widely known as a town where a lot of octopus is caught.
说起这座城市具有代表性的特产，那就是“明石烧”。: When it comes to the town's signature specialty, it's "Akashiyaki."
外观和章鱼烧相似，但其实据说当地居民多称它为“玉子烧”。: It looks similar to takoyaki, but in fact the local residents reportedly often call it "tamagoyaki."
因为面糊里用了大量鸡蛋，所以非常柔软、蓬松。: Because the batter uses plenty of eggs, it is extremely soft and fluffy.
和章鱼烧最大的不同在于吃法。: The biggest difference from takoyaki lies in how it is eaten.
不是像章鱼烧那样浇酱汁，而是蘸着温热的高汤吃。: Instead of being topped with sauce like takoyaki, it is dipped in warm dashi broth and eaten.
因为很软，用筷子夹起来的时候，必须轻轻地拿，别弄碎了。: Since it is so soft, when you lift it with chopsticks, you have to handle it gently so that it doesn't fall apart.
在口中散开的高汤香气与鸡蛋的柔和味道，让人吃过一次就难以忘怀。: The aroma of dashi spreading through your mouth and the gentle flavor of the egg are so good that once you've tried it, you'll never forget it.
岩手县流传着一种叫做“碗子荞麦面”的、有点特别的独特荞麦面吃法。: In Iwate Prefecture, a rather unusual and unique way of eating soba called "wanko soba" has been handed down.
小碗里装着一口量的荞麦面，刚吃完的碗里马上又会被添上下一份。: Each small bowl holds a single mouthful of soba, and the moment you finish a bowl, the next serving is put into it right away.
给你添面的店员会充满气势地喊着“来，一碗接一碗”“来，继续继续”。: The staff member serving the soba calls out energetically, "Hai, dondon!" and "Hai, janjan!" ("Here you go, keep it coming!").
吃的客人就要配合着那个节奏一碗接一碗地吃下去。: The customer then keeps eating bowl after bowl, matching that rhythm.
吃饱了，就把碗盖上盖子，作为不再吃的信号。: When you're full, you put the lid on your bowl as a signal that you won't eat any more.
不盖上盖子的话，店员就会一直添下去，所以自己决定在哪里停下很重要。: If you don't put the lid on, the server will keep adding soba forever, so it's important to decide for yourself when to stop.
有的店会数你吃了多少碗，并给你一张纪念证书。: Some restaurants count the number of bowls you ate and give you a commemorative certificate.
据说起源是从前为了真心款待客人，把荞麦面一点一点多次端上来。: It is said to have started long ago, when people who wanted to welcome their guests wholeheartedly served soba a little at a time, over and over again.
配合: to match, to keep in step with
在许多消防署，消防员要从早上一直工作到第二天早上，连续工作二十四小时。: At many fire stations, firefighters work 24 hours straight, from one morning until the next.
工作一开始，首先要逐一确认消防车和工具是否处于能立刻使用的状态。: When their shift starts, they first check, one by one, whether the fire engines and equipment are ready to be used right away.
之后会反复进行搬运沉重水管、攀爬梯子等训练。: After that, they repeat training again and again, such as carrying heavy hoses and climbing ladders.
即使火灾不多，救护车出动的次数却非常多，吃饭吃到一半被叫走的情况也不少见。: Even if there are few fires, ambulances go out very often, and it's not unusual for them to be called out in the middle of a meal.
晚上也轮流小睡，随时准备出动。: At night, too, they take turns getting short periods of sleep while standing by, ready to go out at any moment.
据说从出动警报响起，到上车出发只需要大约一分钟。: Apparently, they get in the vehicle and head out only about a minute after the alarm sounds.
二十四小时的工作结束后，第二天就是休息日。: When the 24-hour shift is over, the next day is a day off.
一位消防员说，被人说一声“谢谢”，正是最大的动力。: One firefighter said that being thanked with a "thank you" is what gives them the most strength.
准备、防备: to prepare for, to be ready for
书店店员写的小卡片: Little cards written by bookstore staff
走进书店，有时会注意到书旁边立着手写的小卡片。: When you walk into a bookstore, you may notice small handwritten cards standing next to the books.
这叫做“POP”，是书店店员为介绍推荐的作品而制作的。: These are called "POP" cards, and bookstore staff make them to introduce works they recommend.
卡片上用简短的句子写着读者真实的感想，比如“读到最后一页，眼泪止不住”。: On the cards, readers' honest impressions are written in short sentences, such as "I couldn't stop crying on the very last page."
与其说是详细说明书的内容，不如说是传达阅读时的感动。: Rather than explaining the book's content in detail, you could say they convey the emotion the person felt while reading it.
书店店员的工作不只是摆书和收银。: A bookstore clerk's job isn't just shelving books and working the register.
从每天大量到货的新书中，找出特别希望顾客读的那一本，也是重要的工作。: Finding, among the many new books that arrive every day, the one book they really want customers to read is also an important part of the job.
因此，据说很多人休息日也在读书，认真思考要写在POP上的表达。: That's why many of them reportedly read books even on their days off and think seriously about how to phrase their POP cards.
他们说，看到有人因为自己的POP而买了书，那份喜悦会让人连疲劳都忘了。: They say that when a customer buys a book after seeing their POP card, the joy makes them forget all about being tired.
稻农的一年，从春天育秧开始。: A rice farmer's year begins in spring with raising seedlings.
往稻田里放水、把土弄平之后，用机器插秧。这就叫“插秧”。: After filling the paddies with water and leveling the soil, farmers plant the seedlings using machines. This is called "taue" (rice planting).
夏天，检查稻田水量、除草等工作几乎每天都在持续。: In summer, work such as checking the water level in the paddies and pulling weeds goes on almost every day.
据说每当台风临近，就担心稻子会不会倒伏，有时整夜睡不着。: Whenever a typhoon approaches, farmers apparently sometimes spend sleepless nights worrying that the rice plants will be knocked down.
到了秋天，收割变成金黄色的稻子。: In fall, they cut and harvest the rice, which has turned golden.
冬天让稻田休养，同时为来年做准备、保养机器。: In winter, while letting the paddies rest, they get ready for the next year and maintain their machines.
因为“米”字可以拆成“八十八”，所以一直有种说法：种稻要花多达八十八道工夫。: Because the character 「米」 (rice) can be written as 「八十八」 (eighty-eight), it has long been said that growing rice takes as many as 88 steps of work.
之所以被教导一粒饭也不要剩下，正是因为有这样的辛苦和努力。: It's precisely because of all this hardship and effort that people are told not to leave even a single grain of rice.
买竹耙的酉市: Buying a kumade rake at Tori no Ichi
一到十一月，以关东地区为中心，各地的神社都会举办“酉市”。: In November, "Tori no Ichi" fairs are held at shrines in many places, mainly in the Kanto region.
因为在旧历中相当于“酉日”的日子举行，所以有了这个名字。: The fair got this name because it is held on days that fall on the "Day of the Rooster" in the old calendar.
酉市上最受欢迎的商品，是用竹子做的、叫做“熊手（竹耙）”的装饰品。: The most popular item at Tori no Ichi is a bamboo decoration called a "kumade" (rake).
竹耙原本是收集落叶的工具，所以寓意着“把幸福和财富都搂过来”。: Since a kumade is originally a tool for gathering fallen leaves, it carries the meaning of "raking in happiness and money."
竹耙卖出后，店家和顾客会一起拍手，这叫做“手缔”。: When a kumade is sold, the seller and the customer clap their hands together in a ritual called "tejime."
据说每年换一个比前一年稍大的竹耙，生意就会更加顺利。: It is said that if you replace your kumade every year with one slightly bigger than the year before, your business will do even better.
因此可以看到经营店铺的人们一脸认真地挑选竹耙的身影。: That's why you can see business owners choosing their kumade with serious expressions.
热闹的声音和寒夜的空气，告诉人们一年即将结束。: The lively voices and the cold night air tell you that the end of the year is near.
炎热时节寄来的明信片: Postcards that arrive in the summer heat
日本有一种在夏季炎热时期寄明信片关心对方健康的传统，叫做“暑期问候”。: Japan has a tradition of sending postcards called "shochu mimai" during the hot summer months to show concern for the recipient's health.
一般是在梅雨季结束后，到历法上秋天开始的“立秋”之前寄出。: They are generally sent in the period from the end of the rainy season until "risshu," the day fall begins according to the calendar.
立秋每年在八月七日前后，所以在那之后寄的话，按规矩要写成“残暑问候”。: Risshu falls around August 7 every year, so if you send one after that, the rule is to write "zansho mimai" (late-summer greetings) instead.
也就是说，即使天还很热，按历法来看已经是秋天了。: In other words, even if it's actually still hot, it's considered fall already according to the calendar.
明信片上常用西瓜、金鱼、牵牛花等光是看着就让人觉得凉爽的图案。: The postcards often have pictures that make you feel cooler just by looking at them, such as watermelons, goldfish, and morning glories.
正文似乎多以“炎热的日子还在持续，您还好吗”这样的话开头。: The message often seems to begin with words like "The hot days continue. How are you?"
最近用邮件了事的人也多起来了，但收到手写的明信片还是会很开心。: Recently, more people make do with email, but receiving a handwritten postcard still makes you happy.
不只是贺年卡，夏天也写上一张怎么样？: Why not try writing one in the summer, too, and not just New Year's cards?
一百零八下除夕钟声: The 108 bell strikes of New Year's Eve
一到除夕夜，日本各地的寺庙里就会传来“咚——”的钟声。: Late at night on New Year's Eve, the deep "bong" of bells can be heard from temples all over Japan.
这叫做“除夜钟”，在许多寺庙要敲一百零八下。: This is called "joya no kane" (the New Year's Eve bell), and at many temples it is struck 108 times.
广为人知的一种说法是，一百零八这个数字是扰乱人心的“烦恼”的数目。: A well-known theory says that 108 is the number of "bonno," the worldly desires that lead the human heart astray.
人们认为每敲一下钟，就去除一种烦恼。: It is believed that each strike of the bell removes one of these worldly desires.
有的寺庙会在进入新年之后再敲最后一下。: At some temples, the last strike is made after the new year has begun.
另外，也有任何人都可以参加敲钟的寺庙，人们会在寒冷中排起等待的长队。: There are also temples where anyone can take part in striking the bell, and long lines of people waiting their turn form in the cold.
也有人在家一边看电视，一边静静地侧耳倾听远处传来的钟声。: Some people watch TV at home while quietly listening to the sound of bells drifting in from far away.
一边听着宁静的钟声一边回想这一年发生的事，总觉得心里自然而然地变得整齐，迎接新年: As you listen to the quiet sound and recall the events of the year, you feel as if your mind naturally sorts itself out and you are gradually getting ready to welcome the new year.
迷惑: to be confused, to go astray
漫画要从右往左读: Manga is read from the right
第一次拿起日本漫画的外国人，有时会不知道该从哪里开始读。: People from other countries who pick up a Japanese manga for the first time sometimes aren't sure where to start reading.
这是因为日本漫画是向右翻开，页面从右往左推进的。: That's because Japanese manga are made to open from the right, with the pages moving from right to left.
在同一页里，分格也规定按从右上到左下的顺序读。: Within a single page, too, the panels are always read in order from the top right to the bottom left.
这与日语文章竖着写、从右往左推进有密切关系。: This is closely related to the fact that Japanese text is written vertically and runs from right to left.
以前在海外翻译时，经常把图画左右翻转后出版。: In the past, when manga were translated overseas, they were often published with the artwork flipped left to right.
但是，这样一来就会出现右撇子的人物变成左撇子等与原作品不同的地方，这也是个问题。: However, this caused problems: for example, right-handed characters became left-handed, creating differences from the original work.
现在，越来越多的是按作者原画的样子出版，并说明从右往左读的方法。: Nowadays, it is increasingly common to publish manga exactly as the artist drew them and to explain how to read from the right.
只要理解了读法，就能更好地享受日本漫画的世界吧。: Once you understand how to read them, you'll be able to enjoy the world of Japanese manga even more.
犹豫、不知所措: to be unsure, to be at a loss
看动漫的时候，会发现不同角色说话方式明显不同。: When you watch anime or read manga, you notice that the way of speaking clearly differs from character to character.
比如，白胡子的博士会这样说：“这是老夫造的机器人呐。”: For example, a professor with a white beard talks like this: 「わしが作ったロボットじゃ」 ("This is the robot I built, my boy").
富家大小姐会说“那可真美妙呢”，忍者则会说“遵命是也”。: A rich young lady might say 「それはすてきですわ」 ("Why, that is simply lovely"), and a ninja might say 「承知したでござる」 ("It shall be done").
也就是说，只要听说话方式，马上就能想象出是什么性格、什么年龄的角色。: In other words, just by hearing how characters talk, you can immediately imagine what kind of personality they have and how old they are.
然而，现实世界中这样说话的老人或大小姐几乎没有。: In the real world, however, there are almost no elderly people or rich young ladies who talk this way.
这是在故事中为了让角色特点更容易传达而创造出来的语言。: This is language created to convey characters' traits clearly within a story.
学日语的人如果模仿动画里的说话方式，有时会被周围的人笑。: When people studying Japanese imitate the way anime characters talk, the people around them sometimes laugh at them.
通过动画学日语很有趣，但使用的场合应该稍微注意一下。: Learning Japanese through anime is fun, but you should be a little careful about the situations you use it in.
看喜欢的电视剧时，有时会想亲自去那个地方看看。: When you're watching a drama you love, you sometimes want to actually go to the places in it.
拍摄电视剧时用过的地方叫做“取景地”，对粉丝来说是特别的地方。: Places used for filming dramas are called "rokechi" (filming locations), and they are special places for fans.
有人会去主人公向喜欢的人表白的桥、每集都出现的咖啡店等地方，拍下同样场景的照片。: Some people visit places such as the bridge where the main character confessed their feelings to the person they loved, or the café that appears in every episode, and take photos of the same scenes.
当在屏幕上看到的景色展现在眼前时，总觉得好像进入了电视剧中一样。: When the scenery you saw on screen spreads out before your eyes, you feel as if you've stepped into the drama.
最近，城镇制作取景地地图为游客指路的情况也多起来了。: Recently, more and more towns have been making maps of filming locations to guide tourists.
多亏了电视剧，很多人发现了以前不知道的地方魅力。: Thanks to dramas, many people discover the charms of areas they didn't know about before.
不过，取景地往往有人正常居住，或者店铺正在营业。: However, people live ordinary lives at filming locations, and shops there are open for business.
请注意不要大声喧哗给居民添麻烦，也不要未经允许拍摄住宅。: Be careful not to bother the residents by being loud, and don't take photos of people's homes without permission.
深夜看的美食剧: Food dramas to watch late at night
深夜的电视上，经常播放以吃饭为中心的电视剧。: Late at night on TV, dramas centered on eating are often broadcast.
既不会发生什么大事件，也没有恋爱故事。: No big incidents happen, and there are no love stories either.
只是描写主人公在下班回家路上一个人走进店里、津津有味地吃饭的样子而已。: They simply show the main character stopping into a restaurant alone on the way home from work and eating with obvious enjoyment.
主人公心里“这个好吃”的声音直接被播出来，也是这类剧的特点之一。: One of their features is that you hear the character's inner voice saying "Man, this is good!" just as it is.
不少人说，看了这类剧，明明是深夜却饿得受不了。: Quite a few people say that watching these dramas makes them unbearably hungry, even though it's the middle of the night.
用看起来很好吃的料理画面刺激食欲，有时被开玩笑地称为“美食恐袭”。: Stimulating viewers' appetites with shots of delicious-looking food is sometimes jokingly called "meshi tero" (food terrorism).
尽管如此还是很受欢迎，也许是因为看着一个人悠闲享受美食的样子，不知为何会感到安心: Perhaps the reason they're popular anyway is that watching someone leisurely enjoy a meal alone is somehow reassuring.
据说第二天，剧中出现的店铺门前排起长队的情况也不少见。: It's reportedly not unusual for long lines to form the next day in front of restaurants that appeared in the drama.
新干线车头很长的原因: Why the shinkansen has a long nose
看新型新干线的照片，会注意到最前面的“鼻子”非常长。: If you look at photos of the newest shinkansen trains, you'll notice that the "nose" at the very front is very long.
这并不仅仅是为了看起来帅气的形状。: This shape isn't just for looking cool.
新干线高速驶入隧道时，前方的空气会被强力挤压。: When a shinkansen enters a tunnel at high speed, the air in front of it gets pushed hard.
这些空气会从隧道出口一下子冲出，因此会发出“咚”的巨大声响。: Because that air bursts out of the tunnel exit all at once, it makes a loud "boom."
把车头做得又长又流畅，空气就会被一点点挤压，从而能减小这种声音。: If the nose is made long and smoothly shaped, the air is pushed a little at a time, so this noise can be reduced.
有一款新干线参考了跳进水里时几乎不溅起水花的鸟——“翠鸟”的喙。: One shinkansen was designed based on the beak of the kingfisher, a bird that makes almost no splash even when it dives into water.
还有参考了能安静飞行的猫头鹰羽毛、减小车顶上装置噪音的例子。: There is also an example of reducing the noise from equipment on the roof by taking hints from the feathers of the owl, which flies silently.
就这样，自然界生物的智慧支撑着又快又安静的列车。: In this way, the wisdom of living things in nature supports fast, quiet trains.
冲出、跳出: to rush out, to jump out
摇晃之前响起的手机: The phone that rings before the shaking
在日本，大地震来临之前，手机有时会突然响起警报声。: In Japan, smartphones sometimes suddenly sound an alarm before a big earthquake hits.
这是叫做“紧急地震速报”的系统。: This system is called the "Earthquake Early Warning."
地震的晃动分为先到达的小晃动和随后到来的大晃动两种。: Earthquake shaking comes in two types: small tremors that arrive first, and strong shaking that comes afterward.
因为小晃动传播得更快，所以地震仪一捕捉到它，就会立刻计算并发出这一信息。: Because the small tremors travel faster, as soon as seismometers detect them, the system immediately makes calculations and sends out that information.
从收到通知到大晃动到来，只有短短几秒到几十秒。: There are only a few seconds to a few tens of seconds between receiving the alert and the arrival of the strong shaking.
在离震源近的地区，通知有时赶不上晃动。: In areas close to the epicenter, the alert sometimes doesn't arrive before the shaking does.
即便如此，对于躲到桌子下面、关掉火来说，这也是足够宝贵的时间。: Even so, it is valuable enough time to hide under a desk or turn off the stove.
警报响了不要慌，要冷静行动，先保护好自己的头部。: When the alarm sounds, don't panic: act calmly, and protect your head first.
端菜的猫咪机器人: The cat robot that carries food
最近，在家庭餐厅里能见到端菜的机器人了。: Recently, you've started to see robots carrying food in family restaurants.
机器人记住了店内的地图，能自动移动到指定的餐桌。: The robots have a map of the restaurant stored in memory and move automatically to the assigned table.
途中遇到有人，它会好好地避开或停下，以免撞上。: If someone is in the way, they properly steer around them or stop so as not to bump into them.
其中还有屏幕上显示猫脸、用可爱声音说话的机器人。: Some robots even display a cat's face on their screen and talk in a cute voice.
摸摸它的头，它就会露出开心的表情，所以非常受孩子们欢迎。: When you pat them on the head, they make a happy face, so they're very popular with children.
在店里人手不足的情况下，机器人帮忙承担了搬运沉重菜品的工作。: With restaurants short of workers, the robots help out with the job of carrying heavy dishes.
多亏了它，店员与客人交谈、提供细致服务的时间就增加了。: Thanks to this, staff have more time to talk with customers and provide attentive service.
人与机器人一起工作的情景，今后将会变得越来越普遍吧。: The sight of people and robots working side by side will probably become more and more ordinary from now on.
自从在东京工作以后，每到周日晚上，乡下的父亲就会打来电话。: Ever since I got a job in Tokyo, my father back home in the countryside has started calling me every Sunday night.
说的内容总是一样，只有“吃饭了吗”“工作怎么样”这两句。: We always talk about the same things, just two of them: "Have you eaten?" and "How's work?"
忙碌的那些周，说实话，有时也觉得被反复问同样的问题有点烦。: During busy weeks, to be honest, I sometimes found it a bit of a bother to be asked the same questions over and over.
有一个周日，电话一直没响，过了晚上十点。: One Sunday, ten o'clock at night came and went without the phone ringing.
我突然担心起来，为了确认父亲的情况主动打了过去，父亲说：“感冒了，在睡觉。”: Suddenly worried, I called him myself to check on him, and he said, "I caught a cold and was in bed."
听到父亲的声音，我松了一口气。: Hearing my father's voice, I breathed a sigh of relief.
那时我才意识到，每周等着那通电话的，不是父亲，而是我自己。: That was when I realized that the one who had been waiting for the weekly call was actually not my father, but me.
从那以后，我有时会主动先给他打电话。: Since then, I've made a point of sometimes calling him first.
驾校日记① 第一阶段: Driving school diary 1: The first stage
因为从春天开始要开车上班，我开始去附近的驾校上课了。: Since I'll be commuting by car starting in spring, I've started going to a driving school in my neighborhood.
第一次上车那天我很紧张，握方向盘的手太用力了。: On the first day I got in the car, I was so nervous that I was gripping the steering wheel far too tightly.
踩刹车晚了、忘了打转向灯，被提醒了好多次。: I was slow to hit the brakes and forgot to use my turn signal, and I got corrected many times.
副驾驶座上的教练脚下有副刹车，所以说不定其实教练比我还紧张。: The instructor in the passenger seat has an auxiliary brake at their feet, so maybe the instructor was actually more nervous than I was.
我最不明白的，是教练反复说的“确认”。: What I understood least was the "checking" the instructor kept telling me to do.
虽然照着说的转了头，但为了什么、在看哪里，其实自己也不太清楚。: I was turning my head as I was told, but I didn't really understand myself where I was looking or why.
可是到了第五天左右，我忽然明白了：变更行驶路线之前，为什么要先用后视镜看后面的车: But around the fifth day, I suddenly understood why, before changing lanes, you look at the cars behind you in the mirror and then also check your blind spot with your own eyes.
明白了每一个确认都有它的意义之后，身体就能自然地做出动作，小失误也渐渐少了。: Once I understood that every single check had a purpose, my body began to move naturally, and my small mistakes gradually decreased.
学科的练习题，一开始也不及格了好几次。: At first, I also failed the practice questions for the classroom lessons many times.
不过，我没有让错题就那么过去，而是弄清原因再往下学，分数一点点提高，终于拿到了满: Still, once I stopped leaving the questions I got wrong as they were and made sure I understood why before moving on, my scores gradually went up, and I finally got a perfect score.
就这样顺利结束了第一阶段，接下来终于是在驾校外面的道路上行驶的第二阶段了。: Now that I've safely completed the first stage, next comes the second stage, where at last I'll drive on roads outside the driving school.
我觉得是开车让我明白了：只要从失败中学习，就一定会进步。: I feel that driving has taught me that if you learn from your mistakes, you will definitely improve.
驾校日记② 阶段考试和临时驾照: Driving school diary 2: The stage test and a provisional license
去驾校上课已经两周了，第一阶段最后一次考试的日子到了。: Two weeks after I started going to driving school, the day of the final test for the first stage arrived.
在场地里，要当着考官的面，一项一项完成S弯、直角弯、坡道起步、在铁路道口暂停等项: On the course, you perform maneuvers one by one in front of the examiner, such as an S-curve, a crank (a narrow zigzag with right-angle turns), a hill start, and a full stop at a railroad crossing.
