分数从一百分开始，每出一次错就扣分，最后剩下七十分以上就算合格。: You start with 100 points, points are taken off every time you make a mistake, and if you have 70 or more left, you pass.
起步和确认都做得很冷静，可是坡道起步的时候，我没把手刹完全放下就踩了油门。: I managed starting off and checking calmly, but during the hill start, I stepped on the gas without fully releasing the parking brake.
警报一响，我一慌又把手刹拉了起来，连自己都差点笑出来。: The moment the warning sound went off, I panicked and pulled the parking brake back up again, and I almost burst out laughing at myself.
尽管如此还是总算过了，接着又参加了学科考试。: Even so, I somehow passed and went on to the written test afterward.
学科考试共五十道题，答对四十五道以上就合格，我答对了四十八道。: The written test has 50 questions, and you pass if you get 45 or more right; I got 48 right.
一起考的十三个人里只有一个人没合格，要第二天再考一次。: Of the thirteen people who took it with me, only one didn't pass and had to take it again the next day.
没能大家一起高兴，有点遗憾。: It was a little disappointing that we couldn't all celebrate together.
就这样拿到了临时驾照，那天傍晚，我第一次开上了驾校外面的道路。: And so I received my provisional license, and that evening, I drove on the roads outside the driving school for the first time.
外面已经天黑了，而且下着大雨。: It was already dark outside, and on top of that, it was pouring rain.
在场地里稍微开快一点都觉得害怕，可到了马路上，却必须一下子开到时速六十公里。: On the course, even going a little fast had scared me, but on the road I had to speed right up to 60 kilometers per hour.
自己开车经过真的有人在走的人行横道、聚集了很多车的十字路口，这还是第一次。: It was my first time driving myself through crosswalks with real people crossing and intersections crowded with cars.
明明应该是和坐在后座时一样的景色，可只是坐到驾驶座上，看起来就这么不一样，让我很: It should have been the same scenery I'd seen from the back seat, but I was amazed at how different it looked just from sitting in the driver's seat.
按照教练说的回到驾校，在一直练习的场地里跑了一圈。: As the instructor told me to, I returned to the driving school and drove one lap of the course I'd been practicing on.
在外面的马路上开过之后，以前那么害怕的速度，一点也不觉得可怕了。: After driving on the roads outside, the speeds that used to scare me so much weren't scary at all.
那时候我明白了：只要经历过一次更难的事，以前觉得难的事就会变得简单。: That's when I realized that once you've experienced something difficult, even just once, the things that used to seem difficult start to feel easy.
在日本，给警察打电话时拨110。: In Japan, when you call the police, the number is 110.
发生火灾，或者生病、受伤的时候，拨119。: For fires, illnesses, or injuries, it's 119.
119是叫消防车或救护车的号码。: 119 is the number for calling a fire engine or an ambulance.
但是，不可以为了好玩而拨打这些号码。: But you must not call these numbers for fun.
请在真正遇到困难的时候再打电话。: Please call when you are really in trouble.
不管是住在日本的人还是来日本旅游的人，都请好好记住这两个号码。: Whether you live in Japan or have come to Japan on a trip, please remember these two numbers well.
在日本写信的时候，地址是从大的地方开始写的。: When you write a letter in Japan, you write the address starting from the largest area.
最前面写七位数字的邮政编码。: At the very beginning, you write the seven-digit postal code.
接着写县，然后写市或町，最后写门牌号。: Next you write the prefecture, then the city or town, and then the house number.
名字写在这些的后面。: The name is written after that.
英语的信是从小的地方开始写的。: In English letters, you write starting from the smallest part.
中国和日本一样，是从大的地方开始写的。: In China, it's the same as in Japan: you write starting from the largest area.
新年的时候，我们在电视上看驿传。: At New Year's, we watch the ekiden on TV.
驿传是几个人接力跑完一段很长的路的运动。: An ekiden is a sport in which a team of several people runs a long route.
一个人跑完后，把“襷带”交给下一个人。: One person runs and then hands a "tasuki" to the next person.
襷带是一条斜挂在肩上的长布条。: A tasuki is a long piece of cloth worn over the shoulder.
一月二日和三日，大学生们从东京跑到箱根，再跑回东京。: On January 2 and 3, university students run from Tokyo to Hakone and then back to Tokyo.
虽然是寒冷的早晨，路边还是有很多人为他们加油。: The mornings are cold, but lots of people cheer them on along the road.
我每周六都去学剑道。: I take kendo lessons every Saturday.
剑道使用一种竹子做的“竹刀”。: In kendo, you use a bamboo sword called a "shinai."
头上和手上要戴“护具”。: You wear "bogu" (protective gear) on your head and hands.
一开始，我觉得大声喊很难为情。: At first, I was embarrassed to shout loudly.
但是现在，大声喊出来以后，我就浑身是劲。: But now, after I shout, I feel full of energy.
比赛前后，都要向对手鞠躬。: Before and after a match, you bow to your opponent.
学习（技艺）: to learn (a skill), to take lessons
发出，拿出: to let out (a sound), to take out
名字全对: I got my name completely right
今天，小武在学校考了试。: Today, Takeshi had a test at school.
小武：“有一个地方全对了。”: Takeshi: "There was one part I got completely right."
小武：“其他地方，下周老师会教我的。”: Takeshi: "The teacher's going to teach us the other parts next week."
会叼报纸的狗: The dog that brings the newspaper
田中：“我家的狗每天早上都会把报纸叼回来。”: Tanaka: "My dog brings in the newspaper every morning."
田中：“是啊。不过，我有点头疼。”: Tanaka: "Yes. But it's a bit of a problem."
田中：“因为我家根本没订报纸。”: Tanaka: "Because we don't subscribe to a newspaper."
为难，头疼: to be troubled, to be at a loss
“风吕敷”是一块有四个角的大布（方形的布）。: A "furoshiki" is a large cloth with four corners.
自古以来，日本人就用它包东西、带着走。: Since long ago, Japanese people have used it to wrap things and carry them around.
盒子、书、瓶子都能包。: It works for boxes, books, and even bottles.
不用的时候，把它弄得小小的放进包里。: When you're not using it, you fold it up small and put it in your bag.
现在也有人在买东西时使用风吕敷。: Even today, some people use one when they go shopping.
风吕敷有很多漂亮的颜色和有趣的图案。: There are lots of them in pretty colors and with fun designs.
剑玉是日本自古就有的玩具。: Kendama is a toy that has been around in Japan since long ago.
它由木制的“剑”和系着长绳的“球”组成。: It has a wooden "ken" (stick) and a "tama" (ball) attached to a long string.
把球抛上去，让它落在剑尖或小托盘上。: You swing the ball up and land it on the tip of the ken or on one of the small cups.
虽然很难，但是非常有趣。: It's difficult, but a lot of fun.
我爷爷玩剑玉非常厉害。: My grandfather is very good at kendama.
爷爷说：“请每天练一点。会慢慢变厉害的。”: My grandfather said, "Please practice a little every day. You'll gradually get better."
我爸爸有一台旧相机。: My father has an old camera.
那是爸爸年轻时买的第一台相机。: It's the first camera he bought when he was young.
他用那台相机拍了很多全家福。: He took lots of family photos with that camera.
我出生那天的照片，也是用那台相机拍的。: He also took the photos of the day I was born with that camera.
爸爸说“这个送给你”，就把相机给了我。: My father said, "I'm giving this to you," and gave me the camera.
这次，我想给爸爸妈妈拍照片。: This time, I want to take pictures of my father and mother.
小林春天从中国来到了日本。: Lin came to Japan from China in the spring.
她的日语还不太好。: Her Japanese wasn't very good yet.
在学校里，她总是一个人吃午饭。: At school, she always ate lunch alone.
有一天，坐在旁边的小樱说：“要不要一起吃？”: One day, Sakura, who sat next to her, said, "Would you like to eat together?"
小樱总是慢慢地跟她说话。: Sakura always spoke slowly for her.
现在，两个人每天都一起吃午饭。: Now the two of them eat lunch together every day.
小林说：“小樱是我在日本的第一个朋友。”: Lin says, "Sakura is my first friend in Japan."
在车站哭泣的男孩: The boy who was crying at the station
车站里，一个小男孩独自在哭。: At the station, a little boy was crying all by himself.
一位车站工作人员走过来问：“怎么了？”: A station attendant came over and asked, "What's wrong?"
男孩说：“妈妈不见了。”: The boy said, "My mom isn't here."
工作人员拉着男孩的手，和他一起在车站里找妈妈。: The attendant took the boy's hand, and together they looked for his mother inside the station.
十分钟后，妈妈跑了过来。: Ten minutes later, his mother came running.
男孩笑了，大声对工作人员说：“谢谢。”: The boy smiled and said "Thank you!" to the attendant in a loud voice.
工作人员也笑着说：“太好了。”: The attendant smiled too and said, "I'm so glad."
一个冬天的早晨，下了很大的雪。: One winter morning, a lot of snow fell.
隔壁家里住着一位独居的老奶奶。: An elderly woman lives alone in the house next door.
老奶奶家门前也积了很多雪。: There was a lot of snow in front of her house, too.
我和弟弟早早起床，把老奶奶家门前的雪清理干净了。: My younger brother and I got up early and cleared away the snow in front of her house.
第二天，老奶奶端来了热乎乎的红豆年糕汤。: The next day, she brought us some hot oshiruko (sweet red bean soup).
虽然天很冷，心里却很温暖。: It was a cold day, but our hearts were warm.
天妇罗是把蔬菜或鱼裹上面粉和水，再用油炸的菜。: Tempura is a dish made by coating vegetables or fish in flour and water and deep-frying them in oil.
星期天，我和妈妈一起做了天妇罗。: On Sunday, I made tempura with my mother.
我们炸了虾、茄子和红薯。: We fried shrimp, eggplant, and sweet potatoes.
妈妈说：“油很烫，要小心。”: My mother said, "The oil is hot, so please be careful."
天妇罗做好后要马上吃。: Tempura is eaten right after it's made.
酥酥脆脆的，非常好吃。: It was crispy and very delicious.
天妇罗可以蘸盐或“天妇罗蘸汁”吃。: Tempura is eaten with salt or "tentsuyu" (tempura dipping sauce).
我最喜欢蘸盐吃。: I like eating it with salt best.
日本的早饭里常常有味噌汤。: Japanese breakfasts often include miso soup.
味噌汤里会放豆腐、裙带菜、蔬菜等各种东西。: Various things go into miso soup, such as tofu, wakame seaweed, and vegetables.
放什么东西，每家都有些不一样。: What goes in differs a little from home to home.
我家总是放豆腐和葱。: In my family, we always put in tofu and green onions.
每天早上，妈妈都早早起来，在厨房里做。: Every morning, my mother gets up early and makes it in the kitchen.
我就着白米饭，慢慢地喝味噌汤。: I slowly drink my miso soup along with white rice.
寒冷的早晨喝上一碗热味噌汤，身体就暖和起来了。: When you drink hot miso soup on a cold morning, your body warms up.
海中的红色鸟居: The red torii in the sea
广岛县有一座叫宫岛的岛。: In Hiroshima Prefecture, there is an island called Miyajima.
这里有一座立在海中的红色大鸟居。: Here there is a large red torii gate that stands in the sea.
涨潮的时候，鸟居就在海水中。: When the tide is high, the torii is in the sea.
退潮的时候，人们可以走到鸟居旁边。: When the tide is low, people walk right up to the torii.
宫岛上还有很多鹿。: There are also lots of deer on Miyajima.
从广岛坐船去宫岛。: You go to Miyajima from Hiroshima by boat.
我也想有一天去宫岛。: I want to go to Miyajima someday, too.
站立；矗立: to stand; to rise (of a structure)
镰仓是从东京坐电车约一个小时就能到的城市。: Kamakura is a town about an hour from Tokyo by train.
镰仓有很多古老的寺庙和神社。: Kamakura has many old temples and shrines.
其中最有名的是大佛。: The most famous of all is the big Buddha.
这尊大佛不在建筑物里面，而是在露天。: This Buddha isn't inside a building; it's outdoors.
在蓝天下看，它又高大又美丽。: Seen under a blue sky, it is very big and beautiful.
也有很多外国人来拍照。: Many people from other countries also come to take pictures.
在日本的学校里，进了室内要穿“室内鞋”。: At Japanese schools, students wear "uwabaki" (indoor shoes) inside.
早上到了学校，先在鞋柜那里脱下鞋子。: When they arrive at school in the morning, they take off their shoes at the shoe lockers.
然后换上室内鞋。: Then they change into their indoor shoes.
星期五把室内鞋带回家洗干净。: On Friday, they take their indoor shoes home and wash them.
星期一再把干净的室内鞋带去学校。: On Monday, they bring the clean indoor shoes back to school.
日本家里的浴室分为洗身体的地方和浴缸。: Bathrooms in Japanese homes have a place for washing your body and a bathtub.
先在浴缸外面把身体洗干净。: First, you wash your body outside the tub.
然后再进浴缸里，慢慢地泡暖身子。: Then you get into the tub and slowly warm up.
浴缸里的热水是全家人一起用的。: The whole family uses the same hot water in the tub.
所以，不能在浴缸里洗身体。: That's why you must not wash your body in the tub.
因为下一个人也想泡干净的热水嘛。: After all, the next person wants to get into clean hot water, too.
暖和起来: to warm up, to get warm
青森县位于日本的北部。: Aomori Prefecture is in the north of Japan.
它是日本苹果产量最多的县。: It is the prefecture that grows the most apples in Japan.
一到秋天，苹果树上就结满了红红的苹果。: In the fall, lots of red apples grow on the apple trees.
青森还有苹果汁和苹果点心。: Aomori also has apple juice and apple sweets.
买苹果当伴手礼也很不错。: Apples make a nice souvenir, too.
静冈县以茶闻名。: Shizuoka Prefecture is famous for its tea.
山脚下有很多绿油油的茶园。: Near the mountains, there are lots of green tea fields.
天气好的日子，能看到茶园那头的富士山。: On days with good weather, you can see Mount Fuji beyond the tea fields.
春末时节，用新叶制成的茶叫作“新茶”。: Tea made from the new leaves around the end of spring is called "shincha" (new tea).
新茶闻起来非常香，也很好喝。: Shincha smells wonderful and tastes delicious.
静冈人每天都常喝茶。: People in Shizuoka drink a lot of tea every day.
大家要不要也去静冈喝一喝好喝的新茶呢？: Why don't you all drink some delicious shincha in Shizuoka, too?
对面，那边: the other side, over there, beyond
邮递员的一天: A day in the life of a mail carrier
邮递员一大早就去邮局。: The mail carrier goes to the post office early in the morning.
在那里，把当天要送的信和明信片按路线顺序排好。: There, they sort the letters and postcards to be delivered that day in the order of the route.
然后骑上红色的摩托车，在镇上挨家挨户地送。: Then they ride a red motorbike around town.
不管是下雨天还是下雪天，都要把信送到。: They deliver letters on rainy days and snowy days alike.
我们镇上的邮递员总是精神饱满地说“你好”。: The mail carrier in my town always says "Hello!" cheerfully.
我也会对邮递员说“谢谢您”。: I say "Thank you very much" to the mail carrier, too.
他每天早上五点起床去公司。: He gets up at five every morning and goes to work.
上车之前，他会仔细检查轮胎和车门。: Before getting on the bus, he checks the tires and doors carefully.
乘客上车时，爸爸会说“早上好”。: When passengers get on, my father says, "Good morning."
老爷爷老奶奶上车时，他会等他们坐到座位上。: When elderly men or women get on, he waits until they sit down in their seats.
然后再慢慢地把车开出去。: Then he slowly pulls the bus away.
我最喜欢爸爸温柔的开车方式了。: I love my father's gentle driving.
日本的夏天，有很多蝉在叫。: In summer in Japan, lots of cicadas sing.
从早上起就“咪——咪——”“吱——吱——”地叫个不停。: From the morning on, they go "meen meen" and "jee jee."
一听到蝉鸣，就会觉得：“啊，夏天来了。”: When you hear the cicadas, you think, "Ah, it's summer."
蝉在土里待很长时间。: Cicadas spend a long time in the ground.
只有到了夏天，它们才从土里出来，在树上鸣叫。: They come out of the ground and sing in the trees only in summer.
暑假里，孩子们会在公园里捉蝉。: During summer vacation, children catch cicadas in the park.
（虫、鸟）叫: to sing, to chirp (of insects and birds)
日本的圣诞节，很多家庭都会吃蛋糕。: At Christmas in Japan, many families eat cake.
很多人喜欢白色奶油配红色草莓的蛋糕。: Many people like cake with white cream and red strawberries.
在日本，圣诞节不是放假的日子。: In Japan, Christmas isn't a holiday.
早上，大家都去上学或上班。: In the morning, everyone goes to school or work.
不过，晚上回到家，会和家人或朋友一起吃蛋糕。: But in the evening, they go home and eat cake with family or friends.
圣诞节一过，商店马上就开始卖新年用品了。: As soon as Christmas is over, stores start selling New Year's goods.
日本的漫画是从右往左读的。: Japanese manga is read from right to left.
一页之内，也是从右上往左下读。: Within a single page, too, you read from the top right to the bottom left.
和英语书正好相反。: It's the opposite of English books.
我一开始觉得很难。: At first, it was difficult for me.
我常常问朋友：“从哪里开始读？”: I often asked my friends, "Where do I start reading?"
不过，现在已经不难了。: But now it isn't difficult anymore.
迈克是美国的大学生。: Mike is a university student in America.
他从小就喜欢日本动画。: He has liked Japanese anime since he was a child.
他通过看动画学习日语。: He studied Japanese by watching anime.
去年，他第一次来到了日本。: Last year, he came to Japan for the first time.
可是，迈克说话的方式和动画角色一模一样。: But Mike's way of speaking was the way anime characters speak.
朋友笑着说：“迈克的日语是动画里的日语呢。”: His friends laughed and said, "Mike, your Japanese is anime Japanese!"
现在，他通过和日本朋友聊天来学习。: Now he studies by talking with his Japanese friends.
每周四晚上九点，她都在电视上看电视剧。: Every Thursday at 9 p.m., she watches a drama on TV.
那个时间，她连电话都不接。: During that time, she won't even answer the phone.
我也和妈妈一起看。: I watch it with her, too.
电视剧一结束，我们俩就会聊“下周会怎么样呢”。: When the drama ends, the two of us talk: "I wonder what will happen next week."
爸爸说：“比起电视剧，还是新闻好。”: My father says, "I prefer the news to dramas."
可是，最后十分钟他总是跟我们一起看。: But he always watches the last ten minutes with us.
电视剧里的咖啡馆: The café I saw in a drama
我在一部日本电视剧里看到了一家小咖啡馆。: I saw a small café in a Japanese drama.
剧中的女主角总是在那家店里喝咖啡。: The woman in the drama always drank coffee at that café.
休息日，我和朋友去了那家店。: On my day off, I went to that café with a friend.
店里和电视剧里一模一样。: Inside, it was just like in the drama.
我也坐在和女主角同样的座位上喝了咖啡。: I drank coffee in the same seat as the woman in the drama, too.
店员说：“也有很多客人从国外来呢。”: The person working there said, "Lots of customers come from other countries, too."
昨天，我和家人去了一家餐厅。: Yesterday, I went to a restaurant with my family.
机器人的脸是一张可爱的猫脸。: The robot's face was a cute cat face.
机器人在桌子前停下来，说：“让您久等了。”: The robot stopped in front of our table and said, "Sorry to keep you waiting."
拿走菜、按下按钮，机器人就回去了。: When you take your food and press the button, the robot goes back.
弟弟对机器人说了声“谢谢”。: My little brother said "Thank you" to the robot.
日本家庭里大多有“电饭锅”。: Japanese homes often have a "suihanki" (rice cooker).
电饭锅是做米饭的机器。: A suihanki is a machine that makes rice.
晚上放好米和水，设定好时间。: At night, you put in rice and water and set the time.
第二天早上一起床，热腾腾的米饭已经做好了。: The next morning, when you get up, hot rice is already ready.
早上不需要花时间做饭。: You don't need to spend time making rice in the morning.
用电饭锅还可以做粥和蛋糕。: People also make rice porridge and even cakes in a suihanki.
我妈妈说：“这是我们家最好的朋友。”: My mother says, "This is our home's best friend."
车靠左，人靠右: Cars on the left, people on the right
按照日本的交通规则，汽车靠道路左侧行驶。: Under Japan's traffic rules, cars drive on the left side of the road.
所以，驾驶座在车的右侧。: For this reason, the driver's seat is on the right side of the car.
因为和中国、美国正好相反，很多游客都会吃一惊。: Since this is the opposite of China and America, many travelers are surprised.
不过，在没有人行道的路上，行人必须靠右侧走。: On roads without sidewalks, however, pedestrians must walk on the right side.
这是为了让行人能看清迎面开来的车。: This is so that they can clearly see cars coming toward them.
据说在车站的自动扶梯上，东京人多站在左边，大阪人多站在右边。: On station escalators, it is said that in Tokyo many people stand on the left, while in Osaka many stand on the right.
一开始也许不习惯，但应该很快就会习惯。: You may not be used to it at first, but you should get used to it quickly.
来日本的话，过马路时可要特别注意左右哦。: When you come to Japan, be especially careful to look right and left when crossing the street.
在日语里，数的东西不同，数法也会跟着变。: In Japanese, the way you count changes depending on what you're counting.
比如，铅笔、雨伞这类细长的东西用“本”。: For example, for thin, long things like pencils and umbrellas, you use 「本」.
纸、衬衫这类薄的东西用“枚”。: For thin, flat things like paper and shirts, it's 「枚」.
小动物用“匹”，大动物用“头”。: Small animals are counted with 「匹」, and large animals with 「頭」.
以前，人们有时也会像数鸟一样，用“一羽、二羽”来数兔子。: In the past, rabbits were sometimes counted 「一羽、二羽」, the same way as birds.
至于为什么这样数，有各种各样的说法。: There are various ideas about why they were counted that way.
全部记住并不容易，所以弄错了也没必要太担心。: Memorizing all of them isn't easy, so there's no need to worry too much if you make mistakes.
不知道该怎么数的时候，用“一つ、二つ”也没问题。: When you don't know how to count something, it's fine to use 「一つ、二つ」.
弓道是用长弓射箭的日本古老武道。: Kyudo is an old Japanese martial art in which you shoot arrows with a long bow.
到箭靶一般有二十八米左右。: The target is usually about 28 meters away.
弓有两米多长，比人的身高还长得多。: The bow is more than two meters long, much longer than a person is tall.
在弓道中，重要的并不只是箭能否射中箭靶。: In kyudo, whether the arrow hits the target isn't the only thing that matters.
用正确的姿势站立、让内心平静，也被认为很重要。: Standing in the correct form and calming your mind are also considered important.
比赛会场非常安静，只能听到箭的声音。: Competition halls are very quiet, and you can hear nothing but the sound of the arrows.
高中的社团里也有弓道，有的学生穿着白色衣服和裙裤练习。: There are kyudo clubs at high schools too, and some students practice wearing white tops and hakama (wide pleated trousers).
听说一开始很难，但每天练习的话，箭就能笔直地飞出去了。: It's hard at first, but they say that if you practice every day, your arrows will start to fly straight.
听得见: to be audible, can be heard
北海道的冬天非常寒冷，雪下得很多。: Winters in Hokkaido are very cold, and a lot of snow falls.
北海道的雪含水少、很轻，所以被称为“粉雪”。: Hokkaido's snow contains little water and is light, so it is called "powder snow."
轻到即使捧在手里，也会马上沙沙地散落下来。: It is so light that even if you scoop some up in your hand, it immediately trickles away.
因此，有很多人从世界各地来这里滑雪、滑单板。: That's why lots of people come from all over the world to ski and snowboard.
我去年也在北海道第一次体验了滑雪。: Last year, I also tried skiing for the first time, in Hokkaido.
我拼命练习，但滑雪比想象中难，摔了好多次。: I practiced as hard as I could, but skiing was harder than I expected, and I fell down many times.
不过因为雪很软，一点儿都不疼。: But because the snow was soft, it didn't hurt at all.
滑完雪后，带着冻僵的身体泡进温泉时，真是舒服极了。: After skiing, getting into a hot spring with my body chilled through felt really wonderful.
滑: to slide, to glide, to ski
变冷，发凉: to get cold, to become chilled
游得太累的鱼: The fish that swam too much
有位客人走进了附近的一家鱼料理店。: A customer went into a fish restaurant in the neighborhood.
客人问店员：“这条鱼新鲜吗？”: The customer asked the server, "Is this fish fresh?"
店员回答：“当然啦。它昨天还在活蹦乱跳地游泳呢。”: The server answered, "Of course. It was swimming around happily until yesterday."
客人放了心，尝了一口。: Reassured, the customer took a bite.
可是，他突然露出了奇怪的表情。: But suddenly he made a strange face.
店员想了一会儿，礼貌地这样回答：: The server thought for a moment and then politely replied:
“是吗？一定是游得太多，累坏了吧。”: "Is that so? It must have tired itself out from swimming too much."
走路比坐公交还快: Walking is faster than the bus
旅行途中，有个人顺路来到了乡下的一个村子。: During a trip, a traveler stopped by a village in the countryside.
那个人向附近的一位老爷爷打听去车站的路。: The traveler asked an old man nearby the way to the station.
“不好意思，我有点赶时间，到车站要多长时间？”: "Excuse me, I'm in a hurry. How long does it take to get to the station?"
“走路二十分钟。坐公交的话，大概四十分钟吧。”: "Twenty minutes on foot. By bus, about forty minutes, I'd say."
那个人觉得很奇怪，又问道：: Thinking this was strange, the traveler asked again.
“诶？一般来说公交车更快啊，这是为什么呢？”: "What? The bus is usually faster, so why is that?"
老爷爷笑着，亲切地回答了他：: The old man laughed and kindly answered:
“因为下一班公交车三十五分钟后才来啊。”: "Because the next bus comes in thirty-five minutes."
顺路去: to stop by, to drop in
赶紧，着急: to hurry, to be in a hurry
前往: to go to, to head for
在夏天或秋天的祭典上，镇上的人们会抬起“神轿”。: At summer and fall festivals, the townspeople carry a "mikoshi" on their shoulders.
神轿的形状像一座小小的神社。: A mikoshi is shaped like a small shrine.
人们认为，祭典期间神明就坐在里面。: During the festival, a god is believed to be riding inside it.
因为非常重，必须由几十个人扛在肩上一起使劲抬。: It is very heavy, so dozens of people have to put it on their shoulders and carry it together with all their might.
“嘿哟、嘿哟”的响亮号子声，整个镇上都听得到。: Energetic shouts of "Wasshoi! Wasshoi!" can be heard all over town.
也有的祭典会一边让神轿大幅度摇晃一边前进。: At some festivals, the mikoshi is shaken wildly as it moves along.
据说这样做，神明的力量就会变强。: It is said that doing this makes the god's power stronger.
祭典那天，平时安静的小镇会变得非常热闹。: On festival days, the usually quiet town becomes very lively.
在日本，新年第一次用毛笔写字叫作“书初”（新春试笔）。: In Japan, writing characters with a brush for the first time in the new year is called "kakizome."
这是从古代一直延续下来的新年习俗。: It is a New Year's custom that has continued since long ago.
一般在一月二日写。: It is usually done on January 2.
人们会在大纸上写下“希望”“梦想”等当年想努力的事或喜欢的词语。: People write things they want to work hard at that year or words they like, such as 「希望」 (hope) or 「夢」 (dream), on a large sheet of paper.
小学生也常常把书初当作寒假作业来完成。: Elementary school students often do kakizome as winter vacation homework.
我每年都和爷爷一起写书初。: Every year, I do kakizome with my grandfather.
爷爷总是说：“不用想着要写得多好。”: My grandfather always says, "You don't have to try to write well."
“一个字一个字地，用心去写。”: "Write each character with all your heart."
今年我选了“笑脸”这个词来写，并把它挂在了房间的墙上。: This year, I chose the word 「笑顔」 (smile), wrote it, and hung it on the wall of my room.
爷爷去世已经一年了。: It has already been a year since my grandfather passed away.
收拾爷爷房间的时候，我发现了一块旧手表。: While I was tidying up his room, I found an old wristwatch.
听说那是爷爷年轻时用第一份工资买的手表。: Apparently it was a watch he bought with his first paycheck when he was young.
虽然它已经不走了，但这是爷爷珍爱的手表，所以我舍不得扔掉。: It no longer worked, but it was a watch my grandfather had treasured, so I couldn't throw it away.
拿去钟表店的时候，我担心它能不能修好。: When I took it to a watch shop, I was worried about whether it could be fixed.
不过，店员仔细地帮我修好了，并这样说道：: But the person at the shop carefully repaired it and said this:
“真是块好表啊。看得出来，它一直被人珍惜地使用着。”: "What a nice watch. I can tell it has been used with great care."
现在，这块手表戴在我的手腕上，又重新走了起来。: Now that watch is on my wrist, running again.
收拾，整理: to tidy up, to put in order
动，运转: to move, to work (of a machine)
上了大学，我开始一个人生活。: When I started university, I began living on my own.
第一天晚上，我正觉得有点寂寞的时候，爸爸发来了一条很短的消息。: On the first night, when I was feeling a little lonely, I got a short message from my father.
“还好吗？饭要好好吃啊。”: "How are you doing? Make sure you eat properly."
爸爸平时话不多，所以我有点吃惊。: My father usually doesn't talk much, so I was a little surprised.
从那以后，每周日爸爸都一定会发来差不多的消息。: Since then, every Sunday without fail, my father sends me a similar message.
听妈妈说，爸爸写一条消息要花整整三十分钟。: According to my mother, he spends a whole thirty minutes writing each message.
我想，那短短的消息里装满了爸爸的心意。: I think his short messages are full of his feelings.
我也每次都会回一条短短的消息。: I make a point of sending a short reply every time, too.
最近，我开始期待星期天的到来了。: These days, I've started looking forward to Sundays.
上小学时，我和朋友打棒球，球飞向邻居家的窗户，把玻璃打碎了。: When I was in elementary school, I was playing baseball with my friends when the ball flew into a neighbor's window and broke the glass.
我们害怕极了，马上就逃走了。: We got scared and ran away right away.
可是那天晚上，我怎么也睡不着。: But that night, I just couldn't sleep.
第二天，我一个人去那户人家道歉。: The next day, I went to that house by myself to apologize.
出来的老爷爷没有生气，而是说：“谢谢你诚实地来找我。”: The old man who came out didn't get angry; he said, "Thank you for coming and being honest."
然后，他说不用赔玻璃钱，希望我帮他打扫院子。: Then he said that instead of paying for the glass, he would like me to help him clean his garden.
从那以后，我开始每周都去老爷爷家。: After that, I started going to his house every week.
我从老爷爷那里学到了很多东西。: He taught me a lot of things.
田中老师在这所小学教了三十多年书。: Tanaka-sensei has taught at this elementary school for more than thirty years.
三月，老师就要离开学校了。: In March, the teacher was going to leave the school.
最后一堂课那天，老师在黑板上大大地写下了“谢谢”。: On the day of the last lesson, the teacher wrote "Thank you" in big letters on the blackboard.
然后说：“我从你们身上学到了很多很多。”: Then the teacher said, "I have learned so many things from all of you."
就在这时，教室的门开了，很多大人走了进来。: Just then, the classroom door opened, and lots of adults came in.
教室里的孩子们吓了一跳，回头看去。: The children in the classroom turned around in surprise.
他们都是以前跟着田中老师学习、从这所学校毕业的学生。: They were all students who had been taught by Tanaka-sensei long ago and had graduated from this school.
他们是为了向老师道谢而聚到一起的。: They had gathered to thank their teacher.
老师泪流满面，一句话也说不出来了。: In tears, the teacher could no longer say a word.
寿喜烧是用甜酱油味煮牛肉和蔬菜的料理。: Sukiyaki is a dish of beef and vegetables simmered in a sweet soy sauce flavor.
人们常在特别的日子全家聚在一起吃。: Families often get together to eat it on special days.
不过，关东和关西的做法有些不同。: However, the way it's made is a little different in the Kanto and Kansai regions.
关东一般是先准备好一种叫“割下”的甜酱汁。: In Kanto, people usually prepare a sweet sauce called "warishita" beforehand.
再把肉和蔬菜放进去，慢慢煮熟。: They put the meat and vegetables into it and cook them slowly.
关西则是先煎肉，再撒上砂糖、浇上酱油来调味。: In Kansai, people first sear the meat, then flavor it by adding sugar and soy sauce.
不过两边都一样，要蘸着打散的生鸡蛋吃。: In both styles, though, it's eaten dipped in beaten egg.
我家爸爸是关东人，妈妈是关西人。: In my family, my father is from Kanto and my mother is from Kansai.
所以，每次决定用哪种做法时，都会吵起来。: So every time we have to decide which way to make it, it turns into an argument.
烤，煎: to grill, to sear, to fry
生鸡蛋拌饭的早晨: A morning of tamago kake gohan
生鸡蛋拌饭，就是在热米饭上浇一个生鸡蛋，再加一点酱油来吃。: Tamago kake gohan is a dish in which you pour a raw egg over hot rice, add a little soy sauce, and eat it.
做法非常简单，但喜欢它的人很多。: It's very simple to make, but lots of people love it.
在国外，一般没有吃生鸡蛋的习惯。: In other countries, there usually isn't a custom of eating raw eggs.
在日本之所以能吃生鸡蛋，是因为生产时非常注意安全。: Raw eggs can be eaten in Japan because they are produced with great attention to safety.
日本超市卖的鸡蛋包装盒上写着“赏味期限”。: Egg cartons sold in Japanese supermarkets have a "shomi kigen" (best-before date) printed on them.
据说这指的是可以生吃的日期。: This is said to be the date until which the eggs can be eaten raw.
过了那一天的鸡蛋，最好充分加热后再吃。: Eggs past that date are better eaten after being thoroughly cooked.
只有酱油味也很好吃，不过我特别喜欢加点海苔和葱一起吃。: It's delicious with just soy sauce, but I especially like eating it with nori and green onions.
即使是忙碌的早晨也能轻松做好，所以我经常做。: It's easy to make even on busy mornings, so I make it often.
鹿儿岛县南边的海上，有一座叫屋久岛的岛。: In the southern waters of Kagoshima Prefecture, there is an island called Yakushima.
岛上的山里，有一棵据说已经活了几千年的大杉树。: In the mountains of this island, there is a huge cedar tree said to have lived for thousands of years.
为了看这棵树，很多人去爬山。: Many people climb the mountain to see that tree.
往返要花十个小时左右，所以要做好充分准备再去爬。: The round trip takes about ten hours, so prepare well before you climb.
屋久岛以雨水非常多而闻名。: Yakushima is known as an island with an extremely large amount of rain.
甚至有“一个月下三十五天雨”的说法。: There is even a saying that "it rains 35 days a month."
因为雨多，岛上到处是绿色的森林。: Because there is so much rain, the island is full of green forests.
这座岛也被列为世界遗产，景色非常美丽。: It is also a World Heritage Site, and the scenery on the island is truly wonderful.
这是一个值得去一次的地方。: It's a place you'll want to visit at least once.
坐夜班大巴去旅行: Setting off on a trip by night bus
我试着坐夜班大巴从东京去大阪旅行。: I tried traveling from Tokyo to Osaka by night bus.
晚上十一点左右出发，预计第二天早上七点左右到达。: It is scheduled to leave around 11 p.m. and arrive around 7 the next morning.
因为可以在睡觉的时候到大阪，能很好地利用时间。: Since you can get to Osaka while you sleep, you can make good use of your time.
而且比新干线便宜，这也是让人高兴的地方。: Plus, another nice thing is that it's cheaper than the shinkansen.
车里又暗又安静，座位上还装着帘子。: Inside, the bus was dark and quiet, and the seats had curtains.
一开始怎么也睡不着，回过神来天已经亮了。: At first I had trouble falling asleep, but before I knew it, it was morning.
我下了车，开始在清晨的大阪街头散步。: I got off the bus and started walking around Osaka in the morning.
一边走在街上，我一边觉得有点赚到了。: As I walked around the city, I felt like I'd gotten something extra out of the trip.
在日本的社区里，有一种叫“传阅板”的东西会在邻居之间挨家挨户地传。: In Japanese neighborhoods, something called a "kairanban" (circulating notice board) gets passed from house to house.
它是用来向社区里的大家传达重要通知的。: It is used to pass on important information to everyone in the neighborhood.
里面夹着垃圾收集日变更、社区祭典、地震和火灾演练等通知。: Inside are notices about things like changes to garbage collection days, local festivals, and earthquake and fire drills.
看完后，必须在自己名字旁边做个记号，再送到隔壁家。: After you read it, you have to put a mark next to your name and take it to the house next door.
刚搬来的时候，我不知道传阅板是干什么用的，结果在家里放了整整一个星期。: When I had just moved in, I didn't know what the kairanban was for, and I left it sitting in my house for a whole week.
结果，隔壁的太太笑着来取，说：“下一家是我们哦。”: Then the woman next door came over to get it, saying with a laugh, "We're next, you know."
我非常不好意思，马上道了歉。: I was very embarrassed and apologized right away.
从那以后，我都尽量看完就马上传给隔壁。: Since then, I make sure to pass it on to the house next door as soon as I've read it.
听到“欢迎光临”该怎么回答？: How should you answer 「いらっしゃいませ」?
走进日本的商店，店员会说“欢迎光临”。: When you enter a shop in Japan, the staff say 「いらっしゃいませ」 ("Welcome").
第一次来日本的外国人里，有人因为不知道该怎么回答而发愁。: Some foreigners who come to Japan for the first time are at a loss because they don't know how to respond.
不过，顾客什么都不回答也没关系。: But customers don't have to say anything in reply.
轻轻点一下头，或者微微一笑就足够了。: Just a slight bow of the head or a smile is enough.
什么都不说就在店里看看，也并不失礼。: It isn't rude to look around the shop without saying anything.
不过，离开店的时候，很多人会说“多谢款待”或“谢谢”。: However, many people say 「ごちそうさまでした」 ("Thank you for the meal") or 「ありがとう」 ("Thank you") when they leave.
特别是在小饭馆里这么说，店里的人也会很高兴。: Especially at small diners, the staff are happy when you say that.
话虽然短，心意却能好好地传达到。: Even a few short words get your feelings across.
福冈县的博多以明太子闻名。: Hakata in Fukuoka Prefecture is famous for mentaiko.
明太子是用一种叫鳕鱼的鱼的卵做成的食物。: Mentaiko is a food made from the roe of a fish called tara (cod).
因为用辣椒等腌渍调了味，所以有点辣。: It is marinated in chili pepper and other seasonings, so it's a little spicy.
因为和米饭特别搭，也有人早饭时吃。: It goes especially well with rice, so some people eat it for breakfast.
据说它最初源自韩国的料理。: It is said to have originally come from a Korean dish.
最近，它被用在饭团、意大利面等各种料理中。: These days, it's used in all kinds of dishes, such as rice balls and pasta.
博多机场和车站的特产柜台里摆满了明太子。: The souvenir sections at Hakata's airport and station are lined with lots of mentaiko.
有辣的，也有不太辣的，挑选也是一种乐趣。: There are spicy kinds and not-so-spicy kinds, and choosing is part of the fun.
很多人会把它当作带给家人的伴手礼，或送给关照过自己的人的礼物。: Many people buy it as a souvenir for their family or as a gift for people who have helped them.
腌，泡: to marinate, to pickle, to soak
合适，相配: to suit, to go well with
新潟县是日本有名的产米之乡。: Niigata Prefecture is one of Japan's famous rice-producing regions.
冬天特别冷，会下很多雪。: Winters are especially cold, and a lot of snow falls.
到了春天，那些雪融化，变成清澈的水。: In spring, that snow melts and turns into clean water.
这样的清水对种植大米非常重要。: This clean water is very important for growing rice.
多亏了这样的水和夏天的炎热，才能种出美味的大米。: Thanks to that water and the summer heat, delicious rice can be grown.
在新潟，用这里的米和水酿酒也很兴盛。: In Niigata, sake brewing using that rice and water is also thriving.
到了秋天，稻田变成一片金黄，景色非常美丽。: In the fall, the rice paddies turn golden, creating a beautiful landscape.
在新米上市的季节，光吃米饭就已经足够好吃了。: In the season when the new rice is harvested, plain rice alone is delicious enough.
去新潟的话，请一定尝一次那里的饭团。: If you go to Niigata, be sure to try a rice ball at least once.
花店的早晨来得早: Mornings start early at the flower shop
在花店工作的佐藤先生，一天从早上五点开始。: For Sato, who works at a flower shop, the day begins at five in the morning.
他先去市场，仔细挑选当天要卖的花。: First, he goes to the market and carefully chooses the flowers to sell that day.
回到店里后，把花的下端剪掉一点，泡进水里。: Back at the shop, he cuts a little off the bottom of the stems and puts the flowers in water.
据说这样做，花能好好吸水，开得更久。: Doing this apparently helps the flowers absorb water well, so they bloom longer.
冬天早上的水特别冰冷，有时手都会冻疼。: On winter mornings, the water is especially cold, and sometimes it even makes his hands hurt.
即便如此，佐藤先生说他非常喜欢这份工作。: Even so, Sato says he loves this job.
佐藤先生笑着说：“来买花的客人，心里总是想着某个人。”: "Customers who come to buy flowers are always thinking of someone," Sato says with a smile.
他说，做生日或庆祝用的花束时最幸福。: He says he is happiest when putting together flowers for birthdays and celebrations.
早上开始工作后，首先要把车辆和工具一件件检查一遍。: When they start work in the morning, they first check the vehicles and equipment one by one.
没有火灾的时候，也必须扛着沉重的水管练习跑步。: Even when there are no fires, they have to practice running while carrying heavy hoses.
晚上轮流睡觉，可一旦警铃响起，就要马上起来做准备。: At night they take turns sleeping, but when the bell rings, they get up immediately and get ready.
不只是火灾，用救护车运送病人也是他们的重要工作。: Fires aren't their only job: carrying sick people by ambulance is also important work.
第二天早上，下一班的人来了以后，才终于可以回家。: The next morning, when the next shift arrives, they can finally go home.
这是非常辛苦的工作，但一位消防员这样说道。: It's very hard work, but one firefighter says this:
“镇上的人能安心睡觉，是我最高兴的事。”: "What makes me happiest is that the people in town can sleep peacefully."
检查，调查: to check, to examine, to investigate
酉市的竹耙: Kumade rakes at Tori no Ichi
十一月的酉日，各地的神社等地会举办叫作“酉市”的节庆。: On the Days of the Rooster in November, a festival called "Tori no Ichi" is held at shrines and other places here and there.
店铺里摆满了用竹子做的“熊手”（竹耙）。: The stalls are lined with lots of bamboo "kumade" (rakes).
熊手原本是用来收集落叶的工具。: A kumade is originally a tool for gathering fallen leaves.
因为寓意“把财富和幸福聚集过来”，做生意的人常常购买。: Because it carries the meaning of "gathering money and happiness," people who run businesses often buy them.
买了熊手，店里的人会聚过来一起拍手。: When you buy a kumade, the stall staff gather around and all clap their hands together for you.
这叫作“手缔”（击掌祝福），到处都能听到充满活力的声音。: This is called "tejime," and lively voices can be heard from all around.
也有人每年都换买一个比前一年稍大一点的熊手。: Some people replace theirs every year with a kumade slightly bigger than the year before.
冬天临近的夜晚，神社里灯笼明亮，人头攒动，十分热闹。: On these nights with winter approaching, the shrines are lively with the glow of paper lanterns and crowds of people.
听着除夕的钟声: Listening to the New Year's Eve bells
十二月三十一日的夜晚，日本的寺庙会撞钟。: On the night of December 31, temples in Japan strike their bells.
这叫作“除夜之钟”，一般要撞一百零八下。: This is called "joya no kane," and the bell is usually struck 108 times.
据说人的心里有一百零八种烦恼。: It is said that the human heart has 108 worries.
听说钟声会把这些烦恼一个个消除。: The sound of the bell is said to erase them one by one.
也有的寺庙谁都可以去撞钟。: At some temples, anyone can strike the bell.
我家每年在这个特别的夜晚，都一边吃跨年荞麦面，一边听远处传来的钟声。: Every year on this special night, my family eats toshikoshi soba (year-end noodles) while listening to the sound of the bells drifting in from far away.
最后一声钟响的时候，新的一年就开始了。: Around the time the last bell rings, the new year begins.
在安静的夜里听着钟声，会想起这一年里的种种往事。: Listening to the bells on a quiet night, I remember all sorts of things from the past year.
来自越南的小安在日本的大学读书。: Anh, who came from Vietnam, is studying at a university in Japan.
小安之所以对日本产生兴趣，是因为小时候看了日本的动画。: Anh became interested in Japan because she watched Japanese anime as a child.
起初她看字幕，后来渐渐想直接听懂日语原声。: At first she watched with subtitles, but gradually she came to want to understand the Japanese voices just by listening.
于是，上高中时，她开始自学日语。: So when she was in high school, she began studying Japanese on her own.
现在她不仅对动画，对日本的历史和文学也很感兴趣。: Now she is interested not only in anime but also in Japanese history and literature.
小安说：“动画是架在我和日本之间的桥梁。”: "Anime is a bridge between me and Japan," Anh says.
她说将来想从事把日本动画翻译成越南语的工作。: In the future, she apparently wants to work translating Japanese anime into Vietnamese.
为了这个梦想，她现在也在努力地继续学习。: For the sake of that dream, she is still studying as hard as she can.
拼命，努力: with all one's might, very hard
日本漫画里会出现“扑通扑通”“轰轰轰”等很多拟声词。: Japanese manga are full of sound words, such as 「ドキドキ」 (a pounding heart) and 「ゴゴゴ」 (a menacing rumble).
其中最有意思的是“シーン”这个词。: One especially interesting one is the word 「シーン」.
这是在没人说话、一点声音也听不到的时候用的词。: It's a word used when nobody is saying anything and no sound can be heard at all.
用拟声词来写“没有声音”，有点与众不同吧。: Using a sound word to describe the absence of sound is a little unusual, isn't it?
据说这个“シーン”是从早期的漫画开始使用，后来用的人渐渐多了起来。: This 「シーン」 is said to have first been used in old manga, after which more and more people gradually started using it.
现在，日常对话中也会说“教室里一下子鸦雀无声”。: Today, it's even used in everyday conversation, as in 「教室がシーンとした」 ("The classroom went dead silent").
比如，老师提了一个难题的时候，教室里有时会一片安静。: For example, when a teacher asks a difficult question, the classroom sometimes goes completely silent.
读漫画的时候，也请留意一下画面里的拟声词。: When you read manga, try paying attention to the sound words in the pictures, too.
想不看字幕看懂日剧: I want to watch without subtitles
我开始学日语已经两年了。: It's been two years since I started studying Japanese.
我的梦想是能不看字幕看懂日本的电视剧。: My dream is to be able to understand Japanese dramas without looking at the subtitles.
为此，我每天晚上看一集喜欢的电视剧。: To that end, I watch one episode of a drama I like every night.
第一遍打开日语字幕，把不懂的词查一查，记在笔记本上。: The first time, I turn on Japanese subtitles, look up words I don't know, and write them down in my notebook.
第二遍当作复习，关掉字幕，模仿演员的台词说一说。: The second time, as review, I turn off the subtitles and try saying the actors' lines, imitating them.
电视剧里的日语和课本上的日语不同，语速快、简短的说法多。: The Japanese in dramas is different from textbook Japanese: it has lots of fast, short expressions.
一开始完全听不懂，但每晚坚持下来，渐渐也习惯了快速的日语。: At first I couldn't understand anything at all, but as I kept at it every night, I gradually got used to fast Japanese.
上周，我第一次在不用字幕的情况下从头看懂到尾，开心极了。: Last week, for the first time, I understood a story all the way to the end without using subtitles, and I was so happy.
有用，有帮助: to be useful, to be helpful
追了三个月的电视剧，今晚终于迎来大结局。: Tonight is finally the last episode of the drama I've been watching for three months.
在公司里，午休时大家也都在聊这件事。: At the office, too, everyone was talking about it during lunch break.
“你觉得两个人最后会结婚吗？”: "Do you think the two of them will get married in the end?"
为了赶上晚上九点的播出，我匆匆忙忙地完成了工作。: I hurried to finish my work so I'd be in time for the 9 p.m. broadcast.
回到家后，我坐在电视机前，等着节目开始。: When I got home, I sat down in front of the TV and waited for the show to start.
节目结束后，听着片尾曲，我愣愣地发了好一会儿呆。: After the show ended, I sat there in a daze for a while, listening to the closing song.
第二天早上，我和同事一对上眼，两个人同时说：“看了吗？”: The next morning, when I made eye contact with a coworker, we both said at the same time, "Did you watch it?"
新干线最前面的车厢，像鼻子一样又长、前端又尖细。: The front car of a shinkansen is long like a nose and narrows toward the tip.
这不仅仅是为了好看。: This isn't just to make it look cool.
高速列车进入隧道时，里面的空气会被用力挤压。: When a fast train enters a tunnel, the air inside gets pushed hard.
因此，有时会在出口发出很大的声音。: Because of this, there is sometimes a loud noise at the exit.
把车头做长，就能把这种声音变小。: Making the nose longer makes it possible to reduce this noise.
有一款新干线，是参考一种叫翠鸟的小鸟的喙的形状设计出来的。: One shinkansen was designed by studying the shape of the beak of a small bird called the kingfisher.
因为翠鸟扎进水里的时候，也几乎不溅起水花。: That's because a kingfisher makes almost no splash, even when it dives into water.
从大自然学到的东西，在技术上派上了用场。: Things learned from nature are proving useful in technology.
有用，起作用: to be useful, to serve a purpose
地震前响起的手机: The phone that rings before an earthquake
上课的时候，教室里所有人的手机突然大声响了起来。: During class, everyone's smartphones in the classroom suddenly started ringing loudly.
这是在强烈的地震摇晃到来之前，通过手机和电视通知大家的东西。: This is a system that alerts people through their smartphones and TVs before the shaking from a big earthquake arrives.
地震发生时，最先到来的是小的震波，之后才是强烈的摇晃。: When an earthquake occurs, small waves arrive first, followed by strong shaking.
它会分析这些小震波，通知大家随后到来的摇晃会有多强。: The system analyzes these small waves and announces how strong the shaking that follows will be.
从手机响起到开始摇晃，有时只有几秒钟。: Sometimes there are only a few seconds between the phone going off and the shaking starting.
即便如此，也足够让人钻到桌子底下或者关掉火。: Even so, it gives you time to get under a desk or turn off the stove.
那天摇晃并不大，但老师说：“下次也要像这样行动哦。”: That day, the shaking was small, but our teacher said, "Next time, move the same way, okay?"

在车站前美发店工作的山田，一天从早上9点半打扫店内开始。: For Yamada, who works at a hair salon in front of the station, the day begins at 9:30 in the morning with cleaning the salon.
10点开门，但在那之前必须准备毛巾、确认预约等。: The salon opens at 10, but before then she has to get the towels ready, check the reservations, and so on.
客人来了以后，她首先会仔细询问头发方面的烦恼，以及想要什么样的感觉。: When a customer comes in, she first asks carefully about any concerns they have with their hair and what kind of look they want.
很多人会拿照片给她看，但据说根据发质不同，有时也剪不成一样的。: Many people show her photos, but she says that depending on the type of hair, it sometimes won't turn out the same.
这种时候，她会如实说明，尽量和客人一起考虑适合的发型。: In such cases, she makes a point of explaining honestly and thinking together with the customer about a hairstyle that will suit them.
周六和周日预约都排满了，忙得连吃午饭的时间都没有。: On Saturdays and Sundays she is fully booked, and so busy that she doesn't even have time to eat lunch.
因为一整天都站着，下班后脚非常累。: Since she is on her feet all day long, her feet are very tired when work is over.
关门后，为了掌握新技术，她还和后辈一起继续练习剪发。: Even after closing, she keeps practicing cuts with her junior colleagues in order to learn new techniques.
山田说，看到客人高兴地说着“清爽多了”离开时的表情，疲劳也就忘掉了。: Yamada says that when she sees the faces of customers who leave happy, saying, "That feels so much fresher," she forgets all about being tired.
适合: to suit, to look good on
留学生开银行账户: An international student opens a bank account
来日本两周左右的时候，为了领打工的工资，我决定去开一个银行账户。: About two weeks after I came to Japan, I decided to open a bank account so I could receive my wages from my part-time job.
我在柜台取了写着号码的纸，坐在椅子上等着叫到自己的号码。: I took a numbered ticket at the counter and sat in a chair, waiting until my number was called.
申请表上除了地址和电话号码以外，还有一栏要写开户的目的。: On the application form, besides my address and phone number, there was also a space to write my purpose for opening the account.
正当我面对满是汉字的文件发愁时，银行的工作人员亲切地教了我怎么写。: As I sat puzzling over the paperwork full of kanji, a bank employee kindly showed me how to fill it out.
出示了在留卡和护照后，手续不到一个小时就办完了。: Once I showed my residence card and passport, the procedure was finished in less than an hour.
这家银行的提款卡不能当场拿到，说是一周左右以后会邮寄过来。: At this bank, I couldn't get my cash card on the spot; I was told it would arrive by mail about a week later.
临走时，工作人员还告诉我，在深夜或节假日使用ATM，有时会收取手续费。: As I was leaving, they told me that using the ATM late at night or on holidays can sometimes cost a fee.
一周后，打开寄到信箱里的信封、把卡拿在手里时，我真的很高兴。: A week later, when I opened the envelope that had arrived in my mailbox and held the card in my hand, I was really happy.
我觉得自己好像又适应了一点日本的生活。: I felt as though I had gotten a little more used to life in Japan.
报春的大风: A strong wind that announces spring
二月初立春过后，会有某一天突然从南边刮来又强又暖的风。: Shortly after risshun, the traditional start of spring in early February, there comes a day when a strong, warm wind suddenly blows in from the south.
这种风叫做“春一番”，它告诉人们冬天快要结束了。: This wind is called 「春一番」 (haru ichiban), and it tells us that winter is nearing its end.
在天气预报里听到这个词，很多人都会觉得春天快到了吧。: When they hear this word in the weather forecast, many people probably feel that spring is just around the corner.
不过，春一番刮过的第二天，又变冷的情况也不少。: However, it is not unusual for the cold to come back the day after haru ichiban blows.
据说这原本是在海上干活的渔民们之间使用的词。: It is said that it was originally a word used among fishermen who worked at sea.
因为强风会让海上波涛汹涌，有时会发生事故，所以它作为需要警惕的风而为人所知。: Because the strong wind could make the sea rough and sometimes caused accidents, it was known as a wind to watch out for.
现在这一天电车也可能晚点，晾的衣服也可能被吹走。: Even today, on this day trains are sometimes delayed and laundry hung out to dry gets blown away.
另外，因为花粉和沙尘会一下子飞起很多，也能看到戴着口罩出门的人。: Also, since a lot of pollen and dust gets blown around all at once, you see people going out wearing masks.
春天的到来虽然令人高兴，但刮大风的日子出门时要多加小心。: The beginning of spring is a happy thing, but on windy days, let's take care when going out.
立春: Risshun, the first day of spring (in the traditional calendar)
（海）波涛汹涌: (of the sea) to be rough, to be stormy
在车站站台或检票口附近，有站着吃的荞麦面店。: On station platforms and near ticket gates, there are soba shops where you eat standing up.
很多店没有椅子，客人站在柜台前匆匆吃面。: Many of these shops have no chairs, and customers stand at the counter and eat their soba quickly.
点餐后转眼间就端出来，对忙碌的上班族来说是很难得的店。: Since your food comes out in no time after you order, they are a godsend for busy office workers.
有的店采用先买餐券再点餐的方式。: At some shops, the system is that you buy a meal ticket first and then order.
受欢迎的是放了什锦炸天妇罗的荞麦面，以及放了甜煮油豆腐的狐狸荞麦面。: Popular choices are soba topped with kakiage, a mixed tempura fritter, and kitsune soba, topped with sweet simmered fried tofu.
关东多是颜色偏黑的浓汤汁，关西多是颜色浅的汤汁，各地味道不同也是有趣之处。: In the Kanto region the broth is usually dark and strong, while in the Kansai region it is usually light in color, and the way the flavor differs from region to region is another interesting point.
我早上有时会晚坐一班电车，在这里吃一碗热荞麦面。: In the morning, I sometimes take a later train and eat a bowl of hot soba here.
寒冷的冬天早上，吸溜一口冒着热气的荞麦面，身体从里到外都暖和起来。: On cold winter mornings, slurping steaming soba warms you up from the inside.
吃完后把碗还回去，说一声“我吃好了”，是这种店的小礼节。: When you finish eating, returning your bowl and saying 「ごちそうさま」 (gochisosama) is a little bit of etiquette at shops like this.
空出一张桌子的早晨: The morning one desk was empty
上周五，坐在我旁边的佐藤辞职了。: Last Friday, Sato, who sat next to me, left the company.
我刚进公司时，从头开始教我做事的就是佐藤。: When I joined the company, it was Sato who taught me how to do the work from scratch.
我犯错情绪低落的时候，她总会在我桌上放一罐咖啡，笑着说“下次就没问题了”。: Whenever I made a mistake and felt down, she would put a can of coffee on my desk and say with a smile, "You'll be fine next time."
听说她决定回老家，帮忙打理家里的店。: I heard she decided to go back to her hometown to help out at her family's shop.
周一早上来到公司，旁边的桌子已经收拾得干干净净。: When I came to work on Monday morning, the desk next to mine had been neatly cleared.
我带着有点寂寞的心情打开自己的抽屉，里面放着一张字迹熟悉的便条和一罐咖啡。: Feeling a little lonely, I opened my drawer, and inside were a note in familiar handwriting and a can of coffee.
便条上写着“今后就轮到你教新人了哦”。: The note said, "From now on, it's your turn to teach the new people."
读到这句话，我差点哭了。: Reading those words, I almost cried.
对于下个月要来的新人，我打算像佐藤对我那样温柔地教他。: I intend to teach the newcomer who joins next month kindly, just as Sato did for me.
消沉: to feel down, to be depressed
老家；娘家: one's family home; (a married woman's) parents' home
收拾: to tidy up, to put away
太相信地图应用的朋友: My friend who trusted his map app too much
我的朋友健太是个严重的路痴。: My friend Kenta has a terrible sense of direction.
所以据说他最近不管去哪儿，都尽量用手机的地图应用。: So lately, he says, he makes a point of using the map app on his phone wherever he goes.
上周我们俩约好去一家新开的咖啡馆，在车站西口碰头。: Last week, the two of us planned to go to a newly opened café, and we met up at the west exit of the station.
健太说“今天有应用，交给我吧”，信心满满地走了起来。: Kenta said, "Today I've got the app, so leave it to me," and set off walking, full of confidence.
然而，走了好一会儿，咖啡馆还是没出现。: But even after we had walked for a while, there was no sign of the café.
不仅如此，我们又走回了刚才经过的那个公园门口。: Worse still, we came out in front of the same park we had passed earlier.
我觉得奇怪，给店里打了电话，店员告诉我们：“出了车站东口，就在正对面哦。”: Thinking something was off, I called the café, and the clerk told us, "Come out of the east exit of the station, and we're right in front of you."
结果回到车站，从另一侧的出口出去，咖啡馆真的就在出口正前方。: In the end, when we went back to the station and came out of the exit on the opposite side, the café really was right in front of the exit.
健太说“不是应用的错，是路自己绕远了”，可谁也不信。: Kenta says, "The app wasn't wrong. The road took a detour," but nobody believes him.
路痴: poor sense of direction, person who easily gets lost
眼前: right in front of one's eyes
绕远: detour, going the long way around
送到病房的视频信: A video letter delivered to a hospital room
去年秋天，住在乡下的爷爷住院了。: Last fall, my grandfather, who lives in the countryside, had to go into the hospital.
医院很远，在东京工作的父亲和上大学的我都很难去看他。: The hospital was far away, and neither my father, who works in Tokyo, nor I, a university student, could easily go to see him.
于是我们决定做一个视频信，让家人和亲戚每人说一段简短的话。: So we decided to make a video letter in which family members and relatives each said a short message.
小表弟唱了歌，妈妈拍下了自己做爷爷爱吃的萩饼的样子。: My little cousin sang a song, and my mother filmed herself making ohagi, my grandfather's favorite sweet.
做好的视频，我们拜托护士用病房的平板电脑放给他看。: We asked a nurse to show him the finished video on a tablet in his hospital room.
后来听护士说，爷爷把同一个片段反复看了好多遍。: Later, the nurse told us that my grandfather had watched the same scene over and over.
那是我一边展示小时候和爷爷去钓鱼的照片一边讲话的片段。: It was the scene where I talked while showing a photo of the time I went fishing with my grandfather when I was little.
冬天出院后，爷爷在电话里对我说：“我们再一起去钓鱼吧。”: When he was discharged in the winter, my grandfather said to me on the phone, "Let's go fishing together again."
今年春假，我打算按照约定，和爷爷一起去河边。: This spring break, as promised, I plan to go out to the river with my grandfather.
住院: hospitalization, being admitted to the hospital
一拆开就发热的暖宝宝: Heat packs that warm up when you open the bag
日本冬天不可缺少的东西之一，是一次性暖宝宝。: One of the things you can't do without in a Japanese winter is the disposable heat pack, or kairo.
从袋子里拿出来一会儿，明明没用火，却会慢慢地热起来。: When you take one out of its bag, after a little while it gradually grows warm, even though no fire is involved.
这是因为里面的铁粉和空气中的氧气结合时会放出热量。: This is because the iron powder inside gives off heat when it combines with the oxygen in the air.
这和铁生锈是同样的反应，不过加入了盐和水等，设计得让反应进行得更快。: It is the same reaction as iron rusting, but salt, water, and other things are added so that it proceeds faster.
它装在袋子里出售，是为了在使用前不接触空气。: They are sold sealed in bags so that they don't come into contact with air before use.
暖宝宝有贴在衣服外面的类型、拿在手里用的类型等各种各样的种类。: There are many kinds of heat packs, such as the type you stick on over your clothes and the type you hold in your hand.
不过，长时间放在同一个地方，有可能会造成低温烫伤。: However, if you keep one against the same spot for a long time, there is a risk of getting a low-temperature burn.
特别是睡觉的时候，要注意不要直接贴在皮肤上。: Especially when you go to sleep, be careful not to stick one directly on your skin.
用完的暖宝宝，请按照所住城市的规定扔掉。: Please dispose of used heat packs according to the rules of the town where you live.
设法；花心思: devising a way; putting thought into something
接触: to touch, to come into contact with
在乒乓球部学到的东西: What I learned in the table tennis club
上初中时，不擅长运动的我随随便便就进了乒乓球部。: When I started junior high school, I was bad at sports, and I joined the table tennis club without much thought.
因为我觉得就算个子小、力气不大，好像也能打。: That was because I thought I could probably manage it even though I was small and not very strong.
然而真正打起来才发现，乒乓球是比想象中激烈得多的运动。: But when I actually tried it, table tennis turned out to be a much more intense sport than I had thought.
为了能对快球做出反应，我们几乎每天都要跑步、练习步法。: To be able to react to fast balls, we ran and practiced our footwork almost every day.
一年级的夏天，参加比赛总是第一轮就输。: In the summer of my first year, whenever I played in a match, I always lost in the first round.
我很不甘心，决定每天早上早早去学校，坚持对着墙练习击球。: It was so frustrating that I decided to go to school early every morning and keep practicing hitting the ball against a wall.
结果，在二年级秋天的比赛中，我第一次打进了第三轮。: Then, at a tournament in the fall of my second year, I made it to the third round for the first time.
比起赢球，更让我高兴的是明白了只要坚持就会一点点改变。: More than winning, what made me happy was realizing that if I kept at it, things would change little by little.
现在每当事情不顺利时，我也会让自己想起那时早上的练习。: Even now, whenever something isn't going well, I make a point of remembering those morning practices.
一把扇子演落语: Rakugo, performed with a single folding fan
落语是从江户时代延续下来、用讲述逗人发笑的日本传统表演艺术。: Rakugo is a traditional Japanese performing art, dating back to the Edo period, that makes people laugh through storytelling.
穿着和服的落语家独自坐在坐垫上讲故事。: A rakugo storyteller in a kimono sits alone on a zabuton cushion and tells a story.
无论有多少个登场人物，他都一个人通过改变脸的朝向和声调来分别扮演所有人。: No matter how many characters there are, the storyteller plays them all single-handedly, telling them apart by changing which way they face and the tone of their voice.
使用的道具基本上只有扇子和手巾两样。: Basically, only two props are used: a folding fan and a tenugui hand towel.
扇子时而变成吃荞麦面的筷子，时而变成写信的毛笔。: The fan can become chopsticks for eating soba or a brush for writing a letter.
手巾常用来表示钱包、书之类扁平的东西。: The tenugui is often used to represent flat objects, such as a wallet or a book.
落语家发出声音吸溜荞麦面的场面，看起来就像真的在吃一样，令人吃惊。: In scenes where the storyteller noisily slurps soba, it is amazing how it really looks as though they are eating.
也就是说，观众从很少的道具展开想象，在脑海中构建故事的世界。: In other words, the audience lets their imagination expand from just a few props and builds the world of the story in their heads.
东京和大阪有叫做“寄席”的落语剧场，可以轻松地去欣赏。: In Tokyo and Osaka, there are rakugo theaters called 「寄席」 (yose), where you can casually go and enjoy it.
曲艺场: theater for rakugo and other traditional comic arts
像白鹭一样的姬路城: Himeji Castle, like a white bird
位于兵库县的姬路城是日本最有名的城堡之一。: Himeji Castle in Hyogo Prefecture is one of the most famous castles in Japan.
白色的墙壁非常美丽，样子看起来像展翅的白鸟，因此也被称为“白鹭城”。: Its white walls are very beautiful, and because its shape looks like a white bird spreading its wings, it is also called 「白鷺城」 (Hakuro-jo), "White Heron Castle."
现在的天守阁建于江户时代初期，挺过了战争和地震，至今保持着当时的样子。: The present keep was built at the beginning of the Edo period, and having survived wars and earthquakes, it still stands just as it was back then.
1993年，它和奈良的法隆寺一起，被登录为日本最早的世界文化遗产。: In 1993, together with Horyuji Temple in Nara, it was registered as one of Japan's first World Cultural Heritage sites.
要登上天守阁，必须爬好几段又陡又窄的木楼梯。: To climb the keep, you have to go up several steep, narrow wooden staircases.
里面比想象中宽敞，好几根粗柱子支撑着建筑。: Inside, it is more spacious than you might expect, and many thick pillars hold up the building.
从天守阁最高处可以远眺姬路的街景。: From the top of the keep, you can look out far across the city of Himeji.
从姬路站可以笔直走到城堡，所以坐新干线的话，当天往返也足够尽兴。: You can walk straight to the castle from Himeji Station, so if you take the shinkansen, you can fully enjoy it even on a day trip.
樱花季节，白色城堡和粉色樱花交相辉映，景色格外美丽。: In cherry blossom season, the white castle and the pink blossoms overlap to create especially beautiful scenery.
挺过；克服: to survive, to get through; to overcome
当天往返: going and returning the same day, day trip
南蛮鸡是诞生于宫崎县的鸡肉料理。: Chicken nanban is a chicken dish that originated in Miyazaki Prefecture.
把裹上面衣炸好的鸡肉在酸甜的酱汁里过一下，上面再浇上满满的塔塔酱。: Battered, fried chicken is dipped in a sweet-and-sour sauce and then topped with plenty of tartar sauce.
外面酥脆，里面柔软，是让人一口接一口扒饭的味道。: It is crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, with a flavor that keeps you reaching for more rice.
据说它起源于昭和中期宫崎县延冈市的一家西餐馆，最初是做给店员吃的员工餐。: It is said to have started in the middle of the Showa era as a staff meal for employees at a Western-style restaurant in Nobeoka, Miyazaki Prefecture.
不过，据说最初的吃法并不浇塔塔酱，是后来别的店才配上了塔塔酱。: However, it was originally eaten without tartar sauce, and apparently a different restaurant later added the tartar sauce.
现在在宫崎的很多食堂和便当店都能吃到。: Today, you can eat it at many diners and bento shops in Miyazaki.
它也出现在全国的便利店和家庭餐厅里，成了大家非常熟悉的味道。: It is now also sold at convenience stores and family restaurants across the country and has become a thoroughly familiar flavor.
在家也能做，不过在当地的店里吃的话，你一定会惊叹于酱汁和塔塔酱的绝妙平衡。: You can make it at home too, but if you eat it at a restaurant in its home region, you are sure to be amazed at how well the sweet-and-sour sauce and the tartar sauce are balanced.
去宫崎旅行时，请一定去几家店比较着尝尝看。: When you travel to Miyazaki, be sure to try it at several restaurants and compare them.
正宗产地: home (of something), authentic place of origin
读懂对话框的形状: Reading the shapes of speech balloons
看漫画时，我们不仅从画面，也从对话框的形状接收到很多信息。: When we read manga, we take in a great deal of information not only from the pictures but also from the shapes of the speech balloons.
圆润平滑的对话框表示普通的对话。: Round, smooth balloons indicate ordinary conversation.
如果边缘呈锯齿状，就能看出是在大声喊叫或者在生气。: If the edges are jagged, you can tell that the character is shouting loudly or is angry.
像云一样蓬松的形状，多数情况下表示没说出口、只在心里想的事。: Puffy, cloud-like shapes often show something a character is thinking without saying it out loud.
用虚线画的对话框，大概是在小声嘀咕吧。: If a balloon is drawn with a dotted line, the characters are probably whispering in low voices.
另外，在日本漫画里，对话框里的文字一般是竖着写的。: Also, in Japanese manga, the text inside speech balloons is usually written vertically.
因此对话框多是竖长的形状。: For that reason, speech balloons are often tall and narrow.
我听说翻译成外语时，要配合这种形状填入文字是件很费劲的事。: I have heard that when manga is translated into foreign languages, fitting the text to this shape is quite a challenge.
留意对话框重新读一遍的话，也许会发现作者细致的用心。: If you reread a manga while paying attention to the speech balloons, you may notice the author's careful little touches.
小时候暑假的白天，电视上常常播放老电视剧的重播。: When I was a child, reruns of old dramas were often shown on TV in the daytime during summer vacation.
不想写作业的日子，和奶奶并排坐着看那些电视剧是我的乐趣。: On days when I didn't feel like doing my homework, sitting next to my grandmother and watching those dramas was something I looked forward to.
那是我出生前拍的校园剧，剧中人物的衣服和电话的样子在我看来都很稀奇。: It was a school drama made before I was born, and the characters' clothes and the shapes of the telephones looked very unusual to me.
节目一开始，奶奶每次都说同样的话：“这个老师真好啊。”: Whenever the show started, my grandmother would say the same thing every time: "This teacher is so good."
长大后的现在，我在视频平台上偶然发现了那部剧。: Now that I'm an adult, I happened to come across that drama on a video streaming service.
怀着怀念的心情点开第一集，那时听不懂的台词深深打动了我。: Feeling nostalgic, I played the first episode, and lines I hadn't understood back then struck a chord in my heart.
看到老师不责备学生的失败、一直相信和等待的样子，我不禁流下了眼泪。: Seeing the teacher, who never blamed the students for their failures but believed in them and waited for them to the very end, I couldn't help crying.
我觉得终于明白了奶奶夸那位老师的理由。: I feel I finally understand why my grandmother praised that teacher.
下次回老家，我打算和奶奶一起再看一遍。: Next time I go home to my family, I plan to watch it once more with my grandmother.
回响；打动: to echo; to move, to strike a chord
在日本想坐出租车，刚伸手去拉门，门就突然开了，被吓一跳的外国人不少。: Quite a few foreigners have been startled in Japan when they reached for a taxi door and it suddenly swung open.
日本的出租车大多可以让司机坐在座位上开关后排左侧的车门。: In most Japanese taxis, the driver can open and close the rear left door while staying in their seat.
驾驶座附近有一根拉杆，扳动它门就会打开或关上。: There is a lever near the driver's seat, and moving it opens or closes the door.
因此，上车和下车时，乘客都不需要自己开关车门。: So passengers don't need to open or close the door themselves, either when getting in or when getting out.
据说这种装置是在昭和中期左右普及开来的。: This system is said to have spread around the middle of the Showa era.
这是为了让乘客舒服乘车的服务，不过也有说法称，是为了防止车门被粗暴关上而损坏车辆: It is a service to give passengers a pleasant ride, but there is also a story that it was meant to keep the cars from being damaged by doors being slammed.
不习惯的话，差点会被打开的车门撞到，所以稍微离远一点等比较好。: If you are not used to it, you might nearly get hit by the opening door, so it is a good idea to wait a little way back.
另外，下车时想自己关门的话，司机可能会对你说“就那样放着没关系”。: Also, if you try to close the door yourself when getting out, the driver may tell you, "That's all right, you can leave it."
对从国外来的人来说，这似乎也是日本的小惊喜之一。: For people from abroad, this seems to be another of Japan's little surprises.
伸: to stretch out, to reach out
傍晚响起的旋律: The melody that plays in the evening
在日本很多城镇，一到傍晚，全镇的喇叭里就会响起旋律。: In many towns in Japan, a melody plays from speakers all over town when evening comes.
曲子因地而异，常用的是童谣《晚霞》。: The song differs from town to town, but a children's song called 「夕焼け小焼け」 (Yuyake Koyake) is often used.
听到这个，在公园里玩的孩子们就知道“该回家了”，纷纷往家走。: When they hear it, children who have been playing in the park head home, thinking, "It's time to go home."
很多地方是五点，不过也有的地方冬天早一些、夏天晚一些。: In many places it plays at five o'clock, but some towns apparently make it earlier in winter and later in summer.
其实这个广播不仅是告诉孩子回家的时间，还有另一个重要的目的。: Actually, this broadcast has another important purpose besides letting children know it's time to go home.
那就是每天确认地震、暴雨等灾害时使用的喇叭能否正常工作。: That is to check every day whether the speakers used during disasters such as earthquakes and heavy rain are working properly.
万一紧急时声音传不到，就无法保护居民的生命。: If announcements cannot reach people in an emergency, the lives of the town's residents cannot be protected.
刚来日本的时候，我对这音乐为什么每天都放感到很奇怪。: When I had just come to Japan, I wondered why this music played every day.
知道理由后，每次听到这旋律，心里都会感到有点安心。: Since learning the reason, I feel a little reassured every time I hear the melody.
在水族馆照顾海豚的中村，早上从准备鱼开始。: For Nakamura, who looks after the dolphins at an aquarium, the morning begins with preparing fish.
每头海豚吃的鱼的种类和量都是定好的，每天都要仔细称重。: The type and amount of fish each dolphin eats is set individually, and the fish are carefully weighed every day.
因为吃的量和吃法的变化，是了解身体状况的重要线索。: That is because changes in how much they eat and how they eat are important clues to their physical condition.
在表演练习中，海豚做得好，就马上吹哨，然后喂鱼。: In practice for the shows, as soon as a dolphin does something well, she blows a whistle and gives it a fish.
据说这样一来，海豚就会记住做什么能被表扬。: Apparently, by doing this, the dolphins learn what they need to do to be praised.
海豚也各有各的性格，没心情的日子完全不听话。: Each dolphin has its own personality, and on days when they're not in the mood, they won't listen to her at all.
那种日子不勉强它，而是增加玩耍时间，努力建立信赖关系。: On such days, she makes a point of not pushing them; instead, she spends more time playing with them to build a relationship of trust.
冬天水很冷，打扫水池非常辛苦，但她从没想过辞职。: The water is cold in winter and cleaning the pool is very hard work, but she has never once wanted to quit.
据说看到表演结束后孩子们眼睛闪闪发光，她就觉得选择这份工作真好。: She says that when she sees the children's eyes shining after a show, she feels glad she chose this job.
用便签本交谈的客人: The customer who talked with me through a notepad
我是大学生，在车站附近的咖啡馆打工。: I'm a university student, and I work part-time at a café near the station.
有一天，一位来到收银台的上了年纪的男士没有开口点单，而是递出了一个小便签本。: One day, an elderly man came to the register and, without saying his order, held out a small notepad.
上面写着：“我耳朵听不见。请给我一杯热咖啡。”: On it was written, "I can't hear. One hot coffee, please."
我有点慌，但还是借过便签本，写上“要什么杯型？”给他看。: I was a little flustered, but I borrowed the notepad, wrote, "What size would you like?" and showed it to him.
那位男士笑了笑，写下“小杯就好”。: The man smiled and wrote, "A small one."
从那天起，那位男士每周一早上都会来店里。: From that day on, the man started coming to the café every Monday morning.
我在收银台旁放了一本自己用的便签本，决定每次写上一两句天气之类的话和他交流。: I kept a notepad of my own next to the register and decided to talk with him by writing a line at a time about things like the weather.
有一天早上，我从他那里收到一张写着“和你聊天是我一周的乐趣”的便条。: One morning, the man gave me a note that said, "Talking with you is what I look forward to all week."
那时我才第一次意识到，语言并不是只能靠声音传达的。: At that moment I realized for the first time that words are not something conveyed by voice alone.
递出: to hold out, to hand over
“不好意思”太多的一天: A day of too many 「すみません」
刚来日本的留学生小王，对“すみません”这个词感到非常不可思议。: Wang, an international student who had just come to Japan, found the word 「すみません」 (sumimasen) endlessly puzzling.
叫店员时、问路时、收到东西道谢时，日本人都说“すみません”。: When calling a server, when asking for directions, and even when receiving something and saying thank you, Japanese people say 「すみません」.
一直以为这是道歉用语的小王，不明白为什么大家都那么爱道歉。: Wang had learned that it was a word for apologizing, so he couldn't understand why everyone apologized so much.
于是他决定先试试自己也对什么事都说“すみません”。: So he decided that, for the time being, he would try saying 「すみません」 about everything himself.
那天，小王在电车上被人让座时说“すみません”，在车站问路时也说“すみません”。: That day, Wang said 「すみません」 when someone gave up their seat for him on the train, and 「すみません」 when he asked for directions at the station.
在拉面店叫店员时说“すみません”，拿到水又说“すみません”。: At a ramen shop, he said 「すみません」 to call the server, and 「すみません」 when he was given water.
结果回家路上被人踩了脚时，他也不由自主地说了“すみません”。: Then, on his way home, when someone stepped on his foot, he found himself saying 「すみません」 without thinking.
踩人的那位也吓了一跳，连忙说“すみません”道歉，两个人互相鞠了好几次躬。: The person who had stepped on him was startled too and apologized with a 「すみません」, and the two of them bowed to each other again and again.
据说那天晚上，小王在日记里写道：“今天我离日本人又近了一步。”: That night, Wang reportedly wrote in his diary, "Today I came one step closer to being Japanese."
让: to give up (a seat, etc.), to yield
日本的夏天不仅气温高，湿度也大，所以中暑的人不少。: Japanese summers are not only hot but also humid, so quite a few people suffer from heatstroke.
中暑是在体内积聚热量、无法顺利散发到体外时发生的。: Heatstroke occurs when heat builds up inside the body and can no longer be released properly.
起初会感到头晕、头痛、乏力等，严重时可能会失去意识。: At first you feel dizziness, a headache, fatigue, and so on, and when it gets worse you may even lose consciousness.
不仅在外面运动时会发生，待在家里也会发生，所以需要注意。: It can happen not only when you are exercising outdoors but also when you are at home, so you need to be careful.
为了预防，要在口渴之前就勤补充水分。: To prevent it, make a point of drinking fluids frequently, before you feel thirsty.
出了很多汗的时候，不只是水，补充盐分也很重要。: When you have sweated a lot, it is important to take in not only water but also salt.
在室内请不要硬撑，要开空调，别让温度太高。: Indoors, please don't try to tough it out; use the air conditioner and don't let the temperature get too high.
外出时戴帽子、选阴凉的地方走也有效果。: When you go out, wearing a hat and choosing shady places to walk are also effective.
如果附近有看起来不舒服的人，要把他带到凉快的地方，帮他给身体降温。: If someone near you looks unwell, take them to a cool place and help them cool their body down.
带竹枝回家的十日戎: Toka Ebisu, where you take home a bamboo branch
每年1月9日到11日，大阪的今宫戎神社都会举行名为“十日戎”的祭典。: Every year from January 9 to 11, a festival called 「十日戎」 (Toka Ebisu) is held at Imamiya Ebisu Shrine in Osaka.
惠比寿神作为生意之神，自古以来就受到商人们的尊崇。: Ebisu has long been revered by merchants as the god of business.

人们领取叫做“福笹”的竹枝，请人在上面挂上金币、米袋形状的装饰。: People receive bamboo branches called 「福笹」 (fukuzasa), "lucky bamboo," and have ornaments shaped like old gold coins and rice bales attached to them.
给人挂装饰的，是被称为“福娘”的年轻女性们。: The ones who attach the ornaments are young women called 「福娘」 (fukumusume).

我受公司前辈邀请，第一次去了十日戎。: At the invitation of a senior colleague at work, I went to Toka Ebisu for the first time.
人多得让我吃惊，但拿着竹枝走路的人们脸上都很开朗，连我也变得有精神了。: I was surprised by the crowds, but the faces of the people walking with their bamboo branches were all bright, and it lifted my spirits too.
为了今年一年工作顺利，我把那根竹枝装饰在公司桌子旁边。: So that my work will go well all this year, I have put that bamboo branch on display beside my desk at the office.
亲子丼是把鸡肉用甜咸的高汤煮好，再用鸡蛋包裹起来，盖在米饭上的料理。: Oyakodon is a dish of chicken simmered in a sweet and savory broth, bound with egg, and served over rice.
因为鸡是父母、蛋是孩子，据说因此起名为“亲子”。: It is said to have gotten the name 「親子」 (oyako), "parent and child," because the chicken is the parent and the egg is the child.
第一次听到这个名字的含义时，我觉得有点可怜，但还是忍不住笑了出来。: When I first heard what the name meant, I felt a little sorry for them, but I couldn't help laughing.
那么，用牛肉或猪肉代替鸡肉的话，叫什么呢？: So what is it called when beef or pork is used instead of chicken?
也就是说，因为牛、猪和鸡蛋不是亲子，而是“外人”。: The idea is that a cow or a pig and an egg are not parent and child; in other words, they are strangers (tanin).
做好吃亲子丼的诀窍，是不要把蛋搅得太匀，也不要煮得太老。: The trick to making delicious oyakodon is not to beat the eggs too much and not to overcook them.
趁鸡蛋还半熟时关火，马上把它滑到米饭上。: Turn off the heat while the egg is still soft and immediately slide it onto the rice.
也有的店使用专用的小平底锅，一份一份地快速做出来。: Some restaurants use small special pans and quickly make each serving one at a time.
在家也能很快做好，非常适合忙碌日子的午饭。: You can make it at home in a short time too, so it is perfect for lunch on a busy day.
富山县的名产之一是“鳟鱼寿司”。: One of Toyama Prefecture's specialties is 「ますずし」 (masuzushi), trout sushi.
它是在圆形木盒里铺上竹叶，把醋饭和腌过的鳟鱼肉叠放压紧做成的，是押寿司的一种。: It is a type of pressed sushi made by spreading bamboo leaves in a round wooden container, then layering vinegared rice and salt-cured trout and pressing them together.
自古以来人们就认为竹叶有让食物不易变质的作用。: Since long ago, bamboo leaves have been thought to help keep food from spoiling.
因为从上面压上重物来定型，米饭和鱼充分融合，味道恰到好处。: Because a weight is placed on top to set its shape, the rice and fish meld together well and the flavor turns out just right.

吃的时候打开竹叶，用菜刀或刀子把整块圆形的饭切开。: To eat it, you open the bamboo leaves and cut the round block of rice into portions with a kitchen knife or a table knife.
像切蛋糕一样切开吃，对第一次吃的人来说好像很新鲜。: Cutting it up like a cake to eat it seems to strike first-timers as novel.
每家店鳟鱼的厚度和醋的浓淡都不同，寻找自己喜欢的味道也是乐趣之一。: The thickness of the trout and the strength of the vinegar vary from shop to shop, so searching for the flavor you like is part of the fun.
因为比较耐放，也常被选作旅行的伴手礼。: Because it keeps well, it is also a popular choice as a souvenir from a trip.

跳舞的傻子，看舞的傻子: Fools who dance and fools who watch
每年8月盂兰盆节前后，德岛县都会举行“阿波舞”。: Every year around Obon in August, the 「阿波おどり」 (Awa Odori) dance festival is held in Tokushima Prefecture.
这是据说有四百多年历史的盂兰盆舞，整座城市都被三味线和太鼓的声音包围。: It is a Bon dance said to have more than four hundred years of history, and the whole city is filled with the sound of shamisen and taiko drums.
舞者以叫做“连”的团体为单位，一边跳一边沿街前进。: The dancers make their way down the streets, dancing in groups called 「連」 (ren).
男性压低身体有力地跳，女性则戴着斗笠、连指尖都整齐优美地跳，这是它的特点。: Its hallmark is that the men dance powerfully in a low stance, while the women wear straw hats and dance in beautiful unison right down to their fingertips.
阿波舞的歌里有一句有名的话：“跳舞的是傻子，看舞的也是傻子，同样是傻子，不跳就吃: The Awa Odori song contains the famous line 「踊る阿呆に見る阿呆、同じ阿呆なら踊らにゃそんそん」: "The dancers are fools and the watchers are fools; if we're all fools alike, you lose out if you don't dance!"
意思是光看太可惜了，一起来享受吧。: It means that just watching would be a waste, so come and join the fun.

每二十年焕然一新的伊势神宫: Ise Jingu, reborn every twenty years

江户时代有“一生要去一次伊势参拜”的说法，有人从远方花好几天走来。: In the Edo period, people said, "Make the pilgrimage to Ise at least once in your life," and some walked for days from far away.
伊势神宫有一项叫“式年迁宫”的仪式，每二十年把社殿全部重新建造一次。: Ise Jingu has a ceremony called 「式年遷宮」 (Shikinen Sengu), in which all the shrine buildings are completely rebuilt once every twenty years.
据说这从约一千三百年前延续至今，最近一次是在2013年举行的。: It is said to have continued for about 1,300 years, and the most recent one was held in 2013.
通过每二十年建造同样形状的建筑，把建造技术传给下一代。: By building structures of the same form every twenty years, they pass on the techniques for building them to the next generation.
参拜内宫之前，要走过一座叫宇治桥的大木桥。: Before worshipping at the Inner Shrine, you cross a large wooden bridge called Uji Bridge.
走在森林中的参道上，空气清新，心情自然就平静下来。: As you walk along the approach through the forest, the air is clean, and you naturally begin to feel calm.
参拜之后，一边逛附近的街道一边吃名产伊势乌冬面，也是一大乐趣。: After worshipping, it is also a pleasure to stroll through the nearby streets and eat the local specialty, Ise udon.
伊势乌冬面是在又粗又软的面条上拌上黑色偏甜的酱汁来吃。: Ise udon is eaten by coating thick, soft noodles in a dark, sweetish sauce.
参拜道路: approach (path) to a shrine or temple
源自一支笔的公司名: A company name born from a single pencil
不用削就能一直写的自动铅笔，是日本学生不可缺少的文具。: The mechanical pencil, which lets you keep writing without sharpening it, is a piece of stationery Japanese students can't do without.
一点点推出笔芯来使用的这种笔，其原型诞生于外国。: The prototype of this pencil, which you use by pushing the lead out a little at a time, was born abroad.
1915年，在东京从事金属加工的早川德次对其进行改良，做出了结实好用的笔。: In 1915, a man named Tokuji Hayakawa, who was doing metalwork in Tokyo, improved on it and made one that was sturdy and easy to use.
他将其命名为“Ever-Ready Sharp Pencil”开始销售。: He named it the "Ever-Ready Sharp Pencil" and put it on the market.
这种笔在海外也很畅销，“自动铅笔”这个词也传遍了日本。: This pencil sold well overseas too, and the word 「シャープペンシル」 (sharp pencil), the Japanese term for a mechanical pencil, spread all over Japan.
然而，1923年的关东大地震让他失去了工厂，早川迁到大阪，重新开始创业。: However, after losing his factory in the Great Kanto Earthquake of 1923, Hayakawa moved to Osaka and started a new business.
那家公司后来开始制造收音机和电视，并以笔的名字为公司名，叫做“夏普”。: That company later began making radios and televisions, and it took the company name "Sharp" from the name of the pencil.
知道以电器闻名的公司名字来自一支笔，也许会有点吃惊。: You may be a little surprised to learn that the name of a company famous for electronics comes from a single pencil.
铅笔盒里的自动铅笔，也有这样悠久的历史。: Even the mechanical pencil in your pencil case has such a long history.
我妈妈每周五晚上都在附近小学的体育馆打排球。: Every Friday night, my mother plays volleyball in the gym of a nearby elementary school.
那是当地的妈妈们聚在一起组成的队伍，这种活动被叫做“妈妈排球”。: It is a team formed by mothers in the community, and this kind of activity is called 「ママさんバレー」 (mama-san volleyball).
成员从三十多岁到六十多岁都有，她们做完工作和家务后来练习。: The members range from their thirties to their sixties, and they come to practice after finishing their work and housework.
妈妈学生时代在排球部，她说能回想起从前，很开心。: My mother was on the volleyball team in her school days, so she says it's fun because it brings back the old days.
有一天，我也跟着妈妈去看练习。: One day, I went along with my mother to watch practice.
大家虽然有说有笑，但球一来就表情认真，扑向地板救球。: Everyone was laughing, but when the ball came their way, their faces turned serious and they dove to the floor.
六十多岁的成员比我动作还快，扣出了有力的球，真的让我很吃惊。: I was really surprised when a member in her sixties moved faster than I do and hit a powerful spike.
练习后，大家一起用拖把把体育馆的地板擦干净再回家。: After practice, everyone mops the gym floor together to clean it before going home.
妈妈说：“即使上了年纪，有活动身体的地方和伙伴也是件幸福的事。”她的脸上神采奕奕: "Even when you get older, having a place to move your body and friends to do it with is a happy thing," my mother said, and her face was full of life.
去了远方的好友: My best friend who moved far away
从小学起就在一起的好友小唯，高二那年春天因为父亲工作的关系要搬去福冈。: In the spring of our second year of high school, my best friend Yui, who had been with me since elementary school, had to move to Fukuoka because of her father's work.
从东京到福冈很远，不是能随便见面的距离。: Fukuoka is far from Tokyo, not a distance where you can casually meet up.
最后一天在车站送她的时候，我为了不哭，一直低着头。: On the last day, when I saw her off at the station, I kept my eyes on the ground the whole time so I wouldn't cry.
小唯说了句“我每天晚上都会给你发消息哦”，就上了电车。: Yui said, "I'll send you a message every night, okay?" and got on the train.
最初一个月，我们真的每晚都互相报告学校里发生的事。: For the first month, we really did tell each other what had happened at school every night.
但是，随着彼此的新生活变得忙碌，联系渐渐少了。: But as we each got busier with our new lives, we were in touch less and less.
一连几天没有回复，我就不安起来，担心她是不是已经把我忘了。: When day after day went by without a reply, I started to worry that she had already forgotten about me.
就在这时，有一天家里收到一个小包裹，里面是福冈的点心和一封信。: Then one day, a small package arrived at my house, and inside were sweets from Fukuoka and a letter.
信上写着：“就算不能每天聊天，我们也永远是好朋友。”: The letter said, "Even if we can't talk every day, we'll always be best friends."
那时我才意识到，重要的不是联系的次数，而是想着对方的心意。: At that moment I realized that what matters is not how often you are in touch but how much you care about each other.
电话那头的声音: The voice on the other end of the line
小林在一家家电厂商的客服中心工作，负责回答客户的咨询。: Kobayashi works at the call center of a home appliance manufacturer, answering inquiries from customers.
早上9点开始受理后，电话几乎不间断地响个不停。: Once the lines open at 9 a.m., the phones keep ringing almost without a break.
“洗衣机不转了”“不知道遥控器怎么用”等等，每天的内容各种各样。: The calls are different every day: "My washing machine won't run," "I don't know how to use the remote," and so on.
因为看不到对方的脸，必须只靠语言准确地理解情况。: Since she can't see the caller's face, she has to understand the situation accurately from words alone.
小林注意不用专业术语，配合对方慢慢地说明。: Kobayashi makes a point of explaining slowly, at the caller's pace, without using technical terms.
其中也有一开始就生气、大声嚷嚷的客户。: Some customers are angry from the start and raise their voices.
据说即使在那种时候，重要的也是先把话听完，理解对方为难的心情。: Even then, she says, what matters is to first hear them out to the end and acknowledge how troubled they feel.
问题解决后，听到对方说“找你咨询真是太好了”，疲劳一下子就烟消云散了。: When a problem is solved and she is told, "I'm glad I talked to you," her tiredness vanishes all at once.
据说下班后，为了让嗓子休息，她会喝杯热茶，悠闲地度过。: After work, to rest her throat, she makes a point of drinking warm tea and taking it easy.
中断: to be interrupted, to break off
留心；注意: to bear in mind; to take care to
买了自行车要做防盗登记: Bought a bicycle? Get it registered
在日本买自行车时，店员会引导你办理“防盗登记”手续。: When you buy a bicycle in Japan, the store staff will walk you through the procedure for 「防犯登録」 (bohan toroku), anti-theft registration.
防盗登记是把自行车编号和车主的姓名、地址记录下来的制度，是法律规定的义务。: Anti-theft registration is a system for keeping a record of a bicycle's number along with its owner's name and address, and it is required by law.
手续可以在买车的店里当场办理，只要出示身份证件，很快就能办完。: You can complete the procedure on the spot at the store where you bought the bicycle, and if you show ID, it is done right away.
登记完成后，自行车上会贴上一张写着编号的小贴纸。: Once registration is complete, a small sticker with the number on it is put on the bicycle.
在日本，警察有时会叫住骑自行车的人，核对登记号码。: In Japan, police officers sometimes stop people riding bicycles and check their registration numbers.
这是为了确认是不是被盗的自行车。: This is to make sure the bicycle isn't a stolen one.
我刚来留学的时候，也在回家路上被叫住，非常紧张。: When I had just started studying abroad, I was stopped on my way home too, and I was very nervous.
不过因为登记得好好的，只用了几分钟，警察就对我说“路上小心”。: But since my registration was properly in order, after only a few minutes the officer said, "Have a safe trip home."
从朋友那里接手自行车时，需要重新登记，可别忘了。: When you take over a bicycle from a friend, you need to register it again, so don't forget.
叫住: to call out to (someone) to stop
家族传承的小标志: A small emblem passed down in the family
日本有一种叫“家纹”的标志，代表各个家族。: In Japan, there are emblems called 「家紋」 (kamon) that represent individual families.
多是在圆圈里组合花、叶、鸟等的设计，种类多得数不清。: Many are designs that combine flowers, leaves, birds, and so on inside a circle, and there are so many kinds that they can hardly be counted.
据说最初是平安时代的贵族把它加在自己的车和随身物品上。: They are said to have started with Heian-period nobles putting them on their carriages and belongings.
后来武士为了在战场上区分敌我，开始把它用在旗帜等上面。: Later, samurai began to use them on banners and the like so they could tell friend from foe on the battlefield.
现在婚礼上穿的黑色和服、墓碑上，有时也会有家纹。: Even today, family crests sometimes appear on the black kimono worn at weddings, on gravestones, and so on.
我在奶奶家翻看旧相册时，注意到和服胸前有一个小图案。: While looking through an old photo album at my grandmother's house, I noticed a small pattern on the chest of a kimono.
问了奶奶，她告诉我那是我家的家纹，是三片叶子组合在一起的形状。: When I asked my grandmother, she told me it was our family crest, a design made of three leaves put together.
知道自己家也有这样的标志，我感觉好像和遥远的祖先联系在了一起。: Learning that my family has such an emblem too, I somehow felt connected to my distant ancestors.
现在还有用家纹做设计的T恤和小物件，在年轻人中也很受欢迎。: Nowadays there are also T-shirts and accessories that use family crests in their designs, and they are becoming popular among young people as well.
上大学后，我开始了扮成动画角色的“cosplay”。: After I started university, I took up 「コスプレ」 (cosplay), dressing up as anime characters.
最开始穿的是买来的服装，但渐渐地开始在意细节。: At first I wore costumes I had bought, but gradually I started to be bothered by the small details.
于是我决定从零开始，自己做喜欢的作品里主人公的衣服。: So I decided to try making the outfit of the main character from my favorite series myself, from scratch.
我把动画画面暂停了好多次，连衣服的形状、颜色、纽扣的数量都仔细确认。: I paused scenes of the anime over and over, carefully checking the shape and colors of the clothes, right down to the number of buttons.
