自从初中上课以来就没用过缝纫机，一开始连直线都缝不好。: It was my first time using a sewing machine since class in junior high school, and at first I couldn't even sew a straight line.
我一边在视频上查做法、向手工艺店的人请教怎么选布料，花了两个月终于做好了。: Looking up how to make it in videos and asking the staff at a craft store how to choose fabric, I spent two months finishing it.
第一次穿着那套衣服去参加活动时，有陌生人问我：“这衣服是你自己做的吗？”: When I wore that costume to an event for the first time, a stranger came up to me and asked, "Did you make that outfit yourself?"
和同样喜欢这部作品的人聊得很投机，时间一下子就过去了。: We had a lively conversation with others who loved the same series, and the time flew by.
制作虽然辛苦，但我觉得通过喜欢的东西交到朋友，才是cosplay最大的魅力。: Making it was hard work, but I think the greatest appeal of cosplay is being able to make friends through the things you love.
血型能看出性格吗？: Can your blood type reveal your personality?
在日本，有时会被刚认识的人问：“你是什么血型？”: In Japan, people you have just met sometimes ask you, "What's your blood type?"
因为不少人认为可以通过血型知道性格，比如“A型人认真”“O型人大方”。: That is because quite a few people think blood type reveals personality, as in "Type A people are serious" or "Type O people are easygoing."
电视和杂志上也经常介绍血型占卜。: Blood-type fortune-telling has also often been featured on TV and in magazines.
从中国来的我，起初不明白这个问题的意思，还以为是医院里才会问的问题。: Having come from China, I didn't understand what this question meant at first and thought it was the kind of thing you get asked at a hospital.
然而，血型与性格之间存在关系的科学证据并没有找到。: However, no scientific evidence has been found that there is a relationship between blood type and personality.
即便如此它依然是流行的话题，也许是因为它作为和对方聊天的契机很方便。: Even so, it may be because it is handy as a way to start a conversation that it has spread as a topic.
实际上，聊起血型，和初次见面的人也很快就能聊得热火朝天。: In fact, if you bring up blood types, the conversation livens up right away, even with someone you have just met.
不过，也有人被断定“因为是B型所以自私”而感到不快，所以需要注意。: However, some people have had unpleasant experiences of being labeled, as in "You're selfish because you're type B," so you need to be careful.
当作游戏来玩没关系，但最好不要把它当作判断一个人的依据。: It's fine to enjoy it as a game, but it's best not to use it as grounds for judging people.
体检的前一天: The day before the health checkup
公司职员田中有个习惯，每年春天体检一临近，就会突然改变生活方式。: Tanaka, an office worker, has a habit of suddenly changing his lifestyle every spring as his health checkup approaches.
从一周前开始戒酒，每晚慢跑，晚饭光吃蔬菜。: Starting a week before, he gives up drinking, goes jogging every night, and eats nothing but vegetables for dinner.
本人非常认真地说：“我要在一周里完成一年份的努力。”: "I'm putting a whole year's worth of effort into one week," he says, completely in earnest.
今年他也同样努力，前一天晚上什么都没吃就早早睡了。: This year he worked just as hard, and on the night before, he went to bed early without eating anything.
第二天早上，田中信心满满地前往公司附近的医院。: The next morning, Tanaka headed confidently to the clinic near his office.
在前台报了名字后，护士一脸疑惑地看了看预约表。: When he gave his name at the reception desk, the nurse looked at the appointment list with a puzzled expression.
“田中先生，您的体检是下周一哦。”: "Tanaka, your health checkup is scheduled for next Monday."
田中沉默了一会儿，终于小声说道：: Tanaka was silent for a while, but eventually he spoke up in a small voice.
“那么，还得再忍一个星期不喝啤酒了……”: "So I have to go without beer for another week, then..."
静静等待的导盲犬: The guide dog that waits quietly
我每天早上坐的电车上，有一位和导盲犬一起通勤的女士。: On the train I take every morning, there is a woman who commutes with her guide dog.
狗安静地趴在女士脚边，即使电车摇晃也一动不动。: The dog lies still at the woman's feet and doesn't move a bit, even when the train sways.
因为太可爱了，有一天我不由得伸手想去摸它。: It was so adorable that one day I reached out to pet it without thinking.
这时那位女士察觉到了动静，温和地说：“不好意思，它现在正在工作。”: The woman sensed it and said gently, "I'm sorry, but it's working right now."
后来查了才知道，不能随便摸导盲犬或者跟它说话。: I looked it up later and learned that you must not touch or talk to a guide dog without permission.
因为狗的注意力一旦被打断，就可能无法安全地为主人引路。: That is because if the dog's concentration is broken, it may not be able to guide its owner safely.
从那以后，我只在心里对它说“今天也加油哦”。: Since then, I only say to it silently, "Do your best today too."
一个下雨的早上，我在车站楼梯看到那位女士有些为难，就问她：“需要帮忙吗？”: One rainy morning, I saw the woman having trouble on the station stairs and asked her, "Can I help you with anything?"
女士笑着回答：“谢谢，能陪我走到检票口吗？”: The woman smiled and replied, "Thank you. Could you walk with me to the ticket gate?"
狗也轻轻摇了摇尾巴，好像在道谢一样。: The dog also gave a little wag of its tail, just as if it were saying thank you.
穿过海底的隧道: A tunnel beneath the sea floor
本州和北海道之间，隔着一片叫津轻海峡的海。: Between Honshu and Hokkaido lies a stretch of sea called the Tsugaru Strait.
从那片海的海底下面穿过、连接两座岛的就是青函隧道。: The Seikan Tunnel passes beneath the floor of that sea, connecting the two islands.
全长约54公里，1988年开通。: It is about 54 kilometers long and opened in 1988.
据说从勘察到完工花了二十多年，克服了海水涌入事故等许多困难。: It reportedly took more than twenty years from the surveys to completion, overcoming many difficulties, such as accidents in which seawater flooded in.
隧道建成之前，人们乘坐叫“青函联络船”的船往返于青森和函馆之间。: Before the tunnel was built, people traveled between Aomori and Hakodate by the ship called the 「青函連絡船」 (Seikan Renrakusen), the Seikan ferry.
据说天气不好时船有时无法出航，冬天出行非常辛苦。: It is said that the ship sometimes couldn't sail in bad weather, so traveling in winter was very hard.
现在北海道新干线经过这条隧道，从东京到新函馆北斗不用换乘就能到达。: Today the Hokkaido Shinkansen runs through this tunnel, and you can go from Tokyo to Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto without changing trains.
我去年也坐过，隧道里一片漆黑，不太有身在海底的真实感。: I rode it last year, but it was pitch dark inside the tunnel, and I didn't really feel like I was under the sea.
即便如此，想到过去人们的辛劳，就能深深体会到这条隧道的重要。: Even so, when I think of the hardships people went through in the past, I fully understand how important this tunnel is.
秋夜鸣叫的虫: Insects that sing on autumn nights
夏天的暑热平息后，夜里的草丛中开始传来各种虫鸣。: Once the summer heat settles down, you begin to hear the voices of all kinds of insects from the grass at night.
像铃铛一样“铃——铃——”叫的是金钟儿，“叮叮咚咚”叫的是松虫。: The one that chirps "riin, riin" like a little bell is the suzumushi (bell cricket), and the one that chirps "chinchirorin" is the matsumushi (pine cricket).
听虫鸣感受秋意的习惯，自古就存在于日本人的生活中。: The custom of sensing autumn in the voices of insects has been part of Japanese life since long ago.
古代的和歌里，也有很多以虫鸣为题材的作品。: Many classical waka poems, too, take the voices of insects as their subject.
据说江户时代还有一种叫“听虫”的消遣，人们专门去原野欣赏虫鸣。: In the Edo period, there was apparently even a pastime called 「虫聞き」 (mushikiki), "insect listening," in which people went out to the fields especially to enjoy the insects' songs.
据说许多日本人觉得虫鸣就像音乐一样。: It is said that many Japanese people hear insect sounds as something like music.
另一方面，从国外来的朋友说：“听起来不过是噪音而已。”: On the other hand, a friend from abroad told me, "It just sounds like noise to me."
即使是同样的声音，也许听起来的感觉也会因成长环境不同而改变。: Perhaps even the same sound is heard differently depending on the environment you grew up in.
今晚不如把窗户打开一点，关掉电视，侧耳倾听虫儿们的演奏吧？: Tonight, why not open the window a little, turn off the TV, and listen to the insects' performance?
倾（耳）: to incline (one's ear), to lend (an ear)
红豆面包是在面包里包入甜豆馅、诞生于日本的面包。: Anpan is a Japanese-born bread with sweet red bean paste inside.
据说它是明治初期东京银座的一家面包店“木村屋”想出来的。: It is said to have been invented at the beginning of the Meiji era by Kimuraya, a bakery in Tokyo's Ginza district.
对当时的日本人来说，面包还是不熟悉的食物。: For Japanese people at the time, bread was still an unfamiliar food.
于是他们包入日本人喜欢的豆馅，并用做酒馒头时的酵母让面团发起来。: So the bakers wrapped it around red bean paste, which Japanese people loved, and made the dough rise using the yeast used for sake manju buns.
据说这种面包一上市就大受好评，店门前排起了长队。: As soon as this bread went on sale, it reportedly became the talk of the town, and lines formed in front of the shop.
此外还做出了在中央放上盐渍樱花的款式，因进献给天皇而出了名。: They also created a version with a salt-pickled cherry blossom placed in the center, which became famous after it was presented to the Emperor.
现在除了细豆沙和颗粒豆馅，还有奶油、青豌豆馅等各种各样的种类。: Today, besides smooth bean paste and chunky bean paste, there are many other varieties, such as cream and sweet green pea paste.
结合了面包和日式点心优点的红豆面包，可以说正是东西方相遇而诞生的味道吧。: Combining the best of bread and wagashi, anpan could truly be called a flavor born from the meeting of East and West.
我累了的时候，配着牛奶吃红豆面包是一个小小的乐趣。: When I'm tired, eating anpan with a glass of milk is one of my small pleasures.
姐姐成为护士的契机: How my sister came to be a nurse
我姐姐在大学医院当护士。: My older sister works as a nurse at a university hospital.
姐姐立志做这份工作的契机，是初中时看的一部医疗剧。: What first made her set her sights on this job was a medical drama she watched when she was in junior high school.
那是以急救中心为舞台的故事，据说她被为了救人而四处奔忙的护士的身影打动了。: It was a story set in an emergency medical center, and she says she was moved by the nurses running around to save lives.
从那以后，姐姐每晚都努力学习原本不擅长的理科，一直学到很晚。: From then on, my sister started working hard every night until late at science, which had been her weak subject.
我问现在在真正的医院工作的姐姐，电视剧和实际工作有什么不同。: I asked my sister, who now works in a real hospital, how the dramas differ from the actual work.
姐姐笑着说：“并不是像电视剧那样每天都会发生戏剧性的事。”: She laughed and said, "It's not as if dramatic things happen every day like in a drama."
据说实际上大部分是写记录、听患者说话之类不起眼的工作。: In reality, she says, most of the work is unglamorous, like writing up records and listening to patients.
不过她说，被出院的患者道谢的那一刻，比电视剧还要感人。: Even so, she said, the moment a patient leaving the hospital says "thank you" is more moving than any drama.
看着姐姐，我觉得一部电视剧有时也能改变一个人的人生。: Watching my sister, I think a single drama can sometimes change a person's life.
立志；以……为目标: to aspire to; to aim for
在东海道新干线的线路中，冬天最费周折的地方之一是岐阜县关原一带。: Of all the stretches the Tokaido Shinkansen runs along, one of the most troublesome in winter is the area around Sekigahara in Gifu Prefecture.
这里群山环绕，受来自日本海的冷风影响，有时会下大雪。: This area is surrounded by mountains, and because of the cold winds that come from the Sea of Japan, it sometimes gets a lot of snow.
由于新干线速度很快，车辆底部附着的雪如果中途掉落，可能会把轨道上的石子溅起来，打: Because the shinkansen runs so fast, if snow stuck to the underside of a car falls off along the way, it can kick up stones from the track and break windows and other things.
于是人们采用了在轨道旁设置洒水器洒水的方法。: So a method is used in which sprinklers are placed beside the tracks to spray water.
用水把雪打湿，雪就不容易飞扬起来，可以减少附着在车辆上的量。: Wetting the snow makes it less likely to fly up, which reduces the amount that sticks to the cars.
即便如此，下大雪的日子因为要减速行驶，到达时间有时会稍有延误。: Even so, on days of heavy snow, the trains run at reduced speed, so they sometimes arrive a little late.
另外据说在沿途车站，作业人员会清除附着在车辆上的雪。: Also, at stations along the way, workers apparently clear off the snow stuck to the cars.
每当冬天从新干线的窗口眺望白茫茫的关原，我都会想起这些洒水器。: Every time I look out from the shinkansen window at snow-white Sekigahara in winter, I think of those sprinklers.
总是准点运行的新干线背后，有着这样踏实的创意和努力。: Behind the shinkansen, which always runs on time, lies steady ingenuity and effort like this.
飞扬: to fly up, to swirl up
搬纸箱的春天: A spring of carrying cardboard boxes
大二那年春假，我决定去搬家公司打工。: During spring break in my second year of university, I decided to work part-time at a moving company.
三月到四月因为升学、工作调动而搬家的人多，是一年中最忙的时期。: March through April is the busiest time of the year, because many people move to start school or for job transfers.
早上7点在公司集合，坐上卡车，前往当天第一位客户的家。: We gather at the company at 7 a.m., get in the truck, and head to the home of the day's first customer.
到了之后，首先铺开厚垫子，保护地板和墙壁不被划伤。: When we arrive, we first spread out thick sheets to protect the floors and walls from getting scratched.
前辈教我，搬重物时不要靠手臂的力气，而要弯曲膝盖用腿的力量抬起来。: A senior coworker taught me that when carrying something heavy, you should lift it with your legs by bending your knees, not with the strength of your arms.
冰箱、洗衣机这样的大件，要两个人一边互相招呼一边慢慢地搬下楼梯。: Large items like refrigerators and washing machines are carried slowly down the stairs by two people calling out to each other.
有时一天要跑三户人家，累得一回家就睡着了。: Some days we went to three homes, and I was so tired that I fell asleep as soon as I got home.
尽管如此，把东西全部搬进新家后，听到客户说“这下可以开始新生活了”，我就很高兴。: Even so, when we had finished carrying everything into the new place and the customer said, "Now I can start my new life," it made me happy.
我觉得这是一份能帮助别人迈出新一步的美好工作。: I think it's a wonderful job that lets you help people make a fresh start.
升学: advancing to the next level of school
爷爷教我的将棋: The shogi my grandfather taught me
上小学时，暑假去爷爷家，他总是在檐廊上教我下将棋。: When I was in elementary school and went to my grandfather's house during summer vacation, he always taught me shogi on the veranda.
将棋是先让对方的王将无路可走的一方获胜的日本传统游戏。: Shogi is a traditional Japanese game in which the winner is the player who first leaves the opponent's king unable to move.
它和国际象棋相似，但可以把吃掉的对方棋子当作自己的棋子使用，这是它的一大特点。: It is similar to chess, but its big distinguishing feature is that you can use your opponent's pieces that you have captured as your own.
爷爷很厉害，我一次都没赢过，每次输了都不甘心地哭。: My grandfather was strong, and I never once beat him; every time I lost, I cried out of frustration.
有一年夏天，也许是爷爷故意让着我，我第一次赢了他。: One summer, perhaps because my grandfather let me win on purpose, I was able to beat him for the first time.
对欣喜若狂的我，爷爷说：“输了会不甘心，正是这种心情让人变强啊。”: As I jumped for joy, my grandfather said to me, "Feeling frustrated when you lose is what makes a person stronger."
如今爷爷已经去世，只有那副旧将棋盘留在我的房间里。: My grandfather has since passed away, and only his old shogi board remains in my room.
最近我开始教上小学的儿子下将棋，儿子一输也马上哭起来。: Recently I started teaching shogi to my son, who is in elementary school, and he too bursts into tears as soon as he loses.
看着这样的儿子，我就想起当年在檐廊上哭的自己，不由得笑了出来。: Watching him, I'm reminded of myself crying on that veranda, and I can't help laughing.
檐廊: veranda (along the outside of a Japanese house)
日本的节日中，有些不是按日期，而是规定为“几月的第几个星期一”。: Some Japanese national holidays are set not by date but as "the Nth Monday of a given month."
比如，成人节是1月的第二个星期一，敬老节是9月的第三个星期一。: For example, Coming of Age Day is the second Monday of January, and Respect for the Aged Day is the third Monday of September.
以前成人节是1月15日，敬老节是9月15日，都是按日期规定的。: In the past, these were fixed by date: Coming of Age Day was January 15, and Respect for the Aged Day was September 15.
把这些节日挪到星期一的就是“快乐星期一制度”，从2000年起陆续实施。: What moved these holidays to Mondays is the "Happy Monday System," which was introduced in stages starting in 2000.
现在，成人节、海洋日、敬老节、体育日这四个节日适用这一制度。: Currently, four holidays are covered by this system: Coming of Age Day, Marine Day, Respect for the Aged Day, and Sports Day.
星期一放假的话，接着周六周日就成了三连休。: When Monday is a day off, it follows Saturday and Sunday to make a three-day weekend.
出游变得方便了，旅游景点和交通工具都热闹起来。: It has become easier to go on trips, and tourist spots and transportation have gotten busier.
另一方面，也有人反对这一制度，认为“原来的日期是有意义的”。: On the other hand, some people oppose this system, saying, "But the original dates had meaning."
此外，还能听到大学的烦恼：总是周一的课放假，课时比其他日子少。: You also hear of a problem at universities: Monday classes keep getting canceled for holidays, so there are fewer of them than on other days of the week.
在享受三连休的同时，也想稍微想一想每个节日的意义。: While enjoying the three-day weekends, it would be nice to think a little about the meaning of each holiday as well.
奶奶过了七十岁以后，开始在附近的公园打门球。: After she turned seventy, my grandmother took up gateball at a nearby park.
门球是用木槌击球，让球依次穿过三个球门，最后撞击终点柱的运动。: Gateball is a sport in which you hit a ball with a wooden stick, send it through three gates in order, and finally hit the goal pole with it.
这是战后诞生于日本的运动，由每队5人的两支队伍对战。: It is a sport that was born in Japan after the war, played by two teams of five people each.
不太需要力气，但把对方的球击出去、帮助己方的球等战术很重要。: It doesn't take much strength, but strategy is important, such as knocking your opponents' balls away and helping your teammates' balls along.
奶奶起初说“不就是打打球嘛”，好像没什么兴趣。: At first my grandmother said, "You just hit a ball, don't you?" and didn't seem very interested.
然而，在和伙伴们商量战术的过程中，她完全着了迷。: But as she discussed strategy with her teammates, she became completely hooked.
现在她每天早上早早起床去公园，吃晚饭时也满嘴都是当天比赛的事。: Now she gets up early every morning to go to the park, and even at dinner she talks about nothing but that day's games.
前几天她在镇上的比赛中得了亚军，把小奖杯郑重地摆在了玄关。: The other day, she took second place in a town tournament and displayed the small trophy in the entryway as if it were a treasure.
出门的机会多了，奶奶好像比以前精神多了。: With more chances to get out of the house, my grandmother seems to have become much livelier than before.
自己人；己方: one's own people; one's own side
每天早上五点的闹钟: My five o'clock alarm every morning
我家不需要闹钟。: My house doesn't need an alarm clock.
因为每天早上一到五点，家里养的猫桃桃就会跳到我脸上。: That's because every morning at five o'clock, our cat Momo climbs onto my face.
桃桃的目的当然是早饭。: Momo's goal, of course, is breakfast.
一开始我不理它、装睡，可它渐渐开始咬我耳朵，还用前爪拍我的鼻子。: At first I ignored her and pretended to be asleep, but before long she started biting my ears and batting my nose with her front paws.
为难的我，想出了睡前先把猫粮放好的作战计划。: At my wit's end, I came up with a plan: put her food out before going to bed.
这样的话，早上应该就不会被叫醒了。: That way, I surely wouldn't be woken up in the morning.
然而第二天早上，桃桃还是照常在五点跳到了我脸上。: But the next morning, Momo climbed onto my face at five o'clock as usual.
去厨房一看，猫粮碗已经空空如也。: When I went to look in the kitchen, her food bowl was licked clean.
看来桃桃夜里就把猫粮全吃光了，是跑来要“再来一碗”的。: Apparently Momo had eaten all her food during the night and had come to ask for "seconds."
镇上照相馆的最后一张照片: The last photo at the town photo studio
我家附近有一家开了六十多年的小照相馆。: Near my house, there was a small photo studio that had been in business for more than sixty years.
每逢开学典礼、成人礼，我们全家都会去那里拍照。: Every time there was an entrance ceremony or a coming-of-age ceremony, my family and I went there to have our picture taken.
店主老爷爷很擅长逗紧张的孩子笑。: The old man who owned it was very good at making nervous children laugh.
然而去年听说，老爷爷年纪大了，照相馆要关门了。: But last year, I heard that the old man had decided to close the studio because of his age.
关门前一天，我约上父母，去拍了最后一张全家福。: On the day before it closed, I invited my parents, and we went to have one last family photo taken.
老爷爷从相册里找出我还是婴儿时的照片给我看。: The old man dug out a photo of me as a baby from an album and showed it to me.
他一边说“都长这么大了啊”，一边像往常一样按下了快门。: Saying, "Look how big you've gotten," he pressed the shutter just as he always had.
后来寄到的照片里，我们每个人都笑得特别好。: In the photo that arrived a few days later, all of us had truly wonderful smiles.
虽然现在是用手机就能轻松拍照的时代，但在那家店拍的照片至今仍是我们家的宝物。: We live in an age when you can easily take pictures with a smartphone, but the photos taken at that studio are still my family's treasures.
在神社和寺庙里，可以求到各种各样的护身符。: At shrines and temples, you can receive many different kinds of omamori, protective charms.
按心愿分为交通安全、考试合格、健康等不同的护身符，这一点很有意思。: What's interesting is that the charms are divided according to what you wish for, such as traffic safety, passing exams, and good health.
据说小布袋里装着写有神社或寺庙名字等的纸片或小木片。: Inside the small cloth bag, there is said to be a piece of paper or a small wooden tablet with the name of the shrine or temple, among other things, written on it.
不过，为了看里面的东西而打开袋子，被认为是不好的。: However, opening the bag to see what's inside is considered a bad thing to do.
因为很多人认为一打开就不灵了。: That is because many people believe that if you open it, it will lose its blessing.
护身符一般挂在包上或放进钱包里，随身携带。: It is common to keep omamori close at hand at all times, attached to a bag or tucked into a wallet.
另外，据说过了一年左右，最好还给求来的神社或寺庙，换一个新的。: It is also said to be good to return them to the shrine or temple where you received them after about a year and get new ones.
还回去的护身符，会在仪式上怀着感谢之情被焚烧。: Returned omamori are burned in a ceremony with feelings of gratitude.
我考高中时，一直把妈妈给的合格护身符放在铅笔盒里，直到考试那天。: When I took my high school entrance exams, I kept the charm for passing exams that my mother had given me in my pencil case right up until exam day.
是否真的灵验我不知道，但心里平静了下来是确实的。: I don't know whether it really brought me any divine help, but it certainly calmed my nerves.
（神佛的）保佑；灵验: divine protection (from gods or buddhas); efficacy
不踩门槛和榻榻米的边: Don't step on the threshold or the tatami edges
进和室的时候，你有没有被人说过“不要踩门槛”？: Have you ever been told, "Don't step on the threshold," when entering a Japanese-style room?
门槛是指地上那条带凹槽、用来开关隔扇和纸拉门的细长木条。: The threshold here is the long, narrow strip of wood on the floor with grooves for sliding fusuma and shoji doors open and closed.
自古以来人们就说，踩门槛和踩这家主人的头一样失礼。: It has long been said that stepping on the threshold is as rude as stepping on the head of the master of the house.
实际的理由一般认为是：踩了以后木头会磨损或变形，拉门就开关不顺了。: The practical reason is thought to be that stepping on it wears down or warps the wood, so the doors no longer slide smoothly.
同样，也有不踩榻榻米边缘的礼仪。: Similarly, there is also a rule of etiquette against stepping on the edges of tatami mats.
边缘是缝在榻榻米四周的布条，过去有时还会带有家纹。: The edge is the strip of cloth sewn around the border of a tatami mat, and in the past it sometimes bore a family crest.
踩了边缘布条容易磨损，这大概也是这个礼仪产生的原因之一吧。: The fact that the cloth is easily damaged when you step on the edges is probably one of the reasons this etiquette came about.
第一次被领进朋友老家的和室时，我想起了这件事，一直很在意脚下。: The first time I was shown into the Japanese-style room at a friend's family home, I remembered this and kept worrying about where I was putting my feet.
这时朋友的妈妈笑着说“不用那么在意也没关系哦”，我稍微放心了。: Then my friend's mother laughed and said, "You don't need to worry about it that much," and I felt a little relieved.
从胯下倒看天桥立: Amanohashidate, viewed from between your legs
位于京都府北部的天桥立，与宫城县的松岛、广岛县的宫岛并称“日本三景”。: Amanohashidate, in northern Kyoto Prefecture, is counted as one of the "Three Views of Japan," along with Matsushima in Miyagi Prefecture and Miyajima in Hiroshima Prefecture.
海中有一条长满松树的细长沙洲，绵延3公里以上。: A long, narrow strip of sand lined with pine trees stretches across the sea for more than three kilometers.
据说因为它的样子像一座架在天上的桥，所以得了这个名字。: It is said to have gotten its name because its shape looks like a bridge spanning the heavens.
沙洲上可以步行或骑自行车穿行，在松林中散步十分惬意。: You can walk or ride a bicycle across the sandbar and enjoy a pleasant stroll through the pine forest.
天桥立有一种叫“胯下窥看”的有名观赏方法。: Amanohashidate has a famous way of viewing it called 「またのぞき」 (matanozoki), "peeking between your legs."
在高处的观景台上背对风景站立，身体向前弯下，从自己的胯下窥看风景。: At an observation deck high up, you stand with your back to the view, bend forward, and peek at the scenery from between your legs.
据说这样一来上下颠倒，大海看起来像天空，沙洲就像架在空中的桥。: Then, they say, everything turns upside down, so the sea looks like the sky and the sandbar looks like a bridge spanning the sky.
我也试了一下，可血一下子涌到头上，没什么余裕欣赏风景。: I tried it too, but the blood rushed to my head, and I wasn't really in a state to enjoy the view.
不过，周围的游客都摆着同样的姿势，十分好笑，成了旅途中美好的回忆。: Even so, it was funny to see all the tourists around me in the same pose, and it became a great memory of the trip.
风铃声带来凉意: Cooled by the sound of wind chimes
一到夏天，有些人家会在屋檐下挂上风铃。: When summer comes, some homes hang wind chimes under the eaves.
每当风吹过，听到“叮铃、叮铃”的声音，总会觉得有些凉快。: Hearing them ring, "chirin, chirin," every time the wind blows somehow makes you feel cooler.
温度实际上并不会降低，但通过声音感受到风，大概就能忘记暑热吧。: The temperature doesn't actually go down, but perhaps sensing the wind through sound lets us forget the heat.
风铃有玻璃做的、铁做的等，材料不同，声音也不同。: There are wind chimes made of glass, ones made of iron, and so on, and the sound differs depending on the material.
岩手县南部铁器的风铃，以高而清澈的声音长久回荡而闻名。: Wind chimes made of Nanbu ironware from Iwate Prefecture are known for their high, clear tone that rings on for a long time.
另一方面，在房屋密集的地区，似乎也有人觉得风铃声吵。: On the other hand, in areas where houses are packed closely together, some people apparently find the sound of wind chimes noisy.
因此，也有人晚上会把风铃收进屋里，照顾邻居的感受。: So some people are considerate of their neighbors, for example by bringing their wind chimes inside at night.
我没有挂在阳台上，而是在房间窗边挂了一个小风铃，一个人欣赏它的声音。: I have made a point of hanging a small wind chime by the window of my room rather than on the balcony, so I can enjoy the sound all by myself.
一边听着风扇吹响的铃声一边喝冰麦茶的时光，是我夏天最大的乐趣。: Listening to it ring in the breeze from the electric fan while drinking cold barley tea is my favorite part of summer.
照顾；留心: to be considerate of; to be attentive
5月5日的“儿童节”，自古以来被称为“端午节”。: Children's Day, on May 5, has long been called 「端午の節句」 (Tango no Sekku).
这一天，有在家里的浴缸里放入一种叫菖蒲的植物叶子的习俗。: On this day, there is a custom of putting the leaves of a plant called shobu (Japanese sweet flag) into the bath at home.
菖蒲叶细长，有一股浓郁清爽的香气。: Shobu leaves are long and narrow and have a strong, refreshing scent.
据说古人认为那种香气能够驱除邪恶的东西。: People long ago apparently believed that the scent would drive away evil things.
另外，也有说法认为，因为“菖蒲”的读音和意为崇尚武道的“尚武”相同，所以和男孩子: It is also said that because the sound "shobu" is the same as 「尚武」 (shobu), meaning to value the martial arts, the plant became connected with this festival for boys.
小时候，祖父每年都会从附近的花店买菖蒲回来。: When I was a child, my grandfather bought shobu at the local florist for me every year.
我会把叶子缠在头上，一边说着“这下一年都不会感冒了”一边泡进浴缸。: I used to wrap the leaves around my head and get into the bath saying, "Now I won't catch a cold all year!"
长大成人的现在，一到5月我也总会在超市里找菖蒲。: Even now that I'm an adult, I make a point of looking for shobu at the supermarket when May comes around.
被叶子的香气包围时，我就会想起祖父的笑脸。: When I'm surrounded by the scent of the leaves, I remember my grandfather's smiling face.
端午节: Tango no Sekku (seasonal festival on May 5)
赶走；驱除: to chase away; to drive out
被包围: to be surrounded, to be enveloped
新年快结束的时候，有在1月7日早上吃“七草粥”的习俗。: Around the end of the New Year holidays, there is a custom of eating 「七草がゆ」 (nanakusa-gayu), seven-herb rice porridge, on the morning of January 7.
所谓七草，是指水芹、荠菜、鼠曲草、繁缕、稻槎菜、芜菁、萝卜这七种嫩菜。: The seven herbs are seven young greens: seri (Japanese parsley), nazuna (shepherd's purse), gogyo (cudweed), hakobera (chickweed), hotokenoza (nipplewort), suzuna, and suzushiro.
其中，“すずな”就是芜菁，“すずしろ”就是萝卜。: Of these, suzuna is turnip and suzushiro is daikon radish.
据说把它们放进粥里吃，就能健健康康地度过一年。: It is said that if you put them in rice porridge and eat it, you will be able to stay healthy all year.
另外，据说还有让新年期间吃了太多大餐而疲惫的肠胃休息一下的意思。: It is also said to serve as a way to rest a stomach worn out from eating too much rich food over New Year's.
一到1月初，超市里就会摆出七草配成一套的盒装菜。: In early January, packs of the seven herbs sold as a set line the supermarket shelves.
今年我也决定第一次自己做做看。: This year, I decided to try making it myself for the first time.
只要把切碎的七草放进煮好的粥里，用盐调味就行了。: All you do is put the finely chopped herbs into cooked rice porridge and season it with salt.
粥里有一股蔬菜的清香，比想象的好吃得多。: It had a fresh, green aroma of vegetables and was much more delicious than I had expected.
在寒冷的早晨吃上热乎乎的粥，感觉新的一年真正开始了。: Eating warm porridge on a cold morning, I felt as if the new year had truly begun.
你听过“夏天也快到了，八十八夜”这首歌吗？: Have you ever heard the song that begins 「夏も近づく八十八夜」, "Summer draws near on the eighty-eighth night"?
所谓“八十八夜”，是指从立春开始数的第八十八天。: 「八十八夜」 (hachijuhachiya), the "eighty-eighth night," is the eighty-eighth day counting from risshun, the traditional start of spring.
每年大约在5月2日前后，到了这个时候很少再下霜，农家正式开始田间的农活。: It falls around May 2 each year; by this time frost has become rare, and farmers begin their work in the fields in earnest.
茶园也迎来了采摘当年第一批嫩叶的“采茶”季节。: At tea plantations, too, the season of 「茶つみ」 (chatsumi), tea picking, arrives, when the first young leaves of the year are plucked.
这样制成的茶被称为“新茶”，以香气好而闻名。: Tea made in this way is called 「新茶」 (shincha), new tea, and is known for its fine aroma.
自古以来就有说法，喝了八十八夜采摘的茶就能长寿。: It has long been said that drinking tea picked on hachijuhachiya will help you live a long life.
因为把“八十八”这三个字组合起来就成了稻米的“米”字，所以被认为很吉利。: When you put together the three characters of 「八十八」 (eighty-eight), they form the character 「米」 (rice), so it is considered a lucky sign.
我的祖母每年到了这个季节，都会去茶叶店买新茶回来。: Every year when this season comes, my grandmother buys new tea at the tea shop.
据说用稍微温一点的水冲泡，是把新茶泡得好喝的诀窍。: She says the trick to making new tea taste good is to brew it with water that is a little on the cool side.
和祖母并排坐着，一边喝新茶一边聊即将到来的夏天，是我的一大乐事。: I look forward to sitting beside my grandmother, drinking new tea and talking about the summer that will soon be here.
摆门松的日子: The day to put up kadomatsu
一到年末，就会看到家门口和店门口摆着门松。: At the end of the year, you see kadomatsu, pine and bamboo decorations, set up at the entrances of homes and shops.
据说门松是为了让新年来到家里的“年神”不迷路而设的标志。: Kadomatsu are said to be markers so that the 「年神様」 (Toshigami-sama), the god of the new year who comes to visit homes at New Year's, will not get lost.
门松大多是把竹子和松枝组合在一起，一年四季都长着绿叶的松树寄托着希望长久健康的心: Most of them combine bamboo and pine, and the pine, which keeps its green needles all year round, carries the wish to stay healthy for a long time.
一般认为最好在12月28日之前摆上。: It is considered best to put them up by December 28.
因为29日的“九”读作“く”，和“苦”同音而被忌讳；31日才摆则叫“一夜饰”，被: That is because the 29th is avoided, since its sound 「く」 (ku, a reading of nine) is the same as the 「苦」 (ku) of 「苦しい」 (kurushii, painful), and putting them up on the 31st is called 「一夜飾り」 (ichiya-kazari), "one-night decorating," which is thought to be disrespectful to the god.
撤下来的时间因地区而异，关东大多到1月7日，关西大多到1月15日。: When they are taken down differs by region; in many places it seems to be January 7 in the Kanto region and January 15 in the Kansai region.
摆放门松的这段时间叫做“松之内”。: The period during which the kadomatsu are kept up is called 「松の内」 (matsu no uchi).
最近住公寓的人增多了，在门上挂小装饰来代替大门松的人家也多了起来。: Recently, more people live in apartments, and many households now hang a small decoration on the door instead of a large kadomatsu.
即使形式变了，想要心情舒畅地迎接新年的心意，大概还是和过去一样吧。: Even if the form has changed, the wish to welcome the new year in good spirits is probably the same as in the past.
松之内（新年装饰期间）: matsu no uchi (New Year's decoration period)
取号码牌乘坐的公交车: Buses where you take a numbered ticket
去地方小城旅行时，发现公交车的乘坐方式和东京不一样，吓了一跳。: When I traveled to a town in the countryside, I was surprised that the way you ride the bus was different from Tokyo.
在东京常坐的公交车是从前门上车先付钱，那辆公交车却是从后门上车。: On the buses I usually take in Tokyo, you board at the front and pay first, but that bus was set up so that you board through the rear door.
上车时要从车门旁边的机器上取一张写着数字的小纸片。: When you get on, you take a small slip of paper with a number on it from a machine beside the door.
这叫“整理券”，用来表示乘客是从哪一站上的车。: This is called a 「整理券」 (seiriken), and it shows which bus stop you got on at.
驾驶座上方有一个大显示屏，按整理券的号码分别显示着车费。: Above the driver's seat there is a large display showing the fare for each ticket number.
车费每过一站都会变，所以下车前一直得盯着看。: The fares change every time the bus passes a stop, so you can't take your eyes off it until you get off.
下车时，要把整理券和钱一起投进前门附近的投币箱。: When you get off, you put your ticket and the money together into the fare box near the front door.
投币箱不找零，所以没有零钱的话，必须事先用兑币机换好。: It doesn't give change, so if you don't have small change, you have to change your money at the change machine beforehand.
我不知道这个规矩，差点把一千日元的纸币投进去，司机教了我兑币机的用法。: Not knowing that, I almost put in a thousand-yen bill, and the driver showed me how to use the change machine.
最近能用IC卡的公交车越来越多了，但取整理券的这种方式在各地依然可以看到。: Recently more buses accept IC cards, but this method of taking a numbered ticket can still be seen in many places.
刚来日本的时候，在收银台最让我紧张的，就是店员会问我各种各样的问题。: When I had just come to Japan, what made me most nervous at the register was being asked all sorts of questions by the clerks.
一拿出商品，首先会被问“您有积分卡吗？”: When I put down my items, I would first be asked, 「ポイントカードはお持ちですか」 ("Do you have a point card?").
一开始我听不懂，随口回答了“有”，结果让店员很为难。: At first I didn't understand what it meant, so I just answered 「はい」 ("Yes"), which put the clerk in an awkward position.
接着又被问“需要袋子吗？”，然后还有“需要筷子吗？”: Next I would be asked, 「袋はご利用ですか」 ("Will you be needing a bag?"), followed by 「お箸はおつけしますか」 ("Would you like chopsticks?").
后面有人排队的时候，我一着急，有时连人家问了什么都搞不清了。: When there were people lined up behind me, I sometimes got so flustered that I lost track of what I had been asked.
于是我决定把经常被问到的问题和回答方法写在本子上记下来。: So I decided to write the questions I was often asked and how to answer them in a notebook and memorize them.
我明白了，没有积分卡的时候说“没有”，不需要袋子的时候说“不用了”就可以。: I learned that when I don't have a point card I can say 「ないです」 ("I don't"), and when I don't need a bag I can say 「大丈夫です」 ("I'm fine").
现在，无论被问什么我都能从容地回答了。: Now I can answer any of these questions calmly.
前几天，我第一次主动拿出在药妆店办的积分卡时，心里有点小小的自豪。: The other day, when I handed over the point card I had gotten at a drugstore without being asked for the first time, I felt a little proud.
着急: to get flustered, to be impatient
冷静；沉着: to keep calm; to be composed
在车站前走着的时候，听到有人喊“请协助献血”。: As I was walking in front of the station, I heard a voice calling out, "Please help by donating blood."
我以前就一直想试一次，于是下定决心走进了献血室。: I had been wanting to try it at least once, so I took the plunge and went into the blood donation center.
在前台回答了一些简单的问题后，我和医生谈了话，量了血压。: After answering some simple questions at the reception desk, I talked with a doctor and had my blood pressure taken.
接下来，在正式献血前会先抽一点血，检查是否可以献血。: Next, before the actual donation, they take just a little blood to check whether you can donate.
扎针的时候有点疼，之后就只是躺在床上而已。: It hurt a little when the needle went in, but after that all I had to do was lie on a bed.
结束后，工作人员叮嘱我不要马上站起来，要休息一会儿。: When it was over, I was told not to stand up right away but to rest for a while.
休息区里可以随意喝饮料，其他人也都一边看书一边慢慢休息。: In the rest area you could help yourself to drinks, and the other people were taking their time resting, reading books and so on.
据说收集到的血液，会用于因疾病或受伤正在接受治疗的人。: Apparently, the blood collected is used for people receiving treatment for illnesses or injuries.
想到自己的血能帮上某个素不相识的人，心里不由得高兴起来。: When I thought that my blood would help some stranger somewhere, it somehow made me happy.
下决心: making up one's mind, taking the plunge
吃饭时或大笑之后，有时会突然“呃”地打起嗝来停不下来。: During a meal or after laughing, you sometimes suddenly start going "hic" and can't stop hiccuping.
打嗝是由于胸腔和腹腔之间一块叫做横膈膜的肌肉突然收缩而引起的。: Hiccups happen when the muscle between the chest and the abdomen, called the diaphragm, suddenly contracts.
这时气息被猛地吸进去，同时喉咙深处关闭，于是就发出了那种独特的声音。: At that moment, air is sucked in forcefully, and at the same time the back of the throat closes, which produces that distinctive sound.
据说吃得太急，或者喝了很多碳酸饮料，就容易打嗝。: They are said to happen more easily when you eat in a hurry or drink a lot of carbonated drinks.
关于止嗝的方法，人们知道各种各样的办法，比如一口气喝水、暂时屏住呼吸等。: Various ways of stopping hiccups are known, such as drinking water in one go or holding your breath for a while.
也有人说“突然吓一跳就会停”，但效果并没有得到明确的证实。: Some people say, "They stop if someone suddenly startles you," but this has not been clearly proven to work.
大多数情况下，过一会儿就会自然停止，所以不用太担心。: In most cases they stop on their own after a while, so there is no need to worry too much.
不过，如果连续好几天都不停，最好还是去医院咨询一下。: However, if they go on for several days, it would be best to consult a doctor.
婴儿也经常打嗝，据说大多是不需要担心的。: Babies often get hiccups too, but apparently in most cases they are nothing to worry about.
一口气: in one go, all at once
确认；证实: to check, to confirm; to verify
四年一次的闰年: Leap years, once every four years
看日历会发现，2月有的年份只到28日，有的年份有29日。: If you look at a calendar, February goes up to the 28th in some years and up to the 29th in others.
有2月29日的年份叫做“闰年”，基本上每四年来一次。: A year with a February 29 is called a 「うるう年」 (uruudoshi), a leap year, and it basically comes around once every four years.
地球绕太阳转一圈，需要365天零大约6个小时。: It takes the Earth 365 days and about six hours to go once around the sun.
如果把一年定为365天，那6个小时的误差每年都会一点点累积起来。: If a year is counted as 365 days, that six-hour gap builds up little by little every year.
过了四年，误差大约就有一天了，所以要在那一年加上一天来调整。: After four years the gap comes to about one day, so a day is added in that year to adjust for it.
不过，误差并不正好是6小时，而是比这稍微短一点。: However, the gap is not exactly six hours but just slightly shorter.
因此，还有一条规定：能被100整除的年份不设为闰年。: For that reason, there is also a rule that years divisible by 100 are not leap years.
而能被400整除的年份，作为例外又是闰年。: On top of that, years divisible by 400 are leap years as an exception.
2000年之所以是闰年，就是因为这条规定。: This rule is why the year 2000 was a leap year.
据说2月29日出生的人，有时会被开玩笑说生日四年才来一次。: People born on February 29 are apparently sometimes teased that their birthday comes only once every four years.
时差反应与身体的时钟: Jet lag and the body's clock
你有没有过这样的经历：出国旅行第一天，明明是白天却困得不行？: Have you ever had the experience of being unbearably sleepy in the middle of the day on the first day of a trip abroad?
这被称为“时差反应”，乘飞机去时差大的地方时经常发生。: This is called "jet lag," and it often happens when you travel by plane to a place with a large time difference.
我们的身体里有一个以大约24小时为节律运转的“生物钟”。: Our bodies have a "body clock" that keeps a rhythm of about 24 hours.
生物钟决定着我们什么时候犯困、什么时候肚子饿等等。: The body clock determines things like when we get sleepy and when we get hungry.
可是，乘飞机在短时间内去到远方，生物钟和当地时间就会错开。: However, when you travel far in a short time by plane, your body clock and the local time fall out of sync.
生物钟一天只能调整一点点，所以身体适应需要好几天。: The body clock can only adjust a little at a time each day, so it takes several days for your body to get used to the change.
一般认为，向东的旅行比向西的旅行更容易出现严重的时差反应。: It is generally said that jet lag tends to be worse when traveling east than when traveling west.
据说要减轻时差反应，最好在当地的早晨多晒晒太阳。: To ease jet lag, it is said to be good to soak up plenty of sunlight in the morning, local time.
即使困了，午睡也要短一些，晚上尽量按当地时间睡觉。: Even if you are sleepy, keep naps short, and try to go to bed at night according to the local time.
刻；（钟表）计时: to carve; to keep time, to tick away (of a clock)
晒；沐浴: to be exposed to (sunlight); to bathe in
在动物园当饲养员的田中，早晨从四处查看动物们的情况开始。: For Tanaka, who works as a keeper at a zoo, the morning begins with going around to see how the animals are doing.
走路是否精神，有没有食欲，有没有和平时不一样的地方，他都一一确认。: One by one, he checks whether they are walking around energetically, whether they have an appetite, and whether anything seems different from usual.
特别重要的是看粪便的形状和量。: What is especially important is looking at the shape and amount of their droppings.
因为动物没法用语言表达身体不适，所以注意到细微的变化很重要。: Animals can't tell us in words that they feel unwell, so it is important to notice small changes.
之后，他就开始打扫动物们的住处、准备饲料。: After that, he gets to work cleaning the animals' quarters and preparing their feed.
田中负责的长颈鹿非常喜欢树叶。: The giraffes that Tanaka looks after love tree leaves.
他把树枝挂在高处，想办法让长颈鹿能用接近自然的方式进食。: He hangs branches up high, coming up with ways for them to eat in a manner close to how they would in nature.
开园之后，还有给游客讲解长颈鹿的导览时间。: After the zoo opens, there is also a guided session in which he explains about the giraffes to visitors.
据说每当孩子们两眼放光地听他讲解时，他就觉得选择这份工作真好。: He says that when children listen to him with shining eyes, he feels glad he chose this job.
夜里站在前台的人: The person at the front desk at night
在酒店前台工作的佐藤，每周要上几次夜班。: Sato, who works at a hotel front desk, works the night shift several times a week.
傍晚上班后，他首先确认当天入住客人的预订。: When he arrives at work in the evening, he first checks the reservations of the guests staying that night.
过了晚上10点，乘晚班飞机或电车到达的客人还在陆续办理入住。: Even after 10 p.m., check-ins continue for guests arriving on late flights and trains.
很多客人带着疲惫的神情到来，所以他尽量把手续办得又快又周到。: Many guests arrive looking tired, so he tries to handle the check-in procedures as quickly and courteously as possible.
到了深夜，前台安静下来，但并不是没有工作了。: Late at night the front desk gets quiet, but that doesn't mean there is no work to do.
他要在电话里回应各种请求和问题，比如“房间太冷了”“附近有没有还开着的药店”。: He answers requests and questions over the phone, such as "My room is cold" or "Is there a pharmacy open nearby?"
在这些间隙，他处理第二天早上的准备工作和电脑上的事务性工作。: In between, he takes care of preparations for the next morning and office work on the computer.
到了早上，前台又因为办理退房的客人而热闹起来。: In the morning, the front desk gets busy again, this time with guests checking out.
据说听到客人说“睡得很好”，通宵未眠的疲惫也会减轻一些。: He says that when guests tell him, "I slept well," the fatigue from staying up all night feels a little lighter.
上班: going to work, arriving at work
深夜: late at night, the middle of the night
雨天的翻译导游: An interpreter-guide on a rainy day
林女士从事为外国游客介绍日本的翻译导游工作。: Hayashi works as an interpreter-guide, showing travelers from abroad around Japan.
不仅要讲解寺庙和神社的历史，挑选餐馆、教客人怎么坐电车也是重要的工作。: Besides explaining the history of temples and shrines, choosing restaurants and teaching people how to ride the trains are also important parts of the job.
有一天，本来计划在京都去看庭园，结果从早上就下起了大雨。: One day, they had planned to go see a garden in Kyoto, but it rained heavily from the morning on.
客人们一脸失望，林女士立刻决定更改行程。: The guests looked disappointed, but Hayashi immediately decided to change the plan.
她选了和果子制作课堂和有屋顶的市场，作为下雨也不会淋湿、可以尽情游玩的地方。: As places they could enjoy without getting wet even in the rain, she chose a wagashi-making class and a covered market.
在课堂上，大家神情认真地做了花朵形状的点心。: In the class, everyone made flower-shaped sweets with serious looks on their faces.
在市场里，大家对第一次见到的食物不断提问。: At the market, one question after another came up about foods they were seeing for the first time.
回程的车里，客人说“说不定下雨天反而更有意思”，林女士这才松了一口气。: In the car on the way back, the guests told her, "The rainy day might have been even more fun," and Hayashi felt relieved.
据说为了让客人无论什么天气都能玩得开心，时刻准备好备选方案，是这份工作的诀窍。: She says the trick to this job is to always have another plan ready so that guests can enjoy themselves whatever the weather.
学校供餐中心的早晨: Morning at a school lunch center
在为小学制作午餐的供餐中心，厨师们从一大早就开始工作。: At school lunch centers, which make lunches for elementary schools, the cooks are at work from early in the morning.
因为要做几千个孩子的饭菜，用的锅大得好像人都能钻进去。: Because they cook food for thousands of children, the pots they use are so big it looks as if a person could fit inside.
搅拌的时候，要用像船桨一样的大铲子。: When stirring, they use a big spatula that looks like a boat oar.
洗菜、切菜、煮菜等，所有工作都必须在规定的时间内完成。: All the work, such as washing, cutting and simmering the vegetables, has to be done within a set time.
因为送到学校的时间是固定的，所以一点也耽误不得。: The time for delivering to the schools is fixed, so not even the slightest delay is allowed.
其中特别注意的，是为有食物过敏的孩子准备的饭菜。: Among their tasks, what they are especially careful about is the meals for children with food allergies.
他们另外做不含致敏食物的饭菜，装进写着名字的容器里送过去。: They separately make dishes that don't use any foods that cause allergies, put them in containers labeled with the child's name, and deliver them.
为了不出差错，好几个人反复检查好几遍。: To make sure there are no mistakes, several cooks check them over and over.
据说下午，看到从学校送回来的空空的容器，厨师们都会不由得露出笑容。: It is said that in the afternoon, when the containers come back empty from the schools, the cooks can't help smiling.
山口县下关市作为河豚之城闻名全国。: Shimonoseki in Yamaguchi Prefecture is known throughout Japan as a pufferfish town.
据说当地人常把河豚叫做“ふく”。: Locally, people apparently often call fugu (pufferfish) "fuku."
因为“ふく”和“福”同音，被认为很吉利。: This is because "fuku" sounds the same as 「福」 (good fortune), so it is considered lucky.
河豚身体的一部分带有剧毒，所以只有具备资格的厨师才能烹制。: Parts of a pufferfish's body contain a powerful poison, so only licensed chefs are allowed to prepare it.
河豚料理中最有名的，是切得非常薄的刺身。: Particularly famous among fugu dishes is sashimi sliced very thin.
刺身像花一样摆在大盘子里，薄到透过鱼肉能看见下面盘子的花纹。: It is arranged like a flower on a large plate, so thin that you can see the pattern of the plate beneath through the flesh.
蘸着橙醋酱油吃，鱼肉紧实，越嚼越有味道。: Dipped in ponzu, the flesh is firm, and the more you chew, the more flavor comes out.
放了鱼骨和鱼肉的火锅也很好吃，最后用那锅汤做杂烩粥吃。: Hot pot with the bones and meat in it is also delicious, and at the end you use the broth to make zosui (rice porridge) and eat it.
河豚在寒冷时节尤其美味，所以很多人冬天去下关旅行。: Fugu is especially delicious in the cold season, so many people travel to Shimonoseki in winter.
秋田县有一种叫做“いぶりがっこ”的腌菜。: Akita Prefecture has a pickle called "iburi-gakko."
“がっこ”在秋田方言里是腌菜的意思，“いぶり”是用烟熏的意思。: "Gakko" is the Akita word for pickles, and "iburi" means smoking something.
一般来说，做萝卜腌菜时，要把萝卜晾在外面减少水分。: Usually, when making pickled daikon, you hang the daikon outside to dry and reduce their moisture.
但是秋田冬天来得早，雪又多，很难在外面把萝卜晾干。: But in Akita, winter comes early and there is a lot of snow, so it was difficult to dry the daikon sufficiently outdoors.
于是，人们开始在屋里生火，把萝卜吊在火上方，一边用烟熏一边烘干。: So people began building fires inside the house, hanging the daikon above them, and drying them while smoking them.
之后，再放进米糠等里面慢慢腌制。: After that, the daikon are packed in rice bran and the like and left to pickle slowly.
做好的烟熏萝卜咸菜呈深褐色，有一股篝火般的香气。: Finished iburi-gakko is dark brown and has an aroma like a campfire.
一咬就发出嘎吱嘎吱的清脆声音，配米饭、配茶都很合适。: When you bite into it, it makes a nice crunching sound, and it goes well with both rice and tea.
据说最近和奶油奶酪一起吃的人也越来越多了。: These days, the number of people who eat it with cream cheese is apparently growing too.
想到这是为了度过严冬的智慧所造就的味道，就觉得更加美味了。: When you think of it as a flavor born from the wisdom of getting through harsh winters, it tastes even better.
晾；晒: to hang out to dry; to dry in the sun
作为长崎县的特产而有名的，是方方正正的黄色点心——长崎蛋糕。: Famous as a souvenir from Nagasaki Prefecture is castella, a square, yellow confection.
据说长崎蛋糕的原型点心，是16世纪前后由葡萄牙人传入的。: The confection that castella is based on is said to have been brought to Japan by the Portuguese around the 16th century.
当时的长崎是对外贸易的窗口，各种各样的新文化从这里传了进来。: At the time, Nagasaki was the gateway for trade with foreign countries, and all sorts of new culture came in through it.
日本的工匠们对它加以改良，使之符合日本人的口味，做出了如今的长崎蛋糕。: Japanese artisans adapted it to suit Japanese tastes and created the castella of today.
材料是鸡蛋、面粉、砂糖、麦芽糖等，非常简单。: The ingredients are very simple: eggs, wheat flour, sugar, starch syrup and so on.
但是据说要烤得湿润松软，需要多年的经验。: However, baking it so that it comes out moist and soft apparently takes many years of experience.
长崎蛋糕大多在底部留有大颗的砂糖粒，吃起来有一种沙沙的口感。: Many Nagasaki castellas have large grains of sugar left on the bottom, which give a gritty crunch when you eat them.
也有人喜欢这些砂糖粒，总是从底部开始吃。: Some people like these sugar grains so much that they always eat from the bottom first.
我最喜欢就着冰牛奶吃长崎蛋糕。: Personally, I like eating castella with cold milk best.
嚼劲；口感: firmness to the bite, chewiness; texture
去岐阜县飞驒地区一个叫高山的小城旅行时，旅馆的早饭上了一道“朴叶味噌”。: When I traveled to a town called Takayama in the Hida region of Gifu Prefecture, "hoba miso" was served at breakfast at the ryokan.
朴叶是把一种叫日本厚朴的树的大叶子晒干而成的。: Hoba are the large leaves of a tree called the hoonoki (Japanese bigleaf magnolia), dried.
把叶子放在小炉子上，放上拌有葱和菌菇的味噌，一边用火烤一边吃。: You put a leaf on top of a small stove, place miso mixed with green onions and mushrooms on it, and eat it as it roasts over the flame.
味噌烤起来以后，叶子的清香和味噌的焦香弥漫了整个房间。: As the miso began to cook, the scent of the leaf and the savory aroma of the miso filled the whole room.
据旅馆的人说，飞驒冬天非常寒冷，自古以来就很重视能长期保存的味噌。: According to the people at the inn, winters in Hida are bitterly cold, and since long ago people there have valued miso, which keeps well.
朴树叶不容易燃烧，所以即使直接放在火上也不会马上烧焦。: Hoba leaves don't burn easily, so even if you put them directly over the flame, they don't scorch right away.
把烤好的味噌放在热乎乎的米饭上，感觉光是这样就能吃好几碗。: When I put the grilled miso on warm rice, I felt I could eat bowl after bowl with just that.
镇上的早市里，当地的老奶奶们摆着蔬菜和腌菜，热情地招呼客人。: At the town's morning market, local elderly women line up vegetables and pickles and call out to you cheerfully.
我也想在家里做做看，于是决定回去时在早市上买些朴叶带回家。: I wanted to try making it at home too, so I decided to buy some hoba leaves at the morning market on my way back.
烤: to roast, to grill (over a flame)
我从小就不会游泳，一直觉得很难为情。: Ever since I was a child, I had always been embarrassed that I couldn't swim.
五十岁那年春天，我下定决心报名了附近体育俱乐部面向成年人的游泳班。: In the spring I turned fifty, I took the plunge and signed up for an adult swimming class at a sports club in my neighborhood.
第一天，光是把脸埋进水里就很紧张，怎么也睁不开眼睛。: On the first day, just putting my face in the water made me nervous, and I just couldn't bring myself to open my eyes.
教练说“不用着急”，从怎么呼气开始教我。: The coach said, "There's no need to rush," and started by teaching me how to breathe out.
同一个班里还有六七十岁的人，大家都练得很开心。: There were people in their sixties and seventies in the same class, and everyone seemed to be enjoying the practice.
我决定每周两次，下班后去游泳池。: I decided to go to the pool twice a week on my way home from work.
过了半年左右，我已经能靠打水一点点往前游了。: After about half a year, I was able to move forward little by little with a flutter kick.
然后一年后，我终于能够中途不停地游完25米了。: Then, a year later, I was finally able to swim the full 25 meters without stopping.
碰到泳池边的时候，伙伴们为我鼓掌，我差点忍不住流下眼泪。: When I touched the end of the pool, my classmates applauded, and I almost burst into tears.
现在，我正朝着下一个目标50米继续练习。: Now I'm continuing to practice toward my next goal of 50 meters.
学会双摇跳绳的那天: The day she did a double under
上小学三年级的女儿，整个寒假都在练习跳绳的“双摇”。: My daughter, who is in third grade, practiced "double unders" with her jump rope all through winter vacation.
所谓双摇，就是跳一次的时间里让绳子转两圈的跳法。: A double under is a way of jumping in which you swing the rope around twice during a single jump.
班上好几个朋友都已经会了，自己却不会，她好像很不甘心。: Several of her classmates could already do it, and she seemed frustrated that she was the only one who couldn't.
她每天早上都在家门口练习，可绳子老是绊到脚。: She practiced in front of our house every morning, but the rope kept catching on her feet.
有一天，住在附近、曾经是体操运动员的老爷爷看了她练习，给了她建议。: One day, an elderly man in the neighborhood who used to be a gymnast watched her practice and gave her some advice.
老爷爷说：“不要大幅度地甩胳膊，试试用手腕快速地转。”: He told her, "Don't swing your arms in big circles; try turning the rope quickly with your wrists."
从那以后，女儿练习时就注意跳高一点、用手腕发力。: From then on, my daughter practiced while focusing on jumping high and using her wrists.
然后在寒假的最后一天，伴随着“嗖嗖”的声音，她终于成功跳了一个双摇。: Then, on the last day of winter vacation, with a "whoosh, whoosh" sound, she finally succeeded in doing one double under.
女儿高兴坏了，马上跑到老爷爷家去道谢。: Overjoyed, my daughter immediately ran all the way to the man's house to thank him.
绊住；挂住: to get tripped up on; to get caught (on)
我们公司每年举办一次保龄球比赛，用来促进员工之间的交流。: At my company, we hold a bowling tournament once a year to promote interaction among employees.
比赛不分部门，四人一组，所以和平时不怎么说话的人也能熟络起来。: We're split into teams of four regardless of department, so you can get friendly even with people you don't usually talk to.
今年，我们队里有一位以严厉出名的部长。: This year, my team included a department manager known for being strict.
一开始大家都很紧张，即使打出全中也只是小声地鼓鼓掌。: At first everyone was nervous, and even when someone got a strike, we only gave a quiet round of applause.
没想到，部长投出的第一个球径直掉进了旁边的沟里。: But the first ball the manager threw went straight into the gutter at the side.
部长一边说“好久没打了”，下一球又掉进了沟里。: Saying, "It's been a while," the manager sent the next ball into the gutter too.
大家忍不住笑了起来，部长也不好意思地笑了。: Everyone burst out laughing in spite of themselves, and the manager laughed too, looking embarrassed.
从那以后队里的气氛一下子活跃起来，每当有人投球，大家都会大声互相加油。: After that, the team's mood brightened all at once, and whenever someone bowled, we cheered each other on loudly.
结果虽然是倒数第一，但回去时部长笑着说“明年我会练好了再来”。: We finished in last place, but on the way home the manager laughed and said, "Next year I'll practice before I come."
从星期一开始，我觉得跟部长说话容易多了。: Since Monday, I feel it has become easier to talk to the manager.
积雪的信号灯: Traffic lights that pile up with snow
最近，街上的信号灯陆续从灯泡换成了LED。: Recently, traffic lights in towns have been changing one after another from light bulbs to LEDs.
LED耗电少、寿命长，而且明亮易见，优点很多。: LEDs have the advantages of using little electricity and lasting a long time, as well as being bright and easy to see.
然而，在多雪的地区，却出现了一个意想不到的问题。: However, in regions with a lot of snow, an unexpected problem arose.
以前的灯泡会发热，附着在信号灯上的雪会被那热量自然融化。: Old light bulbs gave off heat, so the snow that stuck to the traffic lights melted naturally from that heat.
但LED几乎不发热，雪融化不了就堆积起来，信号灯的颜色就看不清了。: But LEDs give off almost no heat, so the snow piles up without melting, making it hard to see the color of the signal.
于是，雪国想了各种各样的办法。: So in snow country, various measures have been devised.
比如，有的信号灯装上了小型加热器来融雪。: For example, some traffic lights have been fitted with small heaters to melt the snow.
另外，在北海道和东北等地，常用的不是横向的信号灯，而是竖向的信号灯。: Also, in places such as Hokkaido and Tohoku, vertical traffic lights are often used instead of horizontal ones.
因为做成竖的，积雪的地方就变小了，也能防止信号灯被积雪压坏。: This is because making them vertical reduces the area where snow can pile up, and also prevents the traffic lights from breaking under the weight.
由此可见，便利的新技术也需要根据使用场所下功夫改进。: This shows that it is important to adapt even convenient new technology to suit the place where it is used.
最近，经常能看到车站站台边缘装上了齐腰高的栅栏和门。: Recently, we often see waist-high fences and doors installed at the edge of station platforms.
这叫“站台门”，只在电车停稳时才会打开。: These are called "platform doors," and they are designed to open only when a train has stopped.
目的是防止有人从站台跌落，或者和驶来的电车相撞等事故。: Their purpose is to prevent accidents such as people falling off the platform or being hit by an approaching train.
尤其对视力有障碍的人、或者边看手机边走路的人来说，站台变得更安全了。: In particular, they make the platform a safe place for people who are visually impaired and for people who walk while looking at their smartphones.
不过，安装站台门并不简单。: However, installing platform doors is not easy.
因为即使是停靠同一车站的电车，不同车辆的车门数量和位置也可能不一样。: This is because even among trains that stop at the same station, the number and position of the doors can differ depending on the train car.
于是，人们还想出了用好几根绳索或横杆上下移动来代替门的类型。: So a type was also devised in which several ropes or bars move up and down instead of doors.
这样一来，即使开来的电车车门位置不同，也能应对。: With this, it can handle trains even when their doors are in different positions.
有时还需要加固站台，完工可能要花很长时间。: In some cases, construction work to strengthen the platform is needed, and it can take a long time to complete.
保障安全的设施，正是在许多人的努力下一点点普及开来的。: Safety equipment like this is spreading little by little thanks to the ingenuity of many people.
我一直以为圆珠笔写的字擦不掉，但现在有了可擦圆珠笔。: I used to think that you couldn't erase writing done with a ballpoint pen, but now there are erasable ballpoint pens.
用笔尾的橡胶一擦，写的字就干干净净地看不见了。: If you rub with the rubber on the end of the pen, what you wrote disappears cleanly.
这并不是像橡皮那样把字擦下来。: This doesn't mean it scrapes the writing off the way an eraser does.
这种笔的墨水，是一种温度一升高颜色就会消失的特殊墨水。: The ink in this pen is a special ink that loses its color when its temperature rises.
原理是摩擦时产生的热量让墨水变得透明。: The way it works is that the heat produced when you rub makes the ink transparent.
有意思的是，消失的字有时还会重新出现。: What's interesting is that erased writing can sometimes reappear.
这种墨水有一种特性：变得非常冷时，颜色会恢复。: This ink has the property of getting its color back when it becomes very cold.
因此，据说把有擦掉字迹的纸放进冷冻室，字可能会重新显现。: For that reason, if you put paper with erased writing in the freezer, the writing may apparently come back.
相反，如果放在炎热的车里，写的字也可能会消失。: On the other hand, if you leave it in a hot car, what you wrote may disappear.
虽然是便利的工具，但要注意不要用在重要的文件和信件上。: They are convenient tools, but be careful not to use them for important documents or letters.
擦掉；消除: to erase, to rub out; to eliminate
削；刮: to shave, to sharpen; to scrape
年末重糊纸拉门: Re-papering the shoji at year's end
祖母家的和室里，至今仍有纸拉门。: My grandmother's house still has shoji in the Japanese-style room.
纸拉门是在木框上糊上薄薄的和纸做成的门，能把光线柔和地引进房间。: Shoji are doors made of thin washi paper stretched over a wooden frame, and they let light into the room softly.
不过因为是纸做的，会破洞，也会被太阳晒得发黄。: However, since they're made of paper, they get holes in them and turn yellow from the sun.
所以祖母家每年年末都会全家一起重新糊纸拉门。: So at my grandmother's house, the whole family re-papers the shoji together at the end of every year.
首先，把纸拉门拆下来搬到院子里，撕掉旧纸。: First, we take the shoji out, carry them to the yard, and peel off the old paper.
小时候，只有这一天用手指在纸拉门上戳洞也不会挨骂，所以我非常期待。: When I was a child, this was the one day I wouldn't get scolded for poking holes in the shoji with my fingers, so I really looked forward to it.
用沾了水的刷子把框擦干净后，涂上浆糊，糊上新纸。: After cleaning the frames with a brush dampened with water, we apply paste and put on the new paper.
最后用喷壶喷上水晾干，纸就会绷得紧紧的，褶皱也没了。: Finally, when we spray it with water from a mister and let it dry, the paper becomes taut and the wrinkles disappear.
把雪白的纸拉门装回原处，就感觉房间一下子亮堂了。: When we put the pure-white shoji back in their places, the room suddenly feels brighter.
祖母总是高兴地说：“这下可以舒舒服服地迎接新年了。”: My grandmother always says happily, "Now we can welcome the new year in good spirits."
揭下；撕掉: to peel off; to tear off
我在东京的老城区参加了江户切子的体验课。: I took part in a hands-on Edo kiriko class in one of Tokyo's old downtown neighborhoods.
江户切子是据说始于江户时代末期的玻璃工艺。: Edo kiriko is a glass craft said to have begun toward the end of the Edo period.
用旋转的工具打磨玻璃表面，一点点刻出精细的花纹。: You grind the surface of the glass with a rotating tool, carving fine patterns into it.
打磨带颜色的玻璃，只有那部分会变透明，花纹就会漂亮地浮现出来。: When you grind colored glass, only that part becomes transparent, so the pattern stands out beautifully.
课上，工匠师傅先给我们做了示范。: In the class, a craftsman first gave us a demonstration.
他手法干净利落，转眼间就刻出了漂亮的线条。: With sure, unhesitating hands, he cut beautiful lines one after another in no time at all.
可是自己一试，线条歪歪扭扭，偏离了想要的位置。: But when I tried it myself, my lines wouldn't come out straight and strayed from where I meant them to go.
师傅笑着说：“稍微弯一点，反而更有手工的味道哦。”: The craftsman smiled and said, "It has more of a handmade feel when it's a little crooked."
做好的杯子虽然有点不太好看，却是世界上独一无二的宝贝。: The finished glass is a little clumsy-looking, but it's a treasure, the only one of its kind in the world.
倒入冰茶后，花纹在光线下闪闪发亮。: When I pour cold tea into it, the pattern catches the light and sparkles.
手法；手势: way of using one's hands, technique; hand movements
在神社参拜的礼仪: Etiquette for praying at a shrine
在日本的神社参拜时，有自古流传下来的礼仪。: When you pray at a shrine in Japan, there is etiquette that has been handed down since long ago.
首先，在穿过鸟居之前，轻轻鞠一躬。: First, before passing through the torii gate, bow lightly once.
参道的正中间被认为是神明走的路，所以要尽量靠边走。: The middle of the approach is said to be the path of the gods, so try to walk along the side as much as possible.
参拜之前，要在叫做“手水舍”的净手处洗手漱口，使身心洁净。: Before praying, purify your hands and mouth at a water station called the "temizuya."
用长柄勺舀水，按左手、右手的顺序洗，最后用手接水漱口。: Scoop up water with a ladle, wash your left hand and then your right hand, and finally rinse your mouth with water poured into your hand.
到了正殿前，投入香火钱，如果有铃铛就摇响它。: When you reach the front of the main hall, put in an offering of money, and if there is a bell, ring it.
然后，就像常说的“二拜二拍手一拜”那样，深深鞠两次躬，拍两次手。: Then, following what is known as "two bows, two claps, one bow," bow deeply twice and clap your hands twice.
双手合十许愿之后，最后再鞠一躬。: After putting your hands together and making a wish, bow once more at the end.
不过，有的神社做法略有不同，所以事先看看指示牌之类的会比较放心。: However, some shrines do things a little differently, so it's reassuring to check the information signs and so on beforehand.
了解了这些礼仪，即使是第一次去的神社，也能从容地参拜吧。: If you know the etiquette, you'll be able to pray calmly even at a shrine you're visiting for the first time.
香火钱: offering money (at a shrine or temple)
口头禅是“总会有办法的”的母亲: My mother's catchphrase: "It'll work out somehow"
我母亲的口头禅是“哎，总会有办法的”。: My mother's catchphrase is, "Well, it'll work out somehow."
小时候，不管我考试没考好，还是运动会上摔倒了，母亲总是这么说着笑笑。: When I was a child, whether I got a bad score on a test or fell down at sports day, my mother always said that and laughed.
说实话，那时候的我觉得母亲的话有点不负责任。: To be honest, back then I thought my mother's words were a bit irresponsible.
我也曾心怀不满，希望她能更认真地替我担心。: There were times I felt dissatisfied, wishing she would worry about me more seriously.
长大后，在工作中犯了一个大错时，我久违地给母亲打了电话。: As an adult, when I made a big mistake at work, I called my mother for the first time in a long while.
听我说完，母亲果然还是说了句“哎，总会有办法的”。: When she had heard me out, my mother said, just as I expected, "Well, it'll work out somehow."
不可思议的是，一听到那句话，我就感到肩上的力气一下子卸了下来。: Strangely enough, the moment I heard those words, I felt the tension drain right out of my shoulders.
后来听父亲说，母亲以前每次遇到难事，也都是这样对自己说的。: Later, my father told me that for years, whenever something difficult happened, my mother had been telling herself the same thing.
那句话非但不是不负责任，或许正是母亲支撑这个家的力量。: Far from being irresponsible, those words may have been the strength that let my mother support our family.
现在，每当后辈情绪低落时，我也会对他们说同样的话。: Now I've started saying the same words to my juniors at work when they're feeling down.
劝说；告诫: to persuade; to admonish, to tell (someone) firmly
在妹妹婚礼上读的信: The letter I read at my sister's wedding
上个月，比我小五岁的妹妹结婚了。: Last month, my sister, who is five years younger than me, got married.
婚礼前，妹妹拜托我：“姐姐，你能讲几句话吗？”: Before the ceremony, my sister asked me, "Sis, would you say a few words?"
我不擅长在人前讲话，但又不能拒绝。: I'm not good at speaking in front of people, but I couldn't very well refuse.
想着要讲些什么的时候，小时候的回忆一个接一个地浮现出来。: As I was thinking about what to say, memories from our childhood came to mind one after another.
我们俩常常吵架，总是抢玩具、抢电视频道。: We often fought, always squabbling over toys and the TV channel.
不过，我考试落榜躲在房间里哭的时候，还在上小学的妹妹曾默默地把自己的零食放下就走: But once, when I had failed my entrance exams and was crying in my room, my sister, who was still in elementary school, silently left her own snack for me and went away.
婚礼当天，我把这件事写成信读了出来。: On the day, I wrote about that in a letter and read it aloud.
读到一半声音发抖，停了好几次，总算读完了。: Partway through, my voice started to tremble, and stopping again and again, I somehow managed to read it to the end.
抬起头，看见妹妹用手帕捂着眼睛，笑着点了点头。: When I looked up, my sister was pressing a handkerchief to her eyes, smiling and nodding.
那时零食的味道我已经不记得了，但妹妹的温柔我会一直记着。: I don't remember the taste of that snack, but I think I'll never forget my sister's kindness.
浮现: to come to mind, to surface
争抢: to fight over, to scramble for
抽屉深处的记事本: The planner at the back of the drawer
在收拾老家的时候，从父亲书桌抽屉的深处翻出了一本旧记事本。: While I was clearing out my family home, an old planner turned up from the back of a drawer in my father's desk.
封面已经完全褪色，看了日期，是我出生那年的。: The cover had completely faded, and when I checked the date, it was from the year I was born.
里面用小字密密麻麻地写满了工作安排和会议记录。: Inside, work schedules and meeting notes were crammed in, written in tiny handwriting.
父亲话不多，在家几乎从不谈工作上的事。: My father was a man of few words who hardly ever talked about work at home.
一页页翻下去，在某一天的栏里，有一行和工作无关的字。: As I turned the pages, I found a line in one day's box that had nothing to do with work.
上面写着：“今天，女儿第一次笑了。”: It said, "Today, my daughter smiled for the first time."
在那下面，用似乎有些颤抖的字，只补了一句“加油吧”。: Below that, in handwriting that looked a little shaky, he had added just, "I'll do my best."
我第一次知道，父亲在忙碌的日子里，是怀着这样的心情工作的。: It was the first time I learned that my father had been working with such feelings during his busy days.
那本记事本如今放在我书架上最容易拿到的地方。: That planner now sits on my bookshelf, in the spot where it's easiest to take out.
话的多少: how much one talks, number of words spoken
伞变成三把的那天: The day I ended up with three umbrellas
我经常把伞忘在什么地方。: I often leave my umbrella somewhere and forget it.
光是今年，就已经丢了四把伞。: This year alone, I've already lost four umbrellas.
一个下雨的早上，妻子对我说“今天一定要带回来哦”，我就出门了。: One rainy morning, my wife told me, "Make sure you bring it home today," and I left the house.
可是一到公司，雨就完全停了。: But by the time I got to the office, the rain had completely stopped.
傍晚想起伞的事，看了看伞架，除了自己的伞，还有两把眼熟的伞。: In the evening, I remembered my umbrella and looked at the umbrella stand, and besides my own umbrella, there were two umbrellas that looked familiar.
那是我以前留在公司、然后忘得一干二净的伞。: They were umbrellas I had left at the office earlier and completely forgotten about.
我觉得这是个好机会，决定三把一起带回家。: Thinking this was a good opportunity, I decided to take all three home together.
在晴朗的夜路上，抱着三把伞走路的我，引得擦肩而过的人们投来奇怪的目光。: As I walked along the street on that clear night with three umbrellas in my arms, the people I passed gave me puzzled looks.
到家后，我一脸得意地给妻子看了三把伞。: When I got home, I proudly showed my wife the three umbrellas.
妻子却问：“那么，今天早上那把是哪一把？”: Then my wife asked, "So, which one is the umbrella from this morning?"
仔细一看，今天早上带出去的那把蓝伞并不在其中。: When I looked closely, the blue umbrella I had taken with me that morning wasn't among them.
忘在某处: to leave (something) behind, to forget (something) somewhere
抱着: to hold in one's arms, to carry
擦肩而过: to pass each other (going opposite ways)
哥哥上个月在家人面前宣布：“从明天起认真减肥。”: Last month, my older brother announced in front of the family, "Starting tomorrow, I'm going on a diet for real."
第二天早上，哥哥早早起床，出门去附近跑步了。: The next morning, he got up early and went out for a run around the neighborhood.
可是回来的时候，哥哥手里提着便利店的袋子。: But when he came back, he had a convenience store bag in his hand.
他说“跑了这么多，这是奖励”，从里面拿出了一个大菠萝包。: Saying, "I ran a lot, so this is my reward," he took a big melon pan out of it.
再下一天，他说“好像要下雨了”，就没去跑步。: The day after that, he skipped his run, saying, "It looks like it's going to rain."
第三天，他说“今天是朋友生日，算特例”，吃烤肉吃到很晚才回来。: On the third day, saying, "Today's my friend's birthday, so it's a special occasion," he went out and ate yakiniku until late at night.
一周后，哥哥战战兢兢地站上了体重秤。: A week later, my brother nervously stepped onto the scale.
默默地盯着数字看了一会儿，哥哥一脸认真地说：: After staring at the number in silence for a while, my brother said this with a serious look on his face.
“这个体重秤，是不是坏了啊？”: "I think this scale might be broken."
第二天，家里收到了一台新的体重秤，可哥哥的减肥至今依旧停留在“从明天起”。: The next day, a new scale arrived at our house, but my brother's diet is still "starting tomorrow."
“けっこうです”到底是哪个意思？: Is 「けっこうです」 yes or no?
来日本三个月左右的时候，我和朋友进了一家咖啡馆。: When I had been in Japan for about three months, I went into a coffee shop with a friend.
咖啡快喝完的时候，店员问我：“要续杯吗？”: As I was finishing my coffee, the server asked me, "Would you like a refill?"
我决定用一下刚在课本上学到的“けっこうです”。: I decided to try using 「けっこうです」, which I had just learned from my textbook.
我记得“けっこう”是“好”的意思，所以本意是“好的，请再来一杯”。: I remembered that 「けっこう」 meant 「いい」 ("good"), so I meant it as "Yes, one more cup, please."
可是店员微微一笑，就这么走开了。: But the server just smiled and walked away.
正当我纳闷时，朋友笑着告诉了我原因。: While I was puzzling over this, my friend laughed and explained.
原来在这种场合，“けっこうです”多半是“不用了”的意思。: Apparently, in situations like this, 「けっこうです」 often means "I don't need any more."
同一个词，根据场合既能表示“好”又能表示“不要”，我觉得日语真难。: I thought Japanese was really difficult, since the same word can mean either 「いい」 ("good") or 「いらない」 ("I don't want it"), depending on the situation.
从那以后，想要什么东西的时候，我都会清楚地说“拜托了”。: Since then, whenever I want something, I make sure to say 「お願いします」 ("yes, please") clearly.
结果那天，我忍住了想再喝一杯的念头，离开了咖啡馆。: In the end, that day I fought back the urge to have another cup and left the shop.
最后一天的每日套餐: The daily set meal on the last day
大学附近有一家深受学生们喜爱的小食堂。: Near my university, there was a small diner that had long been loved by students.
那是一家只有老板和老板娘两个人经营的店，米饭可以免费随便添。: It was run by just the two of them, the owner and his wife, and refills of rice were free, no matter how many bowls you had.
我上学时也几乎每天都在那里吃每日套餐。: When I was a student, I ate the daily set meal there almost every day, too.
毕业十年后的某一天，我听说那家食堂这个月就要关门了。: One day, ten years after I graduated, I heard that the diner would be closing at the end of the month.
最后一天，我请假去了店里，店门前排起了长队。: On the last day, I took the day off work and went to the diner, and there was a long line in front of it.
排队的都是和我一样，过去受过这家店照顾的毕业生们。: The people in line were graduates who, like me, had been helped by this diner in the past.
好不容易坐下，老板娘说：“哎呀，过得好吗？”她竟然还记得我。: When I finally got a seat, the owner's wife remembered my face and said, "Oh my, how have you been?"
那天的套餐，正是我学生时代最喜欢的姜汁烧肉。: That day's set meal was shogayaki (ginger pork), which had been my favorite when I was a student.
吃了一口，我就想起了那时候——即使没钱，只要来这里就能吃饱。: With one bite, I remembered those days when, even if I had no money, I could fill my stomach just by coming here.
临走时，我深深地鞠了一躬，说：“这么多年来，谢谢你们了。”: As I was leaving, I bowed deeply and said, "Thank you for all these years."
等待最后一名跑者的掌声: The applause that waited for the last runner
去年秋天，我在镇上的市民马拉松比赛中，作为志愿者站在终点附近。: Last fall, I was standing near the finish line as a volunteer at our town's community marathon.
速度快的跑者们接连冲过终点，会场被热烈的欢呼声包围。: Fast runners crossed the finish line one after another, and the venue was filled with loud cheers.
然而随着时间推移，冲过终点的跑者越来越少。: But as time went on, the number of runners crossing the finish line gradually dwindled.
临近限制时间时，远远看到一位上了年纪的男士正慢慢地跑过来。: As the time limit approached, I saw an elderly man in the distance, running slowly toward us.
他几乎是拖着腿，却始终没有停下来走，坚持向前跑。: Although he seemed almost to be dragging his legs, the man kept moving forward without ever walking.
这时，正要回去的观众们停下了脚步，一个接一个地聚集到道路两旁。: Then spectators who had been about to leave stopped in their tracks and, one after another, gathered on both sides of the road.
“还差一点！”“加油！”的喊声从四面八方响起。: Shouts of "Almost there!" and "Keep going!" rose up from all around.
那位男士撞线的一瞬间，会场响起了当天最热烈的掌声。: The moment the man broke the finish tape, the venue filled with the loudest applause of the day.
后来听说，那个人战胜了疾病，时隔多年重新回到了赛场。: I heard later that he had overcome an illness and come back to the race for the first time in years.
我明白了，无论名次如何，坚持到底的身影都能打动人心。: I learned that, regardless of ranking, the sight of someone who never gives up until the end moves people's hearts.
上初中的时候，我得到了姐姐用过的自行车。: When I started junior high, I was given the bicycle my older sister had been using.
也就是所谓的“旧物传承”。: It was what you call a "hand-me-down."
朋友们都骑着新自行车，说实话，我有点不好意思。: All my friends were riding new bicycles, so to be honest, I was a little embarrassed.
车漆也褪了色，每次刹车都会发出“吱”的一声巨响。: Its color had faded, too, and every time I put on the brakes, it made a loud "squeak."
我一个劲儿地抱怨，还对姐姐说了“我想要新的”这种过分的话。: I did nothing but complain, and I even said something awful to my sister: "I wanted a new one."
有一天，我发现自行车车筐底部夹着一张折得小小的纸。: One day, I noticed a small folded piece of paper tucked into the bottom of the bicycle basket.
打开一看，上面是姐姐的字迹：“下坡要早点刹车哦。这辆自行车，载着我度过了整整三年: When I opened it, it said in my sister's handwriting, "Brake early on hills, okay? This bike carried me through all three of my years."
读了那张纸，我才第一次知道姐姐一直很珍惜这辆自行车。: Reading that note, I learned for the first time that my sister had treasured this bicycle.
下一个周末，我和姐姐一起去了自行车店，请人修好了刹车。: The next weekend, I went to the bike shop with my sister and had the brakes fixed.
之后的三年里，我也每天骑着这辆车去上学。: For the next three years, I too rode this bicycle to school every day.
毕业那天，我也在车筐底部放了一封信，留给下一个骑它的弟弟。: On graduation day, I also left a letter in the bottom of the basket for my younger brother, who would ride it next.
和歌山县的熊野古道，是古人为了去熊野的神社参拜而走的道路。: The Kumano Kodo in Wakayama Prefecture is the trail that people long ago walked to pray at the shrines of Kumano.
2004年，它作为“纪伊山地的圣地与参拜道”的一部分，被列入了世界遗产。: In 2004, it was registered as a World Heritage Site as part of the "Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range."
我和朋友两个人，从几条路线中选了走的人最多的一条。: Out of the several routes, my friend and I chose one that is especially popular with walkers.
路上还保留着石板路，两侧高大的杉树绵延不绝。: Stone paving still remained on the trail, and tall cedar trees lined both sides the whole way.
一路上，随处可见被称为“王子”的小神社。: As you walk, here and there you come across small shrines called "oji."
据说古人就是在这样的地方歇脚，花上好几天继续旅程。: People in the old days apparently rested at places like these as they continued their journey over many days.
雨后的石板路很滑，我们好几次停下脚步调整呼吸。: The stone paving was slippery after the rain, and we stopped many times to catch our breath.
尽管如此，在只听得见鸟鸣和树叶沙沙声的山林中行走，感觉非常舒畅。: Even so, walking through a place where all you could hear was birdsong and the rustling of leaves felt wonderful.
傍晚到达目的地神社时，腿已经僵得像木棍一样，心里却出奇地清爽。: When we reached our destination shrine in the evening, my legs were as stiff as sticks, but my mind felt strangely refreshed.
调整呼吸: to catch one's breath, to steady one's breathing
乘水牛车游竹富岛: Touring Taketomi Island by water buffalo cart
从冲绳县石垣岛的港口坐船不一会儿，就到了一个叫竹富岛的小岛。: Take a short boat ride from the port of Ishigaki in Okinawa Prefecture and you will reach a small island called Taketomi.
岛上保留着红瓦屋顶的房子、白沙路、石头垒起的围墙等古朴的冲绳风景。: Traditional Okinawan scenery remains on the island, such as houses with red-tiled roofs, white sand roads and walls of piled-up stones.
屋顶上有驱邪的风狮爷守护着房子。: On the roofs sit shisa, guardian figures that ward off evil, protecting the houses.
这个岛上很受欢迎的，是乘坐水牛拉的车，在村落里慢悠悠地游览。: What is popular on this island is sightseeing in a cart pulled by a water buffalo, slowly touring the village.
水牛以比人走路还慢的速度，悠闲地沿路前行。: The water buffalo moves leisurely along the road, at a pace even slower than a person walking.
赶车的人给我们讲岛上的生活，还弹起三线琴给我们唱冲绳的歌。: The driver told us about life on the island and played the sanshin, singing Okinawan songs for us.
转弯时，水牛自己记得路，不用停就稳稳地拐了过去，让我很惊讶。: When turning corners, the water buffalo remembered the way by itself and turned neatly without stopping, which surprised me.
在这个时间仿佛慢慢流淌的岛上，连看表都会忘记。: On this island, where time seems to flow slowly, you even forget to look at your watch.
旅行的最后，我骑着自行车沿白沙路，去看了沉入大海的夕阳。: At the end of the trip, I rode a bicycle along the white sand roads to go see the sun setting into the sea.
驱邪: warding off evil, charm against evil
沉落: to sink, to set (of the sun)
北海道的小樽，是一座以运河和成排老仓库的风景而闻名的港口城市。: Otaru in Hokkaido is a port town known for its scenery of a canal lined with old warehouses.
从明治到大正时期，小樽作为北海道的物流中心非常繁荣。: From the Meiji era into the Taisho era, Otaru flourished greatly as the hub of distribution in Hokkaido.
据说为了存放船运来的货物，运河沿岸建起了很多石砌的仓库。: To store the cargo brought in by ship, many stone warehouses were apparently built along the canal.
如今这些仓库被用作餐厅和商店。: Today those warehouses are used as restaurants and shops.
我去的时候是冬天的傍晚，正是运河沿岸的煤气灯开始亮起来的时候。: I visited on a winter evening, just as the gas lamps along the canal were starting to light up.
积雪的仓库倒映在水面上，简直就像明信片上的风景。: The snow-covered warehouses were reflected on the water's surface, making a scene just like a picture postcard.
看完运河后，我在附近的街上逛了逛玻璃工艺品店和八音盒店。: After seeing the canal, I strolled along a nearby street, peeking into shops selling glasswork and music boxes.
打开小八音盒的盖子，温柔的乐声在寒冷的店里回荡。: When I opened the lid of a small music box, a gentle sound filled the cold shop.
回酒店的路上，看到雪地上只有自己的脚印一路延伸，我感受到了这座小城夜晚的宁静。: On my way back to the hotel, I saw only my own footprints trailing through the snow, and I felt the quiet of the town at night.
在高千穗峡划船: Rowing a boat in Takachiho Gorge
宫崎县的高千穗峡，是被高高的悬崖环绕的美丽峡谷。: Takachiho Gorge in Miyazaki Prefecture is a beautiful valley surrounded by high cliffs.
据说这些悬崖是很久以前阿苏火山喷发时流过来的熔岩冷却凝固而成的。: These cliffs are said to have formed when lava that flowed here during an eruption of the Aso volcano long, long ago cooled and hardened.
之后河流花了漫长的时间侵蚀岩石，形成了如今这样的深谷。: After that, the river wore away the rock over a long time, creating the deep valley you see today.
峡谷中有一道名叫“真名井瀑布”的瀑布，水从高处笔直地落入河中。: In the gorge is a waterfall called "Manai Falls," where water drops straight down from a great height into the river.
在这里可以租船，自己一边划一边游览峡谷。: Here, you can rent a boat and see the gorge while rowing it yourself.
我是第一次划船，一开始船怎么也不往前走，一直在原地打转。: It was my first time rowing a boat, and at first it wouldn't go straight, and I ended up going around and around in the same spot.
终于掌握诀窍划到瀑布附近，细细的水花溅到脸上，非常凉爽。: When I finally got the hang of it and made it close to the waterfall, a fine spray hit my face, and it felt very cool.
从下面仰望的悬崖比想象中高得多，让我感受到了大自然力量的强大。: Looking up from below, the cliffs were far higher than I had expected, and I felt the immense power of nature.
因为是热门景点，据说暑假等时候，要等很久才能坐上船。: It's a popular spot, so during summer vacation and other busy times, you may apparently have to wait a long time to get on a boat.
片尾要看到最后: Watching the ending all the way through
以前的我，动画正片一结束，就马上播放下一集。: I used to start playing the next episode as soon as the main part of an anime episode ended.
我一直觉得放片尾曲的时候是很无聊的时间。: I thought the time while the ending song was playing was boring.
可是，在看某部作品的时候，朋友告诉我：“片尾绝对不能跳过。”: But when I was watching a certain series, a friend told me, "You absolutely can't skip the ending."
照她说的看到最后，歌曲结束后竟然播放了一小段场景。: When I watched to the end as she told me, a short scene played after the song finished.
那段场景里藏着与下一集有关的重要线索。: That scene contained a hidden clue that was important for the next episode.
从那以后，我都会坚持把片尾看到最后。: Since then, I've made a point of watching the ending all the way through, too.
仔细看会发现，片尾的画面里常常描绘着正片中看不到的角色们的日常。: If you look closely, the ending visuals often depict the everyday lives of the characters, which you don't get to see in the main story.
画面上滚动的众多名字，都属于为制作这部作品而工作的人们。: The many names that scroll across the screen belong to the people who worked to make the series.
看着那长长的名单，我真切地感受到，动画确实是靠众人的力量完成的。: Looking at that long list, I truly feel that anime is made through the efforts of a great many people.
现在，片尾的时间我也能作为作品的一部分来享受了。: Now I've come to enjoy the ending, too, as part of the work.
正片: main part (of a show or film), main feature
为漫画增色的网点图案: The dot patterns that bring color to manga
仔细看黑白漫画，会发现有很多看起来是灰色的部分。: If you look closely at black-and-white manga, you'll see many areas that look gray.
其实其中大多是由非常小的黑点聚集而成的图案。: In fact, most of them are patterns made up of very tiny black dots.
以前的漫画家会使用一种印有这种点状图案、叫做“网点纸”的贴纸。: Manga artists in the past used sheets called "screentone" with these dot patterns printed on them.
用美工刀切成需要的形状，贴到原稿上。: They would cut them into the shapes they needed with a craft knife and stick them onto the manuscript.
改变点的大小和排列方式，就能表现天空颜色的渐变、衣服的花纹、夜晚的昏暗等等。: By changing the size and arrangement of the dots, they can express things like changes in the color of the sky, patterns on clothes and the darkness of night.
因为是精细的工作，据说助手有时要花好几个小时贴网点。: Because it was detailed work, assistants apparently sometimes spent hours applying tone.
另外，漫画家们还各显神通，比如刮擦网点让画面看起来闪闪发光。: Manga artists also each came up with their own techniques, such as scraping tone to make something look as if it were shining.
最近，用电脑或平板画漫画的人多了，网点也能用数码方式轻松地贴上了。: These days, more and more people draw manga on computers and tablets, and tone can now be applied easily in digital form.
尽管如此，漫画里的每一个小点，都倾注着想让作品更美的心意。: Even so, each and every tiny dot in manga carries the wish to make the work look beautiful.
下功夫；想方设法: to put effort into; to devise ways
让我爱上历史的学习漫画: The educational manga that made me love history
上小学的时候，我很不擅长社会课，尤其是历史。: When I was in elementary school, I was really bad at social studies, especially history.
光是要背人名和年号，我完全不知道有什么意思。: All we ever did was memorize people's names and era names, and I had no idea what was interesting about it.
一个下雨天，我在图书馆打发时间时，发现了一套用漫画描绘日本历史的丛书。: One rainy day, while killing time at the library, I found a series that told Japanese history in manga form.
随手翻开第一册，课本里只是个名字的人物，在书中有哭有怒，活灵活现。: When I casually opened the first volume, figures who had been just names in my textbook were living, crying and getting angry.
从那天起，我每周都去图书馆，一册一册地借后续的书。: From that day on, I started going to the library every week and borrowing the next volume, one at a time.
通过漫画了解了来龙去脉再读课本，各个事件就像一个完整的故事一样连贯起来了。: When I read my textbook after learning the flow of events from the manga, the events seemed connected as a single story.
考试分数也一点点提高了，老师表扬我说“最近很努力嘛”。: My test scores gradually went up too, and my teacher praised me, saying, "You've been working hard lately."
当然，漫画中也有根据作者想象描绘的场面，并不全是史实。: Of course, manga also includes scenes drawn from the author's imagination, so not everything is fact.
尽管如此，那套书为我打开了历史的大门，这一点毋庸置疑。: Even so, there's no doubt that that series opened the door to history for me.
现在，我在中学教社会课。: Now I teach social studies at a junior high school.
当上电视剧群演的那天: The day I was an extra in a TV drama
在朋友的邀请下，我试着报名了电视剧的群众演员。: At a friend's invitation, I tried applying to be an extra in a TV drama.
所谓群众演员，是指路人、店里的客人等出现在场景背景中的人。: Extras are people who appear in the background of a scene, such as passersby or customers in a shop.
拍摄那天，我一早赶到集合地点，那里已经聚集了五十人左右。: On the day of the shoot, when I went to the meeting place early in the morning, about fifty people had already gathered.
我们的角色是走在车站前十字路口的路人。: Our role was to be passersby walking through the intersection in front of the station.
工作人员一再提醒我们：“不要看镜头，请自然地走路。”: The staff warned us again and again, "Please don't look at the camera, and walk naturally."
可是一想到有摄像机，就忘了平时是怎么走路的了。: But once I thought about the camera being there, I couldn't remember how I usually walked.
同一个场面重拍了好多次，回过神来，天已经全黑了。: We reshot the same scene over and over, and before I knew it, the sky had grown completely dark.
主演在漫长的等待时间里，还对每一位群演说“这么冷的天，谢谢大家”。: Even during the long waits, the lead actor spoke to each and every extra, saying, "Thank you for being here in this cold."
