播出那天，我和家人守在电视机前，可我出镜的只有短短一瞬间。: On the day it aired, I waited in front of the TV with my family, but I appeared for only a split second.
尽管如此，我知道了拍一个场面要花多少工夫，看电视剧的眼光也有了些变化。: Even so, learning how much work goes into making a single scene changed the way I watch dramas a little.
报名；应征: applying, signing up; entry (in response to a call)
憧憬校园剧里的老师: Inspired by the teacher in a school drama
初二的时候，我迷上了一部校园剧。: When I was in my second year of junior high, I became hooked on a certain school drama.
主人公是一位年轻老师，认真地面对每一个有烦恼的学生。: The main character was a young teacher who earnestly faced each and every student who was struggling with problems.
即使学生撒谎，老师也不放弃，一次又一次地试着倾听他们的心声。: Even when students lied, the teacher never gave up on them and tried to hear them out again and again.
每周看着那部剧，我也渐渐想将来当一名老师。: As I watched the drama every week, I began to think that I, too, wanted to become a teacher someday.
大学毕业后，如愿当上老师的我，很快就认识到了现实的严峻。: After graduating from university and becoming a teacher as I had long wished, I quickly learned how harsh reality is.
每天忙于备课和文书工作，很难挤出和学生谈话的时间。: Swamped with lesson preparation and paperwork, I can hardly find time to talk with my students.
因为做不到像剧里的老师那样而情绪低落的日子也不少。: There have been quite a few days when I've felt down, thinking that things don't go the way they do for the teacher in the drama.
就在那时，有一天我收到了一位毕业生的来信：“因为老师每天早上都跟我打招呼，我才能: Then one day, a letter came from a former student: "I was able to keep coming to school because you spoke to me every morning."
我意识到，即使做不到电视剧里那样特别的事，点滴的积累也很重要。: I realized that even if I can't do special things like in a drama, it's the accumulation of small things that matters.
现在我也会时不时重看那部剧，提醒自己不忘初心。: Even now, I sometimes rewatch that drama to remind myself of why I started.
抛弃: to abandon, to give up on
忙于: to be swamped (with), to be pressed (by)
从法庭剧到真实的审判: From courtroom dramas to real trials
看了律师大显身手的电视剧后，我开始好奇真正的审判是什么样子。: After watching a drama about lawyers in action, I became curious about what real trials are like.
查了一下，我发现日本的大多数审判，任何人都可以自由旁听。: When I looked into it, I found that most trials in Japan can be observed freely by anyone.
得知既不需要预约也不花钱，我决定去附近的地方法院看看。: Learning that you don't need a reservation and it costs nothing, I decided to go to the nearby district court.
在入口接受行李检查后，看着当天开庭的审判一览表选择法庭。: After getting your bags checked at the entrance, you look at the list of trials being held that day and choose a courtroom.
不过据说受到关注的审判，有时会通过抽签发放旁听券。: However, for trials that are attracting a lot of attention, there is apparently sometimes a lottery for gallery tickets.
法庭里比电视剧里安静得多，几乎没有大声喊叫的场面。: Inside the courtroom, it was much quieter than in dramas, and there were almost no scenes of anyone raising their voice.
法官和律师一边核对文件，一边用平稳的语气不紧不慢地推进审理。: The judges and lawyers moved the proceedings along slowly in calm voices, checking documents as they went.
因为禁止拍照和录音，所以我边做笔记边听。: Taking photos and making recordings are prohibited, so I listened while taking notes.
虽然没有电视剧那样的大逆转，但那里有真实的人生。: There was no dramatic reversal like in a drama, but there was real life there.
从那以后，看法庭剧时，我的心情也和以前有些不同了。: Since then, I've come to watch courtroom dramas with somewhat different feelings.
旁听: attending as a spectator, observing (a trial or hearing)
茶碗蒸是把鸡蛋和高汤混合后，放在带盖的器皿里蒸成的菜。: Chawanmushi is a dish made by mixing egg and dashi and steaming it in a lidded cup.
在寿司店和日料店里经常吃到，要用勺子舀着吃。: It is often served at sushi restaurants and Japanese restaurants, and you scoop it up with a spoon to eat it.
里面放有虾、鱼糕、香菇、银杏等各种配料。: Inside are all kinds of ingredients, such as shrimp, kamaboko (fish cake), shiitake mushrooms and ginkgo nuts.
每吃一口都会吃到不同的配料，有一种寻宝般的乐趣。: As you eat your way through it, you keep finding different ingredients, so it's fun, like a treasure hunt.
母亲教我做法时，我很惊讶它比想象中难。: When my mother taught me how to make it, I was surprised at how much harder it was than I had expected.
火太大的话，表面会出现很多小孔，口感就变差了。: If the heat is too high, lots of tiny holes form on the surface and the texture becomes unpleasant.
因此，据说用小火慢慢蒸很重要。: For that reason, it is apparently important to steam it slowly over low heat.
另外，把鸡蛋和高汤混合后先过滤一遍，做出来会更嫩滑。: Also, if you strain the egg and dashi mixture once after mixing, it turns out smooth.
我第一次自己做的茶碗蒸虽然出现了一些小孔，家人还是说很好吃。: The first chawanmushi I made myself ended up with a few holes, but my family said it was delicious.
下次我打算再挑战一次，争取做出嫩嫩滑滑的茶碗蒸。: Next time, I plan to try again so that I can make perfectly jiggly chawanmushi.
做成；完成: to turn out (when finished); to be completed
夏天临近时，拉面馆和中餐馆门口就会贴出“凉拌中华面开卖了”的告示。: As summer approaches, signs saying "Now serving hiyashi chuka" go up in front of ramen shops and Chinese restaurants.
看到这张告示，应该有很多人觉得夏天终于来了吧。: Many people probably feel that summer has finally arrived when they see this sign.
凉拌中华面是把煮好的中华面用冷水过凉，上面放上五颜六色配料的料理。: Hiyashi chuka is a dish of boiled Chinese-style noodles chilled and firmed up in cold water, with colorful toppings arranged on top.
黄瓜、火腿、切成细丝的煎蛋、番茄等，整齐漂亮地摆在上面，是经典做法。: The classic style is to arrange cucumber, ham, thinly sliced omelet, tomato and so on neatly on top.
酱汁中，酱油加醋的酸甜口味和芝麻口味最受欢迎。: For the sauce, a sweet-and-sour soy sauce and vinegar flavor and a sesame flavor are popular.
名字里虽然带着“中华”，据说却是在日本诞生的料理。: Although its name contains "chuka" (Chinese), it is said to be a dish that was born in Japan.
即使在热得没胃口的日子，因为冰凉清爽，也能吸溜吸溜地吃下去。: Even on hot days when you have no appetite, it's cold and refreshing, so you can slurp it right down.
另外，据说在关西也有人把凉拌中华面叫做“冷面”。: Also, in Kansai, some people apparently call hiyashi chuka "reimen."
在我家，这是暑假午饭的固定菜单，切配料一直是我的活儿。: At my house, it was a summer vacation lunch staple, and cutting the toppings was always my job.
跟祖母学熬高汤: How my grandmother taught me to make dashi
开始一个人生活之前，我跟祖母学了熬高汤的方法。: Before I started living on my own, I learned how to make dashi from my grandmother.
祖母常说：“只要高汤熬得好，味噌汤就会好喝。”: My grandmother always says, "As long as you make the dashi properly, your miso soup will be delicious."
首先，在锅里放入水和海带，就这样泡一段时间。: First, put water and kombu in a pot and let it sit as is for a while.
然后用小火加热，在水快要烧开之前把海带取出来。: Then put it over low heat and take out the kombu just before the water comes to a boil.
据说这是因为一旦煮沸，海带就会析出黏液和苦味。: This is apparently because if you let it boil, the kombu releases sliminess and bitterness.
水开后关火，放入大量木鱼花，等木鱼花沉下去。: Once the water boils, turn off the heat, add plenty of katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes), and wait until the flakes sink.
最后用铺着纱布的笊篱过滤，漂亮的金黄色高汤就做好了。: Finally, strain it through a cloth laid in a colander, and you have beautiful golden dashi.
祖母告诉我，过滤时不要用力挤木鱼花，这是诀窍。: My grandmother told me the trick is not to squeeze the katsuobushi hard when straining.
用自己熬的高汤做味噌汤，香气随着热气升腾起来。: When I made miso soup with dashi I had made myself, a wonderful aroma rose up with the steam.
喝了一口，是从小就熟悉的祖母家的味道，心里不由得暖洋洋的。: When I took a sip, it tasted like my grandmother's home, a flavor I had known since childhood, and somehow I felt warm inside.
当午饭值日生的一周: My week on school lunch duty
这周我是负责盛午饭的值日生。: This week, I'm on school lunch duty.
值日生必须穿戴白色的衣服、帽子和口罩。: The students on duty have to wear white clothes, a cap and a mask.
上午的课一结束，大家就一起去配餐室取饭菜。: When morning classes are over, we all go together to the school kitchen to get the food.
大锅很重，所以两个人一起抬。: The big pots are very heavy, so two people carry them.
回到教室后，就给其他同学的盘子里盛米饭和菜。: When we get back to the classroom, we put rice and side dishes on everyone else's plates.
要把每份盛得一样多，比想象的难。: Serving the same amount to everyone is harder than I thought.
全员准备好之后，全班一起说“我开动了”，然后开始吃。: When everyone is ready, the whole class says 「いただきます」 together and starts eating.
星期五是我喜欢的咖喱日，所以我很期待。: Friday is curry day, which I love, so I'm looking forward to it.
值日: being on duty, turn on duty
修学旅行之夜: A night on the school trip
初三那年春天，我们去京都和奈良修学旅行。: In the spring of our third year of junior high, we went to Kyoto and Nara on a school trip.
三天里参观了很多古老的寺庙和神社。: Over three days, we visited many old temples and shrines.
也有一天是按小组自己决定去哪儿，坐公交和出租车到处转。: There was also a day when we decided in our groups where to go and got around by bus and taxi.
不过，我记得最清楚的，是在旅馆的那个晚上。: But what I remember most is the night at the ryokan.
我和同屋的五个朋友躺在被窝里聊到很晚。: I talked until late with the five friends in my room, lying in our futons.
正聊着喜欢的人，老师突然打开了门。: While we were talking about the people we liked, the teacher suddenly opened the door.
大家马上闭上眼睛，装作在睡觉。: Everyone immediately closed their eyes and pretended to be asleep.
老师说了句“快睡吧”，笑着出去了。: The teacher said, "Go to sleep now," and left, laughing.
现在和那些朋友见面时，还会聊起那天晚上的事。: Even now, when I see those friends, we talk about that night.
我们班每个月都换座位。: In my class, we change seats every month.
座位是抽签决定的，所以不知道会坐到谁旁边。: Seats are decided by drawing lots, so you don't know who you'll end up next to.
这个月，我坐到了几乎没说过话的山田旁边。: This month, I ended up next to Yamada, whom I had hardly ever talked to.
山田总是很安静，我一直以为他是个有点可怕的人。: Yamada was always quiet, and I had thought he was a little scary.
有一天，我把橡皮忘在家里了。: One day, I left my eraser at home.
正发愁时，山田把自己的橡皮切成两半，分了我一半。: While I was at a loss, Yamada cut his own eraser in half and gave me a piece.
从那以后，我们每天都会聊上几句。: After that, we started talking a little every day.
山田对昆虫特别了解，聊起来很有意思。: Yamada knows a lot about insects, and he's interesting to talk to.
我心里想着，要是下次不换座位就好了。: I find myself thinking that I wish the next seat change would never come.
为难: to be troubled, to be at a loss
派出所的警察: The police officer at the koban
日本的街上到处都有叫“交番”的小建筑。: In Japanese towns, there are small buildings called "koban" here and there.
在派出所里，警察守护着街区的安全。: At a koban, police officers keep the town safe.
警察的工作不只是在发生案件和事故时出警。: A police officer's job isn't only to go out when there's an incident or accident.
他们也经常一边给不认识路的人看地图，一边给他们指路。: They also often give directions to people who are lost, showing them a map.
有人送来失物时，他们会填写文件并妥善保管。: When lost items are turned in, they fill out paperwork and take good care of them.
晚上也轮班工作，尽量让派出所里有人。: They also work in shifts at night, trying to keep someone at the koban as much as possible.
不过，有时因为出去巡逻，里面会没有人。: However, sometimes no one is there because they are out on patrol.
这时可以用派出所里的电话和警察署联系。: In that case, you can talk to the police station using the phone inside the koban.
遇到困难时，请放心地去派出所看看吧。: If you're ever in trouble, feel free to stop by a koban.
宠物医院的医生: The vet at the animal hospital
我在镇上一家小宠物医院当兽医。: I work as a veterinarian at a small animal hospital in town.
来看病的多是猫狗，但也有人带兔子和鸟来。: Most of the animals that come in are dogs and cats, but some people bring rabbits and birds too.
所以我会认真听主人讲情况，再仔细检查它们的身体。: So I listen carefully to what the owners tell me and examine the animals' bodies thoroughly.
也有的狗害怕医院，在门口就不肯动了。: Some dogs dislike the hospital and refuse to budge at the entrance.
这种时候，我会喂点零食，或者慢慢地跟它说话。: At times like that, I give them a treat or talk to them slowly.
看到恢复健康的动物摇着尾巴回家，是我最高兴的时候。: What makes me happiest is seeing animals that have gotten better go home wagging their tails.
我希望养宠物的人在宠物生病之前，每年至少带它来做一次体检。: I'd like people who keep animals to bring them in for a checkup at least once a year, before they get sick.
带领: to take (someone) along, to bring along
害怕；不擅长: disliking, being afraid of; being bad at
摇: to wave, to shake, to wag
上大学后，我开始做早上送报纸的兼职。: After I started university, I began a part-time job delivering newspapers in the morning.
每天早上三点起床，去附近的送报站。: Every morning I get up at three and go to the nearby newspaper dealer.
先把广告传单夹进报纸，再装上摩托车出发。: After putting flyers into the newspapers, I load them onto my motorbike and set off.
要送的人家大约有两百户，必须记住每一户的位置。: There are about two hundred houses in all that I deliver newspapers to, and I have to remember where every one of them is.
最辛苦的是下雨下雪的日子。: The hardest days are rainy and snowy ones.
为了不让报纸淋湿，要一份一份地装进塑料袋。: To keep the newspapers from getting wet, I put each copy in a plastic bag.
快送完的时候，东边的天空渐渐亮了起来。: Around the time I finish my deliveries, the eastern sky gradually starts to grow light.
看着那片天空，就算累也觉得心情很好。: When I see that sky, I feel good even if I'm tired.
我家是在栃木县种草莓的农户。: My family has a farm that grows strawberries in Tochigi Prefecture.
草莓是在塑料大棚里种的。: We grow the strawberries in plastic greenhouses.
即使外面很冷，大棚里也像春天一样暖和。: Even when it's cold outside, it's as warm as spring inside the greenhouse.
大棚里还有蜜蜂。: There are also honeybees inside the greenhouse.
多亏蜜蜂在花与花之间飞来飞去，草莓才能长成漂亮的形状。: The honeybees fly from flower to flower for us, and that's why the strawberries grow into nice shapes.
摘草莓的时间大约是从冬天到春天。: We pick strawberries roughly from winter to spring.
草莓很软，容易碰伤，所以要用手一个一个轻轻地摘。: Strawberries are soft and bruise easily, so we gently pick them by hand one at a time.
从一大早就开始干活，很辛苦，但听到别人说“又甜又好吃”，疲劳就全忘了。: It's hard work, since we start early in the morning, but when people tell us, "They're sweet and delicious," we forget how tired we are.
商店街上豆腐店的早晨来得非常早。: Morning starts very early at the tofu shop in the shopping street.
店主每天早上四点左右就开始干活。: The owner starts work at around four o'clock every morning.
把从前一天晚上就泡在水里的黄豆用机器磨碎。: He uses a machine to grind up soybeans that have been soaking in water since the night before.
再把它煮开、过滤，做成豆浆。: He boils that, squeezes it, and makes soy milk.
往豆浆里加入“卤水”，它就会慢慢凝固成豆腐。: When "nigari" (bittern) is added to the soy milk, it gradually sets and becomes tofu.
听说以前卖豆腐的人会骑着自行车、吹着喇叭，在街上走街串巷地叫卖。: In the old days, tofu sellers apparently rode their bicycles through town selling tofu, sounding a horn as they went.
现在是在店里卖，但也有街坊端着锅来买。: Now the tofu is sold in the shop, but sometimes neighbors come to buy it with their own pots.
刚做好的豆腐热乎乎的，什么都不浇也带着一股甜味。: Freshly made tofu is warm and tastes sweet even without anything on it.
我在一家搬家公司工作。: I work for a moving company.
早上八点到客户家后，首先精神饱满地打招呼。: When we arrive at a customer's home at eight in the morning, the first thing we do is greet them cheerfully.
然后为了不刮伤家具和墙壁，要盖上厚布，护好边角。: Then, to avoid scratching the furniture and walls, we cover things with thick cloth and protect the corners.
冰箱、洗衣机这类重东西，两个人一边互相喊着口令一边搬。: Heavy things like refrigerators and washing machines are carried by two people, calling out to each other as they go.
最忙的是三月和四月。: The busiest months are March and April.
因为这是学校和公司迎来新一年的季节，搬家的人非常多。: That's the season when schools and companies start their new year, so a great many people move.
这段时间，有时从早到晚都没有休息的时间。: During this period, there are days when we have no time to rest from morning till night.
在新房间里听到客户说一声“谢谢”，疲劳就一扫而空。: When a customer says "thank you" to us in their new place, our fatigue just melts away.
四月进公司后，我第一次拿到了自己的名片。: When I joined the company in April, I received my own business cards for the first time.
在培训中，反复练习了递名片的方法。: In training, we practiced how to hand over business cards many times.
名片要用双手拿着，朝着对方能读字的方向递过去。: You hold the card with both hands and hand it over facing so that the other person can read it.
接的时候也要用双手接，并说“收下了”。: When receiving one, you also take it with both hands and say 「ちょうだいします」 ("I humbly accept it").
收到的名片在谈话期间要放在桌子上。: While you are talking, you leave the business cards you received on the table.
上周，我第一次跟着前辈去了客户公司。: Last week, I went to a client's company with a senior colleague for the first time.
我太紧张，把自己的名片拿倒了递了出去。: I was nervous and ended up holding out my business card upside down.
客户笑着对我说：“我刚开始也是这样的。”: The client laughed and said, "I was the same when I started."
那句话让我轻松了很多。: Those words made me feel much more at ease.
在美发店说“剪一点点”: "Just a little" at the hair salon
来日本三个月，我第一次一个人去了美发店。: Three months after coming to Japan, I went to a hair salon by myself for the first time.
按预约时间到店后，先给我洗了头。: When I arrived at my appointment time, they started by shampooing my hair.
美发师问我“今天想怎么剪？”，我回答“请稍微剪一点”。: The hairdresser asked, "What would you like today?" so I answered, "Please just cut a little."
可是剪完一看镜子，头发变得非常短。: But when it was over and I looked in the mirror, my hair had become very short.
后来跟日本朋友说起这件事，朋友说：“那是因为你没说剪几厘米呀。”: Later, when I told a Japanese friend about it, my friend said, "That's because you didn't say how many centimeters."
我这才明白，每个人心里的“一点点”是不一样长的。: I realized that how long "a little" is differs from person to person.
下次我打算带着照片去，一边给对方看一边说明。: Next time, I plan to bring a photo and explain while showing it.
反正头发还会长，所以现在我就好好享受短发了。: My hair will grow back anyway, so for now I'm enjoying having short hair.
最近一吃甜的东西，右边靠里的牙就疼。: Recently, whenever I eat something sweet, one of my back teeth on the right starts to hurt.
跟妈妈一说，她就说：“赶快去看牙医吧。”: When I told my mother, she said, "Let's go to the dentist right away."
我最讨厌看牙医了。: I really hate going to the dentist.
因为光听到那种“吱——”的声音就害怕。: That's because just hearing that high-pitched whining sound makes me scared.
可是去了才发现，医生是个很温柔的人。: But when I went, the dentist turned out to be a very kind person.
治疗前，他一边用镜子让我看牙齿，一边给我讲要做什么。: Before the treatment, he showed me my teeth in a mirror and explained what he was going to do.
他说“疼的话就举左手哦”，我稍微安心了一些。: He told me, "If it hurts, raise your left hand," so I felt a little relieved.
治疗大约二十分钟就结束了，没有想象中那么疼。: The treatment was over in about twenty minutes, and it didn't hurt as much as I had expected.
以后我打算每天晚上都认真刷牙。: From now on, I'm going to brush my teeth carefully every night.
刷；擦: to brush (teeth); to polish, to wipe
天气好的日子，日本公寓的阳台上晒着很多被褥。: On sunny days, lots of futons are hung out to air on the balconies of Japanese apartments.
在日本，不睡床、而是在榻榻米上铺被褥睡觉的人也不少。: In Japan, quite a few people sleep on futons laid out on tatami mats rather than in beds.
被褥每晚都用，会渐渐变得潮湿。: When you use a futon every night, it gradually becomes damp.
所以要在晴天拿到外面晒，让它晒晒太阳。: So people hang them outside on sunny days and expose them to sunlight.
晒过的被褥松松软软的，非常舒服。: After airing, futons are fluffy and feel wonderful.
以前，很多人会用棍子拍打晒好的被褥。: In the past, many people used to beat their aired futons with a stick.
不过最近也有人说，与其拍打，不如用吸尘器吸一吸。: But these days, some people say it's better to vacuum them than to beat them.
只是，一直晒到傍晚的话又会返潮，所以最好在三点左右前收进来。: However, if you leave them out until evening, they'll get damp again, so bring them in by around three o'clock.
晒: to dry (in the sun), to air
在日本买自行车时，店员会问你“要做防盗登记吗？”: When you buy a bicycle in Japan, the shop staff will ask you, "Would you like to do the anti-theft registration?"
防盗登记是把自行车车主的姓名和住址登记下来的制度。: Anti-theft registration is a system for registering the name and address of a bicycle's owner.
其实，法律规定骑自行车的人必须做这项登记。: In fact, the law requires people who ride bicycles to do this registration.
登记之后，店家会把写着号码的贴纸贴在自行车上。: When you register, they put a sticker with a number on it on your bicycle.
自行车被偷的时候，有这个号码就更容易找回来。: If your bicycle is stolen, having this number makes it easier to find.
另外，有时也会被警察叫住，查一查号码。: Also, sometimes a police officer may stop you and check the number.
从朋友那里得到自行车时，需要办理重新登记的手续。: When you get a bicycle from a friend, you need to go through the procedure to register it anew.
去登记时，别忘了带身份证件。: When you go to register, don't forget to bring your ID.
去年春天，我在家居建材店买了一棵小番茄苗。: Last spring, I bought a cherry tomato seedling at a home improvement store.
公寓没有院子，所以我决定在阳台上种。: My apartment has no yard, so I decided to grow it on the balcony.
每天早上上班前浇水，成了我的新习惯。: Watering it every morning before going to work became my new habit.
到了六月，开出了黄色的小花。: In June, small yellow flowers bloomed.
之后结出了许多绿色的小番茄，一点点变红了。: Then lots of small green tomatoes formed and little by little turned red.
第一次摘下来的番茄，感觉比店里买的还要甜。: The first tomato I picked tasted sweeter than the ones you buy at the store.
我也分了一些给隔壁的老奶奶，她非常高兴。: When I shared some with the elderly woman in the apartment next door, she was very happy.
从那以后，我们在阳台上碰见时就会聊上几句。: Since then, we've started chatting whenever we see each other on our balconies.
今年我还想试着种黄瓜。: This year, I'd like to try growing cucumbers too.
公民馆的日语教室: The Japanese class at the community center
每周六上午，镇上的公民馆里都会开日语课。: Every Saturday morning, a Japanese class is held at the town's community center.
老师们是住在附近的志愿者。: The teachers are volunteers who live in the neighborhood.
我也是去年来到这个镇子后，开始来这里上课的。: I, too, started coming here after I moved to this town last year.
课上不仅教语法，还教怎么扔垃圾、怎么去医院看病等。: In class, they teach us not only grammar but also things like how to put out the garbage and how to see a doctor at a hospital.
我的老师七十岁，以前是小学老师。: My teacher is seventy and used to be an elementary school teacher.
她总是笑着说：“说错也没关系，多说说吧。”: She always says with a smile, "It's okay to make mistakes, so talk a lot."
上个月，我和老师一起去了附近神社的秋祭。: Last month, I went with my teacher to the autumn festival at a nearby shrine.
能用课上学的话和摊主聊天时，我真的特别高兴。: When I was able to talk with the people at the stalls using words I had learned in class, I was truly happy.
弄错: to make a mistake, to get wrong
第一次一个人生活: Living alone for the first time
考上大学后，我从今年春天开始一个人生活。: I passed my university entrance exams and started living on my own this spring.
起初，自由自在的生活非常开心。: At first, my free lifestyle was a lot of fun.
因为想几点睡就几点睡，想吃什么就吃什么。: That's because I could go to bed whenever I liked and eat whatever I liked.
可是过了两周左右，就慢慢体会到了不容易。: But after about two weeks, I started to realize how hard it was.
洗衣、打扫、做饭，全都得自己来。: Laundry, cleaning, cooking: I have to do it all myself.
有时打开冰箱，里面什么都没有。: Sometimes when I open the fridge, there's nothing in it.
一天晚上，我打电话问妈妈土豆炖肉怎么做。: One night, I called my mother and asked her how to make nikujaga (meat and potato stew).
我照她说的做了，可和妈妈的味道还是有点不一样。: I tried making it just as she told me, but it tasted a little different from my mother's.
对那些在家时觉得理所当然的事，现在我想说声“谢谢”。: Now I want to say "thank you" for the things I took for granted when I lived at home.
考上；合格: passing (an exam), being admitted; meeting the standard
一到夏天，奶奶家的窗边每年都会挂起风铃。: Every year when summer comes, a wind chime hangs in the window of my grandmother's house.
风一吹，就会发出“叮铃、叮铃”的清脆声音。: When the wind blows, it makes a pretty "ting-a-ling, ting-a-ling" sound.
听到那声音，即使是大热天也会觉得凉快一些。: Hearing that sound makes me feel a little cooler, even on hot days.
风铃有玻璃做的，也有铁做的。: There are wind chimes made of glass and ones made of iron.
玻璃风铃上画着图案，看起来也很漂亮。: Glass wind chimes have pictures painted on them and are pretty to look at, too.
岩手县的南部风铃是用铁做的，特点是声音清亮悠长。: Nanbu wind chimes from Iwate Prefecture are made of iron, and they are known for their high, long-lasting sound.
奶奶说：“空调也不错，可夏天还是得有风铃的声音啊。”: My grandmother says, "Air conditioning is nice, but summer isn't summer without the sound of a wind chime."
我也打算给自己的房间买一个。: I'm thinking of buying one for my own room, too.
日本的夏夜，蚊子很多。: On summer nights in Japan, there are lots of mosquitoes.
因此，人们很早以前就开始用蚊香了。: That's why mosquito coils have been used since long ago.
点上蚊香就会冒出烟，蚊子就不会靠近了。: When you light a mosquito coil, it gives off smoke, and mosquitoes stop coming near.
绿色、呈漩涡状的那种最为人熟知。: The best-known kind is green and shaped like a spiral.
听说做成漩涡状，是为了让它能长时间燃烧。: They were apparently made in a spiral shape so that they would keep burning for a long time.
小时候，爷爷家的檐廊上总放着一个小猪形状的容器。: When I was a child, there was always a pig-shaped container on the engawa (veranda) of my grandfather's house.
蚊香就是放在那里面点的。: That was where the mosquito coils were burned.
现在一闻到那个气味，我就会想起暑假里的西瓜和烟花。: Even now, whenever I smell that smell, I remember the watermelon and fireworks of summer vacation.
抱着热水袋入睡的冬天: Winter nights with a hot-water bottle
我的房间朝北，冬天非常冷。: My room is on the north side, so it's very cold in winter.
睡前开空调的话空气会变干，早上嗓子就疼。: If I turn on the air conditioner before bed, the air gets dry and my throat hurts in the morning.
于是，我从去年开始用热水袋。: So last year I started using a yutanpo (hot-water bottle).
热水袋是往里面灌热水、用来暖被窝的工具。: A yutanpo is a device you fill with hot water to warm up your futon.
睡前三十分钟左右，把它放进被子靠脚的那一头。: About thirty minutes before bed, I put it in the foot end of my futon.
钻进被窝，脚暖洋洋的，很快就困了。: When I get into the futon, my feet are toasty warm, and I soon get sleepy.
到了早上，里面的水还有点温，有时我就用它洗脸。: Even in the morning the water is still a little warm, so sometimes I use it to wash my face.
不过，长时间贴着皮肤可能会烫伤，所以请装进套子里使用。: However, if you keep it against your skin for a long time, you can get burned, so use it in a cover.
在日本，从夏天到秋天经常有台风。: In Japan, typhoons often come from summer through autumn.
台风一靠近，就会刮大风、下大雨。: When a typhoon approaches, strong winds blow and a lot of rain falls.
有时电车会停运，学校也会停课。: Sometimes trains stop running and schools close.
所以，在电视或手机上看到台风的新闻后，最好早做准备。: So when you see typhoon news on TV or your smartphone, get prepared early.
首先，把阳台上的花盆等可能被风吹走的东西搬进屋里。: First, bring things inside that might be blown away by the wind, such as flowerpots on the balcony.
为了防备停电，要检查有没有手电筒、手机电量够不够。: In case of a power outage, check whether you have a flashlight and whether your smartphone is fully charged.
再买些水和不用火也能吃的食物，就更放心了。: It's reassuring to buy water and food that can be eaten without cooking ahead of time.
台风过境期间，请尽量不要出门。: While the typhoon is passing through, please try not to go outside as much as possible.
二月的某一天，从早上起就刮着强劲的南风。: One day in February, a strong southerly wind blew from the morning on.
当天晚上的新闻里说：“关东地区刮起了春一番。”: On the news that night, they said, "Haru ichiban has blown in the Kanto region."
春一番指的是从立春到春分期间第一次刮起的、强劲而温暖的南风。: Haru ichiban is the first strong, warm southerly wind to blow between Risshun, the traditional start of spring, and the spring equinox.
人们说，这股风一刮，春天就不远了。: It is said that when this wind blows, spring is near.
大风差点把阳台上晾的衣服吹跑。: The wind was so strong that the laundry on the balcony nearly blew away.
即便如此，风里带着一丝花香，让我很开心。: Even so, there was a faint scent of flowers in the wind, which made me happy.
不过听说，春一番过后的第二天常常又会变冷。: However, the day after haru ichiban apparently often turns cold again.
妈妈笑着说：“所以呀，大衣还不能收起来呢。”: My mother laughed and said, "That's why we can't put the coats away yet."
亲子丼是在米饭上盖着鸡肉和鸡蛋的料理。: Oyakodon is a dish of chicken and egg on top of rice.
把鸡肉和洋葱用酱油、味醂调成的甜汁煮好，最后浇上蛋液让它凝住。: Chicken and onion are simmered in a sweet sauce of soy sauce and mirin, and finally bound together with egg.
之所以叫“亲子”，是因为鸡是父母，蛋是孩子。: It's called "oyako" (parent and child) because the chicken is the parent and the egg is the child.
名字听起来有点吓人，但在日本是非常受欢迎的料理。: It's a slightly creepy name, but it's a very popular dish in Japan.
那么，如果用牛肉或猪肉代替鸡肉，又叫什么呢？: So, what would you call it if you used beef or pork instead of chicken?
因为牛、猪和蛋不是亲子关系，所以叫“他人”。: Cows or pigs and eggs aren't parent and child, so it's called "tanin" (strangers).
知道了名字的由来再吃，也许会觉得更有意思。: Knowing the reasons behind the names may make the food even more fun to eat.
东京有个叫月岛的地方，那里有一条开满文字烧店的街。: In a Tokyo neighborhood called Tsukishima, there is a street lined with monjayaki restaurants.
文字烧是把面粉用水或高汤调开，加入卷心菜等配料煎成的料理。: Monjayaki is a dish made by mixing flour with water or dashi, adding cabbage and other ingredients, and cooking it on a griddle.
它和什锦烧有点像，但水分更多，更软。: It's a little like okonomiyaki, but it has more water and is softer.
做法也很有意思。: The way it's made is interesting, too.
先在铁板上炒配料，把中间空出来，围成一圈“堤坝”。: First, you stir-fry the ingredients on the griddle, then clear a space in the middle to make a round bank.
再往里面倒入剩下的面糊汁，稍微煮开后全部拌在一起。: You pour the rest of the liquid into it, and when it has cooked a little, you mix everything together.
吃的时候，用一种叫“はがし”的小铲子，直接从铁板上铲着吃。: When eating, you use a small spatula called a "hagashi" and eat directly off the griddle.
样子不怎么好看，但焦脆的地方特别香，非常好吃。: It doesn't look very pretty, but the browned bits are fragrant and very tasty.
出差去宫崎县时，客户公司的人带我去了一家南蛮炸鸡店。: When I went to Miyazaki Prefecture on a business trip, someone from a client company took me to a chicken nanban restaurant.
南蛮炸鸡是诞生于宫崎县的鸡肉料理。: Chicken nanban is a chicken dish that was born in Miyazaki Prefecture.
把油炸过的鸡肉浸到酸甜的汁里。: Deep-fried chicken is dipped in a sweet and sour sauce.
再在上面浇上满满的白色塔塔酱来吃。: It's eaten with plenty of white tartar sauce poured over the top.
咬上一口，鲜美的肉汁就从里面流了出来。: When I took a bite, delicious juices came out of the meat.
酸汁和塔塔酱非常搭，让人一口接一口地扒米饭。: The sour sauce and the tartar sauce went really well together, and I kept eating more and more rice.
现在全国的便当店和便利店里也能见到，但在宫崎吃到的味道格外特别。: These days you can also find it at bento shops and convenience stores all over Japan, but the taste I had in Miyazaki was special.
回到东京后，我想在家里试着做，正在查做法。: Since coming back to Tokyo, I've been looking up how to make it, thinking I'll try making it at home.
富山县有名的车站便当之一，是“鳟鱼寿司”。: One of the famous ekiben (station bento) of Toyama Prefecture is "masuzushi."
鳟鱼寿司是用一种叫鳟鱼的鱼和醋饭做的寿司。: Masuzushi is sushi made with a fish called masu (trout) and vinegared rice.
在又圆又扁的木盒里铺上绿色的竹叶，再在上面叠放醋饭和鳟鱼。: Green bamboo leaves are laid in a round, flat wooden container, and vinegared rice and trout are layered on top.
因为是从上面压制而成，所以属于“押寿司”的一种。: Since it is made by pressing from above, it is a type of "oshizushi" (pressed sushi).
吃的时候打开竹叶，就能看到漂亮的粉红色鳟鱼。: When you open the bamboo leaves to eat it, you can see the beautiful pink trout.
因为是圆的，所以要像切蛋糕一样用刀切开来吃。: Because it's round, you cut it into pieces with a knife, like a cake, and eat it.
带着竹叶的清香，和醋饭的味道也非常搭。: It has the pleasant scent of bamboo leaves, and the flavor goes well with the vinegared rice.
有机会去富山的话，请一定在电车上尝一尝。: If you ever have the chance to go to Toyama, be sure to try eating it on the train.
车站便当: ekiben, boxed meal sold at train stations
三重县伊势市有一座叫伊势神宫的古老而宏大的神社。: In Ise City in Mie Prefecture, there is a large, ancient shrine called Ise Jingu.
在那一带自古就有人吃的，就是“伊势乌冬”。: What people around there have eaten since long ago is "Ise udon."
伊势乌冬的面非常粗，软得让人吃惊。: Ise udon noodles are very thick and surprisingly soft.
几乎没有汤，而是把黑色浓稠的酱汁拌在面上吃。: There's almost no broth; you coat the noodles in a dark, thick sauce and eat them.
看到这黑色，会觉得好像很咸。: Looking at the dark color, you'd think it would be very salty.
可尝一口就会发现，味道比想象的甜，很柔和。: But when you try it, it's sweeter than you'd expect and has a gentle flavor.
面之所以这么软，是因为煮了很长时间。: The noodles are soft because they are boiled for a long time.
也有一种说法，说是为了让从远方步行来参拜的人即使累了也容易入口，才把面做得这么软: There is also a story that they were made soft so that people who had walked from far away to visit the shrine could eat them easily even when tired.
参拜: visiting (a shrine or temple) to pray
星期天，四个朋友聚到了我的房间。: On Sunday, four friends gathered at my apartment.
因为大家说好了一起包饺子。: We had decided to make gyoza together.
把肉馅、卷心菜和韭菜切碎，充分拌匀。: We finely chopped ground meat, cabbage and garlic chives and mixed them well.
然后用皮包起来，可这一步还真不容易。: Then we wrapped the filling in the skins, but this was pretty difficult.
从中国来的小林包得又快又漂亮。: Lin, who came from China, wraps them very quickly and neatly.
她告诉我们：“在中国，春节时一家人会一起包饺子哦。”: She told us, "In China, families make dumplings together at Chinese New Year."
在日本煎饺比较常见，但听说在中国更常吃水饺。: In Japan, pan-fried gyoza are more common, but in China, boiled dumplings are apparently eaten more often.
于是我们决定一半煎、一半煮，两种都尝尝。: So we decided to pan-fry half and boil half, and try both.
虽然形状五花八门，但自己包的饺子好吃极了。: The shapes were all over the place, but the gyoza we made ourselves were the best ever.
兵库县姬路市有一座洁白美丽的姬路城。: In Himeji City, Hyogo Prefecture, stands the white and beautiful Himeji Castle.
白色的墙壁和屋顶看起来像展翅的白鸟，所以它也被称为“白鹭城”。: Its white walls and roofs look like a white bird spreading its wings, so it is also called "Shirasagi-jo" (White Egret Castle).
现在的天守阁是四百多年前建造的。: The castle keep that stands today was built more than four hundred years ago.
历经战争和地震，它都没有损毁，一直保存了下来。: Through wars and earthquakes, it survived without being destroyed.
1993年，它与法隆寺等一起，成为日本第一批世界遗产。: In 1993, together with Horyu-ji and other sites, it became one of Japan's first World Heritage Sites.
天守阁里的楼梯非常陡。: Inside the keep, the stairs are very steep.
要脱掉鞋子，扶着扶手慢慢往上爬。: You take off your shoes and climb slowly, holding on to the handrail.
爬到最高处，姬路的街景一览无余。: When you climb to the very top, you get a good view of the city of Himeji.
春天，城的周围开满樱花，显得更加美丽。: In spring, lots of cherry trees bloom around the castle, making it even more beautiful.
伏见稻荷的红色隧道: The red tunnel of Fushimi Inari
京都的伏见稻荷大社以排列着许多红色鸟居而闻名。: Fushimi Inari Taisha in Kyoto is famous for its many rows of red torii gates.
鸟居一座紧挨着一座，宛如一条红色的隧道。: The torii continue one after another without gaps, just like a red tunnel.
据说这些鸟居是个人或公司为了答谢愿望实现等而供奉给神社的。: These torii were apparently offered to the shrine by people and companies, for example as thanks for wishes that came true.
另外，在这里随处可以看到狐狸像。: Also, here you can see statues of foxes all over the place.
因为人们认为狐狸是神的使者。: Foxes are believed to be messengers of the gods.
鸟居之路一直延伸到神社后面的山顶。: The path of torii continues up to the top of the mountain behind the shrine.
全部走一圈，大约要两个小时。: Going all the way around takes about two hours.
早上早点去的话人少，能拍到安静的照片哦。: If you go early in the morning, there are fewer people, and you can take peaceful photos.
拜托了，晴天娃娃: A wish to the teru teru bozu
明天是我盼了好久的郊游日。: Tomorrow is the day of the school outing I've been looking forward to.
可是天气预报说“明天会下雨”。: But the weather forecast said, "Tomorrow will probably be rainy."
于是，我决定和妹妹一起做晴天娃娃。: So I decided to make a teru teru bozu with my little sister.
把白纸巾揉成团当脑袋，用另一张纸巾包住，再用绳子系紧。: We roll up white tissue into a ball for the head, wrap it in another tissue, and tie it with string.
妹妹用笔画上了一张笑脸。: My sister drew a smiling face on it with a pen.
晴天娃娃是希望天晴时挂在窗边的人偶。: A teru teru bozu is a doll that people hang by the window when they want it to be sunny.
反过来，据说倒着挂就会招来雨。: On the other hand, it is said that hanging one upside down calls the rain.
我们唱着“让明天放晴吧”的歌谣睡下了。: We sang the song that goes, "Please make tomorrow a sunny day," and then went to bed.
第二天早上拉开窗帘，天空一片晴朗湛蓝。: The next morning, when I opened the curtains, the sky was clear and blue.
给达摩画上眼睛: Painting the eyes on a daruma
达摩是一种红色、圆滚滚的人偶。: A daruma is a red, round doll.
因为底部比较重，就算推倒了也会马上站起来。: Its bottom is weighted, so even if you knock it over, it immediately rights itself.
因此它寓意着“无论失败多少次都会重新振作”，被认为很吉利。: For that reason, it is said to be lucky, standing for "no matter how many times you fail, you keep trying."
群马县高崎市是以制作达摩而闻名的城市。: Takasaki City in Gunma Prefecture is a town famous for making daruma.
刚买来的达摩是没有画眼睛的。: A newly bought daruma doesn't have its eyes painted in.
许愿时，先画上一只眼睛。: When you make a wish, you first paint in one eye.
等愿望实现了，再把另一只眼睛画上。: Then, when the wish comes true, you paint in the other eye.
很多人应该都在电视上见过选举获胜者给达摩画眼睛的情景吧。: Many people have probably seen someone who won an election painting the eye on a daruma on TV.
站起来: to get up, to stand back up
暑假去爷爷家时，他第一次教我下将棋。: When I went to my grandfather's house during summer vacation, he taught me shogi for the first time.
将棋是两个人在纵横各九格的棋盘上对战的游戏。: Shogi is a game for two players, played on a board with nine squares across and nine down.
棋子有八种，每种的走法都不一样。: There are eight kinds of pieces, and each moves in a different way.
先吃掉对方“王”的一方获胜。: The player who captures the opponent's "king" wins.
和国际象棋最大的不同，是吃掉的棋子可以当作自己的棋子来用。: The big difference from chess is that you can use the pieces you capture as your own.
吃来的棋子之后可以摆到棋盘上，让它重新参战。: Captured pieces can later be placed on the board and made to fight again.
爷爷说：“所以啊，不到最后都不能放弃。”: My grandfather said, "That's why you must never give up until the very end."
我还一次都没赢过，但想在明年夏天前好好练习，赢爷爷一回。: I haven't won even once yet, but I want to practice by next summer and beat my grandfather.
在东京的车站坐电车，关门前会响起一小段音乐。: When you take a train at a station in Tokyo, a short piece of music plays before the doors close.
以前大多用铃声，但铃声又响又刺耳，有人听了会觉得害怕。: In the past, bells were common, but because they were loud and harsh, some people found them frightening.
于是，使用柔和音乐的车站就多了起来。: So more and more stations started using gentle music.
有的车站还会把和当地有关的歌曲做成发车旋律。: Some stations use songs connected to their town as the melody.
比如，东京的高田马场站会播放动画《铁臂阿童木》的主题曲。: For example, at Takadanobaba Station in Tokyo, the song from the anime "Astro Boy" plays.
因为创作阿童木漫画的作者的公司就在这里。: This is because the company of the man who drew the Astro Boy manga is in this neighborhood.
听到旋律响起时，不要硬挤上车，等下一班吧。: When you hear the melody, don't force your way onto the train; wait for the next one.
播放；流动: to be played (of music); to flow
日本的车站和人行道上，铺着一种黄色、凹凸不平的砖。: At stations and on sidewalks in Japan, there are yellow bumpy blocks.
这叫“盲道砖”，是为视力有障碍的人准备的。: These are called "tenji blocks" (tactile paving), and they are for people who are visually impaired.
盲道砖诞生于日本。: Tactile paving was born in Japan.
据说它是1967年在冈山县的道路上首次铺设的。: It was apparently first installed on a road in Okayama Prefecture in 1967.
盲道砖有两种。: There are two kinds of blocks.
排列着线条的，表示“请朝这个方向前进”。: Blocks with rows of lines mean "Please proceed in this direction."
排列着圆点的，表示“请停下，注意”。: Blocks with rows of dots mean "Stop and be careful."
之所以多用黄色，是因为这个颜色对还有一点视力的人来说也容易辨认。: They are mostly yellow because it's a color that's easy to see even for people with some vision.
请不要把自行车或行李放在盲道砖上。: Let's make sure not to leave bicycles or bags on the blocks.
“都”是东京都，“道”是北海道，都各只有一个。: The 「都」 (to) is Tokyo-to, and the 「道」 (do) is Hokkaido; there is only one of each.
“府”是大阪府和京都府两个，剩下的43个是“县”。: There are two 「府」 (fu), Osaka-fu and Kyoto-fu, and the remaining 43 are 「県」 (ken).
面积最大的是北海道，最小的是香川县。: The largest is Hokkaido, and the smallest is Kagawa Prefecture.
北海道非常大，想开车全部转一遍的话，要花好几天。: Hokkaido is so big that if you try to drive all the way around it, it takes many days.
日本的孩子们在小学里学习都道府县的名称和位置。: Japanese children learn the names and locations of the prefectures in elementary school.
看县的形状猜名字的问答游戏，大人小孩都很喜欢。: Quizzes where you guess a prefecture's name from its shape are popular with both children and adults.
喜欢旅行的人当中，也有人把走遍所有都道府县当作目标。: Among people who love to travel, some have made it their goal to visit every prefecture.
乒乓球部的夏天: Summer in the table tennis club
上了初中，我加入了乒乓球部。: When I started junior high, I joined the table tennis club.
因为从小学起，我就喜欢在电视上看乒乓球比赛。: That's because I had liked watching table tennis matches on TV since I was in elementary school.
可是刚入部的时候，前辈们都不让我碰球。: But when I had just joined, they wouldn't let me hit the ball.
每天只是跑步、练习挥拍。: Every day, all we did was run and practice swinging our paddles.
进入暑假后，我终于可以和前辈对打了。: When summer vacation started, I was finally able to rally with the older members.
体育馆里非常热，可一开窗，球就会被风吹偏。: It's very hot inside the gym, but if you open the windows, the wind makes the ball curve.
所以再热也得关着窗练习。: So we practice with the windows closed, even when it's hot.
在夏末的比赛中，我第一次赢了比赛。: At the tournament at the end of summer, I won a match for the first time.
前辈们对我说“干得好”，我高兴极了。: The older members said, "Well done," and I was really happy.
拐弯；弯曲: to turn (a corner); to bend, to curve
爸爸是少年棒球队的教练: My dad, the youth baseball coach
我爸爸周末在附近的少年棒球队当教练。: On weekends, my father coaches a youth baseball team in our neighborhood.
队里有从小学一年级到六年级的二十个左右的孩子。: The team has about twenty children, from first to sixth grade.
爸爸是公司职员，当教练是不拿报酬的志愿工作。: My father is an office worker, and coaching is unpaid volunteer work.
一到星期六早上，爸爸就比平时起得早，出门去球场。: When Saturday morning comes, my father gets up earlier than usual and heads out to the field.
爸爸常对孩子们说的是：“要好好打招呼，要爱惜器材。”: What my father often tells the children is, "Greet people properly and take good care of your equipment."
听说比起赢球的时候，输了以后他反而会讲得更多。: He apparently talks to them more after they lose a game than when they win.
上个月，以前队里的一个孩子上了高中，特地来看望他。: Last month, a kid from his old team, now in high school, came by to say hello.
那时爸爸的表情，是我见过最开心的。: My father's face at that moment looked happier than I had ever seen it.
重要；爱惜: important; to value, to take good care of
受朋友邀请，我第一次去玩了抱石。: A friend invited me, and I went bouldering for the first time.
抱石是一种不用绳索、攀爬较矮岩壁的运动。: Bouldering is a sport in which you climb low walls without using ropes.
墙上装着各种颜色和形状的岩点。: The walls have holds of various colors and shapes attached to them.
只用同一种颜色的岩点爬到顶，就算成功。: If you can climb to the top using only holds of the same color, you've succeeded.
下面铺着厚厚的垫子，掉下来也没关系。: There are thick mats below, so it's fine even if you fall.
一开始我想只靠手臂的力量往上爬，很快就累了。: At first, I tried to climb using only the strength of my arms and quickly got tired.
店员告诉我：“请多用脚。”: The staff told me, "Please use your legs more."
试着用脚把身体往上推，爬起来比之前轻松多了。: When I tried pushing my body up with my legs, I could climb more easily than before.
第二天胳膊疼得连筷子都拿不稳，但我还想再去。: The next day, my arms hurt so much that it was hard even to hold chopsticks, but I want to go again.
想当漫画家的弟弟: My little brother who wants to be a manga artist
上小学五年级的弟弟，梦想是当漫画家。: My little brother, who is in fifth grade, dreams of becoming a manga artist.
他一放学回家，就马上坐到书桌前画漫画。: As soon as he gets home from school, he sits down at his desk and starts drawing manga.
主人公是一只会飞的狗。: The main character is a dog that can fly.
弟弟每周都在笔记本上画八页。: Every week, my brother draws eight pages in his notebook.
有一天，弟弟对我说“你读读看”，把笔记本递给了我。: One day, my brother handed me his notebook and said, "Read it."
老实说，他的画还不算好。: To be honest, his drawings aren't very good yet.
但故事很有趣，看到最后我忍不住笑出了声。: But the story was interesting, and by the end I couldn't help laughing.
我一问“后续什么时候能看到？”，弟弟就露出了特别开心的表情。: When I asked, "When can I read what happens next?" my brother looked really happy.
现在，我是弟弟漫画的第一个读者。: Now I'm the very first reader of my brother's manga.
从时代剧里学来的日语: The Japanese I learned from period dramas
刚开始学日语的时候，我特别喜欢看时代剧。: When I first started studying Japanese, I loved jidaigeki (period dramas).
时代剧是以有武士的古代日本为背景的电视剧。: Jidaigeki are dramas set in old Japan, in the days of the samurai.
每晚看着看着，我就把武士的说话方式全学会了。: As I watched them every night, I completely picked up the way samurai talk.
那是我来日本后第一次参加打工面试时的事。: This happened when I had my first interview for a part-time job after coming to Japan.
我本想对店长说“谢谢您”，结果说成了武士腔的“不胜感激”。: I meant to say 「ありがとうございます」 ("thank you very much") to the manager, but instead I said 「かたじけない」 ("I am much obliged").
而且，我还把自己称作“在下”。: What's more, I referred to myself as 「拙者」 ("this humble one").
店长愣了一下，接着放声大笑。: The manager looked a little surprised, then burst out laughing.
他说“挺有意思，录用了！”，我就这样在那家店工作了。: The manager said, "You're funny, so you're hired!" and that's how I came to work at that shop.
现在店里的人都叫我“武士先生”。: Now everyone at the shop calls me "Samurai-san."
爸爸总说自己是“钓鱼高手”。: My father calls himself a "fishing expert."
星期天早上，爸爸说着“今天我钓条大鱼回来，晚饭就吃鱼”，出门了。: On Sunday morning, my father went out, saying, "I'm going to catch a big fish today, so we're having fish for dinner!"
妈妈和我没抱什么期待，就这么等着。: My mother and I waited without expecting much.
傍晚，爸爸满脸高兴地拎着一条大鱼回来了。: In the evening, my father came home looking pleased, carrying a big fish.
“怎么样，厉害吧！”爸爸挺起了胸膛。: "How about that? Pretty amazing, huh?" my father said, puffing out his chest.
妈妈盯着鱼看了一会儿，然后平静地说：: My mother stared at the fish for a moment, and then she spoke quietly.
“孩子他爸，这条鱼是在海里游的吧？”: "Honey, this fish was swimming in the sea, right?"
“那它身上怎么贴着超市的价签呢？”: "Then why does it have a supermarket price sticker on it?"
姐姐从上个月开始减肥。: My older sister has been on a diet since last month.
她说“夏天之前要瘦三公斤”，每天早上都去跑步。: Saying, "I'm going to lose three kilos by summer," she runs every morning.
听说她还决定不吃甜食了。: She has apparently decided not to eat sweets either.
有一天，妈妈从朋友那里拿回来一个蛋糕盒。: One day, my mother brought home a box of cake she had gotten from a friend.
盒子里装着一个又大又圆的草莓蛋糕。: Inside the box was one big, round strawberry cake.
第二天我放学回家，盒子里已经什么都没有了。: The next day, when I came home from school, there was nothing in the box.
我问：“姐姐，你把蛋糕吃了吧？减肥呢？”姐姐不慌不忙地回答：: When I asked, "Sis, you ate the cake, didn't you? What about your diet?" my sister answered calmly.
确实，蛋糕从一开始就只有一个。: True enough, there had only been one cake from the start.
镇定: to calm down, to be composed
我每天早上经过的车站里，放着一架谁都可以弹的钢琴。: At the station I use every morning, there is a piano that anyone can play.
平时多是学生在弹流行歌曲。: Usually, it's mostly students playing popular songs.
一个下雨的早晨，一位老爷爷坐在钢琴前。: One rainy morning, an elderly man was sitting at the piano.
老爷爷慢慢地弹起了一首老歌。: He slowly began to play an old song.
匆匆赶路的人们一个接一个地停下脚步，静静地听着。: People who had been hurrying stopped one after another to listen to the music.
弹完后，老爷爷小声说：“这是我妻子生前喜欢的歌。”: When he finished playing, he said in a small voice, "This was a song my wife loved."
于是，周围的人们响起了温暖的掌声。: Then warm applause broke out from the people around him.
那天我上班稍微迟到了，却一整天都怀着温柔的心情。: I was a little late for work that day, but I was able to stay in a gentle mood all day long.
停下脚步: to stop (walking), to stop in one's tracks
我家附近住着一位和导盲犬一起生活的田中阿姨。: In my neighborhood, there is a woman named Tanaka who lives with a guide dog.
导盲犬叫花花，是一只棕色的温顺的狗。: The guide dog's name is Hana, and she is a gentle brown dog.
为了让田中阿姨安全行走，花花会在台阶和拐角处停下来提醒她。: Hana stops at steps and corners to let Tanaka know, so that she can walk safely.
小时候，我看到花花，忍不住想去摸它。: When I was little, I saw Hana and, without thinking, tried to pet her.
这时，田中阿姨温和地告诉我：: Then Tanaka kindly explained to me.
“花花现在正在工作呢。所以不要摸它，也不要叫它哦。”: "Hana is working right now. So please don't touch her or call her, okay?"
导盲犬在工作时如果有人跟它打招呼，就会分心。: If someone talks to a guide dog while it's working, it gets distracted.
不过去她家玩的时候，花花会摇着尾巴陪我玩。: Instead, when I go to their house to play, Hana wags her tail and plays with me.
工作时的花花和在家时的花花，我都非常喜欢。: Hana at work and Hana at home: I love her both ways.
小学老师的放学后: An elementary school teacher's after-school hours
我在小学教三年级的一个班。: I teach a third-grade class at an elementary school.
放学后，孩子们虽然回家了，老师还有很多工作没做完。: After school, even when the children have gone home, there is still a lot of work left for the teacher.
首先，把大家交上来的作业一份一份看过，写上简短的评语。: First, I go through the homework everyone handed in one by one and write short comments.
然后和其他老师开会，商量下个月运动会的事。: Then I have a meeting with the other teachers to discuss next month's sports day.
第二天的备课也必须在这段时间完成。: I also have to prepare for the next day's lessons during this time.
工作虽然辛苦，但也有开心的事。: The work is hard, but there are happy moments too.
今天翻开作业本，上面写着“老师，一直以来谢谢您”。: Today, when I opened a homework notebook, it said, "Thanks for everything, Sensei."
虽然很累，但因为这一句话又打起了精神。: I was tired, but those few words lifted my spirits.
剩下: to remain, to be left over
养老院的一天: A day at a nursing home
我在养老院工作快五年了。: I've been working at a nursing care facility for almost five years now.
院里住着很多八十岁以上的老人。: Many elderly people over 80 live at the facility.
早上帮老人们起床、换衣服、洗脸。: In the morning, I help the elderly residents get up, get dressed and wash their faces.
吃饭时，有时会根据每个人的情况，把食物切成方便入口的大小。: At mealtimes, I sometimes cut the food into easy-to-eat sizes to suit each person.
下午大家一起唱歌，做简单的体操。: In the afternoon, we all sing songs together and do simple exercises.
我觉得这份工作最重要的是倾听。: I think the most important thing in this job is listening.
讲起往事的时候，大家的表情都特别好。: When they talk about the old days, everyone's face lights up.
我非常喜欢听他们讲这些。: I love listening to their stories.
护理；照护: nursing; care (for the elderly or disabled)
我在车站附近的一家酒店做前台工作。: I work at the front desk of a hotel near the station.
一到下午三点，办理入住的客人就接连到来。: When it turns 3 p.m., guests checking in arrive one after another.
确认姓名，交给房间钥匙，再说明早餐的时间和地点。: I confirm their names, hand them their room keys, and explain the time and place for breakfast.
最近外国客人多，所以用英语交流的时候也多了。: Lately there have been many guests from abroad, so I speak English more often.
客人会问各种各样的问题。: Guests ask me all kinds of questions.
被问到“附近有好吃的店吗”，我就在地图上做好标记递给他们。: When I'm asked, "Is there a good restaurant nearby?" I mark it on a map and hand it to them.
有一天，一位客人退房时对我说：“那家店太棒了。”: One day, a guest said to me as they were leaving, "That restaurant was the best."
虽然是小事，但这样的话最让我开心。: It's a small thing, but words like that make me happiest.
我是一名带外国游客游览日本的导游翻译。: I am a guide-interpreter who shows foreign travelers around Japan.
今天和从美国来的一家四口在镰仓走了一整天。: Today I spent the whole day walking around Kamakura with a family of four from the United States.
在大佛前，我用英语讲解了它是什么时候、为什么建造的。: In front of the Great Buddha, I explained in English when and why it was made.
因为其中一个孩子对荞麦过敏，所以午饭选了乌冬面店。: One of the children has a soba allergy, so for lunch I chose an udon restaurant.
导游的工作不只是讲解。: A guide's job isn't just explaining things.
要随时留意客人有没有累了。: I always keep a careful eye on whether my clients are getting tired.
下雨的话就改变计划，带他们去有屋顶的地方。: If it rains, I change the plan and take them to places with a roof over them.
分别时，孩子们说“还想再来日本”。: When we said goodbye, the children told me, "We want to come to Japan again."
向导；带路: guiding, showing around; leading the way
我住的公寓里有一位管理员田中先生。: The apartment building where I live has a manager named Tanaka.
田中先生每天早上八点来，先打扫入口和楼梯。: Tanaka comes at 8 every morning and first cleans the entrance and the stairs.
到了扔垃圾的日子，他会检查有没有扔错的垃圾。: On garbage days, he checks whether any garbage has been put out incorrectly.
灯泡坏了或门坏了的时候，只要跟田中先生说一声，他马上就会修好。: When a light bulb burns out or a door breaks, too, he fixes it right away if you tell him.
上周我把房门钥匙弄丢了，非常着急。: Last week, I lost the key to my apartment and was really at a loss.
田中先生和我一起找，结果在自行车停放处找到了钥匙。: Tanaka helped me look for it, and the key turned up in the bicycle parking area.
看到田中先生笑着说“太好了”，我莫名地安下心来。: Seeing Tanaka smile and say, "Well, that's good," I somehow felt reassured.
在学校供餐中心工作的妈妈: My mother at the school lunch center
我妈妈在镇上的学校供餐中心工作。: My mother works at the town's school lunch center.
供餐中心为附近几所小学和初中做午饭。: The school lunch center makes lunches for several elementary and junior high schools nearby.
妈妈每天一早就出门，洗切大量的蔬菜。: My mother leaves home early every morning and washes and cuts lots of vegetables.
大锅里的菜要用大铲子双手搅拌。: The food in the big pots is stirred with both hands, using a large spatula.
有时还要为过敏的孩子另做饭菜。: Sometimes separate dishes are also made for children with allergies.
有一天，我们学校的午饭里有妈妈做的咖喱。: One day, curry that my mother had made was served for lunch at my school.
朋友说“今天的咖喱真好吃”，我有点想炫耀了。: My friend said, "Today's curry is really good," and I felt a little like bragging.
不过因为不好意思，我什么也没说，全吃光了。: But I was too embarrassed, so I ate it all without saying anything.
车站前的小自行车店是一位老爷爷一个人开的。: The small bicycle shop in front of the station is run by an old man all by himself.
店门口总是排着等待修理的自行车。: In front of the shop, there is always a row of bicycles waiting to be repaired.
补胎、调整刹车是主要工作。: His main work is fixing flat tires and adjusting brakes.
据说老爷爷只要听听自行车的声音，就知道哪里出了毛病。: They say the old man can tell what's wrong with a bicycle just by listening to the sound it makes.
高中时，我每天骑自行车上学。: When I was in high school, I rode my bicycle to school every day.
有一天早上车胎爆了，正发愁时，老爷爷马上帮我修好了。: One morning, when I got a flat tire and didn't know what to do, the old man fixed it for me right away.
他对我说“钱回来的时候给就行，快去吧”，我就急忙赶去了学校。: He told me, "You can pay on your way home. Now hurry along," so I rushed off to school.
现在每次路过那家店，我都会和老爷爷打招呼。: Even now, whenever I pass that shop, I say hello to the old man.
往返；上（学）: to go back and forth, to commute; to attend (school)
在日本，很多孩子放学后去上兴趣班。: In Japan, many children take lessons after school.
受欢迎的有游泳、钢琴、英语、书法等。: Popular ones include swimming, piano, English, and calligraphy.
我女儿上小学二年级，星期一学游泳，星期四学钢琴。: My daughter is in second grade, and she goes to swimming on Mondays and piano on Thursdays.
一开始她不会游，每周都在泳池前哭。: At first she couldn't swim, and she cried in front of the pool every week.
但是老师教得很耐心，她渐渐喜欢上了水。: But her teacher taught her gently, so she gradually came to like the water.
上个月她第一次游完25米时，全家人都很高兴。: Last month, when she swam 25 meters for the first time, the whole family was overjoyed.
最近女儿说“还想学跳舞”。: Lately, my daughter has been saying, "I want to take dance lessons too."
她开开心心的固然好，但我有点担心她每天会不会太忙。: It's good that she seems to be enjoying herself, but I'm a little worried that her days might get too busy.
兴趣班；才艺课: after-school lessons; lessons in an art or skill
在日本的很多学校，学生自己打扫教室。: At many schools in Japan, students clean their classrooms themselves.
午休之后，每天都有打扫时间。: Every day, there is cleaning time after the lunch break.
先把桌子全部搬到后面，再用扫帚扫地，用抹布擦。: First the students carry all the desks to the back, and then they sweep the floor with brooms and wipe it with rags.
走廊、楼梯和厕所也由各小组轮流打扫。: Groups also take turns cleaning the hallways, stairs, and restrooms.
来我们学校的留学生迈克一开始非常吃惊。: Mike, an international student who came to my school, was very surprised at first.
据说在迈克的国家，打扫是学校工作人员的工作。: Apparently, in Mike's country, cleaning is the job of the people who work at the school.
但过了一段时间，他变得比谁都先拿起抹布。: But after a while, he started picking up a rag before anyone else.
迈克说：“自己打扫过后，就不想把教室弄脏了呢。”: "When you clean it yourself, you don't want to get the classroom dirty anymore," says Mike.
上周六，我第一次去了车站前的献血室。: Last Saturday, I went to the blood donation room in front of the station for the first time.
在前台写下名字后，回答了关于身体状况的问题。: After writing my name at the reception desk, I answered questions about my physical condition.
之后量了血压，又抽了一点血化验。: After that, they measured my blood pressure and took a small amount of blood to test it.
因为没有问题，终于开始献血了。: There were no problems, so at last the blood donation began.
扎针的时候有点害怕，但没有想象中疼。: I was a little scared when the needle went in, but it didn't hurt as much as I had expected.
结束后，工作人员让我别马上走，先休息一会儿。: When it was over, I was told not to leave right away but to rest for a while.
休息区有饮料，其他人也在安静地看书。: There were drinks in the rest area, and other people were quietly reading books there too.
想到自己的血能帮到别人，心里莫名地高兴起来。: When I thought that my blood would help someone, I somehow felt happy.
刺；扎: to stab, to pierce; to prick (with a needle)
有用: to be useful, to be helpful
我上初三，每周三次去车站附近的补习班。: I'm in my third year of junior high school, and I go to a cram school near the station three times a week.
放学后在家匆匆吃完晚饭，从七点学到九点。: After school, I quickly eat dinner at home and then study from 7 to 9.
补习班老师讲得非常好，学校里没弄懂的地方也能听明白。: The cram school teachers are very good at explaining, so I can understand even the parts I didn't get at school.
班上还有其他初中的学生，我交到了好朋友。: There are also students from other junior high schools in my class, and I've made some good friends.
回家时已经很晚了，所以爸爸开车来接我。: It's late at night when I go home, so my father comes to pick me up in the car.
在车里，爸爸总是只问一句“累了吗”。: In the car, all my father ever asks is, "Tired?"
虽然不怎么说话，但我喜欢那段短短的时间。: We don't talk much, but I like that short time together.
我希望明年春天考上想去的高中，让爸爸高兴。: Next spring, I want to get into the high school I want to go to and make my father happy.
爸爸闪了腰: My father throws out his back
星期天早上，爸爸在院子里搬起沉重的花盆时，“啊”地大叫了一声。: On Sunday morning, as my father lifted a heavy flowerpot in the garden, he let out a loud "Ah!"
他就那样动不了了，妈妈和我把他扶进了屋里。: He couldn't move after that, so my mother and I carried him into the house.
第二天去骨科看了，医生说是闪了腰。: The next day, he was examined at an orthopedic clinic and told that he had thrown out his back.
医生说：“不要勉强，一点一点地活动。”: The doctor said, "Don't push yourself, and move a little at a time."
之后的好几天，爸爸只能慢慢地走路。: For several days after that, my father could only walk slowly.
连穿袜子都很难，每天早上都要妈妈帮忙。: Even putting on socks was hard, so my mother helped him every morning.
现在已经好了，但他搬重东西之前一定会先弯膝盖。: He has recovered now, but he always bends his knees before lifting anything heavy.
爸爸也一遍遍地对我说：“要爱护腰啊。”: My father tells me over and over, too, "Take care of your back."
星期天早上捡垃圾: Picking up litter on Sunday mornings
我们镇上每个月第一个星期日早上，都有在公园捡垃圾的活动。: In my town, there is a litter pickup in the park on the morning of the first Sunday of every month.
谁都可以参加，劳保手套和垃圾袋由町内会准备。: Anyone can take part, and the neighborhood association provides work gloves and garbage bags.
我从去年开始和上小学的儿子一起参加。: Since last year, I have been taking part with my son, who is in elementary school.
除了塑料瓶和空罐，地上还有很多烟头。: Besides plastic bottles and empty cans, there are also lots of cigarette butts lying around.
一开始，儿子不满地说：“为什么要捡别人的垃圾？”: At first, my son seemed unhappy, asking, "Why are we picking up other people's trash?"
但看到小孩子们在变干净的公园里开心地玩耍，他的想法好像变了。: But seeing little children happily playing in the cleaned-up park seems to have changed his mind.
现在他放学路上看到垃圾也会捡回来。: Now, even on his way home from school, he picks up any trash he finds and brings it back.
我开始记账了: I started keeping a household budget
从春天开始一个人住后，我发现钱很快就花光了。: After I started living on my own this spring, I noticed that my money runs out quickly.
于是我决定用手机应用记账。: So I decided to keep a budget using an app on my smartphone.
买完东西只要拍下小票，就会自动记录。: When I buy something, I just take a photo of the receipt, and the app records it automatically.
到了月底一看，在便利店花的钱比想象的多，吓了一跳。: When I looked at it at the end of the month, I was surprised that I had spent more at convenience stores than I thought.
每天的饮料和零食因为便宜，我一直没太在意。: Because the drinks and snacks I bought every day were cheap, I hadn't paid much attention to them.
从那以后，我开始用水壶装茶带着。: Since then, I've made a habit of filling a water bottle with tea and taking it with me.
虽然是小事，坚持下来后，下个月就剩下了一点钱。: It's a small thing, but by keeping it up, I had a little money left over the next month.
我打算用剩下的钱买一直想要的书。: I plan to use the leftover money to buy a book I've wanted for a long time.
一到冬天，我就把奶奶给我织的红围巾拿出来。: When winter comes, I take out the red scarf my grandmother knitted for me.
那是我上初中时生日收到的礼物。: It's something I got for my birthday when I was in junior high school.
那时候的我觉得手织围巾很土。: Back then, I thought hand-knitted scarves were old-fashioned.
所以收到后也几乎没用过，一直收在衣柜里。: So even after I got it, I hardly ever used it and kept it put away in my dresser.
那是我上了大学、开始一个人住在东京后的第一个冬天。: It was my first winter after starting college and beginning to live on my own in Tokyo.
妈妈寄来的包裹里，放着那条围巾。: That scarf was in a package my mother sent me.
围在脖子上，非常暖和，还有奶奶家的味道。: When I wrapped it around my neck, it was very warm and smelled like my grandmother's house.
今年冬天，我打算请奶奶教我织法。: This winter, I plan to have my grandmother teach me how to knit.
今年四月，我成了上班族。: This April, I joined the workforce.
四月底领到第一份工资时，我一直在想该怎么用。: When I received my first paycheck at the end of April, I spent a long time thinking about how to use it.
听说朋友们买了自己想要的衣服和包。: My friends apparently bought clothes and bags they had wanted.
但我决定给父母送点什么。: But I decided to give my parents something.
周末我回到老家，带父母去了附近的餐厅。: On the weekend, I went back to my parents' home and took them to a nearby restaurant.
爸爸一边说着“不用勉强的”，一边比平时说了更多的话。: My father said, "You didn't have to go to all this trouble," but he talked more than usual.
妈妈把餐厅的小票好好地收进了钱包。: My mother carefully put the restaurant receipt away in her wallet.
后来听说，那张小票现在还贴在冰箱上。: I heard later that the receipt is still stuck on their refrigerator.
参加工作的人: working adult, member of the workforce
爸爸最后一天上班: My father's last day at work
爸爸在同一家公司工作了38年。: My father worked at the same company for 38 years.
上个月65岁生日那天，他从公司退休了。: Last month, on his 65th birthday, he retired from the company.
最后一天，爸爸在和平常一样的时间起床，系上和平常一样的领带出了门。: On his last day, my father got up at the usual time, put on the same tie as always, and left for work.
晚上，爸爸抱着一大束花回来了。: In the evening, my father came home with a big bouquet of flowers.
说着“公司的大家送的”，爸爸的眼睛有点红了。: "Everyone at work gave them to me," my father said, his eyes a little red.
妈妈把花插进花瓶，摆在桌子正中间。: My mother put the flowers in a vase and set them in the middle of the table.
我们说着“这么多年辛苦了”，举杯庆祝。: We said, "Thank you for all your hard work all these years," and raised a toast.
第二天早上，爸爸似乎有点落寞，慢慢地看着报纸。: The next morning, my father was slowly reading the newspaper, looking a little lonely.
我的名字写作“空”，读作“sora”。: My name is written 「空」 and read 「そら」.
上小学时，有个作业是回家问家人自己名字的由来。: When I was in elementary school, we had a homework assignment to ask our families where our names came from.
我问了妈妈，她说我出生那天，天空蓝得一片云也没有。: When I asked my mother, she said that on the day I was born, the sky was very blue, without a single cloud.
爸爸是希望我成为一个像天空一样心胸宽广的人，才给我取了这个名字。: She said my father gave me this name because he thought, "I want this child to grow up to have a heart as big as the sky."
说实话，小时候我不太喜欢这个又短又过于简单的名字。: To be honest, when I was a child, I didn't really like my name because it was short and too simple.
但听了那番话后，我开始有点喜欢自己的名字了。: But after hearing that story, I came to like my name a little more.
现在，晴天抬头看天空时，我还会想起父母的话。: Even now, when I look up at the sky on a sunny day, I remember my parents' words.
我有一个比我大三岁的哥哥。: I have a brother who is three years older than me.
我们从小就经常吵架。: Ever since we were kids, we often fought.
吵得最多的是抢电视频道。: Most often, we fought over the TV channel.
有一天晚上，哥哥想看的节目和我想看的动画在同一个时间。: One night, the show my brother wanted to watch and the anime I wanted to watch were on at the same time.
我们抢遥控器，我竟然咬了哥哥的胳膊。: We fought over the remote, and I ended up biting my brother's arm.
哥哥很生气，但没有向妈妈告状，默默地回了房间。: My brother got angry, but instead of telling on me to our mother, he went to his room without a word.
第二周，哥哥把自己的节目录了下来，让我看动画。: The next week, my brother recorded his show and let me watch my anime.
长大成人的现在，我明白了那时的哥哥是多么温柔。: Now that I'm an adult, I understand how kind my brother was back then.
想回国的那个夜晚: The night I wanted to go home
来日本后的第一个冬天，我突然非常想回国。: During my first winter in Japan, I suddenly wanted to go back to my home country.
那是我打工出了错、被店长批评的那天。: It was on a day when I made a mistake at my part-time job and was scolded by the manager.
回到房间也没心情开灯，就在黑暗中一直坐着。: Even after I got back to my room, I didn't feel like turning on the light, and I just sat there in the dark for a long time.
这时，妈妈打来了视频电话。: Just then, I got a video call from my mother.
屏幕里的妈妈正在做我爱吃的菜。: On the screen, my mother was in the middle of cooking my favorite dish.
被问到“有好好吃饭吗？”，我的眼泪止不住了。: When she asked, "Are you eating properly?" my tears wouldn't stop.
妈妈什么也没问，慢慢地给我讲那道菜的做法。: Without asking me anything, my mother slowly explained how to make the dish.
第二天，我在超市买了材料，试着做了同样的菜。: The next day, I bought the ingredients at the supermarket and tried making the same dish.
每天早上给我让座的高中生: The high school student who gave up his seat for me every morning
大二那年冬天，我滑雪时摔断了腿骨。: In the winter of my second year of college, I broke my leg skiing.
有一段时间，我不得不拄着拐杖去上学。: For a while, I had to go to college on crutches.
早上的电车非常挤，站着很难受。: The morning trains were very crowded, and standing was hard.
有天早上，一个穿着校服的高中生说了声“请坐”，把座位让给了我。: One morning, a high school student in uniform said, "Please, take my seat," and gave it up for me.
第二天、第三天，同一个高中生都在同一节车厢里。: The next day, and the day after that, the same high school student was in the same car.
我一上车，他什么也不说，马上就站起来。: Whenever I got on, he would stand up right away without saying a word.
腿好的那天，我递给他小点心和一封信，向他道谢。: On the day my leg had healed, I gave him some small sweets and a letter and thanked him.
高中生不好意思地笑了笑，在下一站下了车。: The student smiled shyly and got off at the next station.
寄宿家庭的最后一个早上: The last morning of my homestay
暑假期间，我在北海道的一户人家寄宿。: During summer vacation, I did a homestay with a family in Hokkaido.
这家有爸爸、妈妈和上小学的悠树三口人。: The family has three members: the father, the mother, and Yuki, who is in elementary school.
悠树每天都教我日本的游戏。: Every day, Yuki taught me Japanese games.
回国那天早上，悠树没有从房间里出来。: On the morning of the day I was going back to my country, Yuki didn't come out of his room.
妈妈叫他，他也只说“不去”。: Even when his mother called him, all he said was, "I'm not going."
正要坐上去机场的车时，悠树跑过来，给了我一张画。: Just as I was about to get into the car to go to the airport, Yuki came running and gave me a picture.
画上是我们俩手拉着手，还用大大的字写着“还要再来哦”。: On it was a drawing of two people holding hands, and in big letters it said, "Come back again!"
小学一年级的时候，我每周都要去医院。: When I was in first grade, I went to the hospital every week.
医院候诊室人很多，总得等很长时间。: The hospital waiting room was crowded, and I always had to wait a long time.
我觉得无聊，总是在妈妈身边哭。: I was bored and did nothing but cry next to my mother.
有一天，坐在旁边的一位老奶奶用折纸给我折了一只纸鹤。: One day, an old woman sitting next to me folded a paper crane for me out of origami paper.
从那以后，老奶奶每次见到我，都会给我折新的东西。: After that, every time we met, she folded something new for me.
青蛙、气球、手里剑……我学会了好几种折法。: I learned how to fold lots of things, like frogs, balloons, and shuriken (ninja throwing stars).
病好了不再去医院以后，我再也没见过那位老奶奶。: Since I got better and stopped going to the hospital, I have never seen her again.
但现在在医院看到哭泣的孩子，我还会从包里拿出折纸。: But even now, when I see a child crying at a hospital, I take some origami paper out of my bag.
每天早上买吐司的老爷爷: The old man who buys bread every morning
我在大学附近的面包店打工。: I work part-time at a bakery near my university.
每天早上七点，总有一位老爷爷来买一个吐司面包。: There is an old man who comes in at 7 every morning without fail to buy one loaf of bread.
老爷爷总是说“今天也好香啊”，笑眯眯的。: He always says, "Smells good again today," and gives a big smile.
可是有一周，老爷爷一次也没来店里。: But one week, he didn't come to the shop even once.
正担心时，下一周的星期一，老爷爷带着有点消瘦的面容来了。: I was getting worried, but on Monday of the following week, he came in, his face looking a little thinner.
他说：“我感冒住院了。好想吃这里的面包啊。”: He said, "I was in the hospital with a cold. I really missed the bread here."
那天店长多送了他一个刚出炉的面包。: That day, the manager put in one extra piece of freshly baked bread for him free of charge.
老爷爷那声“谢谢”，听起来比平时长了一点。: The old man's "Thank you" sounded a little longer than usual.
吐司面包: loaf of white bread, sliced bread
爷爷家的仓库里有一辆很旧的黑色自行车。: In the storage shed at my grandfather's house, there is a very old black bicycle.
据说爷爷年轻时骑着这辆车给镇上的人家送牛奶。: I hear that when he was young, my grandfather used this bicycle to deliver milk to homes in town.
去年夏天，爷爷问我：“要不要骑骑看？”: Last summer, my grandfather said to me, "Want to try riding it?"
自行车很重，刹车也不太灵。: The bicycle was heavy, and the brakes didn't work very well.
于是我和爷爷一起除锈、上油。: So my grandfather and I removed the rust and oiled it.
修好的那天，我骑着那辆车，和爷爷一起在海边的路上骑行。: On the day we finished the repairs, I rode the bicycle along a road near the sea with my grandfather.
爷爷高兴地说：“以前我每天早上都骑过这条路。”: "I used to ride along this road every morning," my grandfather said happily.
那辆自行车现在在我家，休息日我会骑。: That bicycle is now at my house, and I ride it on my days off.
分发；送: to distribute, to hand out; to deliver
四月，从巴西来的安娜转到了我们班。: In April, Ana, a girl from Brazil, transferred into my class.
安娜还不太会说日语，课间总是一个人。: Ana couldn't speak much Japanese yet, and she was always alone during breaks.
有一天，老师对大家说：“我们试着学一点安娜国家的语言吧。”: One day, our teacher said to everyone, "Let's try learning a little of the language of Ana's country."
第二天早上，我们用“Bom dia”向安娜打招呼。: The next morning, we greeted Ana with "Bom dia."
安娜吃了一惊，然后露出了我们从没见过的笑容。: Ana was surprised, and then she broke into a smile we had never seen before.
从那天起，安娜教我们葡萄牙语，我们教她日语。: From that day on, Ana taught us Portuguese, and we taught her Japanese.
现在，安娜成了班上最爱说话的人。: Now, Ana is the most talkative person in the class.
一个星期天，爸爸、妈妈和女儿三个人在客厅看电视。: One Sunday, a father, a mother, and their daughter were watching TV together in the living room.
女儿盯着爸爸的头看了一会儿，问妈妈。: The daughter stared hard at her father's head and asked her mother:
“妈妈，为什么爸爸的头发那么少？”: "Hey, Mom, why does Dad have so little hair?"
妈妈想了想，笑着回答。: Her mother thought for a moment, then smiled and answered.
“因为爸爸总是在想很多很难的事情呀。”: "Well, it's because Dad is always thinking about lots of difficult things."
爸爸满意地连连点头。: The father nodded again and again, looking pleased.
女儿想了一会儿，又问。: The daughter thought for a while and asked again:
“那为什么妈妈的头发那么多？”: "Then why do you have so much hair, Mom?"
我爷爷特别喜欢出谜语。: My grandpa loves giving people riddles.
一见面，他总是说：“先别打招呼，先猜谜。”: Whenever we meet, he always says, "Riddles before greetings!"
“同样叫‘pan’，却不能吃的‘pan’是什么？”: "What kind of パン (bread) is a パン you can't eat?"
这个很简单，答案是“平底锅（furaipan）”。: This one is easy. The answer is 「フライパン」 (a frying pan).
上次的题有点难。: Last time, he gave me a slightly harder one.
“越用越小的东西是什么？”: "What gets smaller the more you use it?"
我想了很久，也没想出来。: I thought about it for a long time, but I couldn't figure it out.
下次我打算想一道能难住爷爷的题。: Next time, I plan to come up with a riddle that will stump Grandpa.
吃掉作业的狗: The dog that ate the homework
“老师，对不起，我的作业被狗吃了。”: "I'm sorry, Teacher. The dog ate my homework."
悠太一说这话，全班都笑了。: When Yuta said this, the whole class laughed.
老师说：“这种话，谁也不会信的。”: The teacher said, "Nobody's going to believe a story like that."
悠太一脸为难，从书包里拿出了什么东西。: Yuta looked troubled and took something out of his bag.
那是一个破破烂烂、留着狗牙印的本子。: It was a tattered notebook covered in dog tooth marks.
老师吓了一跳，道歉说：“原来是真的啊，对不起。”: The teacher was startled and apologized, saying, "So it was true. I'm sorry."
“太好了。为了让狗把它吃掉，我花了整整三天呢。”: "Thank goodness. It took me three whole days to get the dog to eat it."
一位男游客边看地图边在路上走。: A male tourist was walking down the street looking at a map.
怎么也看不到车站，他就问了附近的一位老奶奶。: He just couldn't find the station anywhere, so he asked an old woman nearby.
“不好意思，顺着这条路一直走，能到车站吗？”: "Excuse me, if I go straight along this road, will I get to the station?"
老奶奶微微一笑，回答说：“嗯，能到哦。”: The old woman smiled and answered, "Yes, you will."
男人放下心来，问：“要多长时间？”: Relieved, the man asked, "How long will it take?"
老奶奶想了想，说。: The old woman thought for a moment and then said:
“这个嘛，照你现在的方向，得绕地球一圈，要花好几年吧。”: "Let me see. Going the way you're headed now, you'd have to go all the way around the earth, so it would take years."
体检之后，爸爸说：“从今天开始减肥。”: After his health checkup, my father said, "I'm going on a diet starting today."
从那天晚上开始，爸爸的晚饭就只有沙拉了。: From that evening on, my father's dinner was nothing but salad.
听说他每天早上走路去车站，也尽量不坐电梯。: He says he walks to the station every morning and tries not to use elevators either.
两周后，爸爸满怀期待地站上了体重秤。: Two weeks later, my father eagerly stepped on the scale.
可是，体重一点也没减。: But his weight hadn't gone down at all.
爸爸说：“奇怪啊。这个体重秤是不是坏了？”: My father said, "That's strange. Isn't this scale broken?"
就在那时，爸爸的包里掉出了好多零食袋。: Just then, a bunch of snack bags fell out of my father's bag.
爸爸小声说：“这个，那个，是给公司同事的。”: "These are, um, for giving to people at work," my father said in a small voice.
秋季运动会上，我们班决定参加跳大绳。: Our class was going to take part in the long jump rope event at the fall sports day.
全班同学一起连续跳一根长绳，比跳的次数。: The whole class jumps over a single long rope again and again without stopping, and classes compete on the number of jumps.
第一次练习时，连五下都没跳够。: At our first practice, we couldn't even manage five in a row.
总是在同一个地方，绳子会绊到脚。: The rope always caught on someone's feet at the same point.
于是大家商量后，决定跳的时候一起喊口号。: So we talked it over and decided to call out as we jumped.
大家齐声喊“一、二、一、二”，节奏渐渐合上了。: When we called out "One, two, one, two" together, little by little we fell into rhythm.
运动会那天，我们跳得比练习时还多，获得了年级第二名。: On sports day, we jumped more times than we had in practice and came in second in our grade.
虽然没拿到第一，但大家激动得哭了。: We didn't get first place, but we all cried with joy.
来日本第二年，我开始去附近的空手道道场。: In my second year in Japan, I started going to a karate dojo in my neighborhood.
道场里从小学生到七十多岁的人，各种各样的人都来练习。: All kinds of people come to practice at the dojo, from elementary school kids to people in their seventies.
练习前后一定要正坐，大家一起行礼。: Before and after practice, we always sit in seiza and bow together.
一开始腿麻了，怎么也站不起来。: At first my legs went numb, and I had a hard time standing up.
老师常说：“空手道不只是为了变强。”: Our teacher often says, "Karate isn't just about becoming strong."
据说还要学习尊重对手的心和忍耐的精神。: According to our teacher, we also learn respect for our opponents and a spirit of patience.
半年后，我通过了第一次考试，拿到了新的腰带。: After six months, I passed my first exam and received a new belt.
小朋友们对我说“恭喜”，我非常高兴。: The little kids said "Congratulations!" to me, and I was really happy.
正坐；跪坐: seiza (formal sitting); sitting on one's knees
我奶奶75岁了，每周去两次市民游泳馆。: My grandmother is 75, but she goes to the public pool twice a week.
她是在泳池里走路，做“水中健走”。: She does "water walking," where you walk through the water in the pool.
听说在水里身体会变轻，所以膝盖和腰疼的人也能轻松运动。: Your body becomes lighter in water, so apparently even people with sore knees or backs can exercise easily.
奶奶以前膝盖疼，不怎么出门。: My grandmother used to have sore knees and didn't go out much.
但是开始水中健走之后，她慢慢变得有精神了。: But since she started water walking, she has gradually become more energetic.
她在游泳馆还交到了朋友，结束后会一起去喝茶。: She has also made friends at the pool, and she says they go out for tea together afterward.
看到奶奶说“现在是最快乐的时候”，我也很高兴。: Seeing my grandmother say, "Now is the most fun time of my life," made me happy too.
羽毛球部的学弟: My junior in the badminton club
我上高二，参加了羽毛球部。: I'm a second-year high school student and a member of the badminton club.
今年春天，一年级的佐藤加入了我们部，我也第一次有了学弟。: This spring, a first-year student named Sato joined the club, and for the first time I had a junior of my own.
佐藤从没打过羽毛球，一开始球拍完全碰不到球。: Sato had never played badminton before, and at first he couldn't hit the shuttlecock with his racket at all.
但是他每天早上都比谁都早来体育馆，一个人练习。: But every morning, he came to the gym earlier than anyone else and practiced on his own.
我有时陪他晨练，教他击球方法。: Sometimes I joined him for his morning practice and taught him how to hit.
夏末的比赛，我和佐藤组队打双打。: At a match at the end of the summer, I teamed up with Sato in doubles.
拿下最后一分的，是佐藤的扣杀。: It was Sato's smash that won the final point.
我本以为是在教他，但感觉反而是我从佐藤身上学到了很多。: I thought I was the one teaching him, but I feel like I'm the one who learned a lot from Sato.
后辈；学弟学妹: junior (someone who started later); younger student
组队: to team up, to pair up
四格漫画是用四幅画讲一个故事的短漫画。: Four-panel manga are short comics that tell a single story in four pictures.
经常刊登在报纸和杂志上，从小孩到大人都能看得开心。: They often appear in newspapers and magazines, and everyone from children to adults can enjoy them.
很多四格漫画中，第一格故事开始，第二格接着发展。: In many four-panel manga, the story begins in the first panel and continues in the second.
第三格发生一些意外的事，第四格让读者发笑。: Something unexpected happens in the third, and the fourth makes the reader laugh.
这叫“起承转结”，也是写作文时用的思路。: This is called 「起承転結」 (introduction, development, twist, conclusion), a way of thinking that is also used in writing compositions.
为了学日语，我每天读一则四格漫画。: To study Japanese, I read one four-panel manga every day.
因为很短，就算边查词典边读，也很快就能读完。: Because they're short, I can finish one quickly even while using a dictionary.
在最后一格笑出来的时候，会觉得自己读懂了日语，很开心。: When I can laugh at the last panel, I feel like I understood the Japanese, and that makes me happy.
起承转结: introduction, development, twist, and conclusion (a classic four-part structure)
因为漫画爱上了历史: How manga made me love history
上小学时，我非常讨厌历史。: When I was in elementary school, I really hated history.
因为会出现很多人名和年号，我完全记不住。: That was because so many names of people and eras came up, and I couldn't remember any of them.
爸爸看我这样，从图书馆给我借来了历史漫画。: Seeing me like that, my father borrowed some history manga from the library for me.
在课本里只是一个名字的人物，在漫画里会笑、会生气、会烦恼。: People who had been nothing but names in my textbook were laughing, getting angry, and worrying in the manga.
我入了迷，把那套漫画读了好多遍。: I got hooked and read the series over and over.
结果，考试分数一点点提高了。: Then my test scores gradually started going up.
现在，我在初中当社会课老师。: Now I teach social studies at a junior high school.
上课时，我也时常用漫画来传达历史的乐趣。: In my classes, too, I sometimes use manga to show students how fun history is.
爸爸书架上的旧漫画: The old manga on my father's bookshelf
有一天，我在爸爸房间的书架上发现了旧漫画。: One day, I found some old manga on the bookshelf in my father's room.
纸已经有点发黄了，但封面的画非常帅。: The paper had turned a little yellow, but the cover art was really cool.
读了一下，是一个棒球打得不好的少年和队友一起变强的故事。: When I read it, it turned out to be the story of a boy who was bad at baseball and grew stronger together with his teammates.
我入了迷，当晚就全部读完了。: I got completely absorbed and read the whole thing that same night.
第二天早上，我对爸爸说“那部漫画很有意思”，爸爸很吃惊。: The next morning, when I told my father, "That manga was great," he was very surprised.
原来爸爸上初中时也读了同一部漫画，然后加入了棒球部。: It turns out that when my father was in junior high, he had read the same manga and joined the baseball team.
从那天起，我们经常聊喜欢的场景。: From that day on, we often talked about our favorite scenes.
三十年前的漫画把我和爸爸连在了一起。: A thirty-year-old manga had brought my father and me together.
在文化节上做了动画: We made an anime for the school festival
高中文化节上，我们班决定做一部短动画。: For our high school's culture festival, our class decided to make a short anime.
我们分成想故事的、画画的、配音的几组，从暑假就开始准备。: We split up into people to come up with the story, people to draw the pictures, and people to do the voices, and started preparing during summer vacation.
动画是把略有不同的画一张接一张地连续展示，看起来就像在动。: In animation, showing many slightly different pictures one after another makes them look like they're moving.
哪怕只是几秒钟的场景，也需要很多画，真的很辛苦。: Even a scene just a few seconds long needed lots of drawings, so it was really hard work.
我不擅长画画，所以负责配音。: I'm not good at drawing, so I was put in charge of voices.
因为害羞，我重新录了好多遍。: I was embarrassed and redid the recording many times.
文化节当天，教室里挤满了来看的人。: On the day of the festival, the classroom was packed with people who came to watch.
最后获得热烈掌声时，我打心底觉得大家一起做真是太好了。: When we got a big round of applause at the end, I felt from the bottom of my heart that I was glad we had made it together.
当电视剧群众演员的那天: The day I was an extra in a TV drama
上个月，我被朋友邀请，去当了电视剧的群众演员。: Last month, a friend invited me along, and I took part in a TV drama as an extra.
群众演员就是在车站走路的人、店里的客人等出现在背景里的人。: Extras are the people who appear in the background, like people walking through a station or customers in a shop.
我的角色是在咖啡店喝咖啡的客人。: My role was a customer drinking coffee in a café.
一大早集合，等了好几个小时，拍摄才终于开始。: We gathered early in the morning, and after waiting for hours, filming finally began.
前面那桌，有名的演员正一脸认真地说着台词。: At the table in front of me, a famous actor was delivering lines with a serious face.
我为了不笑出来，一直盯着杯子看。: I kept staring at my cup so that I wouldn't laugh.
同一个场景拍了好多次，我竟然喝了五杯咖啡。: They shot the same scene so many times that I ended up drinking five cups of coffee.
播出那天，我和家人一起看电视，结果画面里只有我的手。: On the day it aired, I watched it on TV with my family, but only my hand was on screen.
映现；出镜: to be reflected, to appear (in an image); to appear on screen
一部电视剧决定的工作: The job a TV drama chose for me
日本有很多以从事各种职业的人为主人公的电视剧。: In Japan, there are many TV dramas whose main characters are people with all sorts of jobs.
不只是医生和律师，还有面包师、做书的人的故事。: There are stories not only about doctors and lawyers, but also about bakers and people who make books.
我上大学时看过一部关于编词典的人的电视剧。: When I was in college, I watched a drama about people who make dictionaries.
为了写一个词的释义要思考好几天的场景，让我非常感动。: I was very moved by a scene where they spent days thinking in order to write the definition of a single word.
以那部剧为契机，我开始想在出版社工作。: That drama is what made me want to work at a publishing company.
现在我在一家小出版社做查找书中错误的工作。: Now I work at a small publishing company, looking for errors in books.
虽然没有像剧里那样帅气的场面，但我每天都在努力。: There aren't many cool moments like in the drama, but I do my best every day.
我想，要是哪天我的工作也能拍成电视剧就好了。: I hope that someday my job will be made into a drama too.
寻找: to look for, to search for
校园剧和真实的高中: School dramas and real high school
在中国的时候，我非常喜欢日本的校园剧。: When I was in China, I loved Japanese school dramas.
我一直很向往在天台吃便当、放学后努力参加社团活动的场景。: I had always longed for scenes like eating bento on the school rooftop and working hard at club activities after school.
高二时，我通过交换留学去日本的高中读了一年。: In my second year of high school, I got to attend a Japanese high school for a year as an exchange student.
我非常期待会不会有和剧里一样的事。: I was really looking forward to seeing whether things would be the same as in the dramas.
可是第一天，我想去天台时，门上着锁。: But on the first day, when I tried to go up to the roof, the door was locked.
问了朋友，朋友说：“天台很危险，很多学校都不让进哦。”: When I asked a friend about it, I was told, "Rooftops are dangerous, so lots of schools don't let you go up there."
我有点失望，但社团活动和剧里一样热血。: I was a little disappointed, but club activities were just as passionate as in the dramas.
加入了管乐部的我，每天和伙伴们练习小号到很晚。: I joined the concert band and practiced the trumpet with my bandmates until late every day.
交换留学: student exchange, studying abroad as an exchange student
用七草粥让肠胃歇一歇: Resting your stomach with seven-herb rice porridge
正月快结束的时候，日本有吃“七草粥”的习惯。: In Japan, around the time the New Year holidays end, there is a custom of eating "nanakusa-gayu" (seven-herb rice porridge).
就是在一月初“七草日”的早上，喝放了七种春季野菜的粥。: On the morning of the "Day of the Seven Herbs" in early January, people eat rice porridge with seven kinds of spring herbs in it.
水芹、荠菜、鼠曲草、繁缕、稻槎菜、芜菁、白萝卜这七种，被称为“春之七草”。: The seven are せり (water dropwort), なずな (shepherd's purse), ごぎょう (cudweed), はこべら (chickweed), ほとけのざ (nipplewort), すずな, and すずしろ, and they are called the "seven herbs of spring."
“すずな”就是芜菁，“すずしろ”就是白萝卜。: すずな means turnip, and すずしろ means daikon radish.
正月里，人们会吃很多大鱼大肉，还会喝酒。: At New Year's, people eat lots of rich food and drink alcohol.
之后喝上一碗味道清淡的粥，让疲惫的肠胃休息一下。: Afterward, they eat mild-tasting rice porridge to give their tired stomachs a rest.
据说还有祈求一年健康平安的含义。: It is also said to carry a wish for good health throughout the year.
