现在超市里有卖七草齐全的套装，谁都能轻松做出来。: These days, supermarkets sell sets that include all seven herbs, so anyone can make it easily.
累，疲劳: to get tired, to be fatigued
让……休息: to let (something) rest, to give a rest
“开”镜饼的日子: The day to "open" the kagami mochi
正月里，家里会摆上两个圆年糕叠在一起的“镜饼”。: At New Year's, people display "kagami mochi," two round rice cakes stacked on top of each other, in their homes.
然后在很多地方，人们会在1月11日把年糕撤下来吃掉。: Then, in many regions, people take the mochi down on January 11 and eat it.
这时年糕已经变硬了，但据说不能用菜刀切。: By then the mochi has become hard, but it is said that you must not cut it with a knife.
因为“切”这个词会让人联想到和别人的缘分断掉。: That's because the word 「切る」 (to cut) suggests your ties with other people being cut.
所以要用木槌之类的东西把它敲成小块。: So instead, people break it into small pieces by hitting it with something like a wooden mallet.
出于同样的原因，也不说“敲碎”，而是说“打开”。: For the same reason, people don't say 「割る」 (to break) either, but 「開く」 (to open).
我家会用敲开的年糕做红豆年糕汤。: In my family, we make oshiruko (sweet red bean soup) with the broken mochi.
在甜甜的红豆汤里，硬邦邦的年糕变得软软的，非常好吃。: In the sweet red beans, the hard mochi becomes soft and very delicious.
全家人一起吃着，就会生出“今年也要加油”的心情。: Eating it together as a family makes me feel like doing my best again this year.
让人联想到: to remind one of, to suggest
红豆年糕汤: oshiruko (sweet red bean soup with mochi)
关东和关西的樱饼: Sakura mochi of the east and west
一到春天，和果子店里就会摆出樱饼。: When spring comes, sakura mochi appear on display in Japanese sweet shops.
这是一种用盐渍樱花叶包着粉色年糕的点心。: They are sweets made of pink mochi wrapped in salt-pickled cherry leaves.
不过，关东和关西的樱饼外观相差很大。: But in the Kanto and Kansai regions, they look quite different.
关东的樱饼是用烤得薄薄的面皮卷着豆沙。: Kanto-style sakura mochi has sweet bean paste rolled up in a thin, pan-cooked crepe.
因为它诞生在东京向岛一座叫长命寺的寺庙附近，所以也叫“长命寺”。: Because it was created near a temple called Chomeiji in Mukojima, Tokyo, it is also called "Chomeiji."
关西的樱饼则是用颗粒分明的糯米包着豆沙。: Kansai-style sakura mochi wraps the bean paste in grainy glutinous rice.
樱花叶可以一起吃，也可以拿掉再吃。: You can eat the cherry leaf along with it or take it off before eating.
叶子微微的咸味和豆沙的甜味很搭，所以我喜欢一起吃。: I like eating them together, because the slightly salty taste of the leaf goes well with the sweetness of the bean paste.
你想尝尝哪一种樱饼呢？: Which sakura mochi would you like to try?
摆放，排列: to be lined up, to be on display
5月5日儿童节这天，有泡放了菖蒲叶的洗澡水的习俗。: On Children's Day, May 5, there is a custom of taking a bath with shobu (Japanese iris) leaves in it.
菖蒲叶细细长长的，气味很浓。: Shobu leaves are long and thin and have a strong scent.
古人认为这种气味能驱除邪祟。: People long ago believed that this scent drove away evil.
另外，“菖蒲”和“胜负”同音，所以也寄托着希望孩子长得强壮的心愿。: Also, because 「しょうぶ」 sounds the same as 「勝負」 (contest, victory or defeat), it carries the wish that children will grow up strong.
这一天，很多家庭还会吃柏饼。: Many families also eat kashiwa mochi on this day.
柏饼是用槲树叶包着豆沙馅年糕的点心。: Kashiwa mochi is a sweet made of mochi filled with bean paste and wrapped in an oak leaf.
槲树在新芽长出来之前，老叶子不会掉落。: The kashiwa oak doesn't drop its old leaves until new buds come out.
因此，人们在柏饼里寄托了家族代代相传的愿望。: That's why it carries the wish that the family line will continue from parents to children.
赶走: to drive away, to chase off
在海边看到的新年第一缕阳光: Watching the first sunrise of the year by the sea
今年元旦，我和爸爸两个人去附近的海边看新年的第一次日出。: On New Year's Day this year, my father and I went to the nearby coast to see the first sunrise of the year.
所谓“初日出”，就是一年里看到的第一次日出。: "Hatsuhinode" means the first sunrise you see in a year.
我们早上五点半出门，外面还是一片漆黑。: We left home at 5:30 in the morning, so it was still pitch-dark outside.
到了海边，发现已经聚了很多人，我吃了一惊。: When we got to the coast, I was surprised to find lots of people already gathered there.
风非常冷，手脚都冻得发疼。: The wind was so cold that my hands and feet hurt.
我捧着爸爸给我买的热可可，等着天空变亮。: Holding the hot cocoa my father had bought me, I waited for the sky to grow light.
过了一会儿，橙色的太阳从海的那边一点点升了起来。: After a while, an orange sun slowly rose from beyond the sea.
周围的人有的双手合十，有的在拍照。: The people around us were putting their hands together in prayer or taking pictures.
我也闭上眼睛，许愿今年是美好的一年。: I closed my eyes too and wished for this year to be a good one.
虽然很冷，但我明年还想再来。: It was cold, but I want to come again next year.
雪国的早晨从铲雪开始: In snow country, mornings start with shoveling snow
我从去年冬天开始住在新潟县的一个山间小镇。: Since last winter, I have been living in a mountain town in Niigata Prefecture.
这里雪非常多，有时一晚上就能积五十多厘米。: It snows a lot here, and sometimes more than 50 centimeters piles up in a single night.
早上起来，首先得把家门口的雪清走。: When I get up in the morning, the first thing I have to do is clear away the snow in front of my house.
不然车开不出去，也走不到车站。: Otherwise, I can't get my car out, and I can't even walk to the station.
一开始，用大铲子非常吃力。: At first, using a big shovel was really hard.
隔壁的老爷爷告诉我，为了不伤到腰，最好一点一点地搬雪。: The old man next door told me that, so as not to hurt my back, it's best to move the snow a little at a time.
屋顶上的雪积多了，房子可能会被压坏，所以也得铲下来。: The snow on the roof also has to be cleared off, because when it gets heavy it can damage the house.
不过屋顶上的活儿很危险，大家都叮嘱不要一个人干。: But working on the roof is dangerous, so we're told never to do it alone.
铲完雪后喝的那杯热茶，真的特别香。: A cup of hot tea after shoveling snow tastes really good.
挪开，清开: to move out of the way, to clear away
弄下来: to take down, to bring down
横手的雪屋: The kamakura snow huts of Yokote
秋田县横手市每年二月中旬都会举办一个叫“雪屋”的活动。: In Yokote, Akita Prefecture, an event called "Kamakura" is held every year in mid-February.
雪屋就像是用雪堆成的小房子。: A kamakura is something like a small house made of snow.
里面的大小能坐下好几个大人，最里面供奉着水神。: Inside, it's big enough for several adults to sit, and at the back, the god of water is enshrined.
到了晚上，雪屋里点起烛光，非常漂亮。: At night, candles are lit inside the kamakura, and they look very beautiful.
孩子们在里面招呼路过的人：“请进来吧！”: From inside, children call out to passersby, saying 「はいってたんせ」.
这是秋田方言，意思是“请进来”。: This is Akita dialect for "Please come in."
进去以后，孩子们会端出甜酒和年糕来招待。: When you go in, they serve you amazake (a sweet rice drink) and mochi.
外面明明很冷，雪屋里却比想象中暖和，据说很多人都会感到惊讶。: Even though it's cold outside, it's warmer inside a kamakura than you'd expect, and apparently many people are surprised by this.
这是雪国小城里一个让人心里暖暖的活动。: It's a heartwarming event in a snowy town.
供奉: to offer (to a deity or the spirits of the dead)
经过: to pass by, to go past
大分县有一道叫“鸡肉天妇罗”的菜。: Oita Prefecture has a dish called "toriten."
就是把鸡肉腌入味，再像天妇罗那样裹上面衣油炸。: It's chicken that is seasoned, coated in batter like tempura, and deep-fried.
它和炸鸡块很像，但面衣软软的，吃起来口感蓬松轻盈。: It's similar to karaage, but the batter is soft, and it feels light and fluffy when you eat it.
当地人说，这是把炸鸡块和天妇罗的优点合二为一的一道菜。: Local people say it's a dish that combines the best of karaage and tempura.
蘸柚子醋或黄芥末吃，是大分常见的吃法。: In Oita, the usual way to eat toriten is dipped in ponzu or hot mustard.
大分县还以鸡肉吃得多而出名。: Oita is also known as a prefecture where people eat a lot of chicken.
据说不光是餐馆，家里的晚饭和学校的营养午餐里也会出现。: Apparently it's served not only at restaurants but also at dinner at home and in school lunches.
去大分的话，泡完温泉后，请尝尝热乎乎的鸡肉天妇罗吧。: If you go to Oita, try some piping-hot toriten after a soak in a hot spring.
“开口笑”（サーターアンダギー）是冲绳自古就有的点心。: Sata andagi is a sweet that has been around in Okinawa for a long time.
在冲绳话里，“サーター”是砂糖，“アンダギー”是用油炸的东西。: In the Okinawan language, 「サーター」 means sugar, and 「アンダギー」 means something deep-fried in oil.
把面粉、砂糖和鸡蛋混在一起，团成圆球后下油锅炸。: Flour, sugar, and eggs are mixed together, rolled into balls, and deep-fried in oil.
一炸，表面就会裂开，变成像花朵绽放一样的形状。: When they're fried, the surface cracks open into a shape like a blooming flower.
据说因为这个形状，在喜庆的日子里也常常会做。: Because of this shape, they are said to be often made on days of celebration too.
它外面酥脆，里面湿润。: They're crispy on the outside and moist on the inside.
一个就很大，吃了很顶饱，当零食正合适。: Each one is big and filling, so they're perfect as a snack.
冲绳的市场和特产店里，也有卖加了黑糖或红薯的。: Markets and souvenir shops in Okinawa also sell ones made with brown sugar or sweet potato.
我去冲绳旅游时吃到刚出锅的，好吃得让我惊讶。: On a trip to Okinawa, I ate some fresh out of the fryer and was amazed at how good they were.
鹿儿岛有一种叫“白熊”的刨冰。: Kagoshima has a kind of shaved ice called "shirokuma" (white bear).
在细细的冰上浇满炼乳，再在上面放上水果和豆子。: It's finely shaved ice covered in plenty of condensed milk and topped with fruit and beans.
据说因为从上往下看，水果像一张熊脸，所以起了这个名字。: It's said that it got this name because, seen from above, the fruit looks like a bear's face.
鹿儿岛的夏天非常热，所以冰凉的甜点很受欢迎。: Summers in Kagoshima are very hot, so cold sweets are popular.
白熊不仅在食堂和咖啡馆里能吃到，还做成了杯装冰淇淋在便利店里卖。: Shirokuma isn't only served at diners and cafés; it's also sold at convenience stores as an ice cream cup.
一份分量很大，所以也有人和朋友分着吃。: One serving is big, so some people share it with friends.
炼乳柔和的甜味和水果的酸味很搭，一直吃到最后都不会腻。: The gentle sweetness of the condensed milk goes well with the tartness of the fruit, so you never get tired of it, right to the last bite.
去鹿儿岛的话，请一定在炎热的午后尝一尝。: If you go to Kagoshima, be sure to try it on a hot afternoon.
腻，厌烦: to get tired of, to be fed up with
长崎蛋糕是作为长崎名产而广为人知的点心。: Castella is a sweet known as a specialty of Nagasaki.
据说它源自四百多年前从葡萄牙来的人们带来的点心。: It is said to be based on a sweet brought over by people from Portugal more than 400 years ago.
它是用鸡蛋、砂糖、面粉和麦芽糖做的，做法看起来很简单。: It's made from eggs, sugar, flour, and starch syrup, so the recipe looks simple.
但据说要烤出松软湿润的长崎蛋糕，其实非常难。: But they say that baking castella that is fluffy and moist is very difficult.
很多长崎蛋糕底部的褐色纸上，都粘着叫做“粗砂糖”的大颗糖粒。: Many Nagasaki castellas have large grains of sugar called zarame on the bottom, against the brown paper.
一咬下去会发出沙沙的声音，这也很有意思。: When you bite into it, the grains make a crunchy sound, which is part of the fun.
推荐配着牛奶或热茶一起吃。: I recommend eating it with milk or hot tea.
长崎的特产街上，开着一家又一家长崎蛋糕店。: Nagasaki's souvenir shopping streets are lined with castella shops.
传入，传授: to introduce (from abroad), to pass on
京都有名的特产之一是“八桥饼”。: One of Kyoto's famous souvenirs is "yatsuhashi."
它是用米粉、砂糖和肉桂做成的京都传统点心。: It is a traditional Kyoto sweet made from rice flour, sugar, and cinnamon.
最早的八桥饼是一种烤得薄薄的硬点心，形状微微弯曲。: The original yatsuhashi is a hard, thinly baked sweet with a slightly curved shape.
据说这是模仿了一种叫“筝”的乐器的形状。: This is said to imitate the shape of a musical instrument called the koto.
另外，还有不烤、直接软软地吃的“生八桥”。: There is also "nama yatsuhashi," which isn't baked and is eaten soft.
用生八桥把豆沙包成三角形的那种，如今最受欢迎。: Nama yatsuhashi folded into a triangle around sweet bean paste is now the most popular kind.
店里卖着抹茶、草莓等各种口味的生八桥。: Shops sell nama yatsuhashi in many flavors, such as matcha and strawberry.
很多店可以试吃，比较一下再买也不错。: Many shops let you sample them, so it's a good idea to compare a few before buying.
岩手县盛冈市以面食好吃而闻名。: Morioka in Iwate Prefecture is known as a city with delicious noodle dishes.
尤其是小碗荞麦面、炸酱面和冷面，被称为“盛冈三大面”。: In particular, wanko soba, jajamen, and reimen are called "Morioka's three great noodles."
盛冈冷面是以朝鲜半岛的冷面为基础，在盛冈诞生的一道菜。: Morioka reimen is a dish that was born in Morioka, based on the cold noodles of the Korean Peninsula.
最有意思的是，面条非常筋道，怎么也咬不断。: The most interesting thing is that the noodles are so firm and chewy that they're hard to bite through.
冰凉的汤是用牛肉熬的高汤，口味清爽。: The cold soup is made from beef broth and has a light, refreshing taste.
上面放着泡菜、煮鸡蛋，还有时令水果。: It is topped with kimchi, a boiled egg, and seasonal fruit.
很多店可以通过泡菜的多少来选辣度，不太能吃辣的人也可以放心。: Many shops let you choose how spicy it is by the amount of kimchi, so even people who can't handle spicy food can order without worry.
炎热的夏天自不必说，据说冬天吃的人也很多。: People eat it in the hot summer, of course, but apparently many also eat it in the cold winter.
咬断: to bite through, to bite off
不擅长，怕: not good at, not good with
山口县下关市是有名的河豚之城。: Shimonoseki in Yamaguchi Prefecture is famous as a town of fugu (pufferfish).
不过，下关人常常把河豚叫做“ふく”。: But the people of Shimonoseki often call fugu 「ふく」.
因为“ふく”和“福”同音，有幸福的意思。: That's because 「ふく」 sounds the same as 「福」, which means good fortune.
河豚体内有毒，所以只有拿到特别资格的人才能处理烹调。: Fugu have poison in their bodies, so only people with a special license can prepare them.
河豚刺身切得非常薄，薄到能透过它看见盘子上的花纹。: Fugu sashimi is sliced so thin that you can see the pattern of the plate through it.
摆成花朵形状的刺身，光是看着就让人开心。: Sashimi arranged like a flower is a pleasure just to look at.
一到冬天，很多人从其他城市专程赶来吃河豚火锅。: In winter, lots of people come from other towns to eat fugu hot pot.
据说火锅吃完后，用剩下的汤加米饭煮成的杂烩粥也非常好吃。: They say the zosui, a rice porridge made by adding rice to the leftover broth after the hot pot, is delicious too.
北海道札幌有一道菜叫“汤咖喱”。: Sapporo in Hokkaido has a dish called "soup curry."
它比普通咖喱稀得多，可以像汤一样喝。: It's a curry that is thinner than regular curry, so you can drink it like soup.
里面放了很多切成大块的土豆、胡萝卜、南瓜等蔬菜。: It's full of vegetables cut into big chunks, such as potatoes, carrots, and kabocha squash.
有时还会整只鸡腿直接放在里面。: Sometimes a whole chicken leg is in it.
米饭是另外装在盘子里端上来的。: The rice is served on a separate plate.
很多人用勺子舀一勺饭，浸到汤里再吃。: Many people scoop up rice with a spoon and dip it in the soup.
很多店可以细致地选择辣度，所以爱吃辣和怕辣的人都能吃得开心。: Many shops let you choose the spice level in fine detail, so both people who love spicy food and people who can't handle it can enjoy it.
在寒冷的札幌冬天喝上一碗热汤咖喱，整个人从里到外都暖和起来。: Eating hot soup curry in Sapporo's cold winter warms you from the inside.
变暖: to warm up, to get warm
鲷鱼烧从哪儿开始吃？: Where do you start eating taiyaki?
鲷鱼烧是做成鲷鱼形状的烤点心。: Taiyaki is a baked sweet shaped like a tai, or sea bream.
里面一般包着红豆馅。: It's usually filled with red bean paste.
因为“鲷”的发音和“可喜可贺”相近，所以鲷鱼一直被当作喜庆的鱼而受人喜爱。: Because 「たい」 sounds like the word 「めでたい」 (auspicious, joyous), sea bream has long been favored as a fish for celebrations.
话说回来，鲷鱼烧是从头吃还是从尾巴吃，常常成为大家讨论的话题。: By the way, whether to eat taiyaki head first or tail first is a common topic of conversation.
我姐姐喜欢从馅料多的头部开始吃。: My older sister likes to start with the head, where there's lots of filling.
我则先吃脆脆的尾巴，把头留到最后慢慢享受。: I eat the crispy tail first and save the head as a treat for last.
爸爸是掰成两半从肚子开始吃，总被全家人笑话。: My father breaks it in two and starts from the belly, so the whole family laughs at him.
大家是从哪儿开始吃的呢？: Where do you start eating yours?
掰开: to break in two, to split
涮涮锅是把切得薄薄的肉在锅里的热水中快速涮一下再吃的料理。: Shabu-shabu is a dish in which you quickly swish thin slices of meat through hot water in a pot before eating them.
据说这个名字来自于肉在热水里涮动时的声音和样子。: It is said to have gotten its name from the sound and look of the meat as it is moved through the hot water.
肉一变色就可以吃了。: Once the meat changes color, it's ready to eat.
在热水里放太久的话肉会变老，要注意哦。: If you leave it in the water too long, the meat gets tough, so be careful.
蘸料常用的是芝麻酱和柚子醋。: Sesame sauce and ponzu are the usual dipping sauces.
芝麻酱口味浓郁，柚子醋则很清爽。: Sesame sauce is rich, and ponzu is light and refreshing.
不光是肉，白菜、葱、豆腐等也放进同一个锅里煮来吃。: Not just meat, but also napa cabbage, green onions, tofu, and so on go into the same pot.
最后用剩下的汤煮乌冬面吃，这是我家的老规矩。: In my family, the rule is to finish by putting udon into the leftover broth and eating it.
涮一下，过一下: to pass (something) through, to dip briefly
考试前一天吃猪排盖饭: Katsudon the day before an exam
下周我要参加大学入学考试。: Next week, I'm taking a university entrance exam.
今天晚饭，妈妈给我做了猪排盖饭。: Tonight, my mother made katsudon for dinner.
在日本，有人会在考试或比赛之前吃猪排盖饭或炸猪排。: In Japan, some people eat katsudon or tonkatsu before an exam or a match.
因为“かつ”这个发音和比赛“获胜”的“勝つ”一样。: That's because the sound 「かつ」 is the same as 「勝つ」, as in winning a match.
猪排盖饭是把炸猪排和洋葱一起用甜咸的酱汁煮，再浇上蛋液收汁做成的。: Katsudon is tonkatsu simmered with onions in a sweet and savory sauce and bound with egg.
盖在米饭上，酱汁渗进米饭里，特别好吃。: When it's placed on top of rice, the sauce soaks into the rice, and it's very delicious.
妈妈笑着说：“吃了这个就没问题啦。”: My mother smiled and said, "Eat this and you'll be fine."
虽然不知道是不是真的灵，但妈妈的心意让我很高兴。: I don't know whether it really works, but her thoughtfulness made me happy.
考完试以后，这次我想给妈妈做点什么。: When the exam is over, I'd like to make something for my mother this time.
渗入: to soak in, to seep in
夏天一临近，街上的中餐馆就会贴出“凉面开卖了”的告示。: As summer approaches, Chinese restaurants around town put up signs that say, "Now serving hiyashi chuka."
很多人一看到它，就会感到“啊，夏天来了”。: When they see these, many people feel, "Ah, summer is here."
中华凉面是在冰凉的中华面上，放上切成细丝的黄瓜、火腿、煎蛋等的料理。: Hiyashi chuka is a dish of cold Chinese-style noodles topped with thin strips of cucumber, ham, thin omelet, and so on.
吃的时候从上面浇上酸甜的酱汁。: A sweet and sour sauce is poured over the top before eating.
虽然名字里有“中华”二字，但据说它是在日本诞生的料理。: Even though its name includes 「中華」 (Chinese), it is said to be a dish that was born in Japan.
它颜色鲜艳，在家做的时候，琢磨怎么摆盘也是一种乐趣。: It's colorful, so when you make it at home, figuring out how to arrange the toppings is part of the fun.
据说有的地方还会加蛋黄酱一起吃。: Apparently in some regions people eat it with mayonnaise.
就算是热得没有胃口的日子，凉面也吃得下。: Even on days when it's so hot that I have no appetite, I can eat hiyashi chuka.
东西两地的乌冬汤: Udon broth in eastern and western Japan
常听人说，大阪人在东京吃乌冬面时，被汤色之黑吓了一跳。: You often hear stories of people from Osaka who ate udon in Tokyo and were shocked at how dark the broth was.
关东的汤用的是浓口酱油，所以颜色很深。: Kanto broth uses koikuchi (dark) soy sauce, so it's dark in color.
关西的汤用的是淡口酱油，所以颜色很浅。: Kansai broth uses usukuchi (light) soy sauce, so it's light in color.
不过，淡口酱油虽然颜色浅，咸味却比浓口酱油更重。: But although usukuchi soy sauce is light in color, it actually tastes saltier than koikuchi.
所以，不能光凭颜色判断味道。: So you can't judge the flavor by color alone.
关东常用鲣鱼干熬的高汤，关西则常用海带熬的高汤。: In Kanto, dashi made from katsuobushi (dried bonito) is common, while in Kansai, kombu (kelp) dashi is often used.
坐新干线旅行的时候，比较一下东西两地的乌冬面也很有趣哦。: When you travel by shinkansen, it's fun to compare the udon of the east and the west.
茶碗蒸是把鸡蛋和高汤混合，倒进带盖的碗里蒸出来的料理。: Chawanmushi is a dish made by mixing egg and dashi, pouring it into a lidded cup, and steaming it.
里面放着虾、香菇、鱼糕、白果等。: Inside are things like shrimp, shiitake mushrooms, kamaboko (fish cake), and ginkgo nuts.
它像布丁一样软，所以不用筷子，而是用勺子吃。: It's soft like pudding, so you eat it with a spoon instead of chopsticks.
我小时候第一次看到茶碗蒸，以为是甜布丁。: When I first saw chawanmushi as a child, I thought it was a sweet pudding.
可一尝，是酱油和高汤的味道，跟布丁完全不一样。: But when I tasted it, it tasted of soy sauce and dashi, completely different from pudding.
虽然吓了一跳，但我很快就喜欢上了这种温和的味道。: I was surprised, but I soon came to love its gentle flavor.
在寿司店和日料店，它常常盛在小碗里端上来。: At sushi restaurants and Japanese restaurants, it's often served in a small cup.
冷天里，热乎乎的茶碗蒸能让身体暖和起来。: On cold days, warm chawanmushi warms you up.
边走边吃的横滨中华街: Eating your way through Yokohama Chinatown
横滨中华街被认为是日本最大的中华街。: Yokohama's Chinatown is said to be the largest Chinatown in Japan.
狭窄的街道两旁，中餐馆、茶叶店、礼品店挤得满满当当。: Its narrow streets are packed with Chinese restaurants, tea shops, and souvenir shops.
据说横滨开港以后，从中国来的人们在这里定居下来，才形成了这条街。: It's said that after the port was opened, people from China came to live there, and that's how this neighborhood came to be.
上周，我和朋友两个人去了中华街。: Last week, a friend and I went to Chinatown.
午饭我们没进大餐馆，而是边走边吃店门口卖的肉包和芝麻球。: For lunch, instead of going into a big restaurant, we walked around eating pork buns and sesame balls sold in front of the shops.
街上有好几座红色和金色的牌楼，拍照也很开心。: There were several red and gold gates, and taking pictures was fun too.
一座叫关帝庙的建筑非常漂亮，让人感觉好像身在中国。: A building called the Kanteibyo Temple was very beautiful, and it made me feel like I was in China.
回去的时候，我们在附近的山下公园一边看海一边休息。: On the way back, we rested in nearby Yamashita Park while looking at the sea.
石川县金泽市有一座叫“兼六园”的大型日本庭园。: Kanazawa in Ishikawa Prefecture has a large Japanese garden called "Kenrokuen."
它与水户的偕乐园、冈山的后乐园齐名，被列为“日本三名园”之一。: Along with Kairakuen in Mito and Korakuen in Okayama, it is counted as one of the "Three Great Gardens of Japan."
园内有池塘、小桥和古树，春天的樱花和秋天的红叶都非常美。: It has ponds, bridges, old trees, and more, and both the cherry blossoms in spring and the autumn leaves in fall are very beautiful.
其中最有名的是冬天的“雪吊”。: Most famous of all is the winter "yukitsuri."
为了不让树枝被积雪压断，人们从树顶拉下许多根绳子，把树枝吊起来。: To keep the branches from breaking under the weight of the snow, many ropes are stretched from the tops of the trees to hold the branches up.
金泽的雪含水多、很沉重，所以人们自古就这样保护树木。: Snow in Kanazawa is wet and heavy, so people have protected the trees this way since long ago.
一把把伞一样的绳架在雪中排列开来，是很有金泽冬日特色的景致。: The sight of umbrella-shaped ropes lined up in the snow is a scene typical of Kanazawa in winter.
位于北海道中部的富良野，是以薰衣草闻名的小镇。: Furano, located around the middle of Hokkaido, is a town famous for lavender.
到了七月前后，平缓的山丘一片紫色。: Around July, the gently rolling hills turn completely purple.
暑假时，我和家人去富良野旅行了。: During summer vacation, I took a trip to Furano with my family.
一打开车窗，薰衣草的香味就飘了进来。: When we opened the car windows, the lovely scent of lavender drifted in.
花田附近有卖薰衣草色的冰淇淋，我们全家一起吃了。: Near the fields, they were selling lavender-colored soft serve, and we all had some.
除了薰衣草，还有红、黄、白色的花像条纹一样种在一起的花田，简直像彩虹一样。: Besides the lavender, there were also fields where red, yellow, and white flowers were planted in stripes, just like a rainbow.
北海道的夏天比东京凉爽，非常舒服。: Summer in Hokkaido is cooler than in Tokyo, and it was very comfortable.
总有一天，我也想在下雪的季节去富良野看看。: Someday, I'd like to visit Furano in the snowy season too.
栃木县日光有一座供奉德川家康的日光东照宫。: In Nikko, Tochigi Prefecture, there is Nikko Toshogu, a shrine dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu.
建筑上有许多色彩鲜艳的动物雕刻。: Its buildings have many brightly colored carvings of animals.
其中最有名的，是“不看、不说、不听”的三只猴子。: The most famous of these are the three monkeys of 「見ざる、言わざる、聞かざる」 (see no evil, speak no evil, hear no evil).
三只猴子分别用手捂着眼睛、嘴巴和耳朵。: The three are covering their eyes, mouth, and ears with their hands, respectively.
“ざる”是古语里“不……”的意思，和“猴子（さる）”构成了谐音。: 「ざる」 is old Japanese meaning 「〜ない」 (not), and it's a pun on 「さる」 (monkey).
这三只猴子出现在描绘猴子一生的八幅雕刻之中。: These three monkeys appear in a series of eight carved panels depicting the life of a monkey.
据说意思是：小时候最好不要看、不要说、不要听坏的东西。: They are said to mean that when you're a child, it's better not to see, say, or hear bad things.
东照宫里还有一个叫“眠猫”的著名雕刻，请去找找看吧。: Toshogu also has another famous carving called the "Sleeping Cat," so try to find it.
逛高山的早市: Strolling through the morning markets of Takayama
岐阜县高山市保留着古老的街景，也被称为“飞騨的小京都”。: Takayama in Gifu Prefecture still has its old streetscapes and is also called "the Little Kyoto of Hida."
这里每天早上都会在河边等地方开早市。: Every morning, morning markets are held here, by the river and in other spots.
附近的农户在这里卖刚采收的蔬菜、水果和腌菜等。: Local farmers sell freshly picked vegetables and fruit, pickles, and more.
我去的时候是秋天的早晨，摊位上摆满了苹果和蘑菇。: I went on an autumn morning, and the stalls were full of apples and mushrooms.
摊主老奶奶说“尝尝看”，给了我一点腌菜。: The old woman running one stall said, "Try some," and gave me a few pickles.
能一边聊天一边买东西，这是早市和超市不一样的乐趣。: Being able to chat while you shop is what makes a morning market more fun than a supermarket.
早市上还卖一种叫“猴宝宝”的红色娃娃。: Red dolls called "sarubobo" were also being sold at the market.
在飞騨方言里，它的意思是“猴子宝宝”，据说自古以来就被当作护身符来做。: The name means "baby monkey" in the Hida dialect, and they have apparently been made as good-luck charms since long ago.
街景: streetscape, row of houses along a street
小芥子是用木头做成的日本人偶。: Kokeshi are Japanese dolls made of wood.
它只有圆圆的头和细长的身体，没有手也没有脚。: They have just a round head and a long, slender body, with no arms or legs.
它原本是做给来东北地区泡温泉的人们的伴手礼。: They were originally made as souvenirs for people who visited hot springs in the Tohoku region.
小芥子因产地不同，脸和身体上的花纹也略有差别。: Depending on where they're made, kokeshi have slightly different faces and body patterns.
比如宫城县鸣子的小芥子，转动脑袋时会发出吱吱的声音。: For example, kokeshi from Naruko in Miyagi Prefecture squeak when you turn their heads.
用毛笔画出的脸每一个都不一样，有的看起来在笑，有的看起来很困。: The faces, painted with a brush, are each different; some look like they're smiling, and others look sleepy.
近来，它作为可爱的伴手礼，在外国人中也很受欢迎。: These days, they're also popular with people from abroad as cute souvenirs.
我的房间里也摆着一个奶奶送我的小小芥子。: In my room, too, there's a little kokeshi my grandmother gave me.
震动心底的太鼓: Taiko drums you feel in your gut
上了高中，我加入了太鼓社。: When I started high school, I joined the taiko drum club.
因为第一次听学长学姐们演奏时，鼓声一直震到肚子里，让我非常感动。: That's because when I first heard the older students perform, the sound resonated all the way into my stomach, and I was deeply moved.
最大的鼓比我还高，一敲就感觉全身都在颤动。: The biggest drum is taller than I am, and when I hit it, I feel as if my whole body is shaking.
太鼓并不是只用手来敲的。: You don't play taiko with just your arms.
要叉开双脚站稳，用全身的力量挥下鼓槌。: You stand with your feet apart and bring the drumsticks down using the strength of your whole body.
刚开始时，练完后胳膊和腿都疼，第二天连爬楼梯都很费劲。: At first, my arms and legs hurt after practice, and the next day even climbing stairs was hard.
而且是好几个人一起敲，大家的鼓点不齐的话，就不好听。: Also, since several people play together, it doesn't sound good unless everyone's beats are in sync.
在秋天的文化节上，我第一次登台演奏，赢得了热烈的掌声。: At the fall school festival, I performed on stage for the first time and got a big round of applause.
现在，为了能敲出更快的节奏，我每天都在练习。: Now I practice every day so that I can play faster rhythms.
一致，整齐: to be in unison, to be uniform
用少少的花来插花: Arranging with just a few flowers
插花是日本传统的装饰花的方法。: Ikebana is the traditional Japanese way of arranging flowers.
西式的插花常常用很多花，插得满满的不留空隙。: Western flower arrangements often use lots of flowers and leave no gaps.
与此相对，日本插花会减少花和枝条的数量，连空着的地方也很重视。: In ikebana, by contrast, the number of flowers and branches is kept small, and empty space is valued too.
我每个月两次在附近的教室学插花。: I take ikebana lessons at a nearby class twice a month.
老师常说：“请好好看看花想朝哪个方向。”: My teacher often says, "Look carefully at which way the flower wants to face."
把花和枝条插在一种叫“剑山”的、布满针的工具上，来做出造型。: You create the shape by sticking flowers and branches into a kenzan, a tool covered in many needles.
刚开始我总想把花全用上，被老师说“太多了呢”。: At first I wanted to use all the flowers, and my teacher told me, "That's too many."
现在，要不要剪掉一根枝条，我都会考虑很久。: Now I find myself spending a long time deciding whether or not to cut a branch.
插花的时候，心会变得非常平静。: While I'm arranging flowers, my mind becomes very calm.
在神社参拜的方法: How to pray at a shrine
去神社时，要先在鸟居前轻轻鞠一躬再进去。: When you visit a shrine, first bow lightly in front of the torii gate before going in.
据说参道的正中间是神明走的路，所以最好稍微靠边走。: The middle of the approach is said to be the path the gods walk on, so it's best to walk a little to the side.
参拜前，有一处洗手漱口的水池，要在那里把手和嘴洗干净。: Before praying, you'll find a water basin for washing your hands and mouth, so you purify your hands and mouth there.
往香油钱箱里投了钱之后，摇响铃铛。: After putting money in the offering box, ring the bell.
然后深深鞠躬两次，拍手两次。: Then bow deeply twice and clap your hands twice.
双手合十，在心里许愿。: With your palms still pressed together, make your wish silently.
这是大多数神社的做法，不过也有像出云大社那样拍手四次的神社。: This is the way it's done at most shrines, but there are also shrines like Izumo Taisha where you clap four times.
在寺庙里是不拍手的，注意别弄错了。: At Buddhist temples you don't clap, so be careful not to mix them up.
参拜道: approach to a shrine or temple
香油钱: monetary offering (at a shrine or temple)
手巾的多种用法: The many uses of the tenugui
手巾是用棉布做成的又薄又长的布。: A tenugui is a thin, long, narrow piece of cotton cloth.
自古以来，日本人就用它来擦手擦身体。: Since long ago, Japanese people have used it to dry their hands and bodies.
和毛巾相比，它很薄，干得快，这是它的好处。: Compared with a towel, it's thin, so one of its good points is that it dries quickly.
而且两端没有缝边，所以从那里也更容易干。: Also, the ends aren't hemmed, which helps it dry even faster.
手巾不只能擦东西，还有各种各样的用途。: Tenugui can be used for all sorts of things, not just for wiping.
可以缠在头上挡汗，可以包便当，还可以挂在墙上当装饰。: You can wrap one around your head to keep sweat out of your eyes, wrap a bento in it, or hang it on the wall as decoration.
夏天用水打湿后围在脖子上，非常凉快。: In summer, if you wet it with water and wrap it around your neck, it feels very cool.
还有很多应季图案的手巾，春天的樱花、秋天的红叶图案都很受欢迎。: There are also many tenugui with seasonal designs; cherry blossom patterns are popular in spring, and maple leaf patterns in autumn.
我每次去旅行，都会买当地的手巾收集起来。: Whenever I travel, I buy a tenugui from that town for my collection.
穿和服时，最需要注意的是衣襟的叠法。: When you put on a kimono, the thing you have to be most careful about is how you overlap the collar.
和服要先把自己右侧的衣片贴在身上，再把左侧的衣片叠在上面。: With a kimono, you first place the side that is on your right against your body, and then lay the left side over it.
因为先合右侧，所以这叫做“右衽”。: Because the right side goes on first, this is called "migimae."
反过来的“左衽”，是给去世的人穿和服时的穿法。: The opposite, "hidarimae," is the way a kimono is put on a person who has died.
所以，活着的人穿成左衽，是被视为不可以的。: That's why wearing a kimono hidarimae is considered something living people must never do.
不管男女，和服都同样是右衽来穿。: Men and women alike wear kimono migimae.
据说可以这样记：右手能顺势伸进衣襟里的样子就是对的。: A handy way to remember it is that it's correct if your right hand can slip easily inside the collar.
穿浴衣时也一样，夏日祭之前请确认一下吧。: The same goes for yukata, so check before going to a summer festival.
贴上: to put against, to place on
日本的地图上有很多表示建筑和地点的小标记。: Japanese maps have lots of little marks that stand for buildings and places.
比如，学校用“文”字表示，神社用鸟居的形状表示。: For example, a school is shown with the character 「文」, and a shrine with the shape of a torii gate.
寺庙用“卍”这个符号表示。: A Buddhist temple is shown with the symbol 「卍」.
这是佛教自古以来使用的标志。: This is a sign that has long been used in Buddhism.
地图符号里，也有一些是根据小学生和中学生的创意设计的。: Some map symbols came from ideas by elementary and junior high school students.
养老院的符号是在房子的形状里画了一根拐杖，是孩子们想出来的。: The symbol for a nursing home, a cane drawn inside the shape of a house, was thought up by children.
另外，为了让外国人也容易看懂，还设计了用床的形状来表示酒店的符号。: Also, to make maps easier for visitors from abroad to understand, a symbol showing a hotel as a bed was created.
看懂了地图符号，看陌生城市的地图也会变得有趣起来。: Once you understand map symbols, looking at maps of unfamiliar towns becomes more fun.
在日本，纪年的时候除了公历，还会用“年号”。: In Japan, when counting years, people use not only the Western calendar but also "era names."
现在的年号是“令和”，从2019年开始。: The current era name is "Reiwa," which began in 2019.
在那之前是平成，再之前是昭和。: Before that it was Heisei, and before that, Showa.
政府机关和银行的表格上，常常有要用年号填写出生年份的地方。: Forms at government offices and banks often have a space where you write your birth year using the era name.
比如2000年出生的人，就是“平成12年生”。: For example, someone born in 2000 was "born in Heisei 12."
据说留学生有时会因为不知道自己的出生年用年号怎么算而发愁。: International students apparently sometimes have trouble because they don't know what their birth year is in the era system.
“令和”这个词，取自被称为日本最古老诗歌集的《万叶集》。: The word "Reiwa" was taken from the "Man'yoshu," said to be Japan's oldest collection of poems.
以前的年号都是从中国古籍里取词，从日本典籍中取词这还是第一次。: Earlier era names had taken their words from old Chinese books, so this was the first time one was taken from a Japanese book.
汉字的两种读法: The two ways of reading kanji
日语的汉字有“音读”和“训读”两种读法。: Kanji in Japanese have two kinds of readings: 「音読み」 (on'yomi) and 「訓読み」 (kun'yomi).
音读是以古时汉字从中国传来时的发音为基础的读法。: On'yomi are readings based on the pronunciation the kanji had when they came over from China long ago.
训读是用日本原有的词语来对应汉字意思的读法。: Kun'yomi are readings that match a kanji's meaning with a word that already existed in Japanese.
比如“山”，音读读作“サン”，训读读作“やま”。: For example, 「山」 is read 「サン」 in on'yomi and 「やま」 in kun'yomi.
对说中文的人来说，有些音读和中文发音很像，比较好记。: For people who speak Chinese, on'yomi are sometimes similar to Chinese pronunciation and easy to remember.
不过一个汉字往往有好几种读法，刚开始学会很辛苦。: But a single kanji can have several readings, so it's tough at first.
比如“生”这个字，就有“せい”“しょう”“いきる”“うまれる”等很多读法。: The kanji 「生」 has many readings, such as 「せい」, 「しょう」, 「いきる」, and 「うまれる」.
两个以上汉字组成的词多用音读，单独一个汉字时则多用训读。: Words made of two or more kanji are often read with on'yomi, while a kanji on its own is often read with kun'yomi.
多读，一个词一个词地记，才是最好的捷径。: Reading a lot and learning words one at a time is the best shortcut.
传来: to be introduced, to be passed down
日本最大的湖和最长的河: Japan's biggest lake and longest river
日本最大的湖是位于滋贺县的琵琶湖。: The largest lake in Japan is Lake Biwa in Shiga Prefecture.
看滋贺县的地图，中间很大一块都是湖。: If you look at a map of Shiga Prefecture, a large part in the middle is the lake.
琵琶湖的水支撑着京都、大阪等地许许多多人的生活。: Water from Lake Biwa supports the lives of many people in places like Kyoto and Osaka.
因此，琵琶湖有时被称为“近畿的水缸”。: For this reason, Lake Biwa is sometimes called "the water jar of Kinki."
最长的河是信浓川。: The longest river is the Shinano River.
它从长野县流到新潟县，注入日本海。: It flows from Nagano Prefecture into Niigata Prefecture and empties into the Sea of Japan.
有意思的是，这条河在长野县被叫做“千曲川”，是另一个名字。: Interestingly, in Nagano Prefecture this river goes by a different name, the "Chikuma River."
信浓川流经的新潟，多亏了这条河的水，出产大量好吃的大米。: Thanks to the water of the Shinano River, which flows through it, Niigata produces lots of delicious rice.
天气预报里常用“间或”这个词，比如“晴间或有雨”。: In weather forecasts, the word 「時々」 (now and then) is often used, as in 「晴れ時々雨」 (sunny with occasional rain).
和“间或”很像的词，还有“一时”。: A word very similar to 「時々」 is 「一時」 (for a time).
两个词听起来差不多，其实意思不一样。: They sound like they mean the same thing, but they actually have different meanings.
“一时”是说雨等会连续下，但时间不到预报时段的四分之一。: 「一時」 means that rain or the like falls continuously, but for less than a quarter of the whole forecast period.
“间或”是说雨等时下时停，下的时间加起来不到一半。: 「時々」 means that rain or the like starts and stops, and the total time it falls adds up to less than half the period.
所以，预报说“一时有雨”的日子，往往是在短时间内集中下一阵雨。: So on days with a forecast of 「一時」, the rain often comes all at once in a short period.
预报说“间或有雨”的日子，雨会下了停、停了又下好几次。: On days with a forecast of 「時々」, the rain starts and stops many times.
不管是哪种，出门时带上伞都更放心。: Either way, it's safer to take an umbrella when you go out.
弄懂了天气预报用语的意思，安排一天的计划就更容易了。: Once you understand the words used in weather forecasts, it becomes easier to plan your day.

上世纪90年代末，日本的手机为了让短短的文字也能传达心情而创造了它，这就是绘文字: They began in the late 1990s, when they were created for Japanese cell phones so that feelings could come across even in short messages.
后来，全世界的智能手机都能用了。: Later, they became available on smartphones all over the world.
如今在英语里，也直接使用“emoji”这个日语词。: Now the Japanese word "emoji" is used as is, even in English.
不过，因国家和人的不同，同一个表情也可能被理解成不同的意思。: However, depending on the country or the person, the same emoji can be taken to mean different things.
使用时考虑对方会怎么想，也很重要。: It's also important to think about how the other person will feel when you use them.
当我觉得光有文字会显得冷淡时，就会加上一个表情。: When words alone might seem cold, I try to add an emoji.

晚上回到家，可不能忘了给电池充电。: When you get home at night, you mustn't forget to charge the battery.

它利用的是摩擦时产生的热量。: These make use of the heat produced by rubbing.
这种笔的墨水被设计成温度超过60度左右时，颜色就看不见了。: The ink in these pens is designed so that its color becomes invisible at temperatures above about 60°C.
所以，不用橡胶擦，用吹风机的热风吹一吹，字也会消失。: So instead of rubbing it with the rubber, you can also make the writing disappear by blowing hot air on it with a hair dryer.
反过来，放在非常寒冷的地方，消失的字有时又会显现出来。: Conversely, if you put it somewhere very cold, the erased writing can sometimes come back.
如果把本子放在夏天闷热的车里，字也可能会消失，要注意哦。: If you leave a notebook in a hot car in summer, the writing may disappear, so be careful.

写错了也能马上改，所以我每天学习时都在用。: Even if I make a mistake, I can fix it right away, so I use one every day when I study.
