不过，我们在上面放了很多草莓。: But we put lots of strawberries on top.
晚上，妈妈看到蛋糕，说：“哇，好开心！”: In the evening, our mother saw the cake and said, "Wow, I'm so happy!"
妈妈的眼里还含着一点泪水。: There were a few tears in her eyes.
虽然样子有点怪，但那是一个非常好吃的蛋糕。: It was a strange shape, but it was a very delicious cake.
日本的便当里，经常会放玉子烧。: Japanese bento often have tamagoyaki in them.
玉子烧是把鸡蛋煎好后，一圈一圈卷起来的菜。: Tamagoyaki is a dish made by cooking egg and rolling it up round and round.
星期天，我第一次做了玉子烧。: On Sunday, I made tamagoyaki for the first time.
我用了三个鸡蛋，放了一点糖。: I used three eggs and added a little sugar.
用方形的平底锅煎成薄薄的一层，再卷起来。: You cook a thin layer in a square frying pan and roll it up.
可是，要卷得漂亮真难。: But rolling it up nicely was difficult.
做好的玉子烧，样子不太好看。: The tamagoyaki I made didn't have a very nice shape.
不过甜甜的，非常好吃。: But it was sweet and very delicious.
下次我想做得更漂亮。: Next time, I want to make it look nicer.
炎热的夏天，有一样东西大家经常吃。: There's something people often eat on hot summer days.
把冰刨得细细的，上面浇上甜甜的糖浆。: You shave ice into fine flakes and pour sweet syrup over the top.
糖浆有草莓、蜜瓜、柠檬等各种口味。: The syrup comes in lots of flavors, such as strawberry, melon, and lemon.
我总是吃草莓味的。: I always have the strawberry flavor.
弟弟喜欢蜜瓜味的。: My little brother likes the melon flavor.
吃完刨冰后，弟弟的舌头就变成了绿色。: After eating shaved ice, my little brother's tongue turns green.
我们俩互相伸舌头给对方看，总是笑个不停。: The two of us show each other our tongues and always laugh.
广岛县有一种很有名的点心，叫“红叶馒头”。: Hiroshima Prefecture has a famous sweet called 「もみじまんじゅう」 (momiji manju).
它的形状和枫叶一模一样。: It's shaped just like a maple leaf.
里面包着甜甜的豆沙馅。: Inside, there is sweet red bean paste.
现在也有奶油馅和巧克力馅的。: Now there are also ones filled with cream or chocolate.
去年秋天，我和家人去了广岛的宫岛。: Last fall, my family and I went to Miyajima in Hiroshima.
宫岛有一座立在海里的大鸟居。: On Miyajima, there is a big torii gate that stands in the sea.
山上的红叶也非常美。: The maple leaves on the mountain were also very beautiful.
我们在店里吃了热乎乎的红叶馒头。: At a shop, we ate warm momiji manju.
我们还买了很多当伴手礼。: We also bought lots of them as souvenirs.
北海道是位于日本北部的一个大岛。: Hokkaido is a large island in the north of Japan.
北海道盛产土豆。: A lot of potatoes are grown in Hokkaido.
日本的土豆大多产自北海道。: Most of Japan's potatoes come from Hokkaido.
在北海道，“黄油土豆”很有名。: In Hokkaido, 「じゃがバター」 (jaga-butter, potatoes with butter) is famous.
在热乎乎的土豆上放上黄油来吃。: You put butter on a hot potato and eat it.
北海道有很多奶牛，黄油也很好吃。: There are a lot of cows in Hokkaido, and the butter is delicious too.
去年夏天，我在札幌吃了黄油土豆。: Last summer, I ate jaga-butter in Sapporo.
虽然是很简单的一道菜，但真的很好吃。: It's a simple dish, but it was really delicious.
出产，收获: to be produced, to be harvested
我爸爸是车站附近一家西餐厅的厨师。: My father is a cook at a restaurant near the station.
爸爸的店里做汉堡肉饼、蛋包饭之类的菜。: At my father's restaurant, they make dishes like hamburg steak and omurice.
爸爸每天早上九点去店里。: My father goes to the restaurant at nine every morning.
午饭时间，客人特别多。: At lunchtime, there are a lot of customers.
爸爸晚上十点左右才回家。: My father comes home at around ten at night.
所以，工作日我们不和爸爸一起吃晚饭。: So on weekdays, we don't eat dinner with him.
不过，店里休息的星期三，爸爸会在家做饭。: But on Wednesdays, when the restaurant is closed, my father cooks at home.
爸爸做的蛋包饭，和店里的味道一模一样。: My father's omurice tastes the same as at the restaurant.
我最喜欢星期三的晚饭了。: I like Wednesday dinners the best.
我妈妈是医院的护士。: My mother is a nurse at a hospital.
护士的工作有白班，也有夜班。: Nursing work includes day shifts and night shifts.
妈妈一周大约有两次在医院上夜班。: My mother works at the hospital at night about twice a week.
上夜班的日子，她早上九点左右才回家。: On days when she works the night shift, she comes home at around nine in the morning.
夜班之后，妈妈总是非常累。: After the night shift, my mother is very tired.
星期六早上妈妈下班回来时，我和哥哥会给她做早饭。: When my mother comes home on Saturday morning, my older brother and I make breakfast.
妈妈说“谢谢，真好吃”，然后一直睡到中午。: My mother says, "Thank you, this is delicious," and then she sleeps until noon.
护士的工作很辛苦。: Being a nurse is hard work.
可是，妈妈总是说：“我想帮助生病的人。”: But my mother always says, "I want to help people who are sick."
我非常喜欢这样的妈妈。: I really love my mother for being that way.
有用，帮上忙: to be useful, to be of help
我在商店街开鱼店。: I run a fish shop in a shopping street.
每天早上四点起床，去市场进鱼。: I get up at four every morning and go to the market to buy fish.
最重要的是要有挑好鱼的眼光。: The most important thing is having an eye for good fish.
六点左右回到店里，把鱼整整齐齐地摆好。: I come back to the shop at around six and lay out the fish neatly.
然后，十点开门营业。: Then I open the shop at ten.
客人大多是住在附近的人。: Many of my customers are people who live nearby.
我会告诉他们当天好吃的鱼，以及怎么做。: I tell them which fish are good that day and how to cook them.
有时候，客人会对我说：“上次的鱼很好吃哦。”: Sometimes, a customer says, "The fish I bought last time was delicious."
上周六，我和朋友去了水族馆。: Last Saturday, I went to the aquarium with a friend.
坐电车花了一个小时左右。: It took about an hour by train.
水族馆就在海边。: The aquarium is by the sea.
入口处有一个巨大的水箱。: There was a big tank at the entrance.
里面有很多鱼在游来游去。: Lots of fish were swimming inside it.
最有意思的是海豚表演。: The most fun part was the dolphin show.
海豚高高跃起，碰到了空中的球。: The dolphins jumped high and touched a ball.
坐在前排的人被溅了一身水。: The people in the front seats got splashed with water and got wet.
我们坐在后排，所以没事。: We were in the back seats, so we were fine.
回去的时候，我买了一个企鹅毛绒玩偶。: On the way home, I bought a stuffed penguin.
春假时，我和家人去大阪旅行了。: During spring break, my family took a trip to Osaka.
我们先去看了大阪城。: First, we went to see Osaka Castle.
大阪城是很久以前丰臣秀吉建造的著名城堡。: Osaka Castle is a famous castle that Toyotomi Hideyoshi built long ago.
城的周围有一个很大的公园。: Around the castle, there is a large park.
在城里，我们看了很多古代的东西。: Inside the castle, we saw lots of old things.
从最上面能清楚地看到大阪的街景。: From the very top, we could see the city of Osaka clearly.
可是，爸爸怕高。: But my father doesn't like high places.
所以，爸爸马上就下去了。: So he went back down right away.
晚饭，大家一起吃了章鱼烧。: For dinner, we all ate takoyaki.
我从四月开始加入了学校的网球部。: In April, I joined the school tennis club.
网球我是第一次打。: It's my first time playing tennis.
最初的一个月，我根本没有打球。: For the first month, I didn't hit any balls.
每天就是跑步、捡球。: Every day, I did things like running and picking up balls.
到了五月，终于可以用球拍打球了。: In May, I finally hit the ball with a racket.
可是，球怎么也打不出去。: But the ball just won't go forward.
学长教我说：“要好好看着球。”: An older club member taught me, "Watch the ball carefully."
现在我一点一点地在进步。: Now I'm getting better little by little.
我想参加夏天的比赛。: I want to play in the summer tournament.
会飞的猫的漫画: A manga about a flying cat
我的梦想是当漫画家。: My dream is to be a manga artist.
从上小学的时候起，我每天都在画漫画。: I have been drawing manga every day since I was in elementary school.
主人公是一只会在天上飞的猫。: The main character is a cat that flies through the sky.
画漫画非常花时间。: Drawing manga takes a lot of time.
有时候一页就要画三个小时。: Some days, one page takes three hours.
上周，我第一次画完了一部二十页的漫画。: Last week, I finished a twenty-page manga for the first time.
我拿给班上的朋友们看了。: I showed it to my friends in class.
大家都说：“好想看后续！”: Everyone said, "I want to read what happens next!"
我弟弟特别喜欢警察题材的电视剧。: My little brother loves police dramas.
每周四晚上，他都和爸爸一起看。: Every Thursday night, he watches it with our father.
主人公是一个很帅的警察。: The main character is a cool police officer.
主人公总是在最后说：“犯人就在我们当中！”: At the end, the main character always says, "The culprit is among us!"
有一天，冰箱里的布丁不见了。: One day, the pudding in the fridge disappeared.
弟弟站到全家人面前，说：: My little brother stood in front of the family and said,
大家都看向弟弟的嘴边。: Everyone looked at the area around my little brother's mouth.
那里还沾着一点布丁。: There was a little pudding stuck there.
我是从中国来的留学生。: I'm an international student from China.
我用打工挣的钱买了一台新电脑。: I bought a new computer with money from my part-time job.
以后我就用电脑写日语报告了。: From now on, I'm going to write my reports in Japanese on the computer.
写日语的时候，在键盘上打罗马字。: When I write in Japanese, I type romaji on the keyboard.
比如，用罗马字打“nihongo”，就会变成“にほんご”。: For example, if you type "nihongo" in romaji, it becomes 「にほんご」.
然后按下空格键，就会变成“日本語”这几个汉字。: Then, when you press the space bar, it turns into the kanji 「日本語」.
这和中文的打字方法有点像。: It's a little like the way Chinese is typed.
一开始我打得很慢，现在能打得很快了。: I was slow at first, but now I can type fast.
四月，我从大阪转学到了东京的学校。: In April, I came from Osaka to a school in Tokyo.
班上一个认识的人都没有。: I didn't know a single person in my class.
第一天，我忘了带橡皮。: On my first day, I forgot my eraser.
可是，我怎么也说不出“借我用一下”。: But I couldn't say, "Can I borrow one, please?"
这时，坐在旁边的女孩把自己的橡皮切成了两半。: Just then, the girl sitting next to me cut her own eraser in half.
然后说了声“给你”，把大的那一半给了我。: Then she said, "Here you go," and gave me the bigger piece.
那半块橡皮，现在还放在我的铅笔盒里。: That half eraser is still in my pencil case today.
我弟弟拓海五岁。: My little brother, Takumi, is five years old.
有一天，拓海第一次一个人去买东西。: One day, Takumi went shopping by himself for the first time.
妈妈说“去买面包和牛奶回来哦”，然后把钱交给了他。: Our mother said, "Go buy some bread and milk, okay?" and handed him some money.
那家店离家走路五分钟。: The store is a five-minute walk from our house.
拓海大声说了句“我出门了！”，就走出了家门。: Takumi said in a loud voice, "I'm off!" and left the house.
其实，妈妈和我一直悄悄跟在后面看着。: Actually, my mother and I were quietly watching him from behind.
在路上，拓海停下了一次。: On the way, Takumi stopped once.
可他又继续往前走，进了店里。: But he started walking again and went into the store.
十分钟后，拓海拿着面包和牛奶，精神十足地回来了。: Ten minutes later, Takumi came back cheerfully, carrying the bread and milk.
妈妈说“真了不起”，摸了摸拓海的头。: Our mother said, "Good job!" and patted Takumi on the head.
因为感冒请假了: I stayed home from school with a cold
从昨天晚上开始，嗓子就疼。: My throat has been sore since last night.
今天早上量了体温。: This morning, I took my temperature.
今天向学校请了假。: I stayed home from school today.
我和妈妈一起去了附近的医院。: I went to a nearby hospital with my mother.
医生说：“是感冒。吃了药好好睡一觉吧。”: The doctor said, "It's a cold. Take your medicine and get plenty of sleep."
回到家，我吃了妈妈煮的粥。: When I got home, I ate the rice porridge my mother made.
然后吃了药，睡了很久。: Then I took my medicine and slept a lot.
傍晚，朋友发来消息：“没事吧？快点好起来哦。”: In the evening, I got a message from a friend: "Are you okay? Get well soon!"
请假，休息: to take time off, to rest
在朋友家说“打扰了”: Saying 「おじゃまします」 at a friend's house
星期天，我去了日本朋友家。: On Sunday, I went to a Japanese friend's house.
进门的时候，我说了“打扰了”。: When I went inside, I said 「おじゃまします」 ("Sorry to intrude").
这是进别人家时说的客套话。: This is a greeting you say when you enter someone else's home.
我带了中国茶作为见面礼。: I brought some Chinese tea as a gift.
朋友的妈妈说：“谢谢。快请进吧。”: My friend's mother said, "Thank you. Please, come on in."
大家一起喝着茶，聊了很多。: We all drank tea and talked a lot.
离开的时候，我说了“打扰了”。: When I left, I said 「おじゃましました」 ("Sorry for intruding").
进门时说“します”，离开时说“しました”。: When you arrive, it's 「します」, and when you leave, it's 「しました」.
朋友的妈妈说：“下次再来玩哦。”: My friend's mother said, "Please come again."
爷爷在家后面有一小块菜地。: Grandpa has a small vegetable patch behind the house.
菜地里种着西红柿、黄瓜和茄子。: In the patch, he grows tomatoes, cucumbers, and eggplants.
爷爷每天早上五点起床，去菜地干活。: Grandpa gets up at five every morning and goes out to the patch.
暑假时，我也去菜地给爷爷帮忙。: During summer vacation, I helped out in Grandpa's patch too.
早上很凉快，中午却非常热。: It's cool in the morning, but very hot at midday.
我摘了一个红红的西红柿，就在菜地里吃了。: I picked a red tomato and ate it right there in the patch.
比店里买的西红柿甜多了。: It was much sweeter than tomatoes from the store.
爷爷说：“蔬菜也好，人也好，每天都去看一看，这很重要。”: Grandpa said, "With vegetables and with people, it's important to look at them every day."
秋天有很多好吃的东西。: There are lots of delicious foods in the fall.
秋刀鱼、柿子、红薯，还有栗子。: Pacific saury, persimmons, sweet potatoes, and chestnuts.
我家每年秋天都会做“栗子饭”。: At my house, we make 「くりごはん」 (kuri gohan, chestnut rice) every fall.
栗子饭就是放了栗子一起煮的米饭。: Chestnut rice is rice cooked with chestnuts in it.
所以剥壳很费劲。: So peeling them is hard work.
今年，我也和爸爸两个人一起剥了壳。: This year, I peeled them too, together with my father.
不过，栗子饭里的栗子粉粉糯糯的，非常好吃。: But the chestnut rice was soft and fluffy, and very delicious.
（薯类、栗子等）粉糯: soft and fluffy (of potatoes, chestnuts, etc.)
我从六岁开始学钢琴。: I've been taking piano lessons since I was six.
每周二在老师家上课。: Every Tuesday, I have a lesson at my teacher's house.
上个月，我第一次参加了钢琴汇报演出。: Last month, I performed in a piano recital for the first time.
演出的前一天，我非常紧张。: The day before the recital, I was very nervous.
演出那天，我走上舞台，在钢琴前坐下。: On the day of the recital, I went out on stage and sat down at the piano.
台下坐着很多人。: There were lots of people in front of me.
弹到一半，我弹错了一个音。: Partway through, I played one wrong note.
但我还是坚持弹到了最后。: But I played all the way to the end.
妈妈说：“你真努力。”: My mother said, "You really did your best."
上周，我和朋友去东京玩了。: Last week, a friend and I went to Tokyo for fun.
因为拿着一个大包，所以非常重。: I had a big bag with me, so it was very heavy.
车站里有很多投币储物柜。: There were lots of coin lockers at the station.
我们把包放进储物柜，然后锁上了。: We put our bags in a locker and locked it.
然后，我们在街上慢慢地逛。: Then we took our time walking around the city.
因为没有拿包，所以非常轻松。: Without our bags, it was very easy.
傍晚，我们回到车站，从储物柜里取出了包。: In the evening, we went back to the station and took our bags out of the locker.
现在也有可以用卡的储物柜。: Nowadays, there are also lockers you can use with a card.
有大件行李的时候，投币储物柜非常方便。: When you have big luggage, coin lockers are very convenient.
放进，装入: to put in, to place inside
购物要带自己的袋子: Bring your own bag when shopping
我妈妈去买东西的时候，总会带上一个布袋子。: When my mother goes shopping, she always takes a cloth bag with her.
这就是“自备购物袋”。: This is a 「マイバッグ」 ("my bag," a reusable shopping bag).
在日本的超市和便利店，收银台的袋子一般是要花钱买的。: At supermarkets and convenience stores in Japan, bags at the checkout usually cost money.
所以，很多人会自己带袋子去。: So a lot of people bring their own bags.
妈妈的购物袋是蓝色的，上面有可爱的小鱼图案。: My mother's bag is blue and has a picture of a cute fish on it.
昨天，我一个人去买东西了。: Yesterday, I went shopping by myself.
可是，我忘了带购物袋。: But I forgot my reusable bag.
我用手拿着牛奶、面包和鸡蛋回了家。: I carried the milk, bread, and eggs home in my hands.
从下周开始，我也要带购物袋去。: Starting next week, I'll bring my own bag too.
在日本，自来水一般可以直接喝。: In Japan, you can usually drink tap water as it is.
在我的国家，人们不喝自来水。: In my country, we don't drink tap water.
总是在店里买水喝。: We always buy water at the store.
第一次来日本的时候，我问了酒店的工作人员。: When I first came to Japan, I asked someone at the hotel.
酒店的人说：“能喝，没问题的。”: The hotel employee said, "Yes, it's fine."
我喝了一点，又凉又好喝。: I drank a little. It was cold and tasted good.
公园里也有可以喝水的地方。: There are places to get a drink of water in parks, too.
现在，我每天早上都用杯子喝自来水。: Now I drink a glass of tap water every morning.
壁橱是秘密小屋: The closet is a secret room
我家有一间铺着榻榻米的房间。: My house has a tatami room.
那个房间里有一个大壁橱。: That room has a big closet.
白天，把被褥收进壁橱里。: During the day, we put the futons away in the closet.
晚上，再把被褥拿出来，睡在榻榻米上。: At night, we take the futons out and sleep on the tatami.
弟弟特别喜欢壁橱。: My little brother loves the closet.
他说着“哆啦A梦也睡在壁橱里哦”，时不时就钻进去。: He says, "Doraemon sleeps in a closet too!" and sometimes climbs inside.
弟弟在壁橱里看漫画。: My little brother reads manga in the closet.
妈妈说：“不要在暗的地方看书。”: My mother says, "Please don't read books in dark places."
可是，弟弟会拿着小手电钻进去。: But my little brother takes a small light in with him.
暑假时，我去了乡下的叔叔家。: During summer vacation, I went to my uncle's house in the countryside.
叔叔把一根长竹子劈成两半，放在了院子里。: My uncle split a long bamboo pole in half and set it up in the yard.
从竹子上头放水，再把素面也放下来。: Water is sent down the bamboo from the top, and the somen is sent down too.
这就是“流水素面”。: This is 「流しそうめん」 (nagashi somen, "flowing somen").
我们拿着筷子，站在竹子前面。: We stood in front of the bamboo holding our chopsticks.
素面流得很快，所以一开始我一根也夹不到。: The somen came down very fast, so at first I couldn't catch any at all.
不过，慢慢地就熟练了。: But I gradually got better at it.
夹到的素面，蘸着凉凉的汤汁吃。: You dip the somen you catch in cold dipping sauce and eat it.
在外面和大家一起吃的素面，特别好吃。: The somen we ate outside with everyone was really delicious.
使流动，冲: to let flow, to wash away
年底捣年糕: Making mochi at the end of the year
十二月底，我们在爷爷家捣了年糕。: At the end of December, we made mochi at my grandfather's house.
捣年糕，就是用糯米做年糕。: Mochitsuki means making mochi from sticky rice.
首先把糯米蒸熟，放进一个大“石臼”里。: First, you steam the sticky rice and put it in a big 「うす」 (usu, mortar).
然后，用一种叫“杵”的木头工具来捣。: Then you pound it with a wooden tool called a 「きね」 (kine, mallet).
爷爷拿着杵捣。: My grandfather pounds it with the mallet.
奶奶趁着间隙，用手把米翻一翻。: In between, my grandmother turns the rice over by hand.
发出“啪嗒、啪嗒”的好听声音。: It makes a nice sound: 「ぺったん、ぺったん」 (pettan, pettan).
我也捣了一会儿，可是杵非常重。: I pounded it a little too, but the mallet was very heavy.
做好的年糕又白又软。: The finished mochi is white and soft.
大家蘸着酱油或黄豆粉一起吃了。: We all ate it with soy sauce or kinako (roasted soybean flour).
和爸爸去烤鸡肉串店: To a yakitori restaurant with my father
星期五晚上，我和爸爸去了车站附近的烤鸡肉串店。: On Friday night, I went to a yakitori restaurant near the station with my father.
店里人很多，非常热闹。: The restaurant was crowded and lively.
烤鸡肉串是把鸡肉切成小块，穿在竹签上烤的料理。: Yakitori is a dish of chicken cut into small pieces, put on skewers, and grilled.
店员正在火上烤着鸡肉串。: A man at the restaurant was grilling yakitori over the fire.
酱汁的甜甜的，盐烤的很清爽。: The tare is sweet, and the shio is light and refreshing.
我最喜欢鸡肉和大葱一起烤的“葱间串”。: I like 「ねぎま」 (negima), grilled chicken and green onion, the best.
我还想再和爸爸一起来。: I want to come here with my father again.
热闹: to be crowded, to be bustling
山梨县是在东京旁边的一个县。: Yamanashi Prefecture is next to Tokyo.
山梨县盛产葡萄和桃子。: Lots of grapes and peaches are grown in Yamanashi Prefecture.
用葡萄酿的葡萄酒也很有名。: Wine made from the grapes is also famous.
九月，我们全家去了葡萄园。: In September, my family went to a vineyard.
葡萄一串串地挂在我们的头顶上。: Lots of grapes were hanging above our heads.
我们用剪刀剪下来，放进了篮子里。: We cut them off with scissors and put them in a basket.
摘下来的葡萄，我们马上就吃了。: We ate the grapes we picked right away.
非常甜，很好吃。: They were very sweet and delicious.
从回程的车里，看到了巨大的富士山。: From the car on the way home, we could see Mt. Fuji looming large.
冲绳有一种叫“开口笑”（萨塔安达吉）的点心。: In Okinawa, there is a sweet called 「サーターアンダギー」 (sata andagi).
在冲绳方言里，它的意思是“用砂糖做、用油炸的东西”。: In the Okinawan language, the name means "something made with sugar and fried in oil."
外面是褐色的，有点硬，里面却很松软。: The outside is brown and a little hard, but the inside is soft.
去年夏天，我在冲绳的一家小店里吃过。: Last summer, I ate some at a small shop in Okinawa.
刚炸出来的，热乎乎的，特别好吃。: They were freshly fried, warm, and really delicious.
店里的老奶奶说：“看起来像一张笑脸吧？”: The old woman at the shop said, "It looks like a smiling face, doesn't it?"
开口笑一炸，上面就会裂开，像花一样。: When sata andagi are fried, the top cracks open and they look like flowers.
所以听说在喜庆的日子里也常常做。: That's why, I hear, people often make them on happy occasions too.
我的朋友小咲是爱媛县人。: My friend Saki is from Ehime Prefecture.
爱媛县在四国，以橘子闻名。: Ehime Prefecture is in Shikoku and is famous for mandarin oranges.
小咲奶奶家有一片橘子园。: Saki's grandmother has a mandarin orange orchard at her house.
上个月，小咲给我寄来了一个大箱子。: Last month, a big box arrived from Saki.
箱子里装着满满的橘子。: The box was full of mandarin oranges.
还有一封短信。: There was also a little note.
“这是奶奶园子里的橘子，请大家一起吃吧。”: "These are mandarins from my grandma's orchard. Please share them with everyone."
橘子很甜，皮也很好剥。: The mandarins were sweet, and they peeled easily too.
一天下来，全家人吃了好多。: My whole family ate lots of them in one day.
明年，我也想去爱媛的橘子园看看。: Next year, I want to go to the orchard in Ehime too.
春假时，我去了京都的金阁寺。: During spring break, I went to Kinkakuji in Kyoto.
从大门进去，走了一小段路。: I went in through the gate and walked a little way.
在池塘对面，看见了一座金色的建筑。: Across the pond, I could see a golden building.
那天天气很好，建筑闪闪发光。: The weather was nice that day, and the building was shining very brightly.
池水里也倒映着金色的建筑。: The golden building was reflected in the water of the pond, too.
周围也有很多从国外来的游客。: There were also lots of people from other countries around.
星期天，我和朋友去了东京的浅草。: On Sunday, I went to Asakusa in Tokyo with a friend.
从车站走一小段路，就有一座大门。: A short walk from the station, there is a big gate.
这就是“雷门”。: This is 「雷門」 (Kaminarimon, the Thunder Gate).
门的正中间，挂着一个特别大的红灯笼。: In the middle of the gate, there is a huge red lantern.
我们在灯笼前拍了照片。: We took pictures in front of the lantern.
门的里面有一座古老的寺庙。: Beyond the gate, there is an old temple.
通往寺庙的路上，排列着许多小店。: Along the path to the temple, lots of little shops stand in a row.
店里卖点心、纪念品，还有日本的老式玩具。: They sell sweets, souvenirs, and old-fashioned Japanese toys.
我买了热乎乎的“人形烧”吃。: I bought some warm 「人形焼き」 (ningyo-yaki) and ate them.
里面有豆沙馅，甜甜的很好吃。: They had red bean paste inside and were sweet and delicious.
栃木县的日光，有一座叫东照宫的古老神社。: In Nikko, Tochigi Prefecture, there is an old shrine called Toshogu.
这里的建筑上雕刻着许多漂亮的图案和动物。: Many beautiful pictures and animals are carved into the buildings here.
其中最有名的是三只猴子。: The most famous ones are the three monkeys.
第一只猴子用手捂着眼睛。: The first monkey is covering its eyes with its hands.
第二只捂着嘴，第三只捂着耳朵。: The second monkey is covering its mouth, and the third is covering its ears.
这就是“不看、不说、不听”。: They are 「みざる、いわざる、きかざる」 ("see not, speak not, hear not").
据说意思是“坏事不看、不说、不听”。: It's said to mean "Don't see, say, or hear bad things."
东照宫里还有一只正在睡觉的猫。: At Toshogu, there is also a sleeping cat.
日本最大的湖是琵琶湖。: The biggest lake in Japan is Lake Biwa.
琵琶湖在滋贺县。: Lake Biwa is in Shiga Prefecture.
“琵琶”是一种古代乐器的名字。: 「琵琶」 (biwa) is the name of a musical instrument from long ago.
因为湖的形状很像琵琶，所以就有了这个名字。: The lake got this name because its shape looks like a biwa.
琵琶湖非常大，看起来就像大海一样。: Lake Biwa is so big that it looks like the sea.
可是，湖水不是海水，并不咸。: But the lake water isn't seawater. It isn't salty.
琵琶湖的水经过河流流向京都和大阪。: Water from Lake Biwa flows through a river to Kyoto and Osaka.
夏天，也有人在湖里游泳、坐船。: In summer, some people swim in the lake or go out on boats.
日本人与4和9: The Japanese and the numbers 4 and 9
在日语里，4读作“yon”，也读作“shi”。: In Japanese, 4 is read 「よん」 (yon), but it can also be read 「し」 (shi).
“shi”和“死”的发音一样。: 「し」 sounds the same as the 「し」 in 「死ぬ」 (shinu, to die).
9读作“kyu”，也读作“ku”。: 9 is read 「きゅう」 (kyu), but it can also be read 「く」 (ku).
“ku”和“痛苦”的“苦”发音一样。: 「く」 sounds the same as the 「く」 in 「苦しい」 (kurushii, painful).
所以，也有人不太喜欢4和9。: So some people don't really like 4 and 9.
有的医院和酒店没有4号和9号房间。: Some hospitals and hotels have no rooms numbered 4 or 9.
送人东西的时候，也不太会挑4个一组的。: When giving someone a present, people also don't usually choose sets of four.
在中国也有人不喜欢4吧。: In China, too, there are people who don't like 4, aren't there?
日本和中国在这一点上还挺像的呢。: Japan and China are a little alike, aren't they?
爷爷一个人住在乡下。: My grandfather lives alone in the countryside.
去年，爷爷买了一只机器狗。: Last year, my grandfather bought a robot dog.
波奇会走路，还会摇尾巴。: Pochi walks. It wags its tail, too.
于是，波奇马上就坐下了。: Then Pochi sat down right away.
波奇不吃饭，也不用散步。: Pochi doesn't eat, and it doesn't go for walks.
可是，爷爷每天都在和波奇说话。: But my grandfather talks with Pochi every day.
电话里爷爷的声音，比以前精神多了。: On the phone, my grandfather sounds more cheerful than before.
下次，我也要去见见波奇。: Next time, I'm going to go see Pochi too.
用手机看懂菜单: Reading the menu with my smartphone
来到日本后，我第一次一个人进了餐馆。: After coming to Japan, I went into a restaurant by myself for the first time.
菜单上只有日语，而且汉字很多。: The menu was only in Japanese and had lots of kanji.
我完全看不懂，所以拿出了手机。: I didn't understand it at all, so I took out my smartphone.
用手机摄像头对准菜单，屏幕上就出现了中文。: When I pointed my phone's camera at the menu, Chinese appeared on the screen.
非常方便，让我吃了一惊。: It was so convenient that I was amazed.
吃完以后，我用日语对店员说：“很好吃。”: After I ate, I told the staff in Japanese, 「おいしかったです」 ("It was delicious").
店员笑眯眯地说：“谢谢您。”: The staff member smiled and said, "Thank you very much."
手机虽然方便，但用日语交流更开心。: Smartphones are convenient, but talking in Japanese is even more fun.
在我们小学，一到冬天，大家就一起跳绳。: At my elementary school, when winter comes, everyone jumps rope.
课间休息时，在操场上跳。: We jump in the schoolyard during recess.
我以前不会“双摇跳”。: I couldn't do a 「二重とび」 (nijū tobi, double under).
双摇跳就是跳一下的时间里，绳子要甩两圈。: In a double under, you swing the rope around twice during one jump.
每天放学回家后，我都在家门口练习。: Every day after coming home from school, I practiced in front of my house.
爸爸教我说：“要跳得再高一点。”: My father gave me advice: "Jump higher."
不过，昨天我第一次连续跳了三个双摇。: But yesterday, I was able to do three double unders for the first time.
我每周二和周四都在学空手道。: I take karate lessons every Tuesday and Thursday.
空手道是诞生于冲绳的一项运动。: Karate is a sport that was born in Okinawa.
现在，世界上很多国家的人都在练。: Now people from many countries around the world practice it.
练习前后，大家都要和老师一起鞠躬。: Before and after practice, we all bow together with the teacher.
在空手道里，礼节非常重要。: In karate, greetings are very important.
练习的时候，要穿白色的“空手道服”。: During practice, we wear a white 「空手着」 (karategi, karate uniform).
一边大声喊，一边把手和脚向前出击。: We shout loudly as we thrust our hands and feet forward.
一开始我有点不好意思。: At first I was a little embarrassed.
不过现在，我已经喜欢上大声喊了。: But now I've come to like shouting loudly.
星期天早上，我和妈妈在公园里打了羽毛球。: On Sunday morning, my mother and I played badminton in the park.
妈妈上高中的时候，是羽毛球部的。: My mother was on the badminton team in high school.
那天风有点大。: That day, the wind was a little strong.
我一打，羽毛球就被风吹了回来。: When I hit the shuttlecock, the wind blew it back toward me.
妈妈一打，羽毛球就飞得远远的。: When my mother hit it, it flew far away.
我们两个人笑了好久。: The two of us laughed a lot.
回家路上，妈妈说：“下次去体育馆打吧。”: On the way home, my mother said, "Next time, let's play in a gym."
体育馆里没有风，那就好了。: There's no wind in a gym, so that will be nice.
在电影院看了动画片: I saw an anime at the movie theater
星期六，我和朋友去电影院看了一部动画电影。: On Saturday, I went to a movie theater with a friend to see an anime movie.
这部动画我在电视上也看过，所以特别期待。: I had been watching this anime on TV too, so I was really looking forward to it.
电影院的屏幕比家里的电视大得多。: The screen at the movie theater is much bigger than the TV at home.
声音也很大，太震撼了。: The sound was loud too, and it was amazing.
电影的最后，主人公和朋友分别了。: At the end of the movie, the main character parted ways with a friend.
旁边的朋友也掏出了手帕。: My friend next to me had taken out a handkerchief too.
看完电影后，我们俩走进一家咖啡馆，聊了聊电影。: After the movie, the two of us went into a coffee shop and talked about the movie.
明年的续集，我们也想一起去看。: Next year, we want to see the next movie together too.
我弟弟五岁。: My little brother is five years old.
弟弟特别喜欢星期天早上的英雄节目。: My little brother loves the superhero show on Sunday mornings.
平时，他早上总是起不来。: Usually, he has a hard time getting up in the morning.
可是只有星期天，他会早早起床坐在电视机前。: But on Sundays, and only on Sundays, he gets up early and sits in front of the TV.
节目里的英雄穿着红色的衣服。: The hero on the show wears red clothes.
一有坏人，他马上就冲过去。: Whenever there's a bad guy, he runs straight over.
节目一结束，弟弟也学起了英雄的样子。: When the show ends, my little brother imitates the hero.
他喊着“嘿！”，从沙发上跳下来。: He shouts, "Hyah!" and jumps off the sofa.
妈妈说“很危险哦”，可弟弟根本不听。: My mother says, "That's dangerous," but my little brother doesn't listen.
好想看电视剧的后续: I want to see what happens next in the drama
我每周三晚上都看电视剧。: I watch a drama every Wednesday night.
讲的是一位在医院工作的年轻医生的故事。: It's a story about a young doctor who works at a hospital.
主人公很温柔，总是全力以赴。: The main character is kind and always works hard.
最后，主人公重要的朋友病倒了。: At the end, the main character's dear friend collapsed from an illness.
后续要等到下周才能看到。: I can't see what happens next until next week.
我今天也一直惦记着那个朋友。: Today, too, I keep wondering about the friend.
真希望下周三快点到来。: I wish next Wednesday would hurry up and come.
昨天晚上，他又给我出了一个谜语。: Last night, he gave me another riddle.
弟弟：“同样叫‘パン’，不能吃的‘パン’是什么？”: Brother: "What kind of 「パン」 (pan, bread) can't you eat?"
我：“我知道了，是平底锅（フライパン）。”: Me: "I've got it. A 「フライパン」 (frying pan)."
我：“诶，不是平底锅吗？”: Me: "Huh? It's not a frying pan?"
弟弟：“不是。答案是爸爸的牛仔裤（ジーパン）。”: Brother: "No. The answer is Dad's 「ジーパン」 (jeans)."
弟弟：“因为爸爸的牛仔裤特别大呀。”: Brother: "Because Dad's jeans are really big."
出（题），拿出: to set (a question), to take out
一抬手就疼: It hurts when I raise my arm
田中先生肩膀疼，去了医院。: Tanaka's shoulder hurt, so he went to the hospital.
医生：“好的，怎么了？”: Doctor: "Yes, what seems to be the problem?"
田中：“我像这样把手往上一抬，肩膀就特别疼。”: Tanaka: "When I raise my arm up like this, my shoulder really hurts."
医生：“这样啊。放下来的话怎么样？”: Doctor: "I see. And when you lower it?"
田中：“放下来就不疼。”: Tanaka: "When I lower it, it doesn't hurt."
医生想了一会儿。: The doctor thought for a moment.
医生：“那么，请不要把手往上抬。”: Doctor: "Then please don't raise your arm."
起得太早的爸爸: My father, who got up too early
有一天早上，爸爸六点就起床了。: One morning, my father got up at six.
爸爸急忙洗了脸，穿上衬衫，打好领带。: My father hurriedly washed his face and put on his shirt and tie.
连早饭都没吃就出门了。: He left the house without even eating breakfast.
车站里一个人都没有。: There was nobody at all at the station.
车站的工作人员说：“今天是星期天哦。”: A station worker said, "Today is Sunday."
爸爸慢慢地走回了家。: My father walked slowly back home.
然后，他系着领带，又钻回了被窝。: Then, still wearing his tie, he got back into his futon.
让座的那天: The day I gave up my seat
我每天早上坐公交车去高中。: Every morning, I take the bus to high school.
有一天早上，公交车特别挤。: One morning, the bus was very crowded.
我面前站着一位拄着拐杖的老奶奶。: In front of me stood an old woman with a cane.
我虽然有点不好意思，还是说了声“请坐”，站了起来。: I felt a little embarrassed, but I said, "Please, have a seat," and stood up.
老奶奶说了声“谢谢”，坐了下来。: The old woman said, "Thank you," and sat down.
下一周，我在同一辆公交车上又遇到了那位老奶奶。: The next week, I met the same old woman again on the same bus.
老奶奶递给我一个小袋子。: She gave me a small bag.
里面装着亲手做的饼干和一封信。: Inside were homemade cookies and a letter.
信上写着：“那天，我真的很开心。”: The letter said, "I was so happy that day."
我也变得非常开心。: That made me very happy too.
给我带路的小女孩: The girl who showed me the way
去年夏天，我一个人去了大阪。: Last summer, I went to Osaka by myself.
我想去酒店，可是不认识路。: I wanted to go to my hotel, but I didn't know the way.
我拿着地图，在街上一筹莫展。: I was standing in the street with a map, not knowing what to do.
这时，一个小女孩问我：“您怎么了？”: Just then, a little girl asked, "Is something wrong?"
我把地图给她看，她说了句“在这边”，就开始往前走。: When I showed her the map, the girl said, "It's this way," and started walking.
小女孩一直把我送到了酒店门口。: The girl came with me all the way to the front of the hotel.
我说了声“谢谢”，送给她一些我们国家的点心。: I said, "Thank you," and gave her some sweets from my country.
那天那个小女孩的模样，我至今还记得很清楚。: I still remember that girl's face from that day very well.
为难，发愁: to be troubled, to be at a loss
上个月，姐姐举行了婚礼。: Last month, my older sister had her wedding.
姐姐穿着白色的婚纱，特别漂亮。: My sister wore a white dress and looked very beautiful.
姐姐的丈夫是一个温柔又爱笑的人。: My sister's husband is a kind man who laughs a lot.
婚礼的最后，姐姐给爸爸妈妈读了一封信。: At the end of the wedding, my sister read a letter to our parents.
“爸爸，妈妈，谢谢你们一直以来的照顾。”: "Dad, Mom, thank you so much for everything all these years."
妈妈用手帕擦着眼睛。: My mother was wiping her eyes with a handkerchief.
平时不太说话的爸爸，也有点哭了。: Even my father, who usually doesn't talk much, was crying a little.
我也流下了眼泪。: Tears came to my eyes too.
姐姐已经不在家里住了，我有点寂寞。: My sister doesn't live at home anymore, so I'm a little lonely.
不过，姐姐很幸福，所以我也很高兴。: But my sister is happy, so I'm happy too.
和弟弟吵架的那个晚上: The night I fought with my little brother
昨天晚上，我和弟弟吵架了。: Last night, I had a fight with my little brother.
我想看电视剧。: I wanted to watch a drama.
弟弟想看足球比赛。: My little brother wanted to watch a soccer game.
我们俩大声吵闹，被妈妈骂了。: We were yelling, and our mother scolded us.
今天早上，我的书桌上放着一张小纸条。: This morning, there was a small piece of paper on my desk.
是弟弟的字。: It was in my little brother's handwriting.
我也在纸上写了“我也对不起”，放在了弟弟的书桌上。: I wrote "I'm sorry too" on a piece of paper and put it on his desk.
今晚，我们俩一起看足球。: Tonight, the two of us are going to watch soccer together.
我姐姐是动物园的饲养员。: My older sister is a zookeeper.
饲养员就是照顾动物的工作。: A zookeeper's job is to take care of the animals.
姐姐早上七点去动物园。: My sister goes to the zoo at seven in the morning.
首先，打扫动物的屋子。: First, she cleans the animals' enclosures.
姐姐负责照顾大象。: My sister is in charge of the elephants.
大象的身体很大，所以每天要吃很多东西。: Elephants are big, so they eat a lot every day.
姐姐还会仔细检查大象的眼睛和脚。: My sister also checks the elephants' eyes and feet carefully.
动物不会说“疼”，所以每天仔细观察很重要。: Animals can't say "It hurts," so it's important to watch them carefully every day.
姐姐说：“大象是我的朋友。”: My sister says, "The elephants are my friends."
我叔叔是一名电车司机。: My uncle is a train driver.
他每天载着很多人，开着电车。: Every day, he drives a train carrying lots of people.
早班的日子，他五点左右就起床。: On days when he starts early, he gets up at around five.
叔叔开车的时候，常常用手指指向前方。: When he's driving, my uncle often points ahead with his finger.
然后大声说：“信号，确认！”: Then he says in a loud voice, 「信号、よし」 ("Signal, clear!").
这是为了不出差错，仔细看清楚、确认好。: This is a way of looking and checking so that there are no mistakes.
电车准时运行是很重要的。: It's important for trains to run on time.
所以，叔叔总是在看时间。: That's why my uncle is always looking at the clock.
叔叔说：“乘客的安全是最重要的。”: My uncle says, "The passengers' safety is the most important thing."
载，让……乘坐: to carry (passengers), to give a ride to
八月，我和朋友去了海边。: In August, I went to the beach with my friends.
在海里游完泳后，大家一起玩了“劈西瓜”。: After swimming in the sea, we all played 「すいかわり」 (suikawari, watermelon splitting).
劈西瓜是日本夏天的一种游戏。: Watermelon splitting is a Japanese summer game.
首先，把西瓜放在沙滩上。: First, you put a watermelon on the sand.
一个人用毛巾蒙住眼睛，手里拿着一根长木棍。: One person covers their eyes with a towel and holds a long wooden stick.
其他人喊着：“往右，往右！”“再往前！”: The others shout, "Right, right!" and "Further forward!"
轮到我的时候，听到大家七嘴八舌，我都分不清了。: When it was my turn, I could hear so many voices that I couldn't really tell where to go.
不过，最后朋友把西瓜劈开了。: But in the end, a friend split the watermelon.
大家一起吃的西瓜又甜又凉。: The watermelon we all ate together was sweet and cold.
秋天挖红薯: Digging up sweet potatoes in the fall
十月，我们班的同学一起去田里挖了红薯。: In October, my whole class went to a field and dug up sweet potatoes.
春天，我们种下了小小的苗。: In the spring, we had planted small seedlings.
整个夏天，种田的人一直在细心照料。: During the summer, the farmers took good care of them for us.
红薯长在土里。: The sweet potatoes are under the soil.
用手一刨土，就看见了红色的红薯。: When I dug the soil with my hands, I could see a red sweet potato.
大个的红薯怎么也拔不出来。: The big potatoes just wouldn't come out.
和朋友两个人一起拽，终于拔出来了。: When a friend and I pulled together, one finally came out.
手和衣服都沾满了泥土，变成了褐色，可是特别开心。: Our hands and clothes turned brown with dirt, but it was a lot of fun.
我把红薯带回家，和妈妈一起做了天妇罗。: I took them home and made tempura with my mother.
生平第一次看到雪: The first snow of my life
曼谷一年到头都很热，不下雪。: It's hot in Bangkok all year round, so it doesn't snow.
所以，我从来没见过雪。: So I had never seen snow.
一月的一个早上，窗外变得白茫茫的。: One morning in January, everything outside the window had turned white.
我穿上大衣跑到了外面。: I put on my coat and went outside.
小小的雪花静静地从空中飘落。: Small snowflakes were falling quietly from the sky.
雪花一落到手上，马上就化成了水。: When snow landed on my hand, it turned to water right away.
虽然很冷，但我太高兴了，一直望着天空。: It was very cold, but I was so happy that I kept looking up at the sky.
新年的时候，我去了爷爷家。: For New Year's, I went to my grandfather's house.
爷爷拿出了一个旧的木头陀螺。: My grandfather brought out an old wooden top.
转陀螺是自古以来的一种新年游戏。: Spinning tops is a New Year's game that has been around since long ago.
首先，把绳子绕在陀螺上。: First, you wind a string around the top.
然后，把陀螺扔出去，同时一拉绳子。: Then you throw the top and pull the string.
爷爷的陀螺滴溜溜地转了好久。: My grandfather's top kept spinning round and round for a long time.
我的陀螺一下子就倒了。: My top fell over right away.
爷爷说：“手再放低一点。”: My grandfather said, "Hold your hand a little lower."
到了傍晚，我的陀螺也终于转起来了。: In the evening, my top finally spun too.
爷爷看上去比我还高兴。: My grandfather looked even happier than I was.
日本的神社有一套参拜的方法。: There is a set way of praying at Japanese shrines.
首先，在鸟居前轻轻鞠一个躬。: First, you bow slightly in front of the torii gate.
道路正中间是神明走的路，所以要靠边走。: The middle of the path is for the gods, so you walk along the side.
然后，用水把手和嘴清洗干净。: Then you clean your hands and mouth with water.
到了神殿前，往香钱箱里投钱，再摇响铃铛。: When you reach the front of the shrine building, you put money in the offering box and ring the bell.
接着，鞠两次躬，拍两下手。: Then you bow twice and clap your hands twice.
在心里许完愿后，再鞠一个躬。: After making your wish silently, you bow once more.
一开始可能觉得有点难，不过很快就能记住。: It's difficult at first, but you'll learn it quickly.
暑假时，我们全家去北海道旅行了。: During summer vacation, my family took a trip to Hokkaido.
北海道夏天也很凉爽，非常舒服。: Hokkaido is cool even in summer, and it felt really nice.
我们去了一个很大的牧场。: We went to a big ranch.
宽阔的草地上，有很多黑白花的奶牛。: There were lots of black-and-white cows on the wide grassy field.
牧场的人教我们怎么挤牛奶。: A ranch worker taught us how to milk a cow.
我虽然有点害怕，还是试着用手挤了牛奶。: I was scared, but I tried milking a cow by hand.
之后，我们喝了牧场的牛奶。: After that, we drank milk from the ranch.
味道很浓郁，特别好喝。: It was rich and very delicious.
我家附近有一家老字号的粗点心铺。: There's an old dagashi shop near my house.
粗点心是小孩子买的便宜零食。: 「だがし」 (dagashi) are cheap sweets that children buy.
店里摆满了糖果、口香糖和小块巧克力。: The shop has lots of candies, gum, and little chocolates lined up.
店里的老奶奶已经在这家店待了四十年了。: The old woman at the shop has been there for forty years.
一放学，孩子们就来到这家店。: When school lets out, children come to this shop.
大家拿着零花钱，想了很久要买什么。: They all bring their allowance and spend a long time thinking about what to buy.
老奶奶总是笑眯眯地等着。: The old woman always waits with a smile.
我小时候也每天都来这家店。: When I was a child, I came to this shop every day too.
现在每次经过店门口，都会想起那时候的事情。: Even now, when I pass in front of the shop, I remember those days.
上周，我去了附近的图书馆。: Last week, I went to a nearby library.
我想借书，所以办了一张借书卡。: I wanted to borrow books, so I got a card.
我在柜台把名字和地址写在了纸上。: At the counter, I wrote my name and address on a sheet of paper.
图书馆的工作人员看了我的在留卡，很快就给我办好了卡。: The librarian looked at my residence card and made my card right away.
在这家图书馆，一次最多可以借五本书。: At this library, you can borrow up to five books at a time.
我借了一本简单的日语书，还有一本菜谱。: I borrowed a book in easy Japanese and a cookbook.
书要在两周内还。: Books are due back in two weeks.
从今以后，我想每周都来图书馆。: From now on, I want to come to the library every week.
课间休息时，他和朋友在操场上踢球。: During recess at school, he kicks a ball around in the schoolyard with his friends.
课间休息很短，但大家都跑得很起劲。: Recess is short, but everyone runs a lot.
世界杯每四年举办一次。: The World Cup is held once every four years.
那时候，全家人都会坐在电视机前。: When it's on, our whole family sits in front of the TV.
日本队进球的时候，弟弟会站起来大声欢呼。: When Japan scores a goal, my little brother stands up and shouts.
就算是深夜的比赛，弟弟也不睡觉，一直看着。: Even when a game is late at night, my little brother stays up and watches it.
我妈妈每天早上都洗衣服。: My mother does the laundry every morning.
早饭之前，她把衣服和毛巾放进洗衣机。: Before breakfast, she puts clothes and towels in the washing machine.
洗完的时候，洗衣机会“哔——”地响一声。: When the wash is done, the washing machine goes 「ピーッ」 (beep).
妈妈把衣服晾在阳台上。: My mother hangs the clothes out on the balcony.
在日本，很多人家都把衣服晾在外面。: In Japan, many households hang their clothes outside to dry.
晴天的时候，衣服很快就干了。: On sunny days, clothes dry quickly.
下雨天就晾在房间里。: On rainy days, she hangs them up inside.
我每天都用智能手机。: I use my smartphone every day.
我经常用手机拍照。: I often take pictures with my smartphone.
我拍漂亮的花，也拍好吃的菜。: I take pictures of pretty flowers and delicious food.
在第一次去的城市，我用手机看地图。: In towns I'm visiting for the first time, I look at maps on my smartphone.
马上就能知道去车站和商店的路。: I can quickly find the way to stations and stores.
我经常给住在远方的奶奶发照片。: I often send photos to my grandmother, who lives far away.
日本的便利店里总是摆着很多饭团。: Japanese convenience stores always have lots of onigiri (rice balls) lined up.
有鲑鱼、金枪鱼蛋黄酱、梅干、海带等，口味很多。: There are many flavors, such as salmon, tuna mayonnaise, umeboshi (pickled plum), and kombu (kelp).
饭团有海苔脆脆的，也有海苔软软的。: Some onigiri have crisp nori, and some have soft nori.
海苔脆的饭团，吃之前要把外面的薄膜取下来。: With the crisp kind, you take off the outer plastic wrapper before eating.
请看着1、2、3的号码，慢慢地打开。: Follow the numbers 1, 2, and 3, and open it slowly.
海苔软的饭团，海苔一开始就贴在米饭上。: With the soft kind, the nori is already stuck to the rice from the start.
六月前后，日本下雨的日子变多了。: Around June, there are more rainy days in Japan.
这个季节叫做“梅雨”。: This season is called "tsuyu" (the rainy season).
绣球花在雨中开得很美。: Hydrangeas bloom beautifully in the rain.
下雨天，妹妹穿上红色的雨靴，撑着黄色的雨伞去上学。: On rainy days, my little sister wears red rain boots and carries a yellow umbrella to school.
妹妹非常喜欢雨靴。: My little sister loves her rain boots.
她穿着雨靴在水洼里走，笑着说“真好玩！”: She walks through puddles in her rain boots, laughing, "This is fun!"
我家有一只白色的狗。: We have a white dog at home.
每天早上和傍晚，我都和狗一起散步。: Every day, in the morning and in the evening, I go for a walk with the dog.
早上六点左右，我们走到家附近的公园。: In the morning, at around six, we walk to the park near my house.
在公园里，总是遇到同样的人。: At the park, I always see the same people.
有带着黑狗散步的老爷爷，还有每天早上跑步的女士。: There's an old man walking a black dog, and a woman who goes running every morning.
大家互相说\"早上好\"打招呼。: We all greet each other with "Good morning."
我不知道那些人叫什么，但他们的狗的名字我全都知道。: I don't know those people's names, but I know all of the dogs' names.
我们家周末大家一起看动画片。: At my house, we all watch anime together on weekends.
星期天早上，电视上有很多儿童动画片。: On Sunday mornings, there are lots of children's anime on TV.
吃早饭的时候，我和弟弟就坐到电视机前。: At breakfast, my little brother and I sit in front of the TV.
弟弟喜欢的角色是一个又强又有活力的男孩。: My little brother's favorite character is a strong, energetic boy.
我喜欢一个擅长画画、文静的女孩。: I like a quiet girl who is good at drawing.
爸爸妈妈有时也一起看，一起笑。: Our father and mother sometimes watch with us and laugh too.
真想快点看到下周的动画。: I can't wait to watch next week's anime too.
在日本，有很多骑自行车上学的高中生。: In Japan, many high school students ride their bikes to school.
我每天早上也从家骑自行车去学校，大约二十分钟。: I also ride my bike from home to school every morning, for about twenty minutes.
学校里有一个很大的自行车停车场。: My school has a large bicycle parking area.
停车场里，很多自行车排得整整齐齐。: In the bicycle parking area, lots of bikes are lined up neatly.
骑自行车也有重要的规则。: There are important rules for bicycles too.
晚上天黑，所以请打开车灯。: It's dark at night, so please turn on your light.
下雨天不能撑着伞骑车。: On rainy days, you must not ride while holding an umbrella.
在路上要好好看清车和行人，慢慢地骑吧。: On the road, watch carefully for cars and people, and ride slowly.
每三个月一次的期待: Something to look forward to every three months
日本的电视剧，一部通常三个月左右就播完了。: Japanese TV dramas usually tell one story over about three months.
因此，一到1月、4月、7月、10月，就会有很多新剧开播。: For that reason, lots of new dramas start in January, April, July, and October.
季节变换的时候，挑选看哪部剧也是一种乐趣。: When the season changes, choosing which dramas to watch is part of the fun.
电视剧每周在同一天的同一时间播出。: Dramas are broadcast every week on the same day at the same time.
比如，星期一晚上9点的电视剧被称为\"月9\"，很早以前就很有名。: For example, the 9 p.m. Monday drama is called 「月9」 (getsuku, "Monday 9"), and it has been famous for a long time.
因为一周只能看一集，所以会很想早点看到下一集。: Because you can only watch once a week, you can't wait to see the next episode.
第二天在学校或公司和朋友聊电视剧的人也很多。: Many people talk about the drama with their friends at school or work the next day.
最近，错过的集数也可以在网上看了。: These days, you can also watch episodes you missed on the internet.
尽管如此，仍然有很多人说喜欢每周等着那个时刻。: Even so, there are still many people who say they like waiting for that time slot every week.
乐趣，期待: enjoyment, something to look forward to
日本家庭的厨房里，大多有微波炉。: Most kitchens in Japanese homes have a microwave.
凉了的米饭和菜，用它的话一两分钟就热了。: Even rice or food that has gone cold warms up in a minute or two if you use it.
在便利店买便当时，店员会问\"需要加热吗？\": When you buy a bento at a convenience store, the clerk asks, "Would you like it heated?"
超市里摆着很多冷冻食品。: Supermarkets have lots of frozen food on the shelves.
饺子、意大利面、炸鸡块等，很多东西只要用微波炉加热就能吃。: Many foods, such as gyoza, pasta, and karaage (fried chicken), are ready to eat just by heating them in the microwave.
忙碌的日子里，真是帮了大忙。: This is very helpful on busy days.
但是，使用时也有需要注意的地方。: But there are also things you have to be careful about when using one.
放进铝箔的话，有时会冒出火花，很危险。: If you put aluminum foil in it, it can give off sparks, which is dangerous.
另外，带壳的鸡蛋直接放进去，可能会砰的一声爆裂。: Also, if you put in an egg with its shell still on, it can burst with a loud bang.
第一次使用之前，要先好好阅读说明书。: Before using it for the first time, be sure to read the instruction manual carefully.
去游戏厅玩吧: Let's have fun at the game center
日本的街上有很多游戏厅。: There are lots of game centers (arcades) in Japanese towns.
游戏厅开在车站附近或大商场里，很受学生和成年人的欢迎。: They're near stations or inside big stores, and they're popular with both students and adults.
一走进店里，音乐声和各种声音非常热闹。: When you go inside, it's very lively, with music and all kinds of sounds.
其中，最受欢迎的是抓娃娃机。: The most popular of all are the crane games.
按下按钮，去夹里面摆着的毛绒玩具或零食。: You press buttons to grab the stuffed toys or snacks lined up inside.
看起来很简单，却很难夹到。: It looks easy, but it's surprisingly hard to get anything.
夹不到的时候，有时店员还会帮忙把奖品的位置稍微挪一挪。: When it's not going well, a staff member will sometimes move the prize a little for you.
和朋友一起去的话，也常常拍大头贴。: When I go with friends, we often take purikura (photo sticker booth pictures) too.
拍完照后在屏幕上写字画画，就会变成贴纸出来。: After taking the photos, you write words or draw pictures on the screen, and they come out as stickers.
做好的贴纸大家分一分，好好留着，以便回想起那快乐的一天。: We share the finished stickers and keep them carefully so we can remember the fun day.
有些人喜欢下班后去附近的钱汤。: Some people like going to a neighborhood sento (public bath) after work.
在入口脱下鞋子，放进鞋柜。: At the entrance, you take off your shoes and put them in a shoe locker.
在老式钱汤里，鞋柜的钥匙是木头做的，很有意思。: At old sento, the shoe locker keys are made of wood, which is interesting.
进浴池之前，先用热水冲一冲，把身体弄干净。: Before getting into the bath, you first pour hot water over yourself to clean your body.
钱汤的水常常比家里的洗澡水烫，所以要慢慢地进去，直到适应水温。: The water at a sento is often hotter than a bath at home, so you get in slowly until you get used to it.
洗完出来时，进更衣室之前要先用毛巾把身体擦干。: When you get out of the bath, you dry yourself off with a towel before going into the changing room.
因为地板湿了的话，可能会有人滑倒受伤。: That's because if the floor is wet, someone might slip and get hurt.
出浴后的乐趣，是一瓶冰凉的瓶装牛奶。: The treat after a bath is a well-chilled bottle of milk.
选咖啡牛奶和水果牛奶的人也很多。: Many people choose coffee milk or fruit milk.
一只手叉着腰一口气喝完，是从以前就固定下来的喝法。: Putting one hand on your hip and drinking it all in one go is the traditional way to drink it.
定下来，固定: to be decided, to be fixed
郊游去动物园: A school trip to the zoo
日本的小学在春天或秋天会组织郊游。: Japanese elementary schools have field trips in spring or fall.
郊游常去的地方之一，就是动物园。: One of the places they often go is the zoo.
东京的上野动物园建于1882年，是日本最古老的动物园。: Ueno Zoo in Tokyo, built in 1882, is the oldest zoo in Japan.
孩子们在背包里装上便当、水壶，还有零食，然后出发。: The children pack bento, water bottles, and snacks in their backpacks and set off.
在动物园里，特别想看长颈鹿、大象、狮子等大型动物的孩子很多。: At the zoo, many children especially want to see big animals like giraffes, elephants, and lions.
也有动物园可以从水下观看企鹅游泳的样子。: Some zoos let you watch penguins swimming from underwater.
孩子们会画动物，或者把注意到的事情记在本子上。: The children draw pictures of the animals and write down things they notice in their notebooks.
中午，大家聚到宽敞的地方，一起吃便当。: At noon, they gather in an open area and eat their bento together.
回到家后，孩子们会跟家人讲很多\"今天看到的动物\"。: When they get home, the children tell their families all about "the animals I saw today."
在日本，每天早上的电视节目都会播天气预报。: In Japan, the weather forecast is broadcast on TV programs every morning.
天气预报里，除了晴天、下雨，还常常出现\"降水概率\"。: Weather forecasts don't just tell you whether it will be sunny or rainy; they also often give the 「降水確率」 (kōsui kakuritsu, chance of precipitation).
这指的是下1毫米以上雨或雪的可能性。: This is the probability of 1 millimeter or more of rain or snow falling.
有0%、10%、20%……这样以10%为单位一直到100%。: It goes 0%, 10%, 20%, and so on, in steps of 10% up to 100%.
即使是同一天，上午和下午比起来，概率也可能不同。: Even on the same day, the chance may differ between morning and afternoon.
那么，概率是多少的时候该带伞呢？: So at what percentage should you take an umbrella?
30%也会担心的人，会在包里放一把小折叠伞。: For example, people who worry even at 30% keep a small folding umbrella in their bag.
也有人给自己定下规矩：超过50%就带伞。: Some people have decided they'll take one if it's over 50%.
因为在便利店就能买到伞，所以也有人什么都不带就出门了。: Since you can easily buy an umbrella at a convenience store, some people go out without bringing one at all.
漫画咖啡馆是可以随意阅读大量漫画的店。: A manga cafe is a place where you can read lots of manga freely.
它也被称为\"网咖\"，常开在车站附近。: They are also called 「ネットカフェ」 (net cafes), and they're often near stations.
从热门漫画到老漫画，书架上摆得满满的。: The bookshelves are lined with lots of manga, from popular titles to old ones.
第一次使用时，要在前台办一张这家店的卡。: When you use one for the first time, you get a card for that shop at the front desk.
这时一般需要出示能证明姓名和住址的证件。: At this point, you usually have to show something with your name and address on it.
费用按使用时间计算，所以要先想好待几个小时再进去。: What you pay depends on how long you stay, so you decide how many hours you'll be there before going in.
座位像一个个小房间，有带电脑的，也有可以躺下的。: The seats are like little rooms, and some have computers while others let you lie down.
很多店里果汁和咖啡可以随便喝。: Many places also let you drink as much juice and coffee as you like.
周围的人也都很安静，所以不能大声说话或打电话。: The people around you are being quiet too, so you must not talk loudly or make phone calls.
看完的漫画，请放回原来的地方。: Put manga you've finished back where you found them.
决定，定下来: to be decided, to be settled
日本的城镇里，附近一般都有百元店。: In Japanese towns, there's usually a 100-yen shop nearby.
店里从本子、笔到盘子、杯子，什么都有。: Inside, they have everything from notebooks and pens to plates and cups.
做饭和打扫用的便利工具也很多，光是看看就很开心。: There are also lots of handy tools for cooking and cleaning, so just looking around is fun.
卖的东西会随季节变化，这也是有趣的地方。: One interesting thing is that what they sell changes with the seasons.
秋天会摆出万圣节的装饰品，冬天则会摆出圣诞节和新年的东西。: In the fall, there are Halloween decorations, and in winter, things for Christmas and New Year's.
虽然名字叫“100日元”，但也有一些比这贵的东西，要注意哦。: The name says "100 yen," but some things cost more than that, so be careful.
来日本旅游的人有时也会在这里买很多伴手礼回去。: Visitors to Japan sometimes buy lots of souvenirs there.
对刚搬家的人来说，这也是非常有帮助的店。: It's also a very useful shop for people who have just moved.
在日本，很多人通过快递接收网上买的东西。: In Japan, many people receive things they've bought online by home delivery.
但是，也有很多人因为工作白天不在家。: But many people aren't at home during the day because of work.
如果家里没人，送货司机就会把“不在家通知单”放进信箱后离开。: When nobody is home, the driver puts a 「不在票」 (fuzaihyō, missed-delivery notice) in the mailbox and leaves.
这种情况下，就要用电话或手机申请“再次配送”。: In that case, you request 「再配達」 (saihaitatsu, redelivery) by phone or smartphone.
再次配送对司机来说很辛苦，所以其他方式也多了起来。: Delivering a second time is hard on the drivers, so other options have been increasing.
一种是让对方把包裹放在门前的“放门口”。: One is 「置き配」 (okihai), where you have the package left in front of your door.
另外，也可以在附近的便利店，在自己方便的时间领取包裹。: You can also pick up your package at a nearby convenience store at a time that suits you.
如果使用车站等地方的快递柜，不用见任何人就能取到包裹。: If you use a parcel locker at a station or elsewhere, you can get your package without meeting anyone.
选择适合自己生活的方式，会非常方便。: Choosing the method that fits your lifestyle makes things very convenient.
春天樱花盛开，景色也很美，是非常舒服的季节。: Spring is a very pleasant season, with cherry blossoms in bloom and beautiful scenery.
但是，在日本也有人有点害怕春天的到来。: But in Japan, some people are a little afraid of spring coming.
原因是一种叫“花粉症”的病。: The reason is an illness called 「花粉症」 (kafunshō, hay fever).
得了这种病，就会喷嚏、鼻涕停不下来。: When you have it, you can't stop sneezing and your nose won't stop running.
也有很多人眼睛发痒、发红。: Many people also get itchy, red eyes.
在日本，据说山里大量种植的杉树的花粉是最主要的原因。: In Japan, pollen from the Japanese cedar trees planted in large numbers on the mountains is said to be the biggest cause.
到了这个季节，电视的天气预报也会告诉大家花粉会飞散多少。: During this season, TV weather forecasts also tell you how much pollen will be in the air.
出门的时候，人们戴上口罩、戴上眼镜，注意不让花粉进入眼睛和鼻子。: When going outside, people wear masks and glasses, taking care to keep pollen out of their eyes and noses.
进家门前先把衣服上沾的花粉好好拍掉也很重要。: It's also important to brush the pollen off your clothes well before going inside.
卡拉OK一个人也开心: Karaoke is fun even on your own
卡拉OK诞生于日本，现在全世界的人都在享受它。: Karaoke was born in Japan and is now enjoyed all over the world.
在日本的“卡拉OK包厢”里，人们租一个小房间唱歌。: At a Japanese 「カラオケボックス」 (karaoke box), you rent a small room and sing.
房间里有电视和麦克风，还能用电话或平板点饮料。: The room has a TV and microphones, and you can also order drinks by phone or tablet.
和朋友一起去的话，大家唱自己喜欢的歌，气氛非常热闹。: When you go with friends, everyone sings their favorite songs, and it gets very lively.
还有能给唱歌水平打分的机器，也有人和朋友比分数，看谁能赢。: There are also machines that score how well you sing, and some people compare scores with their friends to compete over who wins.
最近，喜欢一个人去的“一人卡拉OK”的人也多了起来。: Recently, more people have come to enjoy 「ヒトカラ」 (hitokara), going to karaoke alone.
一个人的话，不用顾虑任何人，同一首歌可以练好多遍。: On your own, you don't have to worry about the people around you, and you can practice the same song over and over.
压力大的时候，大声唱歌会让心情变得畅快哦。: When stress builds up, singing at the top of your voice will make you feel refreshed.
暑假早晨的广播体操: Radio exercises on summer vacation mornings
广播体操是跟着广播里的音乐做的简短体操。: Radio taiso (radio exercises) is a short set of exercises done along with music on the radio.
NHK的广播每天早上6点30分开始播放。: On NHK radio, it's broadcast every morning starting at 6:30.
在日本，从小孩到老人，几乎所有人都知道它的做法。: In Japan, almost everyone, from children to the elderly, knows how to do it.
特别是暑假早上的广播体操，很多人都会回想起来。: In particular, many people have memories of radio exercises on summer vacation mornings.
孩子们一大早起床，聚集到附近的公园。: Children get up early in the morning and gather at a neighborhood park.
做完操后，大人会在挂在脖子上的卡片上盖章。: When the exercises are over, they get a stamp on the card hanging around their neck.
如果每天坚持不缺席，最后一天有时还能领到零食等奖励。: If they keep coming every day without missing one, they sometimes get snacks or other treats on the last day.
即使很困，也有很多人为了得到印章而努力起床吧。: Many people probably dragged themselves out of bed, even when sleepy, because they wanted the stamp.
自动售货机的“热乎乎”: The 「あったか〜い」 (nice and warm) drinks in vending machines
在日本，路口和车站等，城里的很多地方都有自动售货机。: In Japan, there are vending machines in all sorts of places around town, such as street corners and stations.
因为晚上也亮着灯，在黑暗的路上会让人稍微安心一点。: They're lit up and bright even at night, so they make you feel a little safer on dark streets.
一台机器同时卖冷饮和热饮是很常见的。: It's common for a single machine to sell both cold and hot drinks.
按钮附近写着“冰凉凉”“热乎乎”，所以一看就懂。: Near the buttons, it says 「つめた〜い」 (nice and cold) or 「あったか〜い」 (nice and warm), so you can tell right away.
秋天到了、天气变冷，“热乎乎”的饮料就会渐渐增多。: When fall comes and the weather turns cold, the number of 「あったか〜い」 drinks gradually increases.
然后到了春天，又会换回冷饮。: Then, when spring comes, they switch back to cold drinks.
热饮不只有咖啡和茶，还有玉米浓汤。: The hot drinks include not only coffee and tea, but also corn soup.
特别是寒冷的冬天早上，光是手里握着一罐热饮，身心就觉得很舒服。: Especially on cold winter mornings, just holding a hot drink in your hands makes both body and heart feel happy.
在喜欢动漫的人之间，“圣地巡礼”这个词经常被使用。: Among anime fans, the phrase 「聖地巡礼」 (seichi junrei, "pilgrimage to sacred sites") is often used.
这是指实际去拜访动漫里出现的城镇。: It means actually visiting towns that appear in anime.
看到动漫里的车站和坡道真的就在那里，会非常感动。: Seeing a station or a sloping street from an anime really there in front of you is very moving.
特别有名的地方之一，是位于神奈川县镰仓市的江之电的道口。: One especially famous spot is a railroad crossing on the Enoden line in Kamakura, Kanagawa Prefecture.
因为它出现在《灌篮高手》的片头里，所以有很多人从国外来到这里。: Because it appears in the opening of Slam Dunk, many people come even from abroad.
喜欢动漫的人们会拍出和动漫画面看起来一样的照片来享受乐趣。: Anime fans enjoy taking photos that look just like the scenes in the anime.
镇上的人也为有很多人来访而高兴。: The local people are also happy that so many people come.
但是，不能忘记那里还有当地居民的生活。: But you must not forget that people live their daily lives there.
不要在路上散开挡道，安静地参观，这是重要的礼仪。: Not spreading out across the street and sightseeing quietly are important manners.
圣地巡礼（走访作品取景地）: pilgrimage to sacred sites (visiting real places that appear in a work)
用声音注入生命的工作: A job that breathes life into characters with the voice
在日本，为动画角色配音的人被称为“声优”。: In Japan, people who give voices to anime characters are called 「声優」 (seiyū, voice actors).
声优不露脸，必须只靠声音来表现喜悦、悲伤、愤怒等情感。: Voice actors don't show their faces; they have to express emotions such as joy, sadness, and anger with their voices alone.
同一个人有时会扮演从活泼的孩子到可怕的反派等完全不同的角色。: The same person may play completely different roles, from a lively child to a frightening villain.
动画的录音被称为“后期配音”，是配合画面把声音录进去。: Recording for anime is called 「アフレコ」 (afureko, after-recording), and the voices are recorded to match what's on screen.
在录音棚里，好几位声优依次站到麦克风前，一边看台本一边表演。: In the studio, several voice actors take turns standing in front of the microphones and act while looking at the script.
静悄悄地行动，不让翻台本的纸声被麦克风录进去，这也是一项重要的技术。: Moving quietly so that the microphones don't pick up the sound of script pages turning is also an important skill.
把外国电影和电视剧配成日语的“配音”，对声优来说也是重要的工作。: 「吹き替え」 (fukikae, dubbing), putting foreign movies and dramas into Japanese, is also important work for voice actors.
最近的声优不只在麦克风前工作，还会参加广播节目和各种活动。: Voice actors these days don't just work in front of a microphone; they also appear on radio programs and at events.
发表歌曲、在舞台上唱歌的人也并不少见。: It's not unusual for them to release songs or sing on stage.
因此，也有很多年轻人为了成为声优，在专门学校里努力学习。: That's why there are many young people studying hard at specialized schools to become voice actors.
NHK的“连续电视小说”被很多人称为“晨间剧”，长期以来深受喜爱。: NHK's 「連続テレビ小説」 (renzoku terebi shōsetsu, "serial TV novel") is called 「朝ドラ」 (asadora, morning drama) by many people, and it has been loved for a long time.
每天早上8点开始播放15分钟，一部作品大约持续半年。: It airs for 15 minutes from 8 every morning, and each drama runs for about half a year.
新作品一般定在春天和秋天开播。: New dramas generally start in spring and fall.
晨间剧大多是讲述一位女性一边克服困难一边成长的故事。: Many asadora are stories of a woman who grows as she overcomes hardships.
以真实人物为原型的作品也很多，也有人看了剧之后开始对那个人物产生兴趣。: Many are based on real people, and some viewers become interested in those people after watching.
主角演员多是通过试镜选出的，有时也会选中还不太出名的人。: The actor who plays the lead is often chosen by audition, and sometimes someone not yet well known is chosen.
因为晨间剧而成名的演员多得数不清。: Countless actors have become famous thanks to asadora.
因为每集很短，很多人似乎是边吃早饭、或边做出门准备边看。: Since each episode is short, many people seem to watch while eating breakfast or getting ready to go out.
因为剧情每天推进一点点，让人在意后续，不知不觉每天早上都会打开电视。: Because the story moves forward a little each day, you want to know what happens next, and you end up turning on the TV every morning.
在公司或学校里，有时会听到“今天早上的晨间剧，看了吗？”这样的对话。: At work or school, you may even overhear conversations like "Did you see this morning's asadora?"
爱、喜爱: to love, to be fond of
主人不在时干活的机器人: The robot that works while you're out
最近，使用能在地板上自动移动打扫的“扫地机器人”的家庭越来越多。: Recently, more and more households are using 「ロボット掃除機」 (robot vacuum cleaners), which move across the floor automatically and clean.
只要用手机预先设定好时间，它就会在家里没人的时候把房间打扫干净。: If you set a time with your smartphone, it cleans your room while you're out.
下班回家时，看到地板干干净净，实在是件令人高兴的事。: Coming home from work to find the floor clean is a truly happy thing.
扫地机器人装有传感器，快要撞到墙壁或家具时，会自己判断并改变方向。: Robot vacuums have sensors, and when one is about to bump into a wall or furniture, it decides for itself and changes direction.
它还能发现楼梯这样的高低差，并停下来以免掉下去。: It can also detect drops like stairs and stop so it doesn't fall.
打扫完毕或剩余电量不足时，它会自己回到充电座。: When it finishes cleaning or its battery is running low, it goes back to its charging dock by itself.
不过，如果地板上一直掉着电线或袜子，它有时会把它们卷进去而停下来。: However, if cords or socks are left lying on the floor, it may get them tangled up and stop.
因此，据说很多人养成了使用前先收拾地板的习惯。: Because of this, many people have reportedly gotten into the habit of tidying up the floor before using it.
在养狗或猫的家庭里，它能吸走每天掉落的宠物毛，所以对保持房间清洁特别方便。: In homes with dogs or cats, it sucks up the pet hair that falls every day, so it's especially handy for keeping rooms clean.
其中还有坐在扫地机器人上在房间里转来转去的猫，那样的视频很受欢迎。: Some cats even ride around the room on top of robot vacuums, and videos of them are popular.
也有人给它起名字，简直像家庭成员一样疼爱它。: Some people give theirs a name and dote on it as if it were a member of the family.
收拾；整理: to tidy up; to put in order
饲养: to keep (a pet), to raise (an animal)
为球场染上颜色的支持者们: The supporters who color the stadium
J联赛是1993年开始的日本职业足球联赛。: The J.League is Japan's professional soccer league, which started in 1993.
每个俱乐部都有被称为“主场城市”的本地城镇，非常重视和当地的联系。: Each club has a local town called its 「ホームタウン」 (hometown), and the clubs value their ties with the community.
球员们有时会去当地的小学访问，或者参加镇上的祭典。: Players sometimes visit local elementary schools or take part in town festivals.
比赛日，球场里挤满了穿着球队颜色球衣的支持者。: On match days, the stadium fills up with supporters wearing jerseys in their team's colors.
特别是球门后方的座位区，支持者们在整场比赛中一直站着唱助威歌。: Especially in the seats behind the goal, supporters stay on their feet the whole match, singing cheering songs.
随着太鼓的节奏，几千人的声音合而为一，那种场面比在电视上看更震撼。: Thousands of voices joining together to the rhythm of the drums is far more powerful than watching on TV.
大家有时还会把挂在脖子上的毛巾围巾一起举过头顶展开，迎接球员。: Sometimes everyone holds the towel scarves from around their necks spread out above their heads to welcome the players.
也有热心的支持者会到很远的城市去为客场比赛加油。: Some passionate supporters even travel to faraway cities to cheer at away games.
赢的日子会和陌生人击掌庆祝，输的日子大家一起分担不甘心。: On days they win, they high-five even strangers, and on days they lose, they all share the frustration.
即使对足球不太了解，也请去球场亲身感受一次那种氛围。: Even if you don't know much about soccer, try experiencing the atmosphere at a stadium at least once.
展开: to spread out, to open up
用手机付款，攒积分: Pay by smartphone and collect points
在日本，这几年用手机付款的人迅速增加了。: In Japan, the number of people paying with smartphones has grown rapidly in the past few years.
在收银台付款时，只需在应用画面上显示条形码给店员看就行。: When paying at the register, you just display a barcode on the app screen and show it to the clerk.
根据店铺不同，也有用自己的手机扫描放在收银台附近的二维码来付款的方式。: At some stores, you can also pay by scanning a QR code placed near the register with your own smartphone.
因为不用掏钱包，着急的时候非常方便。: You don't need to take out your wallet, so it's extremely convenient when you're in a hurry.
手机支付的乐趣之一，是每次购物都能攒下的积分。: One of the pleasures of smartphone payment is the points you earn every time you shop.
攒下的积分可以在下次购物时代替现金使用。: You can use the points you've saved up in place of money on your next purchase.
也有人为了多得一点积分，先比较用哪个应用付款再去购物。: To get even a few more points, some people compare which app to pay with before they shop.
不过，至今只能用现金的小店、老字号食堂也还有不少。: However, even now there are quite a few small shops and long-established diners that only take cash.
另外，如果手机没电了，就无法付款了。: Also, if your smartphone's battery dies, you won't be able to pay.
因此，即使是习惯了手机支付的人，为防万一在钱包里放一点现金也会比较安心。: So even if you're used to paying by smartphone, it's reassuring to keep a little cash in your wallet just in case.
防备、准备: to be prepared for, to prepare
假日在客厅开游戏大赛: Video game tournaments in the living room on days off
以前，好像有很多大人认为“游戏是小孩玩的东西”。: In the past, it seems many adults thought, "Video games are for kids."
但是现在，假日里聚在客厅、全家人一起玩同一款游戏的家庭也不少见了。: But now, it's not unusual for families to gather in the living room on days off and all enjoy the same game together.
小时候沉迷于游戏的一代人当了父母，这大概也是原因之一吧。: One reason is probably that the generation who were crazy about games as children have now become parents.
特别受欢迎的是能在电视前几个人一起玩的游戏。: Especially popular are games that several people can play together in front of the TV.
玩赛车或体育游戏比赛时，有时孩子赢了父母，露出得意的表情。: When they compete in racing or sports games, sometimes a child beats a parent and looks proud of it.
在齐心协力朝一个目标努力的游戏中，对话会自然地多起来。: In games where you work together toward a single goal, conversation naturally increases.
据说也有爷爷奶奶在正月里，在自己家和孙子孙女一起玩游戏。: Some grandparents reportedly play games with their grandchildren at their home over New Year's.
另一方面，对玩游戏的时间定了规矩的家庭也不少。: On the other hand, quite a few families have set rules about game time.
比如“不写完作业就不玩”“每天最多一小时”等，全家人商量着制定规则。: Families talk it over and make rules such as "No playing until your homework is done" and "Up to one hour a day."
据说不只是孩子，父母也认真遵守规则，这才是能开心玩下去的诀窍。: They say the key to keeping it fun is for not only the children but also the parents to follow the rules properly.
应急背包里装什么: What goes in an emergency bag
在地震和台风很多的日本，很多家庭都准备了“应急背包”。: In Japan, where earthquakes and typhoons are common, many households have a 「非常持ち出し袋」 (hijō mochidashi bukuro, emergency grab bag) ready.
这是在灾害发生、必须立刻离开家时，带着逃生用的包。: This is a bag to grab and take with you when a disaster strikes and you have to leave your home right away.
据说为了能腾出双手，应该把东西整理放进双肩背包里。: It's said you should pack everything in a backpack so that both hands are free.
里面要放的东西中最重要的是水和食物。: The most important things to put in it are water and food.
水的大致标准是每人每天3升，食物则是没有热水也能直接吃的东西比较方便。: The guideline for water is 3 liters per person per day, and for food, things you can eat as they are without hot water are convenient.
此外，还需要手电筒、收音机、电池、手机充电器和药品等。: You'll also need things like a flashlight, a radio, batteries, a smartphone charger, and medicine.
如果再放进用来呼救的哨子和少量现金，就更安心了。: It's reassuring to also put in a whistle for calling for help and a little cash.
不过，并不是准备好包就万事大吉了。: However, preparing the bag doesn't mean that's enough.
食物和水有保质期，所以需要定期检查里面的东西，换成新的。: Food and water have expiration dates, so you need to check the contents regularly and replace them with new ones.
在9月1日的“防灾日”等日子里，全家一起检查包里的东西，也事先商量好逃生的地点吧: On days like 「防災の日」 (Disaster Prevention Day) on September 1, check the contents as a family and also talk about where to evacuate to.
元旦的信箱: The mailbox on New Year's Day
元旦早上，在日本的很多家庭里，打开信箱是一件小小的乐事。: On the morning of New Year's Day, opening the mailbox is a small pleasure for many households in Japan.
因为年底前投进邮筒的贺年卡，会在1月1日集中投递。: That's because nengajo (New Year's cards) mailed by the end of the year are delivered all at once on January 1.
一家人一边分贺年卡，一边说着“这是爸爸公司同事寄来的”之类的话，也是很有新年气氛: A family sorting the cards while saying things like "This one's from someone at Dad's company" is one of the classic scenes of New Year's.
贺年卡上常常画着当年生肖的动物。: Nengajo often have a picture of that year's zodiac animal on them.
因为生肖有十二种，所以同一种动物十二年才轮到一次。: There are twelve zodiac animals, so the same animal comes around only once every 12 years.
有小孩的家庭也常常印上全家福，告诉大家孩子成长的情况。: Families with small children often print family photos to let people know how the children have grown.
能知道平时难得见面的朋友的近况，也可以说是贺年卡的好处吧。: Being able to find out how friends you rarely see are doing could also be called one of the good things about nengajo.
但是最近，用电子邮件或社交软件完成拜年的人越来越多了。: But recently, more people have been taking care of their New Year's greetings by email or social media.
告知对方今后不再寄贺年卡的“贺年卡收尾”这个说法，也越来越常听到了。: The phrase 「年賀状じまい」 (nengajo jimai), which means telling people you will stop sending New Year's cards, has also come to be heard often.
即使拜年的方式改变了，在新年伊始想念重要之人的心情，今后也一定不会改变。: Even if the way we send greetings changes, the feeling of thinking of the people who matter to us at the start of a new year will surely never change.
做完，办完: to finish, to take care of
在日本，有很多动画在夜里12点以后才播出。: In Japan, many anime are broadcast after midnight.
这类节目被称为“深夜动画”。: These programs are called 「深夜アニメ」 (shinya anime, late-night anime).
与其说是面向儿童，不如说很多作品是以成人和学生观众为对象制作的。: Rather than being for children, many of them are made for adult and student fans.
因此，故事有时比较复杂，有时也会有一些吓人的场面。: Because of that, the stories may be complex or have somewhat frightening scenes.
不过，忍着困意熬到半夜，实际上是相当辛苦的。: But fighting off sleep to stay up until the middle of the night is actually quite hard.
第二天要上班或上学的人，有时会采取先录下来、到周末再集中看的方法。: People who have work or school the next day sometimes record the shows and watch them all at once on the weekend.
最近，播出结束后马上在网上播放的作品也多了起来。: Recently, more shows are being streamed online right after they air.
只要有智能手机，在上班的电车里也能看。: As long as you have a smartphone, you can watch them even on the train to work.
即便如此，也有粉丝会在播出时间守在电视机前。: Even so, some fans wait in front of the TV for the broadcast time.
因为一边在社交网络上和其他粉丝互相交流感想一边看，实在太有意思了。: That's because watching while sharing reactions with other fans on social media is just too much fun.
据说虽然是半夜，却总觉得屏幕那头有很多同伴。: Even though it's the middle of the night, they say it feels like there are lots of friends on the other side of the screen.
日本的电视剧大多都有“主题曲”。: Japanese dramas usually have a 「主題歌」 (shudaika, theme song).
很多时候，人气歌手或乐队会为这部剧创作新歌。: Popular singers and bands often write new songs for the drama.
因为歌曲每集都会在相似的场景响起，所以会自然地留在观众的记忆中。: The song plays at similar moments in every episode, so it naturally sticks in viewers' memories.
尤其常用的方法是在故事最高潮的地方放这首歌。: In particular, playing the song at the story's most exciting point is a commonly used technique.
电视剧越是成为话题，主题曲也越畅销。: The more a drama gets talked about, the better its theme song sells.
播出期间，在街上的店里和广播里也经常听到这首歌。: While the drama is airing, you often hear the song in shops around town and on the radio.
在卡拉OK唱的人也多了起来，甚至连没看过这部剧的人都记住了这首歌。: More people sing it at karaoke, to the point that even people who haven't watched the drama end up learning the song.
不可思议的是，无论过了多少年，每当听到那首歌，剧中的场景就会浮现在眼前。: Strangely, no matter how many years pass, every time you hear the song, scenes from the drama come to mind.
甚至连自己当时在做什么都能回想起来的人也不在少数。: Quite a few people even remember what they themselves were doing at the time.
主题曲和电视剧一起，成为了观众珍贵回忆的一部分。: Together with the drama, the theme song becomes part of viewers' precious memories.
“推”指的是自己最支持的角色或偶像。: 「推し」 (oshi) means the character or idol you support the most.
而为了支持“推”所做的各种活动，就叫做“推活”。: And all the various activities you do to support your oshi are called 「推し活」 (oshikatsu).
比如收集周边、参加演唱会或活动，都是推活的一种。: For example, collecting merchandise and going to concerts or events are forms of oshikatsu.
也有人会穿着代表自己“推”的颜色的衣服出门。: Some people go out wearing clothes in their oshi's signature color.
在街上也经常能看到背着挂满徽章的包走路的人。: You also often see people around town carrying bags covered in pin badges.
对于做推活的人来说，特别重要的纪念日是“推”的生日。: For people who do oshikatsu, an especially important day is their oshi's birthday.
那一天，大家会准备蛋糕，或者把周边摆好拍照来庆祝。: On that day, they celebrate by getting a cake ready, lining up their merchandise and taking photos, and so on.
即使是现实中并不存在的动画角色，大家也会像对待真正的朋友一样为其庆生。: Even if the oshi is an anime character who doesn't actually exist, fans celebrate their birthday as if they were a real friend.
有时也会有粉丝聚在咖啡馆等地方，举办庆祝会。: Sometimes fans gather at cafes or other places to hold celebrations.
当然，也要注意别因为花太多钱和时间而影响日常生活。: Of course, you also need to be careful not to spend so much money or time that your everyday life suffers.
尽管如此，很多人说多亏有了“推”，每天都变得明亮又幸福。: Even so, many people say that having an oshi has made every day brighter and happier.
东京的秋叶原一直以来以“电器街”闻名。: Tokyo's Akihabara has long been known as 「電気街」 (denki-gai, Electric Town).
据说起源是战争结束后，卖收音机零件的小店聚集到了这一带。: It is said to have started when small shops selling radio parts gathered in this area after the war ended.
之后，“买电视、冰箱等家电就去秋叶原”的时代持续了很久。: After that, for a long time, Akihabara was the place to go if you wanted to buy home appliances such as TVs and refrigerators.
后来电脑店多了起来，游戏和动画的店铺也接连诞生。: Eventually, computer shops increased, and game and anime shops sprang up one after another.
现在走在秋叶原，映入眼帘的是巨大的动画广告牌和手办店。: Walking through Akihabara today, you see big anime billboards and figure shops.
穿着女仆装的店员以“欢迎回来”迎接客人的女仆咖啡厅也很有名。: Maid cafes, where staff dressed as maids greet you with 「お帰りなさいませ」 ("Welcome home"), are also famous.
另一方面，卖小型电子零件的店铺至今仍留在车站附近。: On the other hand, shops selling small electronic parts still remain near the station.
星期天等日子，街区中心的大马路有时会变成步行街。: On Sundays and other days, the main street in the center of the area sometimes becomes a pedestrian-only zone.
最近，来自海外的游客也多了很多。: Recently, the number of tourists from overseas has also grown enormously.
也有人很开心地买走在自己国家看得入迷的动画的周边。: Some happily buy merchandise from anime they were hooked on back in their own countries.
新旧交融的独特氛围，或许这正是秋叶原的魅力所在。: Its unique atmosphere, a mix of old and new, may be exactly what makes Akihabara so appealing.
Comic Market是日本最大的同人志即卖会。: Comic Market is Japan's largest doujinshi sales event.
在粉丝之间，它被简称为“Comike”。: Among fans, it is called by the short name 「コミケ」 (Comiket).
同人志是指非专业人士自己出钱制作的书。: Doujinshi are books that non-professionals make with their own money.
其中既有想象喜爱的动画或漫画的后续而画的作品，也有完全原创的作品。: Some are works that imagine what happens next in a favorite anime or manga, and others are completely original.
它始于1975年，现在每年夏天和冬天各举办一次，地点在东京Big Sight。: It started in 1975 and is now held twice a year, in summer and winter, at Tokyo Big Sight.
会有几十万人从全国各地聚集到会场。: Hundreds of thousands of people gather at the venue from all over the country.
为了买到人气社团的本子，从一大早就排起了长队。: Long lines form from early in the morning as people try to get books from popular circles.
夏天特别热，所以别忘了带上水和毛巾，这很重要。: It's especially hot in summer, so it's important not to forget to bring water and a towel.
也有人cosplay参加，会场简直就像过节一样。: Some people come in cosplay, and the venue is just like a festival.
卖的人和买的人，都因“喜爱”这份心情而连在一起。: Both sellers and buyers are connected by the same feeling: "I love this."
据说在Comike，所有人都不被看作顾客，而被看作“参加者”。: At Comiket, everyone is said to be considered not a customer but a 「参加者」 (participant).
在东京三鹰市的井之头恩赐公园里，有一座吉卜力美术馆。: The Ghibli Museum is in Inokashira Onshi Park in Mitaka, Tokyo.
这座美术馆于2001年开馆，连建筑设计中也用到了宫崎骏导演的许多创意。: This museum opened in 2001, and many of director Hayao Miyazaki's ideas were used even in the design of the building.
要进入这座美术馆，必须提前预约门票。: To enter this museum, you have to reserve a ticket in advance.
门票指定了日期和时间，直接去美术馆是买不到的。: Tickets are for a set date and time, and you can't buy them by going directly to the museum.
馆内没有其他美术馆那样固定的参观路线。: Inside, there's no fixed route like at other museums.
往哪个方向走都可以，所以穿过小楼梯和窄窄的走廊，带着像迷了路一样的心情自由地走，: You can go in any direction you like, so the way to enjoy it here is to wander freely through small staircases and narrow hallways, feeling as if you've gotten lost.
也有介绍动画是如何制作出来、展示其过程的展区。: There's also a section that shows the process of how animated works are made.
小小的电影院里放映着只有在这里才能看到的短片。: In a small theater, short films that can only be seen here are shown.
馆内禁止拍照，所以看到的东西只能留在自己的眼里和心里。: Photography is prohibited inside, so you can only keep what you see in your eyes and heart.
屋顶花园里，一尊《天空之城》中出现的机器人士兵的大雕像，像守护着花园一样静静地伫: In the rooftop garden, a large statue of the robot soldier from Castle in the Sky stands quietly, as if guarding the garden.
无论对大人还是孩子来说，这都是一个能让人感觉仿佛走进了吉卜力故事中的地方。: For adults and children alike, it's a place where you can feel as if you've stepped into a Ghibli story.
冷冻食品是忙碌之人的好帮手: Frozen food: a friend to busy people
去日本的超市或便利店，会惊讶于冷冻食品的种类之多。: When you go to a Japanese supermarket or convenience store, you'll be surprised by the huge variety of frozen foods.
饺子、炒饭、乌冬面、意大利面等，从主食到配菜应有尽有。: They have everything from staples to side dishes, such as gyoza, fried rice, udon, and pasta.
最近，连冷冻蔬菜、水果甚至蛋糕都有卖。: Recently, frozen vegetables, fruit, and even cakes are sold.
只要用微波炉加热几分钟就能享受到店里一样味道的商品也不少。: Quite a few products let you enjoy restaurant-quality flavor just by heating them in the microwave for a few minutes.
特别方便的是便当用的小份配菜。: Especially handy are the small side dishes for bento.
其中还有一些商品，只要冻着直接放进便当盒，到中午左右就正好可以吃了。: Some of them, if you put them in your bento box still frozen, will be just right to eat around lunchtime.
在早上忙碌的时间里，省去了加热的工夫，真是帮了大忙。: Not having to bother heating them during the busy morning is a big help.
而且在解冻的过程中还能代替冰袋，让其他配菜也保持冰凉。: What's more, as they thaw, they act as an ice pack and keep the other dishes cool too.
以前也有人认为“用冷冻食品就是偷懒”。: In the past, some people thought, "Using frozen food is cutting corners."
但现在，它作为工作和育儿繁忙之人的得力帮手，被很多家庭使用。: But now it's used in many households as a powerful ally for people who are busy with work or raising children.
打开家里的冷冻室，或许能稍微看到这户人家的生活。: If you open a home's freezer, you may get a little glimpse of the life of that household.
坐日本的电车时，很多乘客会注意到车厢里非常安静。: When they ride a train in Japan, many passengers probably notice how quiet it is inside the car.
那是因为很多人都注意不给周围的人添麻烦。: That's because many people are careful not to bother those around them.
比如，在电车里用手机打电话，一般被认为是违反礼仪的。: For example, talking on a cell phone on the train is generally considered bad manners.
车厢里也经常播放广播，提醒乘客把手机调成静音模式。: Announcements asking passengers to put their phones on silent mode are also often played on board.
在拥挤的电车里，一般认为最好把双肩包抱在胸前，或者放到行李架上。: On crowded trains, it's considered best to hold your backpack in front of you or put it on the overhead rack.
因为一直背在背上的话，会撞到后面的人。: That's because if you keep it on your back, it will bump into the people behind you.
此外，站在门口附近的人，有时到站后会先下到站台上，为下车的乘客让出通道。: Also, when the train arrives at a station, people standing near the doors sometimes step off onto the platform for a moment to make way for passengers getting off.
车厢里还有被称为“优先席”的座位。: There are also seats on the train called "priority seats."
那是为老年人、身体不便的人、怀孕的人等准备的座位。: They are seats for elderly people, people with disabilities, pregnant women, and others.
如果空着，坐下也没关系，但有需要的人来了，就应该让座。: It's fine to sit in them if they're free, but when someone who needs one comes along, you should give up your seat.
小小的体贴，能让彼此的出行都更加舒适。: Small acts of consideration make the journey more comfortable for everyone.
抱，夹在怀里: to hold, to carry in one's arms
让给: to give up (something to someone), to hand over
奔跑的人与加油的人: Runners and the people who cheer them on
周末的早晨，有些日子城里的大马路上挤满的不是汽车，而是大批跑者。: On some weekend mornings, the big roads in town are filled not with cars but with crowds of runners.
那是市民参加的马拉松比赛。: It's a marathon that ordinary citizens take part in.
据说在日本，自从2007年东京马拉松开始以来，把跑步当作爱好的人大幅增加。: In Japan, the number of people who have taken up running as a hobby is said to have risen sharply since the Tokyo Marathon began in 2007.
参赛者不仅有专业选手，还有上班族、家庭主妇乃至老年人，形形色色。: The participants are not just professional athletes but all kinds of people, from office workers and homemakers to the elderly.
其中也有人打扮成喜欢的角色的样子跑步，让观众看得很开心。: Some even run dressed up as their favorite characters, entertaining the spectators.
全程马拉松的距离是42.195公里，绝不是件容易的事。: A full marathon is 42.195 kilometers, which is by no means easy.
赛道途中有补水站，志愿者会递上水和运动饮料。: There are water stations along the course, where volunteers hand out water and sports drinks.
道路两旁，家人和素不相识的人们都在大声加油。: On both sides of the road, family members and complete strangers cheer loudly.
据说在痛苦的时候听到别人喊“加油”，脚步就会不可思议地向前迈出。: They say that when you're struggling and someone shouts "Keep going!" to you, your legs somehow keep moving forward.
在很多比赛中，跑到终点的选手脖子上会被挂上奖牌，作为完赛的纪念。: At many races, runners who reach the finish line have a medal hung around their neck as a memento of finishing the race.
虽然成绩因人而异，但跑完全程的喜悦是大家共同的。: Finishing times may differ from person to person, but the joy of running all the way to the end is the same for everyone.
家电量贩店的乐趣: The fun of big electronics stores
大型车站附近，经常会有好几层楼高的家电量贩店。: Near large train stations, there are often big electronics stores that are several floors high.
一走进去，就能听到明快的音乐和店员充满活力的声音。: When you go inside, you hear upbeat music and the lively voices of the staff.
卖场里，电视、冰箱、相机、电脑等各种各样的产品多得数不清。: On the sales floors, countless products of all kinds, such as TVs, refrigerators, cameras, and computers, are on display.
家电量贩店的好处是可以实际试用最新的产品。: The great thing about electronics stores is that you can actually try out the latest products.
可以把新手机拿在手里感受重量，也可以在按摩椅上坐一坐。: You can pick up a new smartphone to feel how heavy it is, or try sitting in a massage chair.
在按摩椅卖场，常常能看到舒服地闭着眼睛的人。: In the massage chair section, you often see people with their eyes closed, looking very comfortable.
如果有不明白的地方，店员会耐心地说明各个产品之间的区别。: If you have any questions, the staff will carefully explain the differences between the products.
另一个特点是积分卡。: Another feature is the point card.
购物就能积攒积分，下次购物时可以代替现金使用。: When you shop, you build up points, which you can use instead of cash the next time you buy something.
正因为如此，很多顾客总是在同一家店购物。: That's why many customers always shop at the same store.
即使什么都不买，只是转一转看看新技术，也能玩上半天。: It's a place where you can have fun for half a day just looking around at the new technology, even without buying anything.

便利店店员的一天: A day in the life of a convenience store clerk
田中先生是便利店店员，从早上6点开始在车站前的店里工作。: Tanaka is a convenience store clerk who works at the store in front of the station from 6 a.m.
一到店里，他先听夜班店员交代工作。: On arriving at the store, Tanaka first gets a rundown of the work from the night-shift clerk.
过了7点，很多赶着去公司和学校的人来到店里，客人在收银台前排起队来。: After 7 o'clock, lots of people hurrying to work or school come in, and customers line up at the register.
“需要加热吗？”“您有积分卡吗？”这些话他一天要说很多遍。: "Would you like it heated up?" and "Do you have a point card?" are things Tanaka says many times a day.
他总是很小心，以免把钱找错。: Tanaka is always careful not to hand over the wrong amount of money.
客人少的时候，他把卡车运来的商品摆到货架上。: When there aren't many customers, Tanaka puts the goods delivered by truck out on the shelves.
便当和饭团一天要运来好几次，所以非常忙。: Bento and rice balls are delivered several times a day, so it's very busy.
另外，他还要炸东西、打扫厕所等等。: After that, Tanaka also does things like making fried food and cleaning the restroom.
