中午12点左右，客人又多起来，收银台很拥挤。: Around noon, more customers come in again, and the register gets crowded.
据说被客人说一声“谢谢”，即使很累也会变得高兴。: Apparently, being told "thank you" makes Tanaka happy even when tired.
北海道有一种人们常吃的肉类料理，叫做“成吉思汗烤肉”。: One meat dish that people in Hokkaido often eat is 「ジンギスカン」 (jingisukan, "Genghis Khan").
听到这个名字，你也许会以为它是蒙古料理。: Hearing the name, you might think it's a Mongolian dish.
名字来自蒙古的英雄成吉思汗，但它是在北海道诞生的料理。: The name comes from the Mongolian hero Genghis Khan, but it's actually a dish that was born in Hokkaido.
用的肉不是普通烤肉那样的牛肉或猪肉，而是羊肉。: The meat used is not beef or pork, as in ordinary yakiniku, but meat from sheep.
小羊的肉叫做“lamb（羔羊肉）”，成年羊的肉叫做“mutton（羊肉）”，味道: Meat from young sheep is called "lamb" and meat from adult sheep is called "mutton," and they taste slightly different.
做这道料理时，要准备一种中间像小山一样隆起的特殊铁锅。: To make this dish, you get out a special pan whose center rises up like a mountain.
在中间烤肉的话，肉里出来的油会往下流。: When you grill the meat in the middle, the fat from the meat runs down.
这样一来，周围的蔬菜也会因为这些油而变得好吃。: That fat then makes the vegetables around it tasty too.
听说在北海道，很多人在赏花或烧烤聚会的时候也会享用这道料理。: In Hokkaido, many people apparently enjoy this dish when they get together for cherry blossom viewing or barbecues as well.
诞生；出生: to come into being; to be born
站务员山田先生早上9点左右来到车站，一直工作到第二天早上。: Yamada, a station attendant, comes to the station around 9 a.m. and works until the next morning.
这种工作方式叫做“过夜值班”。: This kind of shift is called 「泊まり」 (tomari, an overnight shift).
晚上可以在车站里稍微睡一会儿。: At night, Yamada can get a little sleep in the station.
早上拥挤的时候，他站在站台上，注意看着让乘客能安全上车。: During the busy morning hours, Yamada stands on the platform, watching carefully so that passengers can board safely.
白天，他在检票口被人问路，或者接听失物的电话。: During the day, Yamada is asked for directions at the ticket gate and answers phone calls about lost items.
有坐轮椅的乘客来时，他会在电车和站台之间放上板子，帮助乘客上车。: When a passenger in a wheelchair comes, Yamada puts a board between the train and the platform and helps them get on.
据说最辛苦的是末班车开走之后，叫醒在车站里睡着的人。: Apparently the hardest part is waking up people who have fallen asleep in the station after the last train has left.
“不过，被人说一声谢谢的时候，我会非常高兴。”山田先生笑着说。: "But when people say thank you, it makes me really happy," Yamada says with a smile.
天气变冷的季节一到，日本便利店的收银台旁边就会开始摆上关东煮。: When the cold season comes, Japanese convenience stores start putting oden next to the register.
关东煮是把萝卜、鸡蛋、魔芋、竹轮等放在热汤里长时间炖煮的料理。: Oden is a dish of daikon radish, eggs, konjac, chikuwa fish cakes, and other ingredients simmered for a long time in hot broth.
客人可以一样一样地挑选自己喜欢的东西来买。: Customers can choose the items they like one by one and buy them.
拜托店员的话，店员会帮你装进杯子里。: If you ask the staff, they'll put them in a cup for you.
听说最受欢迎的是萝卜。: The most popular item is said to be daikon.
长时间炖煮后，味道会渗进萝卜里面，变得非常好吃。: When it's simmered for a long time, the flavor soaks all the way into the daikon, and it becomes really tasty.
关东煮的味道因地区不同而有些差别。: The flavor of oden differs slightly from region to region.
比如在爱知县等地，有时会蘸味噌吃。: For example, in places like Aichi Prefecture, people sometimes eat it with miso.
寒冷的日子里，在回家路上吃的热乎乎的关东煮，是日本冬天的乐趣之一。: Hot oden on the way home on a cold day is one of the pleasures of winter in Japan.
宫城县仙台市以“牛舌”之城而闻名。: Sendai in Miyagi Prefecture is famous as a city of 「牛タン」 (gyutan, beef tongue).
在仙台，会把它切得比普通烤肉更厚，用炭火来烤。: In Sendai, it's cut thicker than ordinary yakiniku meat and grilled over charcoal.
据说这种烤法是战争结束后由一位厨师开始的。: This way of grilling it is said to have been started by a cook after the war ended.
在店里吃饭的话，一般会和牛舌一起端上麦饭和牛尾汤。: When you eat at a restaurant, the beef tongue usually comes with barley rice and oxtail soup.
“tail（尾）”指的是牛的尾巴。: 「テール」 (from the English "tail") refers to the cow's tail.
牛舌很有嚼劲，嚼得越久，就越能尝出好味道。: Gyutan is pleasantly chewy, and the longer you chew it, the more flavor comes out.
仙台站也卖很多作为特产的牛舌，所以旅行回来后在家也能享用。: Lots of beef tongue is also sold as souvenirs at Sendai Station, so you can enjoy it at home after your trip, too.
快递司机的一天，从一大早在营业所把包裹装上卡车开始。: A delivery driver's day begins early in the morning with loading packages onto a truck at the branch office.
一天要送的包裹，多的时候会超过100件。: On busy days, the number of packages to deliver can be more than 100.
司机每天都一边开车，一边考虑按什么顺序跑才能早点结束。: Every day, drivers think as they drive about which order to make their rounds in so that they can finish quickly.
也有规定了送达时间的包裹，所以按计划跑完并不容易。: Some packages have to be delivered at set times, so sticking to the schedule isn't easy.
对司机来说，让人头疼的是送过去对方却不在家的时候。: What gives drivers trouble is when they go to make a delivery and the recipient isn't home.
这种情况下，就在信箱里放一张“不在家通知单”，然后去送下一个包裹。: In that case, they put a "missed-delivery notice" in the mailbox and head off to the next package.
收件人看到通知单后，会通过电话或网上申请再次配送。: The recipient sees the notice and requests redelivery by phone or online.
再次配送一多，司机就不得不一次次跑同一户人家，因此工作迟迟做不完。: When redeliveries increase, drivers have to go to the same homes again and again, and because of that, their work just doesn't get finished.
所以最近，为了减少再次配送，使用快递柜或者“放门口”的人也越来越多了。: That's why, recently, more people have started using delivery lockers or "leave at the door" delivery to reduce redeliveries.
饭团的打开方法: How to open a rice ball
日本的便利店里有各种各样的饭团。: Japanese convenience stores have many kinds of rice balls.
请仔细看看饭团。: Please look closely at the rice ball.
上面写着1、2、3。: The numbers 1, 2, and 3 are written on it.
首先，把1号胶带从中间往下拉到底。: First, pull tape 1 down the middle all the way to the bottom.
接着，把2和3的部分慢慢地向左、向右拉。: Next, slowly pull sides 2 and 3 to the left and right.
海苔和米饭之间有一层薄薄的膜。: There is a thin film between the seaweed and the rice.
所以海苔不会受潮，是脆脆的。: So the seaweed doesn't get damp and stays crispy.
一开始有点难，但很快就会熟练的哦。: It's hard at first, but you'll soon get good at it.
说到秋田县冬天的味道，很多人都会想到“米棒（kiritanpo）”吧。: When it comes to the taste of winter in Akita Prefecture, many people probably think of kiritanpo.
做法是把煮好的米饭捣到半碎，缠在秋田杉木做的棒子上，然后一边转动一边用火烤，让整: It's made by mashing cooked rice until it's about half crushed, wrapping it around a stick of Akita cedar, and then grilling it over a fire, turning it so that it browns all over.
据说它原本是秋田县北部地区在山里干活的人们吃的东西。: It's said that it was originally eaten by people working in the mountains in the northern part of Akita Prefecture.
把烤好的米棒从棒子上取下、切开放进锅里，就是“米棒火锅”。: Grilled kiritanpo taken off the stick, cut up, and put into a pot is called "kiritanpo nabe."
比内地鸡作为秋田的土鸡而闻名，汤底常用它熬的高汤。: Hinai-jidori is known as Akita's local breed of chicken, and stock made from it is often used for the broth.
另外，一般还会加入牛蒡、舞茸、水芹等蔬菜。: Vegetables such as burdock root, maitake mushrooms, and Japanese parsley are usually added as well.
米棒的特点是，即使吸饱了汤汁也不容易散。: A special feature of kiritanpo is that it doesn't easily lose its shape, even after soaking up plenty of broth.
因此，可以一直享受到它软糯的口感。: That's why you can enjoy its soft, chewy texture right to the end.
缠绕: to wrap around, to wind around
在居酒屋打工: A part-time job at an izakaya
大学生林同学每周3次在车站附近的居酒屋打工。: Lin, a university student, works part-time at an izakaya near the station three times a week.
在那之前，必须先把桌子擦干净、准备好湿毛巾。: Before that, the tables have to be cleaned and the wet hand towels prepared.
客人一进门，店员们就一起大声招呼“欢迎光临！”: When customers come in, all the staff greet them together in loud voices: "Welcome!"
特别忙的是公司职员下班的晚上7点左右。: It's especially busy around 7 p.m., when office workers finish work.
很多客人一坐下就马上点：“先来杯啤酒！”，所以必须赶紧端过去。: Many customers order "A draft beer to start!" as soon as they sit down, so the drinks have to be brought out quickly.
最先端上来的小菜叫“お通し”，即使不点也会上。: The small dish served first is called 「お通し」 (otoshi), and it comes even if you don't order it.
刚开始工作的时候，日语太快，很吃力。: When Lin first started working there, the Japanese was so fast that it was really hard.
但是因为她每天努力坚持，现在已经很擅长听客人点单了。: But by working hard and sticking with it every day, Lin has now become very good at taking customers' orders.
点（菜）；请求: to order (food); to ask, to request
便利店是“街头服务窗口”: Convenience stores: the town's service counter
日本的便利店不仅仅是卖吃的喝的的店。: Japanese convenience stores are not just places that sell food and drinks.
电费、燃气费、水费，只要把寄到家里的缴费单拿到收银台，就能当场支付。: You can pay your electricity, gas, and water bills on the spot by taking the bill that came to your home to the register.
店里有ATM，不用去银行，即使深夜也能取现金。: There's an ATM in the store, so you can withdraw cash even in the middle of the night without going to a bank.
使用复印机的话，还可以复印文件、打印照片。: With the copy machine, you can also copy documents and print photos.
还有寄快递、领取网购包裹的服务。: There are also services for sending parcels and picking up packages ordered online.
对于白天不在家的人来说，这是非常方便的服务。: For people who aren't home during the day, these services are extremely helpful.
很多时候还能在店里打印演唱会的门票。: In many cases, you can also have concert tickets issued at the store.
由于很多店24小时营业，它被当作遇到困难时的“街头服务窗口”来使用。: Since many stores are open 24 hours, they are used as the "town's service counter" when people need help.
就这样，便利店逐渐成为人们日常生活中不可缺少的存在。: In this way, convenience stores have become an indispensable part of people's daily lives.
栃木县宇都宫市以“饺子之城”而闻名。: Utsunomiya in Tochigi Prefecture is known as "the city of gyoza."
车站周围和城里有很多饺子店。: There are lots of gyoza restaurants around the station and throughout the city.
也有很多游客一边比较各家店的味道一边品尝。: Many tourists eat their way around, comparing the flavors at different restaurants.
宇都宫站前还有一座被饺子皮包起来的女性雕像。: In front of Utsunomiya Station, there's even a statue of a woman wrapped in a gyoza wrapper.
听说饺子在宇都宫开始被人们常吃，是在战争之后。: Apparently, gyoza became a common food in Utsunomiya after the war.
从中国回来的人们，把在那里吃到的饺子的做法传了过来。: People who came back from China passed on how to make the gyoza they had eaten there.
如今，作为家庭在饺子上花钱很多的城市，它和静冈县滨松市争夺第一。: Today, it competes with Hamamatsu in Shizuoka Prefecture for first place as the city where households spend the most money on gyoza.
不只是普通的煎饺，用开水煮的“水饺”也很受欢迎。: Not only ordinary pan-fried gyoza but also boiled gyoza, cooked in hot water, are popular.
传达；传授: to convey; to pass on (to others)
一个人经营着一家小拉面店的田中先生，他的一天在开店前好几个小时就开始了。: For Tanaka, who runs a small ramen shop single-handedly, the day begins hours before the shop opens.
他在大锅里放入猪骨和蔬菜，不关火，花时间慢慢熬汤。: Tanaka puts pork bones and vegetables into a big pot and makes the soup slowly, without ever turning off the heat.
汤的味道会因当天的气温、湿度和食材而一点点变化，所以他每天一定会尝味道。: The taste of the soup changes slightly depending on the day's temperature and humidity and the ingredients, so Tanaka always tastes it every day.
田中先生认为，始终保持同样的味道，才是对店来说最重要的。: Tanaka believes that always keeping the same flavor is the most important thing for the shop.
一到中午，店门口就排起了长队。: At lunchtime, a long line forms in front of the shop.
客人先在入口的售票机买好餐券，再坐到吧台座位上。: Customers buy a meal ticket from the ticket machine at the entrance and then sit at the counter.
也有很多客人会说出自己的喜好，比如“面要硬一点”。: Many customers say how they like their noodles, for example, "Firm noodles, please."
田中先生把面煮好后马上彻底沥干水，趁热端出去。: As soon as the noodles are boiled, Tanaka drains them thoroughly and serves them while they're hot.
田中先生说：“客人把汤喝到最后一口的时候，就知道他们满意了，疲劳什么的就都消失了: "When customers drink the soup to the last drop, I know they were satisfied, and my tiredness just disappears," says Tanaka.
到了晚上7点左右，超市的便当柜台前开始聚集起人来。: Around 7 p.m., people start gathering at the bento section of the supermarket.
大家等待的是打折贴纸。: What everyone is waiting for is the discount stickers.
店员过来，在便当、沙拉等商品上一个个贴上“八折”或“半价”的贴纸。: A staff member comes and puts "20% off" and "half price" stickers on bento, salads, and other items.
店家希望当天做的东西能在当天就卖完。: The store wants to sell everything it made that day before the day is over.
所以，快到关门的时间时，就会降价。: That's why it lowers its prices as closing time approaches.
对店家来说，扔掉的食物也会变少，所以是件好事。: It's good for the store too, since less food gets thrown away.
对一个人生活的学生和下班路上顺便来的人来说，这是非常让人高兴的事。: For students living on their own and people who stop by on their way home from work, it's a real treat.
不过，受欢迎的便当很快就会卖光。: But popular bento sell out quickly.
所以，如果有想要的东西，最好早点去。: So if there's something you want, it's best to go early.
没有了；卖光: to be gone; to sell out
名古屋美食：味噌猪排和鸡翅: Nagoya food: miso katsu and tebasaki
爱知县名古屋市有很多被称为“名古屋饭”的独特料理。: Nagoya in Aichi Prefecture has many unusual dishes known as "Nagoya meshi" (Nagoya food).
其中特别有名的是“味噌猪排”。: Among them, an especially famous one is "miso katsu."
一般的炸猪排是浇酱汁，但在名古屋会浇上一种颜色发黑的味噌酱。: Ordinary tonkatsu is topped with sauce, but in Nagoya it's topped with a dark miso sauce.
这种酱用的是爱知用大豆做的红味噌，有点甜，味道很浓郁。: This sauce uses Aichi's red miso, which is made from beans, and it tastes slightly sweet and rich.
另一道广为人知的料理是炸鸡翅尖做的“手羽先”。: Another well-known dish is "tebasaki," deep-fried chicken wing tips.
刷上甜辣的酱汁，再撒上胡椒和芝麻来吃。: They're brushed with a sweet and spicy sauce and sprinkled with pepper and sesame seeds.
因为和啤酒非常搭，所以在居酒屋里也很常见。: They go really well with beer, so they're also popular at izakaya.
如果有机会去名古屋旅行，请一定两样都尝一次。: If you ever get the chance to travel to Nagoya, be sure to try both of them.
相配；合适: to go well with; to suit
在温泉旅馆工作的“仲居”，是穿着和服负责照顾客人的人，有时一个人要负责好几个房间: The 「仲居さん」 (nakai-san) who work at hot spring inns are attendants who wear kimono and look after the guests, and sometimes one person is in charge of several rooms.
客人到达后，为了不让客人迷路，她们会带客人到房间，并端上茶和点心。: When guests arrive, the nakai show them to their room so they don't get lost and serve them tea and sweets.
那时还会仔细地说明温泉的位置和晚饭时间等。: At that time, they also carefully explain where the hot spring baths are, what time dinner is, and so on.
有的旅馆会把晚饭送到房间，一边观察客人的情况，一边按顺序一道一道地上菜。: At some ryokan, they bring dinner to the room and serve the dishes one at a time in order, keeping an eye on how the guests are doing.
趁客人吃完饭去泡温泉的时候，她们在榻榻米上铺好被褥。: While the guests are in the bath after finishing their meal, they lay out futons on the tatami.
据说要把沉重的被褥又快又整齐地铺好，在熟练之前是相当难的。: Laying out heavy futons quickly and neatly is apparently quite hard until you get used to it.
第二天早上还要准备早餐，所以仲居们得一大早就开始工作。: The next morning there's breakfast to prepare, so the nakai have to start work early.
虽然是很辛苦的工作，但据说每次看到客人的笑脸，都会感受到工作的喜悦。: It's hard work, but they say that every time they see a guest's smile, they feel the joy of the job.
客人的感谢之词，尤其是“我还会再来的”这句话，对仲居们来说才是最好的奖励。: Words of thanks from guests, especially when they say they'll come again, are the greatest reward for a nakai.
习惯；熟练: to get used to; to become skilled
垃圾分类方法因城市而异: Garbage sorting rules differ from town to town
搬到日本的外国人最先感到吃惊的事情之一，就是垃圾的分类方法。: One of the first things that surprises foreigners who move to Japan is how garbage is sorted.
垃圾必须分成“可燃垃圾”“不可燃垃圾”“资源垃圾”等类别扔出去。: Garbage must be sorted into categories such as "burnable garbage," "non-burnable garbage," and "recyclables" before it is put out.
而且，细则因市町而异，所以搬家后应该一定要确认。: What's more, the detailed rules differ from city to city and town to town, so you should be sure to check them when you move.
扔垃圾的日子也是固定的，很多地区规定要在早上8点左右之前放到指定地点。: The days for putting out garbage are also fixed, and in many areas you're supposed to put it out at the designated spot by around 8 a.m.
塑料瓶一般要取下瓶盖和标签，把里面稍微冲洗后再扔。: Plastic bottles are usually put out after removing the cap and label and giving the inside a quick rinse.
不遵守规则的话，垃圾可能会被贴上警告贴纸而不被收走。: If you don't follow the rules, a warning sticker may be put on your garbage and it may not be collected.
大件家具等“大件垃圾”按规定不事先申请就不能扔。: The rules say that "oversized garbage," such as large furniture, can't be put out unless you apply in advance.
每次扔垃圾都要分类，也许会觉得麻烦，但习惯了自然就能做到了。: Sorting your garbage every time you put it out may feel like a hassle, but once you get used to it, it becomes second nature.
石川县金泽市有一种有点与众不同的咖喱，叫做“金泽咖喱”。: Kanazawa in Ishikawa Prefecture has a slightly unusual curry called "Kanazawa curry."
咖喱酱非常浓稠，颜色是接近黑色的棕色。: The curry sauce is very thick, and its color is a brown that's almost black.
首先在米饭上浇上咖喱酱，再在上面放一块炸猪排。: First, the sauce is poured over the rice, and a cutlet is placed on top.
炸猪排上浇上酱汁，旁边放上切得细细的卷心菜。: The cutlet is topped with sauce, and finely shredded cabbage is placed on the side.
少见的是，它是用不锈钢的银色盘子端上来的。: What's unusual is that it's served on a silver stainless steel plate.
而且很多店不是用普通勺子，而是用叉子或前端分叉的勺子来吃。: And many restaurants have you eat it not with an ordinary spoon but with a fork or a spoon with a split tip.
因为咖喱酱很浓稠，所以即使用叉子，也能轻松地和米饭一起吃。: Because the sauce is so thick, you can easily eat it together with the rice, even with a fork.
如果有机会去金泽，请一定尝一次。: If you ever get the chance to go to Kanazawa, be sure to try it.
出租车司机的工作: The work of a taxi driver
在东京当出租车司机的铃木先生，一次值班从早上干到深夜，大约要工作20个小时。: Suzuki, a taxi driver in Tokyo, works about 20 hours per shift, from morning until the middle of the night.
虽然中途会休息几次，但长时间连续开车并不轻松，所以也必须注意身体健康。: There are several breaks along the way, but driving for that many hours isn't easy, so Suzuki also has to take care to stay healthy.
作为交换，第二天叫做“值班后休息”，可以休息一整天。: In exchange, Suzuki can rest for the whole of the next day, which is called 「明け休み」 (ake-yasumi, a day off after a shift).
这种工作方式叫做“隔日值班”，在出租车行业是很普遍的制度。: This way of working is called 「隔日勤務」 (kakujitsu kinmu, alternate-day shifts), and it's a common system in the taxi industry.
日本的出租车后门由司机开关，所以乘客不需要自己开门。: In Japanese taxis, the driver opens and closes the rear door, so passengers never open it themselves.
据说从国外来的乘客中，有不少人对此感到吃惊。: Quite a few passengers from abroad are apparently surprised by this.
下雨天和末班车之后，在出租车乘车处等车的队伍会变长。: On rainy days and after the last train, the lines of people waiting at taxi stands get long.
铃木先生对小路非常熟悉，所以即使道路拥堵，也能快速把乘客送到目的地。: Suzuki knows the back streets well and can get passengers to their destinations quickly even when the roads are congested.
在日本，城市的很多地方都能看到自动售货机。: In Japan, you can see vending machines (jihanki for short) in all sorts of places around town.
不仅在车站和街角，有时在山里也能看到。: You can find them not only at stations and on street corners but sometimes even in the mountains.
即使放在室外，也几乎不会被破坏。: Even though they stand outdoors, they are hardly ever vandalized.
据说其原因是日本是个安全的国家。: This is said to be because Japan is a safe country.
一台自动售货机同时卖冷饮和热饮两种。: A single vending machine sells both cold and hot drinks.
按钮下方如果是蓝色，就表示“冷的”，如果是红色，就表示“热的”。: If the area under the button is blue, it means 「つめたい」 (cold), and if it's red, it means 「あたたかい」 (warm).
寒冷的冬天早上买一罐热咖啡，冻僵的手和口袋都会变得暖暖的。: If you buy a hot can of coffee on a cold winter morning, your chilly hands and your pockets get nice and warm.
另外，还有一些自动售货机在发生地震等情况时，不投钱也能出饮料。: There are also vending machines that can give out drinks without any money being put in when an earthquake or other disaster strikes.
章鱼烧是大阪的食物。: Takoyaki is a food from Osaka.
它是一种又小又圆的食物，里面有章鱼。: It's a small, round food with octopus inside.
上面浇上酱汁和蛋黄酱，再放上木鱼花和青海苔。: It's topped with sauce and mayonnaise, plus bonito flakes and green laver.
大阪的街上有很多章鱼烧店。: There are lots of takoyaki shops in Osaka.
在大阪，很多人家里也有做章鱼烧的机器。: In Osaka, many people have a takoyaki maker at home.
和朋友在家里做章鱼烧吃，非常开心。: Making and eating takoyaki at home with friends is a lot of fun.
不过里面非常烫，吃的时候请小心。: But the inside is very hot, so please be careful when you eat it.
保育园老师的一天: A day in the life of a daycare teacher
保育园是在父母工作期间照看小孩子的地方。: A daycare center is a place that looks after small children while their parents are at work.
从早上7点左右开始，父母在上班前把孩子送来。: From around 7 a.m., parents bring their children in on their way to work.
老师看着孩子的脸，精神饱满地说“早上好！”: The teachers look at each child's face and cheerfully say, "Good morning!"
上午会去公园散步，或者大家一起唱歌。: In the morning, they go for walks to the park, sing songs together, and so on.
还不会走路的小孩子，就坐在大推车里一起出门。: Little ones who can't walk yet ride in a big cart and go along too.
老师趁孩子们睡觉的时候写“联络本”。: While the children are asleep, the teachers write in the "contact notebooks."
联络本上会写下孩子当天吃了什么、有什么开心的事等，告诉父母。: In the contact notebook, they write down what the child ate that day, what was fun, and so on, to let the parents know.
这是连接父母和老师的重要本子。: It's an important notebook that connects parents and teachers.
钱汤是开在街区里的大浴场。: A sento is a large public bath in town.
以前很多人家里没有浴室，所以大家几乎每天都去钱汤。: In the past, many people didn't have a bath at home, so everyone went to the sento almost every day.
东京的钱汤里，墙上常常有巨大的富士山的画。: Sento in Tokyo often have a big painting of Mt. Fuji on the wall.
在入口处脱鞋，放进鞋柜里。: At the entrance, you take off your shoes and put them in a shoe locker.
进入热水池之前，必须先把身体洗干净。: Before getting into the hot water, you must first wash your body thoroughly.
因为别的客人也泡在同一池水里，所以这是一条重要的规矩。: Other customers get into the same water, so this is an important rule.
不能把毛巾放进池水里。: You must not put your towel in the water.
长头发的人最好先把头发盘起来，以免碰到池水。: If you have long hair, it's best to put it up so that it doesn't touch the water.
泡完澡出来后喝一瓶冰牛奶，也是钱汤的乐趣之一。: Drinking cold milk after getting out of the bath is another of the pleasures of the sento.
大阪一个叫“新世界”的街区，以炸串店多而闻名。: The Shinsekai neighborhood in Osaka is famous for its many kushikatsu restaurants.
炸串是把肉、蔬菜、鱼等串在签子上，裹上面包糠油炸的料理。: Kushikatsu is a dish of meat, vegetables, fish, and so on put on skewers, coated in breadcrumbs, and deep-fried.
店里的桌子上准备着装有酱汁的大容器。: Large containers of sauce are set out on the restaurant tables.
这个酱汁是和别的客人共用的。: This sauce is shared with other customers.
所以，已经放进嘴里的炸串不能再蘸一次酱汁。: So you must not dip a skewer back into the sauce once it has been in your mouth.
这就是被称为“禁止二次蘸酱”的店规。: This is the restaurant rule known as "no double-dipping."
觉得酱汁不够的话，用一起端上来的卷心菜舀起来，浇在炸串上就行了。: If you think you need more sauce, just scoop some up with the cabbage that comes with your order and pour it over your kushikatsu.
吃完油炸食品后再吃卷心菜，嘴里会变得清爽。: Eating cabbage after fried food also leaves your mouth feeling refreshed.
不遵守规矩的话，周围的客人会感到不舒服。: If you don't follow the rule, the customers around you will feel uncomfortable.
第一次去的人，最好在进店之前就牢牢记住这条规矩。: If it's your first time, it's a good idea to memorize this rule before you go in.
通往寿司师傅的漫长道路: The long road to becoming a sushi chef
东京和大阪的早高峰，拥挤程度在世界上都很出名。: The morning rush hour in Tokyo and Osaka is so crowded that it's famous around the world.
电车里挤满了人，连稍微动一下身体都很难。: The trains are packed with people, and it's hard to move your body even a little.
即便如此，多亏很多人遵守规则，很少发生大的混乱。: Even so, because so many people follow the rules, serious chaos rarely occurs.
在站台上，人们沿着地面上画的线排成一列等车。: On the platform, people wait for the train in a single line along the lines marked on the floor.
电车到站后，下车的人先下，上车的人在后面。: When the train arrives, people getting off go first, and people getting on go after them.
在拥挤的车厢里，为了不妨碍周围的人，把背包抱在胸前是一种礼仪。: On a crowded train, it's good manners to hold your backpack in front of you so that you don't get in the way of the people around you.
另外，在车厢里打电话被认为会给其他乘客添麻烦。: Also, talking on the phone on the train is considered a nuisance to other passengers.
早上的时间段，有些线路设有只有女性才能乘坐的“女性专用车厢”。: Some lines have "women-only cars" in the morning that only women can ride in.
京都的冬天，特别希望你尝一尝的料理就是“汤豆腐”。: A dish you really should try at least once in Kyoto in winter is "yudofu" (simmered tofu).
在砂锅底部放上海带、倒入水，然后把豆腐慢慢温热就行，是一道非常简单的料理。: It's a very simple dish: you just put kombu in the bottom of an earthenware pot, pour in water, and gently heat the tofu.
不过，温度太高的话豆腐会变硬，所以要注意火不要开得太大。: However, if the temperature gets too high the tofu becomes hard, so you have to be careful not to turn the heat up too much.
温热的豆腐蘸上以酱油为基础的调味汁，和葱等佐料一起吃。: The warmed tofu is dipped in a soy sauce-based sauce and eaten with condiments such as green onion.
虽然材料很少，却能充分品尝到豆腐本身的味道，这是它的特点。: Its special feature is that, despite using so few ingredients, it lets you really enjoy the flavor of the tofu itself.
关于京都豆腐好吃的原因，据说是因为地下水干净又丰富。: As for why Kyoto's tofu is so good, it's said to be because the groundwater is clean and plentiful.
另外，这似乎也和不使用肉和鱼的寺庙料理，也就是素斋的传统有很深的关系。: It also seems to be closely connected to the tradition of temple cooking that uses no meat or fish, in other words, shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine).
尤其是南禅寺周边，从过去到现在一直聚集着很多汤豆腐店。: Around Nanzenji Temple in particular, many yudofu restaurants have been gathered from long ago right up to the present day.
虽然不是什么华丽的料理，但在寒冷的日子吃，不仅身体，连心都会暖和起来。: It's not a flashy dish, but eating it on a cold day warms not only your body but your heart as well.
鱼市场的早晨，趁城市还黑暗安静的时候就开始了。: Morning at the fish market begins while the city is still dark and quiet.
夜里在海上捕到的鱼，以及用卡车从全国各地运来的鱼，一条接一条地被摆放到市场里。: Fish caught at sea during the night and fish brought in by truck from all over the country are laid out in the market one after another.
东京的中央批发市场于2018年从筑地迁到了丰洲。: Tokyo's central wholesale market moved from Tsukiji to Toyosu in 2018.
丰洲市场特别有名的是金枪鱼的拍卖。: Toyosu Market is especially famous for its tuna auctions.
中间批发商们用灯照着金枪鱼尾巴的切口，仔细确认鱼肉的颜色和油脂的多少。: The intermediate wholesalers shine lights on the cut end of each tuna's tail to check the color of the flesh and the amount of fat in detail.
以铃声为信号，拍卖开始，人们用手势表示价格，转眼之间买家就确定了。: The auction starts at the signal of a bell, and as prices are shown with hand signs, the buyer is decided in no time.
市场里，一种叫“ターレ”的小型搬运车装着货物，忙碌地跑来跑去。: Inside the market, small transport vehicles called 「ターレ」 (tare, short for "turret truck") zip busily around carrying loads.
参观者可以从楼上的参观通道眺望这番景象。: Visitors can watch the scene from an observation walkway on the upper floor.
广岛的什锦烧是叠起来烤的: Hiroshima okonomiyaki is cooked in layers
说到什锦烧，很多人会想到大阪，但广岛的什锦烧也毫不逊色地有名。: Many people think of Osaka when it comes to okonomiyaki, but Hiroshima okonomiyaki is just as famous.
两者最大的区别在于做法。: The biggest difference between the two is in how they're made.
在大阪，是先把卷心菜等材料拌进面糊里再煎。: In Osaka, the cabbage and other ingredients are mixed into the batter before cooking.
而在广岛，是先把面糊煎成薄薄的圆饼，再在上面一层层叠上大量的卷心菜、豆芽和猪肉。: In Hiroshima, on the other hand, the batter is cooked into a thin, round pancake, and lots of cabbage, bean sprouts, and pork are layered on top of it.
而且还会叠上煎好的荞麦面或乌冬面以及鸡蛋，所以一份的量相当大，能吃得很饱。: Fried soba or udon noodles and an egg are layered on too, so each one is quite a large portion and really fills you up.
很多店在点单时可以自己选择放荞麦面还是乌冬面。: At many restaurants, you can choose soba or udon yourself when you order.
广岛人为了能趁热吃，有时会直接用小铲子从铁板上取着吃。: People in Hiroshima sometimes eat it directly off the hot plate with a small spatula so they can eat it while it's still hot.
顺便说一句，听说被外地人称为“广岛烧”时，有的广岛人会不高兴，所以最好避免这种叫: By the way, some people in Hiroshima apparently make a face when people from other regions call it 「広島焼き」 (Hiroshima-yaki), so it's best to avoid that name.
日本的春天，樱花非常美丽。: In spring in Japan, the cherry blossoms are very beautiful.
在东京，三月底到四月初左右，樱花会开放。: In Tokyo, they bloom from around the end of March to the beginning of April.
电视新闻每天都会说“花什么时候开呢”。: Every day, the TV news asks, "When will the blossoms open?"
人们在樱花树下吃饭、喝酒。: People eat and drink under the cherry trees.
这叫做“赏花”。: This is called 「花見」 (hanami, flower viewing).
公园里人非常多，所以也有人一大早去占个好位置。: Parks get very crowded, so some people go early in the morning to save a spot.
不过，花只开一个星期左右。: But the blossoms only last about a week.
所以，大家都非常喜欢樱花。: That's why everyone loves cherry blossoms so much.
百元店里有各种各样的东西。: 100-yen shops have all kinds of things.
有笔和本子，也有杯子和盘子。: They have pens and notebooks, and cups and plates too.
也有卖零食和饮料的店。: Some shops also sell snacks and drinks.
我刚来日本的时候，房间里什么都没有。: When I came to Japan, there was nothing in my room.
所以，我在百元店买了很多东西。: So I bought a lot of things at a 100-yen shop.
现在我也时常去看看有趣的东西。: Even now, I sometimes go to look at interesting things.
香川是日本最小的县。: Kagawa is the smallest prefecture in Japan.
不过，因为乌冬面店非常多，所以也被称为“乌冬面县”。: But because it has so many udon restaurants, it's also called "Udon Prefecture."
这里的乌冬面叫“赞岐乌冬”，尤其以咬起来很有嚼劲而闻名。: The udon here is called "Sanuki udon," and it's especially famous for being firm and chewy when you bite into it.
香川有很多自助式的店。: Kagawa has lots of self-service restaurants.
首先选好想吃的乌冬面，再决定要大份还是小份。: First, you choose the udon you want and decide whether to have a large or a small serving.
然后，从摆着的天妇罗里自己拿喜欢的。: Next, you help yourself to whatever you like from the tempura laid out in a row.
最后在收银台付钱，在空着的座位上吃。: Finally, you pay at the register and eat at any free seat.
听说在香川，从早上就吃乌冬面的人也很多。: Apparently, many people in Kagawa eat udon even in the morning.
因此，也有很早就开门的店。: That's why some restaurants open early in the morning.
空着: to be empty, to be free
从四月底到五月初，有很多节假日。: There are many national holidays between the end of April and the beginning of May.
从4月29日的“昭和日”到5月5日的“儿童节”的假期，叫做黄金周。: The holidays from Showa Day on April 29 to Children's Day on May 5 are called Golden Week.
和周六、周日连在一起的话，有的年份可以休息一周以上。: In some years, when the holidays connect with Saturdays and Sundays, they add up to more than a week off.
这个时候天气好又暖和，所以出门旅行的人非常多。: The weather at this time of year is nice and warm, so lots of people go on trips.
因此，高速公路非常堵。: As a result, the expressways get terribly crowded.
新干线和飞机的座位也很快就没有了。: Seats on the shinkansen and planes also sell out quickly.
5月5日儿童节之前，也有人家挂起像在天空中游泳的“鲤鱼旗”。: Before Children's Day on May 5, some families put up "koinobori," carp streamers that look as if they're swimming in the sky.
据说讨厌拥挤的人不去旅行，而是在家好好休息。: People who hate crowds apparently skip traveling and relax at home instead.
没有了: to be gone, to run out
去邮局吧: Let's go to the post office
走在日本的街上，经常能看到红色的邮筒。: When you walk around a town in Japan, you often see red mailboxes.
邮局的标志是“〒”，地图和明信片上也会用到它。: The symbol for the post office is 「〒」, and it's also used on maps and postcards.
日本的地址有7位数的邮政编码。: Japanese addresses have a seven-digit postal code.
寄信的时候，要把邮政编码和地址一起写上。: When you send a letter, you write the postal code along with the address.
在邮局，不仅能寄信和包裹，还能像银行一样存钱。: At the post office, you can not only send letters and packages but also deposit money, just like at a bank.
包裹送来时如果不在家，信箱里会放着一张通知你“刚才不在家”的单子。: If you're not home when someone comes to deliver a package, you'll find a slip in your mailbox letting you know you were out.
看了那张纸后，可以通过电话或网上决定请他们重新投递的日期。: After reading the slip, you choose a day for them to deliver it again, by phone or online.
一到年底，寄新年当天送达的贺年卡的人就会增多，所以邮局会热闹起来。: At the end of the year, more people send New Year's cards that will arrive on New Year's Day, so the post office gets busy.
高知县自古就以盛产鲣鱼而闻名，鲣鱼的食用量也在日本名列前茅。: Kochi Prefecture has long been known as a place where lots of bonito are caught, and the amount of bonito eaten there is among the highest in Japan.
高知很有名的“炙烤鲣鱼”是只用大火把鲣鱼表面烤一下的料理。: Kochi's famous "katsuo no tataki" is a dish in which only the surface of the bonito is seared over a high flame.
因为里面还是生的，所以能同时享受到外面的焦香和里面的鲜嫩。: Since the inside stays raw, you can enjoy the toasty aroma of the outside and the tenderness of the inside at the same time.
在高知，传统做法是用燃烧稻草产生的大火焰，在短时间内把表面烤好。: In Kochi, the traditional method is to sear the surface quickly over the big flames of burning straw.
据说用稻草烤的话，会带上一种独特的香味。: It's said that searing it over straw gives it a distinctive, pleasant aroma.
烤完后马上冷却，以免里面也被烤熟。: After searing, it's cooled right away so that the inside doesn't cook through.
在切得较厚的鲣鱼上，放上大量切成薄片的大蒜和洋葱来吃。: The bonito is cut into thickish slices and eaten topped with plenty of thinly sliced garlic and onion.
一般是浇上调味汁吃，但只蘸盐吃的“盐炙烤”似乎也很受欢迎。: It's usually eaten with a sauce poured over it, but "shio tataki," eaten with just salt, also seems to be popular.
到了六月左右，日本很多地方都会持续下雨。: Around June, many parts of Japan have one rainy day after another.
据说因为是梅子结果长大时下的雨，所以起了这个名字。: The name, written 「梅雨」 ("plum rain"), is said to come from the fact that this rain falls when ume plums are growing large.
在东京，大概从六月初持续到七月中旬。: In Tokyo, it generally lasts from the beginning of June to the middle of July.
梅雨期间空气潮湿，洗的衣服很难干。: During the rainy season, the air is damp and muggy, and laundry just won't dry.
但是，这个季节绣球花开得非常美丽。: But in this season, hydrangeas bloom beautifully.
孩子们想要天晴的时候，会在窗边挂上一种叫“晴天娃娃”的纸人偶。: When children want it to be sunny, they hang paper dolls called "teru teru bozu" in the window.
北海道没有明显的梅雨，所以也有人在这个时候去北海道旅行。: Hokkaido doesn't have a clear rainy season, so some people travel to Hokkaido at this time.
在日本感冒了，很多人会先去附近的小诊所。: When people in Japan catch a cold, many of them first go to a small clinic in their neighborhood.
在前台出示保险证后，会拿到一张填写当前症状的“问诊单”。: When you show your health insurance card at reception, you are handed a "medical questionnaire" on which to write down your current symptoms.
只要参加了健康保险，大多数人只需支付医疗费的30%。: As long as they have health insurance, most people only have to pay 30% of their medical costs.
被叫到名字后就进入诊室，向医生详细说明症状。: When your name is called, you go into the examination room and explain your symptoms to the doctor in detail.
看完病后，常常拿到的不是药本身，而是一张叫“处方笺”的纸。: After the examination, you often receive not the medicine itself but a piece of paper called a "prescription."
把它拿到医院外面的药房，从药剂师那里领药。: You then take it to a pharmacy outside the clinic and get your medicine from the pharmacist.
这时出示“用药手册”，就能留下以往用药的记录。: If you show your "medication notebook" (okusuri techo) at this point, a record can be kept of the medicines you've taken so far.
它有助于避免药物之间的不良相互作用，所以旅行时也尽量带上，会更放心。: It helps you avoid medicines that don't go well together, so it's reassuring to take it with you when you travel, too.
博多拉面与屋台之夜: Hakata ramen and nights at the food stalls
福冈县福冈市，尤其是博多一带，作为豚骨拉面之城而闻名。: Fukuoka City in Fukuoka Prefecture, especially the Hakata area, is famous for its tonkotsu (pork bone) ramen.
用猪骨长时间熬成的汤，呈白色浑浊状，有一种独特的香味，味道也很浓厚。: The soup, made by boiling pork bones for a long time, is cloudy white with a distinctive smell, and its flavor is strong and rich.
面条非常细而直，可以按自己的喜好选择“超硬”“软”等硬度来点单。: The noodles are very thin and straight, and when you order you can choose how firm you want them, such as 「バリカタ」 (barikata, extra firm) or 「やわ」 (yawa, soft).
细面很快就会泡软，所以为了能在泡软之前吃完，一开始的量比较少。: Thin noodles go soggy quickly, so the first serving is on the small side so that you can eat it before they get soft.
不够的话，就点放进剩下的汤里的续加面条，也就是“加面”。: If that's not enough, you order a second helping of noodles to put into the leftover soup, known as 「替え玉」 (kaedama).
另外，福冈也以屋台（路边摊）多而闻名。: Fukuoka is also known as a city with many yatai (food stalls).
从傍晚到夜里，中洲和天神的街道上摆满屋台，供应拉面、关东煮、烤鸡串等各种料理。: From evening into the night, yatai line the streets of Nakasu and Tenjin, serving all kinds of food, such as ramen, oden, and yakitori.
即使在狭窄的座位上和陌生人坐在一起，也会自然而然地聊得热火朝天，这是屋台的乐趣之: One of the pleasures of yatai is that even if you end up sitting next to a stranger in the cramped seats, a lively conversation starts up naturally.
日本夏天的乐趣之一是烟花大会。: One of the pleasures of summer in Japan is fireworks festivals.
一到七八月份，日本各地的河边和海边都会举办盛大的烟花大会。: In July and August, big fireworks festivals are held near rivers and the sea all over Japan.
特别是东京的隅田川烟花大会以历史非常悠久而闻名。: The Sumida River festival in Tokyo is especially famous for its very long history.
那一天，很多人穿着浴衣出门，车站和道路都非常拥挤。: On the day, lots of people go out wearing yukata, and the stations and streets get very crowded.
会场附近摆满了小摊，卖着炒面和刨冰等。: Food stalls line up near the venue, selling yakisoba, shaved ice, and other treats.
美丽的烟花升上天空时，也有人大声喊“玉屋～！”。: When beautiful fireworks go up into the sky, some people shout 「たまや〜！」 (Tamaya!) at the top of their voices.
据说这是江户时代一家有名的烟花店的名字。: This is said to be the name of a famous fireworks shop from the Edo period.
大会结束后，也有人在自家院子里放小小的线香烟花，享受夏日的夜晚。: After the festival is over, some people enjoy the summer night by lighting small senko hanabi sparklers in their gardens.
投币洗衣店的使用方法: How to use a coin laundry
日本的街上有很多投币洗衣店。: There are lots of coin laundries in Japanese towns.
不仅家里没有洗衣机的人，有洗衣机的人也经常使用。: Not only people without a washing machine at home but also people who have one often use them.
原因是家里洗衣机放不下的大件东西也能在这里洗。: That's because you can wash large items that won't fit in a home washing machine.
比如，很多人来洗冬天用过的毛毯和被子。: For example, many people come to wash the blankets and futons they used in winter.
店里还有大型烘干机，所以即使是下雨天，也能在短时间内弄干。: The laundries also have big dryers, so things dry quickly even on rainy days.
特别是梅雨季节，洗好的衣服在外面很难晾干，所以店里非常拥挤。: Especially during the rainy season, washed clothes just won't dry outside, so the laundries get very crowded.
等待的时候，也有人在附近的咖啡馆喝咖啡。: Some people have coffee at a nearby café while they wait.
也有人一边看杂志或漫画，一边等着衣服洗完。: Others read magazines or manga while they wait for the laundry to finish.
（后接否定）怎么也不……: (with a negative) not easily, just won't
长崎县长崎市是从江户时代起就和外国有贸易往来的港口城市，也深受中国文化的影响。: Nagasaki in Nagasaki Prefecture is a port city that has traded with other countries since the Edo period, and it has also been strongly influenced by Chinese culture.
代表这样一个长崎的料理就是“什锦面（champon）”。: The dish that represents Nagasaki is "champon."
据说是在明治时代，长崎一家中餐馆的老板为来自中国的留学生想出来的。: It is said to have been created in the Meiji period by the owner of a Chinese restaurant in Nagasaki for students who had come from China.
据说它是出于想让当时的留学生们吃到便宜、管饱又有营养的料理这一心意而诞生的。: It reportedly grew out of the owner's wish to give the students of the time a meal that was cheap, filling, and nutritious.
关于“什锦面”这个名字的由来，似乎有好几种说法。: There seem to be several theories about where the name "champon" comes from.
什锦面里有猪肉、虾、鱿鱼、卷心菜、豆芽等各种配料。: Champon contains all sorts of ingredients, such as pork, shrimp, squid, cabbage, and bean sprouts.
它的特点是先炒配料再加汤，粗面条不另外煮，而是直接用这个汤来煮。: What makes it distinctive is that the ingredients are stir-fried before the soup is added, and the thick noodles are cooked in that soup instead of being boiled separately.
用同样的配料、在酥脆的细面上浇上芡汁的“皿乌冬”，也是长崎很有名的料理。: "Sara udon," in which the same ingredients in a thick sauce are poured over crispy thin noodles, is another well-known Nagasaki dish.
现在，这两种料理不只在长崎，在全国各地都能吃到。: Today, both can be eaten not only in Nagasaki but all over Japan.
盂兰盆节是一个人们认为已故家人和祖先的灵魂会回到家中的节日。: Obon is an occasion when the spirits of deceased family members and ancestors are believed to come back home.
在很多地区，主要是从8月13日到16日左右举行。: In many areas, it mainly takes place from around August 13 to 16.
因为很多人在这个时期请假回老家，所以新干线十分拥挤，高速公路也一直堵车。: Many people take time off during this period to go back to their hometowns, so the shinkansen are crowded and the expressways are jammed for long stretches.
盂兰盆节开始时，为了让灵魂不迷路地回到家里，人们在家门前点燃“迎魂火”。: At the start of Obon, people light a "welcoming fire" (mukaebi) in front of their homes so that the spirits can find their way home without getting lost.
也有家庭把一次性筷子插在黄瓜和茄子上，做成马和牛的形状摆着。: Some families stick disposable chopsticks into a cucumber and an eggplant to make them into the shapes of a horse and a cow, and put them on display.
据说这包含着希望祖先骑快马早点回来、骑慢牛慢慢回去的意思。: This apparently means that the spirits ride a fast horse because the family wants them to come home quickly, and a slow cow because the family wants them to go back slowly.
到了晚上，镇上的广场会举办盂兰盆舞，聚集来的人们围成圆圈一起跳舞。: At night, Bon dances are held in town squares, and the people who gather dance together in a circle.
然后在最后一天点燃“送魂火”，把灵魂送回另一个世界。: Then on the last day, people light a "send-off fire" (okuribi) to send the spirits back to the other world.
便当里饱含的心意: The feelings packed into a bento
在日本，不仅是学生，上班族中平时带便当的人也不在少数。: In Japan, quite a few people, not only students but also office workers, regularly take a bento with them.
把米饭和菜漂亮地装进一个盒子里，是日本便当的特点。: A characteristic of Japanese bento is that rice and side dishes are neatly packed into a single box.
颜色搭配也很受重视，据说注意加入红、黄、绿色的食物会更好看。: Color balance is also considered important, and it's said that including red, yellow, and green foods makes a bento look more appealing.
还有为孩子做成动画角色形状的“卡通便当”。: There are also "character bento" (kyaraben), made in the shape of anime characters for children.
因为外观可爱，对孩子来说，打开盖子的那一瞬间成了一种期待。: Because they look so cute, opening the lid becomes a moment for children to look forward to.
运动会那天，全家人围着大大的便当吃饭是一大乐趣。: On sports day, one of the highlights is the whole family gathering around a big bento.
据说“幕之内便当”这个名字，来自于在戏剧幕间休息时食用。: The name 「幕の内弁当」 (makunouchi bento, "between-the-acts bento") apparently comes from the fact that it was eaten between the acts of a play.
正因为包含了制作者的功夫和爱心，便当才吃起来格外美味吧。: It's probably precisely because of the effort and love the maker puts into it that a bento tastes so good.
重视: to value, to place importance on
冲绳有很多有趣的食物。: Okinawa has lots of interesting foods.
“苦瓜”是一种绿色的长长的蔬菜。: Goya (bitter melon) is a long, green vegetable.
冲绳人会把苦瓜、豆腐和鸡蛋一起炒着吃。: People in Okinawa stir-fry goya with tofu and eggs.
“海葡萄”是一种海草。: 「海ぶどう」 (umibudo, "sea grapes") is a kind of seaweed.
上面长着很多又小又圆的绿色颗粒，像葡萄一样。: It's covered in lots of small, round green beads, so it looks like grapes.
吃的时候，在嘴里噗吱噗吱的，非常好吃。: When you eat it, it pops in your mouth, and it's very tasty.
海葡萄不喜欢冷的地方，所以请不要放进冰箱。: Sea grapes don't like cold places, so please don't put them in the fridge.
去赏红叶吧: Let's go see the autumn leaves
一到秋天，山上和公园里的树叶就从绿色漂亮地变成红色和黄色。: When autumn comes, the leaves on the trees in the mountains and parks change magnificently from green to red and yellow.
出门去看这些美丽的树叶叫做“红叶狩”。: Going out to see these beautiful leaves is called 「紅葉狩り」 (momijigari, literally "autumn leaf hunting").
虽然叫“狩”，但并不是真的去捕猎动物，而是欣赏景色的意思。: Although it says 「狩り」 (hunting), it doesn't mean actually catching animals; it means enjoying the scenery.
红叶从气温下降得早的北海道和高山开始，渐渐地向南方地区推移。: The autumn colors start in Hokkaido and on high mountains, where temperatures drop early, and gradually move down to the southern regions.
春天的樱花从南往北推进，而红叶却朝相反的方向推进，这一点很有意思。: What's interesting is that while the cherry blossoms in spring move from south to north, the autumn colors move in the opposite direction.
京都的岚山和东福寺等地很受欢迎，每年都有很多游客，十分热闹。: Places like Arashiyama and Tofukuji Temple in Kyoto are very popular and are bustling with tourists every year.
大阪的箕面还有一种把枫叶用油炸成天妇罗的稀奇点心。: In Minoh, Osaka, there's even an unusual snack made by deep-frying maple leaves as tempura.
也有一些寺庙到了晚上会点灯，可以享受到和白天完全不同的氛围。: Some temples are lit up at night, so you can enjoy a completely different atmosphere from the daytime.
“デパ地下”指的是百货商店地下的食品卖场。: 「デパ地下」 (depachika) refers to the food floor in the basement of a department store.
那里排列着卖熟食、便当、西式点心、日式点心等各种各样的店铺。: It's lined with all kinds of shops selling prepared dishes, bento, Western-style sweets, Japanese sweets, and more.
逛卖场的时候，有时店员还会请你试吃。: As you walk around the floor, shop staff sometimes offer you a free sample.
也就是说，试吃后喜欢的话，还可以当场买回去。: So if you try something and like it, you can buy it right there and take it home.
百货地下层作为购买礼品的地方也很受欢迎。: Depachika are also popular as places to buy gifts.
在夏季“中元”和年末“岁暮”送礼时节，这里挤满了寻找精美包装商品的客人。: During the summer "ochugen" and year-end "oseibo" gift seasons, they are crowded with customers looking for beautifully wrapped items.
因为包装讲究，挑选去别人家拜访时带的伴手礼也很方便。: Because the wrapping is done so carefully, they're also handy for choosing a gift to take when visiting someone's home.
对忙碌的人来说，下班路上买一道熟食添到晚饭里，总觉得是一种小小的奢侈。: For busy people, picking up a prepared dish on the way home from work to add to dinner feels like a small luxury.
关东煮在日本各地都有人吃，但静冈的关东煮和普通的关东煮看起来相当不一样。: Oden is eaten all over Japan, but Shizuoka oden looks quite different from ordinary oden.
汤的颜色像酱油一样黑。: The broth is as black as soy sauce.
第一次看到的人，也许会被那颜色吓一跳。: People seeing it for the first time may be surprised by its color.
这是因为用牛筋熬汤，而且用的是颜色很深的酱油。: This is because the stock is made from beef tendon, and dark soy sauce is used.
也有店铺在汤不够时一边添加新汤一边长时间持续使用。: Some shops keep using the same broth for a long time, adding new broth whenever it runs low.
静冈关东煮的配料全都串在竹签上，所以吃起来很方便。: All the ingredients in Shizuoka oden are on skewers, so they're easy to eat.
最有名的配料是“黑鱼糕”，是用沙丁鱼或青花鱼做的。: The most famous ingredient is 「黒はんぺん」 (kuro hanpen, "black hanpen" fish cake), which is made from fish such as sardines and mackerel.
名字里虽然有“黑”，但其实是灰色的。: Its name says 「黒」 (black), but it's actually gray.
吃之前撒上鱼粉和青海苔，是静冈特别的吃法。: Sprinkling it with fish powder and green laver before eating is the special Shizuoka way to eat it.
听说以前在孩子们常去的小店里也有卖，有的孩子很期待放学路上顺便去吃。: In the past, it was also sold at the small shops children often went to, and some children apparently looked forward to stopping by for some on the way home from school.
年节菜与新年初次参拜: Osechi and the first shrine visit of the year
对日本人来说，正月是一年中最重要的节日之一，人们和家人一起庆祝新年。: For people in Japan, New Year's is one of the most important occasions of the year, and families celebrate the new year together.
除夕夜，人们吃“跨年荞麦面”，祈愿能像荞麦面一样细水长流地长寿。: On New Year's Eve, people eat "toshikoshi soba" (year-crossing soba), wishing for a life that, like soba noodles, is thin but long.
到了半夜，寺庙里敲响108下除夕钟声，送走旧年。: Late at night, temples ring their New Year's Eve bells 108 times to see out the old year.
元旦这天，一家人聚在一起吃装在多层漆盒里的“年节菜”。: On New Year's Day, the whole family sits down together to eat "osechi ryori," New Year's food packed in tiered boxes.
年节菜有各种各样的菜，每一道都代表着某种愿望。: Osechi includes many different kinds of dishes, and each one stands for some kind of wish.
比如黑豆寄托着“能够健健康康、勤勤恳恳地工作”的愿望，虾则寄托着“长寿到弯腰驼背: For example, black beans (mame) carry the wish to be able to stay healthy and work diligently (mame ni), and shrimp carry the wish to live so long that one's back becomes bent.
另外，新年第一次去神社或寺庙参拜叫做“初诣”。: Also, the first visit of the new year to a shrine or temple is called 「初詣」 (hatsumode).
有名的神社挤满了人，抽签来占卜这一年运势的人也不少。: Popular shrines are packed with crowds of people, and many draw omikuji (paper fortunes) to see what luck the year will bring.
快递司机的一天: A day in the life of a delivery driver
快递司机的早晨，从在营业所把包裹装上卡车开始。: A delivery driver's morning begins with loading packages onto a truck at the branch office.
如果不好好按配送顺序装车，之后找包裹就会白白浪费时间。: If drivers don't think carefully about the delivery order when loading, they waste time searching for packages later.
日本快递的特点是可以选择送达的时间段，比如“上午”或“晚上”。: A feature of home delivery in Japan is that you can choose a delivery time slot, such as "morning" or "evening."
对司机来说，令人头疼的是送过去时对方却不在家的情况。: What gives drivers trouble is when they go to deliver a package and the recipient isn't home.
那时就要把未投递通知单放进信箱，第二天等再送一次。: In that case, they have to leave a missed-delivery slip in the mailbox and deliver it again, for example the next day.
最近，选择把包裹放在家门口的“放置配送”的人也多了起来。: Recently, more people have been choosing "leave at the door" delivery, in which the package is left in front of the entrance.
年底，礼品和网购包裹增多，是一年中最忙的时期。: At the end of the year, there are more gifts and online orders, making it the busiest time of the year.
不过据说，被人说一句“一直以来谢谢你”，疲劳就会减轻一些。: Even so, drivers say that when someone tells them "Thanks as always," their tiredness eases a little.
山梨县有一道有名的料理叫“馎饦面（hoto）”。: Yamanashi Prefecture has a famous dish called "hoto."
馎饦面是把扁平的粗面条和南瓜等蔬菜一起放进味噌汤里炖煮的料理。: Hoto is a dish of thick, flat noodles simmered in miso soup with vegetables such as kabocha squash.
面条不先放进开水里煮，而是直接放进锅里，所以汤会变得有点浓稠。: The noodles go straight into the pot without being boiled in water first, so the soup becomes slightly thick.
在火上煮久了，南瓜会变软，慢慢化开。: As it cooks over the heat for a long time, the squash softens and gradually falls apart.
这样一来，汤的味道就会变得有点甜。: This makes the soup taste slightly sweet.
山梨山多，以前很难种大米。: Yamanashi has many mountains, so in the past it was hard to grow rice there.
据说因此，用小麦做的馎饦面代替大米，成了重要的饭食。: It's said that for this reason, hoto, made from wheat, became an important food in place of rice.
寒冷的冬天，吃一碗用铁锅端上来的热乎乎的馎饦面，身体会变得暖洋洋的。: Eating piping hot hoto served in an iron pot in the cold winter warms you up all over.
这一天，日本的家庭会撒豆子。: On this day, Japanese families throw beans at home.
爸爸戴上鬼的面具，孩子们向爸爸扔豆子。: The father puts on an ogre mask, and the children throw beans at him.
大家一起大声喊：“鬼出去！福进来！”: Everyone shouts together, "Ogres out! Good luck in!"
撒完豆子以后，吃和自己年龄一样多的豆子。: After throwing the beans, you eat as many beans as your age.
爷爷奶奶要吃很多，真够辛苦的呢。: Grandpas and grandmas have to eat a lot, so it's tough for them!
另外，也有人吃又粗又长的寿司卷。: Some people also eat a thick, long sushi roll.
车站工作人员看不见的工作: The unseen work of station staff
说起车站工作人员的工作，很多人会想到他们在检票口检查车票的样子。: When it comes to the work of station staff, many people probably picture them checking tickets at the ticket gates.
但实际上，不仅是检查车票，还有很多乘客看不到的工作。: In reality, though, besides checking tickets, there's a lot of work that passengers never see.
在站台上，他们守护乘客不让其掉下轨道，确认电车能否安全发车。: On the platforms, staff watch over passengers so that no one falls onto the tracks and check that trains can depart safely.
坐轮椅的乘客乘车时，他们会拿出踏板帮忙上下车。: When a passenger in a wheelchair boards a train, staff put out a ramp and help with getting on and off.
他们还会事先联系下车的车站，安排那里的工作人员也在等候。: They also contact the station where the passenger will get off in advance, so that staff will be waiting there too.
电车晚点时，有时还会发放用于提交给公司或学校的“延误证明”。: When trains are delayed, they sometimes hand out "delay certificates" for passengers to submit to their workplace or school.
另外，整理几乎每天都会收到的遗失物品也是重要的工作。: Sorting the lost items that come in almost every day is another important job.
末班车开走之后，车站设备的检查和清扫工作还在继续。: Even after the last train has left, the inspection and cleaning of station facilities continues.
正因为有这些看不见的工作，我们每天才能放心地乘坐电车。: It's precisely because of this unseen work that we can use the trains every day with peace of mind.
长野县有一种自古就有的食物，叫做“oyaki（烤包子）”。: Nagano Prefecture has a traditional food called "oyaki."
是用面粉或荞麦粉做的皮，包上各种馅料做成的。: They're made by wrapping all kinds of fillings in a dough made from wheat flour or buckwheat flour.
最受欢迎的是包着长野腌菜“野泽菜”的。: The most popular ones are filled with "nozawana," a Nagano pickle.
除此之外，还有包着红豆馅、南瓜、茄子等的。: There are also ones filled with sweet red bean paste, kabocha squash, eggplant, and so on.
甜的咸的都有，所以可以选自己喜欢的。: There are both sweet and salty kinds, so you can choose whichever you like.
长野山多又寒冷，以前有些地方很难种水稻。: Nagano is mountainous and cold, so in the past there were places where it was hard to grow rice.
于是，用小麦和荞麦做的料理就常被人吃了。: So dishes made with wheat and buckwheat came to be eaten often.
烤包子的做法，每家店、每个家庭都不一样。: The way oyaki are made differs from shop to shop and from home to home.
有的地方是烤的，也有的地方是蒸的。: Some places grill them, and others steam them.
去长野的话，两种都尝一尝比较一下也不错。: If you go to Nagano, it might be nice to try both kinds and compare them.
在日本，圣诞节不是法定假日，所以学校和公司照常上课上班。: In Japan, Christmas isn't a public holiday, so there's school and work as usual.
尽管如此，街道依然被彩灯装饰得闪闪发光，期待着这一天的人很多。: Even so, the streets sparkle with festive lights, and lots of people look forward to the day.
有趣的是，很多家庭在圣诞节吃炸鸡。: What's interesting is that many families eat fried chicken at Christmas.
据说这个习惯是通过1970年代肯德基开始的宣传而普及开来的。: This custom is said to have spread thanks to an advertising campaign that KFC started in the 1970s.
如今这非常受欢迎，在圣诞节前几周就预订的人也不在少数。: It's very popular now, and quite a few people place orders several weeks before Christmas.
当天，想买炸鸡的顾客在店门口排起长队。: On the day itself, long lines of customers wanting to buy chicken form in front of the restaurants.
店员们也戴着圣诞老人的帽子，忙碌地工作着。: The staff wear Santa hats and work busily.
和炸鸡一起，吃放着草莓的白色奶油蛋糕，也是日本独特的圣诞节过法。: Eating a white shortcake topped with strawberries along with the chicken is another uniquely Japanese way to enjoy Christmas.
搭配；合在一起: to combine with; to put together
日本的药妆店不只是卖药的店。: Japanese drugstores aren't just places that sell medicine.
店里摆着很多洗发水、化妆品、卫生纸等生活必需品。: Their shelves are lined with all sorts of everyday necessities, such as shampoo, cosmetics, and toilet paper.
卖零食、饮料、冰淇淋和面包的店也很多。: Many also sell snacks, drinks, ice cream, and bread.
有些东西比附近的超市还便宜，所以专门来购物的人也不少。: Some items are cheaper than at the local supermarket, so quite a few people come to do their shopping there.
不过，买药的时候必须注意。: However, you have to be careful when buying medicine.
有些药效强的药，必须先听药剂师说明之后才能买。: Some strong medicines can't be bought until you've listened to an explanation from a pharmacist.
不知道哪种药好的时候，最好试着把身体的情况告诉店员，和他们商量一下。: If you don't know which medicine is best, try telling the staff how you're feeling and asking for their advice.
选择适合自己的药是很重要的。: It's important to choose the medicine that's right for you.
蝗虫佃煮与信州的昆虫食物: Locust tsukudani and eating insects in Shinshu
在日本，有在正月寄一种叫“贺年卡”的明信片的习惯。: In Japan, there's a custom of sending postcards called "nengajo" at New Year's.
明信片上会写“新年快乐”之类的问候语，也常画上当年生肖的图案。: On the postcards, people write greetings such as 「あけましておめでとうございます」 (Happy New Year), and they often draw a picture of that year's zodiac animal too.
在12月25日左右之前投进邮筒的话，就会在1月1日早上送到。: If you put them in the mailbox by around December 25, they arrive on the morning of January 1.
所以，年底大家都很忙。: That's why everyone is busy at the end of the year.
带有压岁钱抽奖的明信片上有号码，中了奖就能得到礼物。: Postcards with a New Year's lottery have numbers on them, and if your number wins, you get a prize.
那一年有家人去世的人，不寄贺年卡，而是寄出“服丧明信片”。: People who lost a family member that year don't send New Year's cards; instead, they send "mourning postcards."
最近用邮件或社交软件拜年的人也变多了。: Recently, more people have started sending their greetings by email or on social media.
但是，收到手写的贺年卡，还是会觉得很高兴。: But getting a handwritten New Year's card still makes you happy.
正月；新年: New Year's (holiday period); the new year
11月3日是“文化之日”，是国家规定的节假日。: November 3 is Culture Day, a holiday set by the government.
它的意思是“珍视自由与和平、培育文化的日子”。: It's meant to be "a day to cherish freedom and peace and to foster culture."
这一天原本是明治天皇的生日。: This day used to be Emperor Meiji's birthday.
文化之日这天，皇居会举行颁发文化勋章的仪式。: On Culture Day, there's a ceremony at the Imperial Palace where the Order of Culture is presented.
文化勋章由在研究、艺术领域取得重大成就的人获得。: The Order of Culture is given to people who have done important work in research or the arts.
有些美术馆和博物馆在这一天不用付钱也能进去。: Some art galleries and museums let you in without paying on this day.
11月初，学校和大学经常举办文化节。: Around the beginning of November, schools and universities often hold cultural festivals.
学生们会表演话剧、演奏音乐，或者在教室里开咖啡馆。: Students put on plays, perform music, open cafés in their classrooms, and so on.
另外，据说文化之日往往是晴天。: It's also said that Culture Day is often sunny.
如果天气好，出门去看看红叶也不错呢。: If the weather is nice, it would also be lovely to go out and see the autumn leaves.
七五三是为孩子健康长大而高兴、庆祝的日本习俗。: Shichi-go-san (Seven-Five-Three) is a Japanese custom of celebrating, with joy, children growing up healthy.
庆祝的日子是11月15日，但也有很多家庭在前后的休息日庆祝。: The day for the celebration is November 15, but many families celebrate on a day off before or after it.
三岁和七岁的女孩、三岁和五岁的男孩会穿上和服去神社参拜。: Girls aged three and seven and boys aged three and five put on kimono and visit a shrine.
庆祝的年龄因居住地区和家庭不同而略有差异。: The ages at which children are celebrated differ slightly depending on the area and the family.
过去，孩子要健健康康地长大，和现在相比要难得多。: In the past, it was much harder than it is now for children to grow up healthy.
所以家人会向神明道谢，并祈求孩子今后的幸福。: That's why families thanked the gods and prayed for their children's happiness in the years to come.
七五三时得到的“千岁糖”，是红白两色、又细又长的糖。: "Chitose ame" (thousand-year candy), which children receive at Shichi-go-san, is a long, thin red-and-white candy.
里面寄托着家人“希望孩子细水长流、健康长寿”的心愿。: It carries the family's hope that the child will live a healthy life that is thin but long.
装糖的袋子上常常画着鹤和龟。: The bags the candy comes in often have pictures of cranes and turtles on them.
因为鹤和龟被认为是长寿的动物。: That's because cranes and turtles are thought to be long-lived animals.
火锅最后吃什么收尾？: How will you finish off your hot pot?
天一冷，日本家庭做火锅的次数就多起来。: When it gets cold, Japanese households make hot pot dishes more often.
把锅放在桌子正中间，和家人、朋友围在旁边一起吃。: The pot is placed in the middle of the table, and family or friends gather around it to eat.
只要把蔬菜、肉、鱼切好放进去就行，所以即使不擅长做饭的人也能轻松做好。: You just cut up vegetables, meat, and fish and put them in, so even people who aren't good at cooking can make it easily.
火锅有各种口味，有酱油味、味噌味、泡菜味等等。: Hot pots come in many flavors, such as soy sauce, miso, and kimchi.
超市里摆着各种口味的“火锅汤料”。: Supermarkets have shelves of "hot pot base" in all kinds of flavors.
大家一起吃的时候，总会出现想决定先放哪种食材和火候大小的人。: When everyone eats together, someone always turns up who wants to decide which ingredients go in first and how high the heat should be.
这样的人会被开玩笑地称为“火锅奉行”。: People like that are jokingly called 「鍋奉行」 (nabe bugyo, "hot pot magistrate").
火锅的乐趣还在于最后的“收尾”。: Part of the fun of hot pot also lies in the final 「しめ」 (shime), the dish that rounds off the meal.
吃完食材后，在剩下的汤里放进米饭和鸡蛋做成杂烩粥，或者放入乌冬面。: Once the ingredients have been eaten, people add rice and egg to the leftover broth to make zosui (rice porridge), or put in udon noodles.
汤里融入了很多肉和蔬菜的鲜味，所以非常好吃。: The broth is full of savory flavor from the meat and vegetables, so it's really delicious.
（火锅、汤里的）食材: ingredients (in a hot pot or soup)
火锅奉行（吃火锅时爱指挥的人）: hot pot magistrate (someone who likes to take charge of the hot pot)
这是珍视劳动、大家互道“谢谢”的日子。: It's a day to value work and for everyone to say "thank you."
过去这一天叫做“新尝祭”，是把当年收获的稻米献给神明、表示感谢的日子。: In the past, this day was called "Niinamesai," a day for offering the year's newly harvested rice to the gods and giving thanks.
现在，这一天皇居里也仍然会举行新尝祭。: Even today, Niinamesai is held at the Imperial Palace on this day.
在这一天之前，小学里有时会给劳动者写信、画画。: Before this day, elementary schools sometimes have children write letters or draw pictures for working people.
孩子们会给附近派出所的警察、车站工作人员、做学校午餐的人等写下“一直以来谢谢您”: The children write "Thank you for all you do" to people such as the police officers at the local police box, station staff, and the people who make school lunches.
也有孩子在家里向爸爸妈妈表达感谢。: Some children also show their gratitude to their fathers and mothers at home.
据说他们会给爸妈捶捶肩，或者帮忙做晚饭。: Apparently, they do things like giving their parents a shoulder rub or helping with dinner.
哪怕只是一句简短的话，要不要试着对一直辛勤工作的人说声“谢谢”呢？: Why not try saying "thank you," even just in a few words, to people who are always hard at work?
在日本，自古以来十二月也被叫做“师走”。: In Japan, December has long also been called 「師走」 (shiwasu), written with the characters for "master" and "run."
据说“师”指的是老师或寺庙里的僧人。: 「師」 is said to refer to teachers or Buddhist priests at temples.
有一种说法是：这是连平时从容稳重的老师都忙得四处奔走的月份。: One theory is that it's a month so busy that even teachers who are usually calm and composed run around here and there.
不过，它真正的意思并没有定论。: However, its true meaning isn't clearly known.
现在，十二月也有很多事要做。: Even now, there's a lot to do in December.
公司里必须在年内把工作做完，晚上有时还要参加忘年会。: At work, people have to get their work finished before the year is out, and in the evenings they sometimes attend year-end parties.
在家里要写贺年卡、搞大扫除。: At home, people write New Year's cards and do a big year-end cleaning.
街上也因为年末促销和准备过年的购物，人多了起来。: The streets get crowded too, with people shopping at year-end sales and buying things to prepare for New Year's.
正因为是忙碌的月份，要注意别累坏了身体。: It's a busy month, so take care not to wear yourself out and get sick.
第一次当干事: Organizing a party for the first time
进公司第一年的佐藤，被安排担任科里忘年会的干事。: Sato, in the first year at the company, has been given the job of organizing the section's year-end party.
他先问了大家哪天方便，定在了12月的第二个星期五。: First, Sato asked everyone which days suited them and settled on the second Friday in December.
十二月店里很快就会订满，所以必须早点预约。: In December, restaurants fill up quickly, so you have to book early.
佐藤选了一家离公司近、有畅饮套餐的居酒屋。: Sato chose an izakaya close to the office that offers an all-you-can-drink course.
因为也有不喝酒的人，所以他选了软饮料种类多的店。: Since some people don't drink alcohol, Sato went with a place that has a wide selection of soft drinks.
当天，他请部长致干杯辞。: On the day, Sato asked the department manager to give the toast.
聚会结束后，科长对他说：“这家店不错啊，谢谢你。”: When the party was over, the section manager said, "That was a great place. Thanks."
准备工作虽然很辛苦，但听说佐藤非常高兴。: The preparations were a lot of work, but Sato was apparently very happy.
不过，被说了一句“明年也拜托你啦”，他露出了有点为难的表情。: But on being told "I'm counting on you next year too," Sato looked a little troubled.
干事（负责张罗聚会的人）: organizer (person in charge of arranging a party)
冬季奖金用来做什么？: What will you do with your winter bonus?
在日本的很多公司，夏天和冬天一年两次发奖金。: At many Japanese companies, bonuses are paid twice a year, in summer and winter.
冬季奖金多在12月上旬到中旬发放。: The winter bonus is usually paid sometime between early and mid-December.
一到发奖金之前，就常能听到“打算用来干什么？”这样的话题。: As bonus time approaches, you often hear people asking, "What are you going to spend it on?"
公司职员山田打算存一半，剩下的用来带家人去温泉旅行。: Yamada, an office worker, plans to save half and use the rest to take the family on a hot spring trip.
同一家公司的中村说想把用旧了的冰箱换成新的。: Nakamura, from the same company, says it's time to replace the old refrigerator with a new one.
也有人买点稍贵的东西，作为送给努力了一年的自己的礼物。: Some people buy something a little expensive as a present to themselves for working hard all year.
一到发奖金的时候，百货商店和电器店也会开始搞促销。: Around the time bonuses are paid, department stores and electronics stores also start holding sales.
不过，也有很多人用奖金还房贷，并不是全部都能花在自己喜欢的事情上。: But many people use their bonus to pay off their home loan, so they can't spend all of it on things they enjoy.
冬至的柚子浴和南瓜: Yuzu baths and kabocha on the winter solstice
12月下旬的“冬至”，是一年中白天最短的一天。: The winter solstice, which falls in late December, is the day with the shortest daylight of the year.
这一天，日本有泡放了柚子的热水澡的习惯。: On this day in Japan, there's a custom of taking a bath with yuzu citrus fruits in it.
这叫做“柚子浴”，很多钱汤（公共澡堂）也会在这一天准备柚子浴。: This is called 「ゆず湯」 (yuzuyu, a yuzu bath), and many public bathhouses prepare yuzu baths on this day.
柚子散发出好闻的香气，据说能让身体暖和起来。: The yuzu gives off a lovely scent, and it's said to warm your body up well.
另外，很多家庭会在冬至吃南瓜。: Also, many families eat kabocha squash on the winter solstice.
南瓜是夏秋收获的蔬菜，但因为能长时间存放，过去在蔬菜稀少的冬天是很重要的食物。: Kabocha is a vegetable harvested from summer to autumn, but because it keeps for a long time, in the past it was an important food in winter, when there were few vegetables.
煮得甜甜的南瓜特别受孩子们欢迎。: Kabocha simmered until sweet is especially popular with children.
还有一种说法：吃像“胡萝卜”“莲藕”这样名字里带两个“ん”的食物，运气就会变好。: It's also said that eating foods with two 「ん」 in their names, such as 「にんじん」 (carrot) and 「れんこん」 (lotus root), brings good luck.
过了冬至，白天就会一点点变长。: After the winter solstice, the days gradually get longer.
在日本，12月底要把整个家打扫干净，这叫“大扫除”。: In Japan, people do the "osoji," a big cleaning of the whole house, at the end of December.
据说自古以来，这是为了在干净的家里迎接新年之神。: It has long been said that this is to welcome the god of the new year into a clean home.
在寺庙和神社，人们用顶端带着叶子的长竹竿，把高处的灰尘掸下来。: At temples and shrines, people knock down the dust in high places with a tool made of a long bamboo pole with leaves on the end.
在家里，要把平时不太打扫的地方弄干净。: At home, people clean the places they don't usually clean much.
比如窗户玻璃、厨房的抽油烟机、冰箱里面等等。: For example, the windowpanes, the kitchen exhaust fan, and the inside of the refrigerator.
抽油烟机沾满了油污，所以非常费劲。: The exhaust fan is covered in grease, so it's a real chore.
扔掉不需要的东西，也是大扫除的重要工作。: Throwing away things you don't need is also an important part of the big cleaning.
最近也有人不在寒冷的12月，而是趁着暖和的秋天进行大扫除。: These days, some people do their big cleaning while it's still warm in autumn rather than in cold December.
全部做完后，就在干净的房间里舒舒服服地迎接新年。: When it's all done, people welcome the new year feeling good in their clean rooms.
新年第一次去神社或寺庙参拜，叫做“初诣”。: The first visit of the new year to a shrine or temple is called 「初詣」 (hatsumode).
去初诣时，很多人会抽神签。: When they go for hatsumode, many people draw an omikuji.
神签是告诉人们这一年运势的小纸条。: An omikuji is a small slip of paper that tells you your fortune for the year.
“大吉”最好，此外还有“吉”“小吉”等，有时也会抽到“凶”。: 「大吉」 (great blessing) is the best, there are others such as 「吉」 (blessing) and 「小吉」 (small blessing), and sometimes you get 「凶」 (bad luck).
纸上除了运势，还详细写着关于工作、学习、旅行、疾病等方面的内容。: The paper describes in detail not just your luck in general but also things like work, study, travel, and illness.
读完以后，很多人会把神签系在神社的树枝或绳子上再回去。: After reading it, many people tie their omikuji to a tree branch or a cord at the shrine before going home.
据说特别是抽到不好的神签时，最好把它系上再回去。: It's said that if you get a bad fortune in particular, it's best to tie it up there before going home.
也有人把写着好话的神签放进钱包里，好好地带回家。: Some people put an omikuji with good things written on it in their wallet and carefully take it home.
就算抽到“凶”觉得遗憾，只要想着“以后会变好的”就不用担心。: Even if you get 「凶」 and feel disappointed, there's no need to worry if you think, "Things will get better from here."
新年首次参拜: first shrine or temple visit of the New Year
1月的第二个星期一是“成人之日”，是国家法定假日。: The second Monday of January is Coming of Age Day, a national holiday.
这个时候，很多城镇会为年满二十岁的人举办仪式。: Around this time, ceremonies are held in many towns for people who are turning twenty.
在日本，成年年龄已经改成了18岁，但现在仍有很多城镇为二十岁的人举办仪式。: In Japan, the age at which people become adults is now 18, but many towns still hold ceremonies for twenty-year-olds.
仪式那天，很多女性会穿一种叫“振袖”的长袖和服。: On the day of the ceremony, many women wear a long-sleeved kimono called a 「振袖」 (furisode).
和服很难一个人穿好，所以要一大早去美容院，请人帮忙穿和服、做发型。: Putting on a kimono by yourself is difficult, so they go to a beauty salon early in the morning to have the kimono put on and their hair styled.
男性大多穿西装，但也有人穿和服裙裤（袴）。: Many men wear suits, but some wear hakama (traditional pleated trousers).
仪式结束后，大家和初中、高中的朋友久别重逢，拍很多照片。: After the ceremony, people meet up with friends from junior high and high school whom they haven't seen in a long time, and take lots of photos.
晚上有时还会举办同学会。: In the evening, class reunions are sometimes held.
对家人来说，这也是感受到孩子成长的开心的一天。: For families, too, it is a happy day when they can feel how much their children have grown.
穿和服（的技术）: kimono dressing (the skill of putting on a kimono)
祈愿考上的冬天: A winter of wishing to pass
1月到3月是高中、大学入学考试集中的季节。: January through March is the season when many high school and university entrance exams take place.
考生们每天都拼命学习到很晚。: Exam candidates study hard until late every day.
这个时候，供奉“天神”的神社里，会有很多考生和家人来祈求考试合格。: Around this time, many exam candidates and their families come to shrines dedicated to Tenjin-sama to pray that they will pass.
天神指的是古代非常有学问的菅原道真，人们称他为学问之神。: Tenjin-sama is a man named Sugawara no Michizane, who long ago was a brilliant scholar, and he is said to be the god of learning.
在神社里，人们会在绘马上写“希望能考上”，或者买护身符。: At the shrine, people write "Please let me pass" on ema (wooden prayer plaques) or buy omamori (good-luck charms).
家人也会为了考生处处留心。: Families, too, are careful about many things for the candidates' sake.
有的家庭会在考试前一天做猪排饭，因为“猪排（カツ）”和“胜（勝つ）”同音。: Some families make katsudon on the day before the exam, a dish that uses 「カツ」 (katsu, cutlet), which sounds the same as 「勝つ」 (katsu, "to win").
另外，“落下”“滑倒”会让人联想到考试失败，所以有人会尽量不在考生面前说这些词。: Also, because 「落ちる」 (ochiru, "to fall") and 「滑る」 (suberu, "to slip") make people think of failing an exam, some people try not to use these words in front of exam candidates.
为了回应大家的心意，考生们会坚持到最后。: To live up to everyone's good wishes, the candidates keep working hard to the very end.
努力，坚持: to work hard, to keep going
札幌冰雪节的雪雕: The snow sculptures of the Sapporo Snow Festival
在北海道的札幌，每年2月初都会举办“札幌冰雪节”。: In Sapporo, Hokkaido, the Sapporo Snow Festival is held every year around the beginning of February.
位于市中心的大通公园里，排列着许多用雪做成的巨大雕像。: In Odori Park, in the center of the city, many large statues made of snow are lined up.
有著名建筑、动漫角色等各种各样的雪雕。: There are all kinds of snow sculptures, such as famous buildings and anime characters.
其中还有高度超过10米的大雪雕。: Among them are huge snow sculptures more than 10 meters tall.
这个节日起源于1950年，当地的初中生和高中生做了六座雪雕。: The festival began in 1950, when junior high and high school students in Sapporo made six snow sculptures.
现在不仅有来自日本各地的游客，还有很多来自国外的游客。: Today, many visitors come to see it, not only from all over Japan but also from abroad.
到了晚上，雪雕被灯光照亮，呈现出和白天不同的美。: At night, the snow sculptures are lit up, and they have a beauty different from that of the daytime.
薄野会场还陈列着用冰做成的作品。: At the Susukino site, statues made of ice are also on display.
外面非常冷，别忘了带手套、帽子，穿上防滑的鞋子。: It's very cold outside, so don't forget gloves, a hat, and shoes that don't slip easily.
节分那天，有吃粗寿司卷的习惯。: There is a custom of eating a thick sushi roll on the day of Setsubun.
这种寿司卷叫做“惠方卷”。: This sushi roll is called 「恵方巻」 (ehomaki).
“惠方”是这一年的神所在的方位，被认为是会有好事发生的吉利方位。: The 「恵方」 (eho) is the direction where that year's god is, and it is believed to be a direction where good things happen.
惠方每年都会变，所以节分临近时，电视上和商店里都会介绍今年的惠方。: The eho changes every year, so as Setsubun approaches, this year's eho is announced on TV and in stores.
吃法是有规定的。: There is a set way to eat it.
首先，要面朝惠方，不切开，整根地吃。: First, you face the eho and eat the roll whole, without cutting it.
之所以不切，是因为有“不切断缘分”的意思。: It isn't cut because this carries the meaning of "not cutting one's ties with others."
而且，在吃完之前，一句话都不能说。: And you must not say anything until you have finished eating.
据说一说话，好运就会溜走。: It is said that if you talk, your luck will run away.
这本来是大阪等地的习俗，后来便利店等开始售卖，全日本的人都吃起来了。: This custom used to be practiced in places like Osaka, but once ehomaki began to be sold at convenience stores and other shops, people all over Japan started eating them.
规定，决定: to be set, to be decided
举行，进行: to hold (an event), to carry out
比樱花先开的梅花: Plum blossoms that bloom before the cherry blossoms
到了二月，虽然寒冷的日子还在持续，但各处的梅花都开始绽放了。: In February, cold days continue, but plum blossoms begin to bloom here and there.
梅花比樱花开得早，是最先告诉人们“春天就要来了”的花。: Plum trees bloom earlier than cherry trees, so they are the first flowers to announce, "Spring is almost here!"
花的颜色有白色、深粉色、浅粉色等，走近了能闻到甜甜的香味。: The flowers are white, deep pink, light pink, and other colors, and when you get close, they have a sweet smell.
以梅花闻名的地方，是茨城县水户市的偕乐园。: A famous place for plum blossoms is Kairakuen in Mito, Ibaraki Prefecture.
偕乐园里种着各种各样的梅树，每年都会举办梅花节。: Many different kinds of plum trees are planted in Kairakuen, and a plum blossom festival is held there every year.
因为天气还冷，像赏樱那样在户外喝酒吃东西的人很少，多数人是一边散步一边赏花。: Because it is still cold, few people drink and eat outdoors the way they do at cherry blossom viewing; most people look at the flowers while taking a walk.
2月11日是叫作“建国纪念日”的节假日，所以也有家庭在这一天去赏梅。: February 11 is a holiday called National Foundation Day, so some families go to see the plum blossoms on that day.
花谢之后，枝头会结出青青的小梅子，六月前后采摘。: After the flowers are gone, small green plums form on the branches, and they are picked around June.
人们用摘下的梅子做梅干和梅酒。: The picked plums are used to make umeboshi (pickled plums) and umeshu (plum wine).
赏花是一种乐趣，品尝梅子又是一种乐趣，真是让人高兴两次的树啊。: You can enjoy looking at the flowers and enjoy eating the fruit; it is a tree that brings joy twice.
在日本，它作为女性送男性巧克力的日子流行开来。: In Japan, it has become widely known as a day when women give chocolate to men.
送给喜欢的人的巧克力叫作“本命巧克力”。: Chocolate given to someone you love is called 「本命チョコ」 (honmei choco, "true-love chocolate").
出于感谢之情送给同事等人的，是“人情巧克力”。: Chocolate given to people such as coworkers as a token of thanks is 「義理チョコ」 (giri choco, "obligation chocolate").
最近，女生之间互相赠送的“友情巧克力”也很受欢迎。: Recently, 「友チョコ」 (tomo choco, "friend chocolate"), which girls give to and get from each other, has also become popular.
也有人为自己买稍贵一点的巧克力。: Some people also buy slightly expensive chocolate for themselves.
一到二月初，百货商店和超市里就会出现很多巧克力专柜。: Around the beginning of February, many chocolate sections appear in department stores and supermarkets.
也有人在前一天晚上在家亲手做饼干或蛋糕。: Some people make cookies or cakes by hand at home the night before.
收到巧克力的男性，会在3月14日的“白色情人节”回礼。: Men who received chocolate give something in return on White Day, March 14.
据说从国外来的人听到这个习俗，常常大吃一惊。: It seems that people from other countries are often surprised when they hear about this custom.
从二月底前后开始，电视的天气预报里也开始播报花粉量。: From around the end of February, TV weather forecasts also start reporting the amount of pollen.
在日本，有很多人因为杉树花粉而患上花粉症。: In Japan, many people get hay fever from cedar pollen.
公司职员佐藤先生每年一到这个季节，喷嚏和鼻涕就停不下来。: Every year when this season comes, Sato, an office worker, can't stop sneezing and has a nose that won't stop running.
佐藤先生的早晨，从先看天气预报查花粉量开始。: Sato's mornings begin with checking the pollen level in the weather forecast.
遇到“非常多”的日子，他就戴上口罩和眼镜出门。: On days rated "very high," Sato goes out wearing a mask and glasses.
洗好的衣服也不晾在外面，而是晾在屋里。: The laundry isn't hung outside, either; it is hung up indoors.
回到家，他会在门口拍打外套，把花粉抖掉再进屋。: On getting home, Sato brushes off the coat in front of the door to shake off the pollen before going inside.
2月23日是天皇诞辰，放假，但佐藤先生说不太想出门。: February 23 is the Emperor's Birthday, a holiday, but Sato apparently doesn't really want to go out.
佐藤先生笑着说：“下雨天花粉不怎么飞，所以只有在这个季节，下雨才让人高兴。”: "Pollen doesn't fly around much on rainy days, so this is the only season when rain makes me happy," Sato says with a laugh.
弄掉，使落下: to get off (dirt, etc.), to drop
摆女儿节人偶的日子: The day for displaying hina dolls
3月3日是“女儿节”，是祈愿女孩健康成长的日子。: March 3 is 「ひな祭り」 (Hinamatsuri, the Doll Festival), a day to pray that girls will grow up healthy.
也叫作“桃花节”。: It is also called 「桃の節句」 (Momo no Sekku, the Peach Festival).
有女孩的家庭从二月前后开始，就在铺着红布的台阶上摆放女儿节人偶。: In homes with girls, hina dolls are displayed from around February on tiered stands covered with red cloth.
最上面一层并排摆着男雏和女雏。: On the top tier, the male and female dolls (obina and mebina) are placed side by side.
也有人家摆着像楼梯一样多达七层的大套人偶。: Some homes display large sets of hina dolls with as many as seven tiers, like a staircase.
女儿节这天，人们会准备散寿司和文蛤清汤等好吃的来吃。: On the day of Hinamatsuri, people prepare and eat special dishes such as chirashi-zushi and clear clam soup.
粉、白、绿三色的“菱饼”和甜甜的“雏米花”，也是这一天特有的点心。: Pink, white, and green hishimochi (diamond-shaped rice cakes) and sweet hina-arare (puffed rice crackers) are also special treats for this day.
据说女儿节过后，最好早点把人偶收起来。: It is said that hina dolls should be put away soon after Hinamatsuri is over.
因为自古流传着一种说法：人偶收得晚，女儿就会晚婚。: This is because a story has been handed down since long ago that if they are put away late, marriage will also come late.
晚，迟: to be late, to be delayed
祈愿: to pray for, to wish for
收拾，收起来: to tidy up, to put away
这是在情人节收到巧克力的人回礼的日子。: It is a day when people who received chocolate on Valentine's Day give something in return.
这是在日本开始的习俗，据说韩国、台湾等地也有。: It is a custom that started in Japan, but apparently it also exists in places like South Korea and Taiwan.
公司职员木村先生今年在单位收到了五份人情巧克力。: This year, Kimura, an office worker, received five gifts of giri choco (obligation chocolate) at work.
回礼该买什么，木村每年都很难决定。: Every year, Kimura has a hard time deciding what to buy in return.
曲奇、糖果、棉花糖等是常见之选，不过也有人选择手帕、入浴剂之类的东西。: Cookies, candy, marshmallows, and the like are popular choices, but some people choose things like handkerchiefs or bath salts.
还有“回礼要三倍”的玩笑话，所以也有人挑价格稍高一点的东西。: There is also a joke that "a return gift should be worth three times as much," so some people choose something a little more expensive.
木村考虑了很久，最后在车站前的店里买了五小盒曲奇。: After thinking it over a lot, Kimura bought five small boxes of cookies at a shop in front of the station.
每一盒都附上了用工整的字写着“一直以来谢谢您”的卡片。: To each box, Kimura attached a card with "Thank you, as always" written in careful handwriting.
同事对他说“卡片让我很开心”，木村也高兴起来了。: When people at work said, "The card made me happy," Kimura felt happy, too.
第二颗纽扣和集体留言: The second button and group farewell messages
日本的学校一般在三月结束一学年，所以毕业典礼也在三月举行。: Japanese schools usually end their school year in March, so graduation ceremonies are also held in March.
毕业典礼上，学生被一个个点名，大声回答“到”。: At the graduation ceremony, the students' names are called one by one, and each answers "Yes!" in a loud voice.
从校长手中接过毕业证书，最后大家一起唱歌时，也有学生哭了起来。: Students receive their diplomas from the principal, and when everyone sings a song together at the end, some of them start to cry.
典礼结束后，大家回到教室，和朋友们写集体留言。: After the ceremony, they go back to their classroom and write yosegaki (group messages) with their friends.
在大张的纸或相册上，大家互相写下“谢谢”“还要再见哦”之类的话。: On large sheets of paper or in albums, everyone writes messages to each other such as "Thank you" and "Let's meet again."
还有一个关于学生制服“第二颗纽扣”的习俗。: There is also a custom involving the "second button" of the school uniform.
女孩会向喜欢的男孩请求：“请把第二颗纽扣给我。”: A girl asks the boy she likes, "Please give me your second button."
据说因为第二颗纽扣离心脏最近，所以有把“心”交给对方的意思。: It is said that because the second button is closest to the heart, giving it means giving away your "heart."
最近穿西装式校服的学校也很多，但这个故事仍常出现在毕业歌曲和电视剧里。: Many schools now have blazers instead, but this story often appears in graduation songs and TV dramas.
哭起来: to burst into tears, to start crying
赏樱占位置: Saving a spot for cherry blossom viewing
到了三月底，新闻里经常报道“樱花开花”的消息。: Toward the end of March, the news often reports that the cherry blossoms have started to open.
樱花从南方温暖的地方开始开放，逐渐向北推进。: Cherry blossoms start blooming in warm places in the south and gradually move north.
这种移动和天气图上的锋线很像，所以被称为“樱花前线”。: This movement resembles a front on a weather map, so it is called the 「桜前線」 (sakura zensen, "cherry blossom front").
公司组织赏樱时，有时由年轻职员负责“占位置”。: At company cherry blossom viewing parties, young employees are sometimes in charge of 「場所取り」 (bashotori, "saving a spot").
他们一大早去公园，在樱花树下铺开大块垫子，一直等到大家来。: They go to the park early in the morning, spread out a large sheet under a cherry tree, and wait until everyone comes.
一个人等到傍晚很辛苦，所以会看看书、玩玩游戏来打发时间。: Waiting alone until evening is hard, so they pass the time reading books or playing games.
到了晚上，还可以欣赏灯光映照下的“夜樱”。: At night, you can also enjoy 「夜桜」 (yozakura, "night cherry blossoms") lit up by lights.
不过，赏樱也很讲究礼仪。: But manners are also important at cherry blossom viewing.
要遵守把垃圾带回家、不大声喧哗、不折樱花枝等规则。: Let's follow the rules, such as taking our trash home, not making too much noise, and not breaking off cherry branches.
吵闹，喧哗: to make noise, to be rowdy
从四月开始的一年: A year that begins in April
在日本，从4月1日到第二年的3月31日叫做“年度”。: In Japan, the period from April 1 to March 31 of the following year is called the 「年度」 (nendo, fiscal or school year).
学校、公司和政府机关，大多在4月开始新的一年。: For most schools, companies, and government offices, the new year begins in April.
孩子们在4月升入新的年级，公司里也会进来新员工。: Children move up a grade in April, and new employees join companies.
因此，到了3月，开欢送会和搬家的人很多，变得非常忙碌。: Because of this, many people hold farewell parties or move house in March, so it becomes a very busy time.
在公司里，经常会为从4月起调到别的部门或城市工作的人举办欢送会。: At companies, farewell parties are often held for people who will be working in a different department or city from April.
搬家的人也多，所以3月底是搬家公司最忙的时候。: Many people move, too, so the end of March is when moving companies are at their busiest.
这个时候很难预约，最好早点做准备。: It is hard to get a reservation at this time, so it's best to make preparations early.
1月庆祝完新年，到了4月又迎来一次“新的一年”，这是日本有意思的地方。: One interesting thing about Japan is that after celebrating the New Year in January, a "new year" comes around once more in April.
在樱花盛开的季节开始新的事情，心情也会变得明朗起来呢。: Starting new things in cherry blossom season lifts your spirits, too, doesn't it?
4月初，日本的小学会举行入学典礼。: At the beginning of April, entrance ceremonies are held at elementary schools in Japan.
新的一年级学生背着大大的书包，和父母一起去学校。: New first graders carry big randoseru (school backpacks) on their backs and go to school with their parents.
很多家庭会在校门前写着“入学典礼”的牌子旁边拍全家福。: Many families have their photo taken next to the sign reading "Entrance Ceremony" in front of the school gate.
如果樱花正开着，就能拍出非常漂亮的照片。: If the cherry blossoms are in bloom, the photos turn out beautifully.
双肩书包（Randoseru）是用皮革等做成的结实的书包。: A randoseru is a sturdy school bag made of leather or other materials.
因为要用6年，所以很多家庭即使贵一点也会挑好的。: Because it is used for six years, many families choose a good one, even if it costs a little more.
以前男孩多是黑色、女孩多是红色，现在有浅蓝色、紫色等各种各样的颜色。: In the past, most boys had black ones and most girls had red ones, but nowadays they come in all kinds of colors, such as light blue and purple.
由爷爷奶奶（或外公外婆）把书包作为礼物送给孩子的情况也很常见。: It is also common for grandparents to give a randoseru as a present.
一年级学生的书包上，有时会套上黄色的套子。: First graders sometimes have a yellow cover put on their randoseru.
这是为了让开车的人更容易看见，保护孩子免遭交通事故。: This is to make the children easier for drivers to see and to protect them from accidents.
在欢迎会上做自我介绍: Introducing yourself at a welcome party
一到4月，公司和大学的社团经常举办“欢迎会”。: In April, welcome parties (kangeikai) are often held at companies and university clubs.
这是欢迎新来的人、大家一起吃吃喝喝的聚会。: They are parties where everyone welcomes the newcomers and eats and drinks together.
地点多在居酒屋，由被称为“干事”的人负责准备。: They are usually held at izakaya, and the preparations are made by a person called the 「幹事」 (kanji, organizer).
聚会一开始，大家先拿起饮料说“干杯！”: When the party starts, everyone first picks up a drink and says "Kanpai!" ("Cheers!").
不能喝酒的人，用乌龙茶或果汁也没关系。: If you can't drink alcohol, oolong tea or juice is fine.
过了一会儿，新人会一个一个地做自我介绍。: After a while, the newcomers introduce themselves one by one.
