不光说名字和出生的地方，再说说兴趣爱好和喜欢的食物，周围的人就更容易来搭话。: If you talk not only about your name and where you were born but also about your hobbies and favorite foods, it will be easier for the people around you to start talking to you.
最后说一句“今后请多关照”，并鞠一躬。: Finally, you say, "I look forward to working with you," and bow your head.
和在欢迎会上聊过的人，从第二天起在工作中也会更容易交谈吧。: From the next day on, it will probably be easier to talk at work with the people you chatted with at the welcome party.
低下；放低: to lower (one's head); to put down
从4月底到5月初的黄金周，是一年中旅行的人特别多的时候。: Golden Week, from the end of April to the beginning of May, is a time when especially many people travel, even compared with the rest of the year.
为了度过一个愉快的假期，早点制定计划吧。: To make your holiday a fun one, make your plans early.
想预订新干线座位的话，从乘车日一个月前的早上10点起就可以买票。: If you want to reserve a seat on the shinkansen, you can buy tickets from 10 a.m. one month before the day you travel.
热门日子的座位，有时一开售就马上卖完了。: Seats on popular days sometimes sell out right after they go on sale.
酒店和旅馆在这个时候也会比平时更早被订满。: Hotels and ryokan also get fully booked earlier than usual at this time of year.
开车出行的人，事先查一查高速公路什么时候可能会堵，会很方便。: If you are going out by car, it's useful to check in advance when the expressways are likely to be crowded.
讨厌拥挤地方的人，去附近的小城悠闲地休息一下的旅行也不错吧。: If you don't like crowded places, a trip to a nearby town to relax at your own pace might be nice.
假期最后一天路上和电车都很挤，所以也有人提前一天回来。: Roads and trains are crowded on the last day of the holidays, so some people come back a day early.
无论怎么度过，制定适合自己的计划最重要。: However you spend it, the important thing is to make a plan that suits you.
昭和之日和相连的节日: Showa Day and its linked holidays
4月29日是叫做“昭和之日”的国民节日。: April 29 is a national holiday called Showa Day.
这一天原本是昭和天皇的生日，在昭和时代作为“天皇诞辰”来庆祝。: This day was originally Emperor Showa's birthday, and during the Showa era it was celebrated as the Emperor's Birthday.
进入平成后被称为“绿之日”，后来改成了现在“昭和之日”这个名字。: After the Heisei era began, it was called Greenery Day, and later its name was changed to the current Showa Day.
这一天被定为回顾昭和这个时代、思考日本未来的日子。: It is designated as a day to look back on the Showa era and think about Japan's future.
昭和之日也是黄金周开始的日子。: Showa Day is also the first day of Golden Week.
5月3日是宪法纪念日，5月4日是绿之日，5月5日是儿童节，五月初节日连续三天。: May 3 is Constitution Memorial Day, May 4 is Greenery Day, and May 5 is Children's Day, so there are three holidays in a row at the beginning of May.
也就是说，现在的“绿之日”是从4月29日移到了5月4日。: In other words, the current Greenery Day moved from April 29 to May 4.
有的年份，加上周末和带薪休假，有人能休将近十天。: Depending on the year, some people combine these with weekends and paid leave to take nearly ten days off.

如果长假里有机会见到祖父母，不妨听他们讲讲当时的事。: If you have a chance to see your grandparents during the holidays, it's a good idea to ask them about those days.
以前叫做“端午节”，是祈愿男孩健康成长的日子。: In the past, it was called 「端午の節句」 (Tango no Sekku, the Boys' Festival), and it was a day to pray for boys to grow up healthy.
现在已经成为祈愿所有孩子——不论男孩女孩——幸福的节假日。: Now it is a holiday to pray for the happiness of all children, both boys and girls.

鲤鱼旗是用布做的大鲤鱼，风一吹，看上去就像在天空中游泳一样。: Koinobori are large carp made of cloth, and when the wind blows, they look as if they are swimming in the sky.

鲤鱼是即使在水流湍急的河里也能一直往上游的强壮的鱼。: Carp are strong fish that keep pushing upstream, even in fast-flowing rivers.
中国还有鲤鱼登上瀑布后化成龙的传说。: In China, there is also a story about a carp that climbed a waterfall and became a dragon.
所以，挂鲤鱼旗寄托着父母希望孩子像鲤鱼一样健壮成长的心意。: That is why koinobori carry the parents' wish for their children to grow up strong and healthy, like carp.
最近，也有些城镇在河上拉起绳子，让许多鲤鱼旗在空中“游泳”。: Recently, some towns stretch ropes across rivers and let many koinobori "swim" above them.
5月的第二个星期天是“母亲节”。: The second Sunday of May is Mother's Day.
是向妈妈传达“一直以来谢谢您”这份心意的日子。: It is a day to tell your mother, "Thank you for everything."
据说母亲节是一百多年前在美国开始的。: Mother's Day is said to have started in the United States more than 100 years ago.
作为母亲节的花，最有名的是红色康乃馨。: The best-known Mother's Day flower is the red carnation.
一到这个时候，花店门前就摆满了康乃馨。: Around this time, lots of carnations are lined up in front of flower shops.
也有人送粉色、橙色的康乃馨或其他的花。: Some people give pink or orange carnations, or other flowers, as gifts.
小孩子会画妈妈的画像，或者制作“捶肩券”。: Small children draw pictures of their mother's face or make 「肩たたき券」 (katatataki-ken, "shoulder massage coupons").
捶肩券是一种约定：妈妈一用这张券，孩子就要给她捶肩。: A shoulder massage coupon is a promise that when the mother uses it, the child will massage her shoulders by tapping them.
长大成人后，很多人会和妈妈一起吃饭，或者给她打个电话。: Once they are grown up, many people have a meal with their mother or give her a call.
即使不是贵重的礼物，只要能传达心意，妈妈一定会很高兴吧。: Even if it isn't an expensive present, your mother will surely be happy if you can show how you feel.
如何与“五月病”相处: How to deal with the "May blues"
在日本，很多人在四月开始新学校或新公司的生活。: In Japan, many people start a new life at a new school or company in April.
最初的一个月一直处于紧张之中，每天一转眼就过去了。: The first month is full of constant nervous tension, and the days fly by.
然而，黄金周连休结束前后，有的人会突然提不起劲来。: However, around the time the Golden Week holidays end, some people suddenly lose their motivation.
早上怎么也起不来、做什么都不开心，这样的状态被称为“五月病”。: A state in which you can hardly get up in the morning and nothing you do is fun is called 「五月病」 (gogatsu-byo, "May sickness").
五月病并不是正式的病名。: May sickness is not an official name for an illness.
一般认为，与其说是疾病，不如说是在新环境中积累的疲劳表现了出来。: It is said that rather than an illness, it is fatigue that has built up in a new environment and then comes to the surface.
假期中平时的生活节奏被打乱，也被认为是原因之一。: Losing your usual daily rhythm during the holidays is also thought to be one of the causes.
这种时候，据说晚上早点睡、保证充足的睡眠，早上尽量晒晒太阳，会很有效果。: At such times, it apparently helps to go to bed early, get enough sleep, and try to get some sunlight in the morning.
这个季节树叶变成明亮的绿色，也是“新绿”一年中最美的时候。: In this season the leaves on the trees turn a bright green, and it is also the time of year when the fresh new greenery is at its most beautiful.
周末去附近的公园散散步，在大自然中待一会儿，心情也许就会渐渐轻松起来。: If you take a walk in a nearby park on the weekend and spend some time in nature, you may start to feel better.
如果难受的心情持续很久，不要一个人硬撑，去医院找医生咨询一下吧。: If painful feelings go on for a long time, don't just put up with them alone; see a doctor at a hospital for advice.
日本的小学每年举行一次“运动会”。: Elementary schools in Japan hold a sports day (undokai) once a year.
以前很多学校在秋天举办，但现在在五月、六月举办的学校也不少。: In the past, many schools held it in autumn, but now quite a few hold it in May or June.
据说是因为不像夏天那么热，而且能和新班级的同学搞好关系。: Apparently this is because it isn't as hot as in summer, and the children can get to know their new classmates.
孩子们分成红队和白队两支队伍，比拼哪一方获胜。: The children are divided into two teams, red and white, and compete to see which side wins.
不只有赛跑和接力，还有投球入筐、拔河等大家齐心协力完成的项目。: There are not only footraces and relays but also events that everyone does together as a team, such as tamaire (ball toss) and tug-of-war.
气氛最热烈的是最后的接力赛。: The liveliest event is the final relay.
很多家人也会来观看，有的录像，有的大声喊“加油！”: Many family members come to watch, too, filming videos and shouting "You can do it!"
还有父母为了占个好位置，一大早就在校门前排队。: Some parents line up in front of the gate early in the morning to get a good spot.
以前和家人一起吃便当是一大乐趣，不过现在中午之前就结束的运动会也多了起来。: In the past, eating bento with the family was something to look forward to, but now more and more sports days are over by lunchtime.
努力；加油: to try hard; to hang in there
乐趣；期待: enjoyment; something to look forward to
换季，换上夏装: Switching to summer clothes for the new season
在日本，根据季节替换衣服叫做“衣替え（换季）”。: In Japan, switching out your clothes to suit the season is called 「衣替え」 (koromogae).
很多学校和公司以六月一日和十月一日作为换季的日子。: At many schools and companies, June 1 and October 1 are the days for koromogae.
一到六月，初中生和高中生的校服就从黑色、藏青色的冬装换成白衬衫的夏装。: In June, junior high and high school students' uniforms change from black or navy winter uniforms to summer uniforms with white shirts.
街上的景象也一下子显得明亮起来。: The look of the town, too, suddenly seems brighter.
据说换季的习惯始于一千多年前平安时代的宫廷。: The custom of koromogae is said to have begun at the imperial court in the Heian period, more than 1,000 years ago.
现在在家里，比起在固定的那一天换衣服，似乎更多的人会在天气变热的某个周末一次性收: Nowadays, at home, it seems that rather than changing clothes on that set day, many people put everything away at once on a weekend when it has started to get hot.
冬天的毛衣和大衣要洗干净再收起来。: Winter sweaters and coats are washed clean before being put away.
为了不被虫蛀，一起放进防虫剂也很重要。: It is also important to put insect repellent in with them so that they won't get eaten by bugs.
决定；固定: to be decided; to be fixed
梅雨时节，在雨中盛开的绣球花非常美丽。: During the rainy season, hydrangeas blooming wet with rain are very beautiful.
绣球花的颜色有蓝色、粉色、紫色等，因开的地方而不同。: Hydrangea colors, such as blue, pink, and purple, differ depending on where they are blooming.
颜色不同的原因和土壤有关。: The reason for the different colors has to do with the soil.
一般认为，土壤是酸性的话容易变蓝，不是的话容易变粉。: It is said that they tend to turn blue if the soil is acidic, and pink if it isn't.
日本雨水多、酸性土壤多，所以经常能看到蓝色的绣球花。: Japan gets a lot of rain and has a lot of acidic soil, so blue hydrangeas are a common sight.
另外，刚开花时是发白的绿色，颜色会逐渐变化，所以也被称为“七变化”。: Also, when they first start blooming, they are a whitish green, and their color gradually changes, so they are also called 「七変化」 (shichihenge, "seven changes").
据说看起来像花瓣的部分，其实不是花瓣，而是“萼片”。: Apparently, the parts that look like petals are not really petals but sepals (gaku).
神奈川县的镰仓有好几座以绣球花闻名的寺庙。: In Kamakura, Kanagawa Prefecture, there are several temples famous for their hydrangeas.
下雨天出门虽然不方便，但要不要带上伞，去看一次绣球花呢？: Going out on a rainy day is a hassle, but why not bring an umbrella and go see the hydrangeas sometime?
六月的第三个星期日是“父亲节”。: The third Sunday of June is Father's Day.
和母亲节一样，是在美国开始、后来传到日本的。: Like Mother's Day, it started in the United States and was brought to Japan.
母亲节送康乃馨，而父亲节有时会送黄玫瑰。: On Mother's Day people give carnations, while on Father's Day they sometimes give yellow roses as a gift.
因为在日本，黄色被认为是代表父亲节的颜色。: This is because in Japan, yellow is thought of as the color of Father's Day.
不过，也有人说和母亲节相比，父亲节不太引人注意。: However, some people say that compared with Mother's Day, Father's Day doesn't stand out much.
似乎很多人每年都迟迟决定不了送什么好。: It seems many people have a hard time deciding what to give every year.
常被选中的是领带、酒、好吃的东西等。: Popular choices include ties, alcohol, and delicious food.
我去年和爸爸两个人去吃了拉面。: Last year, my father and I went out for ramen, just the two of us.
爸爸笑着说：“比起礼物，这样更让我高兴。”: My father smiled and said, "This kind of thing makes me happier than a present."
传达；传入: to convey; to introduce (to another country)
一年中白天最长的一天: The longest day of the year
六月二十一日前后是“夏至”。: Around June 21 comes the summer solstice (geshi).
是一年中白天最长、夜晚最短的一天。: It is the day of the year with the longest daytime and the shortest night.
在东京，早上四点半左右天就已经开始亮了，太阳一直到晚上七点左右才落下。: In Tokyo, the sky already starts to get light around 4:30 a.m., and the sun stays out until around 7 p.m.
但是在日本这时正值梅雨季节，所以看不到太阳的日子也很多。: However, in Japan it falls right in the rainy season, so there are many days when you can't see the sun.
冬至有泡柚子澡、吃南瓜的习惯，但夏至不太有全日本都做的固定习俗。: On the winter solstice there are customs such as taking a yuzu bath and eating kabocha squash, but on the summer solstice there aren't really any set customs observed throughout Japan.
三重县一个叫二见的地方，海里并排立着两块叫“夫妇岩”的岩石。: At a place called Futami in Mie Prefecture, two rocks called the Wedded Rocks (Meoto Iwa) stand side by side in the sea.
夏至前后，朝阳从两块岩石之间升起。: Around the summer solstice, the morning sun rises from between the two rocks.
据说天气非常晴朗的日子，有时还能看到远处的富士山。: Apparently, on very clear days, you can sometimes see Mt. Fuji in the distance.
夏至的早晨，要不要早点起床去看看美丽的朝阳呢？: On the morning of the summer solstice, why not get up a little early and go see the beautiful sunrise?
在一年的折返点: At the halfway point of the year
六月一结束，一年就正好过去了一半。: When June ends, exactly half of the year has passed.
正月里定下的目标，你还记得吗？: Do you remember the goals you set at New Year's?
也许有人定下了“每天运动”“每月读两本书”，回过神来却发现连手账都不再打开了。: Some people may have decided to "exercise every day" or "read two books a month," only to realize that they had stopped even opening their planners.
话说回来，公司里常把一年分成两半，叫做“上期”和“下期”。: By the way, companies often divide the year in half and call the two halves the 「上期」 (kamiki, first half) and the 「下期」 (shimoki, second half).

因此，也有人觉得六月与其说是“一年的一半”，不如说是“新年度的四分之一”。: For this reason, some people feel that June is not so much "half of the year" as "a quarter of the new fiscal year."
不管怎样，每半年停下脚步回顾一次，是个不错的习惯。: Either way, stopping once every six months to look back on the past is not a bad habit.
与其责备自己没做到的事，不如试着写下三件实际做到的事，意外地会变得积极起来。: Rather than blaming yourself for what you couldn't do, try writing down three things you actually did, and you may find yourself feeling surprisingly positive.
目标不一定非要和最初定的一样。: Your goals don't have to stay exactly as you first set them.
配合现在的生活，做些小调整就好。: You can simply make small changes to fit your current life.
剩下的半年怎么过，这个周末稍微想一想吧？: Why not take a little time this weekend to think about how you will spend the remaining six months?
指: to refer to, to point to
七月七日是叫做七夕的节日。: July 7 is the day of a festival called Tanabata.
这一天快到的时候，车站和超市里会摆上大大的竹枝。: As the day approaches, large bamboo branches are set up in stations and supermarkets.
大家在叫做“短册”的细长纸条上写下心愿，挂到竹枝上。: Everyone writes their wishes on long, narrow strips of paper called 「短冊」 (tanzaku) and hangs them on the bamboo.
有“希望足球踢得更好”“希望家人一直健健康康”等各种各样的心愿。: There are all kinds of wishes, such as "I hope I get better at soccer" and "I hope my family stays healthy forever."
关于七夕，有一个自古流传下来的故事。: There is a story about Tanabata that has been handed down since long ago.
天上银河的这边和那边，住着织姬（织女）和彦星（牛郎）两个人。: On this side and the far side of the Milky Way in the sky live two people, Orihime (the Weaver) and Hikoboshi (the Cowherd).
两个人一年只有一次，只能在七月七日的夜里相见。: The two can meet only once a year, on the night of July 7.
所以孩子们一边想着“七夕晚上可一定要是晴天啊”，一边望着天空。: That's why children look up at the sky, thinking, "I hope it's clear on the night of Tanabata."
这个故事最初是中国的故事，后来传到了日本。: This story originally came from China and was later brought to Japan.
七夕这天，也有人家会吃像银河一样又白又细的素面。: On Tanabata, some families eat somen, noodles that are white and thin like the Milky Way.
装饰；挂上: to decorate; to hang up (as decoration)
7月的第三个星期一是叫做“海之日”的节假日。: The third Monday of July is a holiday called Marine Day.
这是向大海表达感谢之情的日子，和周六、周日连在一起，成为三连休。: It is a day to express thanks to the sea, and together with Saturday and Sunday, it makes a three-day weekend.
这个时候很多海边已经可以游泳了，不少人会觉得“夏天开始了”。: By this time, you can swim at many beaches, and many people feel that summer has begun.
可以游泳的海边沙滩上，只在夏天会出现一种叫“海之家”的店。: On the sand at beaches where you can swim, shops called 「海の家」 (umi no ie, "beach houses") open only during the summer.
在海之家可以吃到炒面、拉面、刨冰等。: At an umi no ie, you can eat things like yakisoba, ramen, and shaved ice.
还可以冲澡、换衣服、寄存行李，非常方便。: You can also take a shower, change clothes, and leave your belongings there, so they are very convenient.
在海里游完泳后吃的炒面，不知为什么格外好吃。: For some reason, yakisoba eaten after swimming in the sea tastes especially good.
不过，夏天的阳光非常强烈，别忘了带防晒霜和帽子。: However, summer sunlight is very strong, so don't forget sunscreen and a hat.
另外，据说过了8月中旬，海里的水母会变多。: Also, it is said that after the middle of August, there are more jellyfish in the sea.
如果要去海里游泳，早一点去也许比较好。: If you're going to swim in the sea, it might be better to go earlier in the summer.
土用丑日与鳗鱼: The Day of the Ox in midsummer and eel
一到夏天，在超市和便利店里常常能看到“土用丑日”这个词。: When summer comes, you often see the phrase 「土用の丑の日」 (doyo no ushi no hi, "the Day of the Ox in doyo") in supermarkets and convenience stores.

“丑”是十二地支之一，日子也是按十二地支排的，所以丑日每12天来一次。: 「丑」 (ushi, ox) is one of the twelve signs of the Chinese zodiac, and since days are also assigned zodiac signs, a Day of the Ox comes around once every 12 days.
夏天的土用丑日在7月底到8月初左右。: The Day of the Ox in the summer doyo falls between around the end of July and the beginning of August.
在日本，有在这一天吃鳗鱼的习惯。: In Japan, there is a custom of eating eel on this day.
吃了鳗鱼补充体力，好不输给炎热的夏天。: People eat eel to build up their strength so that the hot summer won't wear them down.
把蘸上甜酱汁烤好的“蒲烧鳗”放在米饭上，就成了“鳗鱼盖饭”或“鳗鱼重（盒装鳗鱼饭: When 「かば焼き」 (kabayaki), eel grilled with a sweet sauce, is placed on rice, it becomes 「うな丼」 (unadon, eel rice bowl) or 「うな重」 (unaju, eel over rice in a lacquered box).
鳗鱼价格贵，所以很多家庭只在这一天把它当作特别的大餐。: Eel is expensive, so many families make it a special treat just for this day.
另外还有一种说法：不只是鳗鱼，吃乌冬面、梅干等以“う”开头的食物也很好。: It is also said that it is good to eat not only eel but other foods that start with 「う」 (u), such as udon and umeboshi.
第一次穿浴衣的日子: Wearing a yukata for the first time
留学生林同学今年夏天第一次穿着浴衣去看了烟花。: This summer, Lin, an international student, wore a yukata for the first time and went to see fireworks.
浴衣是用棉布等做的、夏天穿的轻便和服。: A yukata is a light kimono made of cotton or a similar material that is worn in summer.
穿法是日本朋友小樱教她的。: Lin's Japanese friend Sakura explained how to put it on.
首先，从自己这边看，先把右边的衣襟贴到身上，再让左边的衣襟叠在上面。: First, you place the side that is on your right (as you look down at yourself) against your body, so that the left side comes over it.
小樱说：“反过来就成了给去世的人穿的穿法，要注意哦。”: Sakura said, "If you do it the other way around, it's the way the dead are dressed, so be careful."
然后把腰带绕在腰上，在背后打成像蝴蝶结一样的形状。: Then you wrap the obi around your waist and tie it in the back in a shape like a bow.
脚上不穿袜子，直接穿木屐。: You don't wear socks; you wear geta (wooden sandals) on your bare feet.
穿上浴衣后，背挺得笔直，走路也不知不觉变慢了。: In the yukata, Lin's back straightened, and Lin began walking more slowly without even realizing it.
一边看烟花，林同学一边想：“感觉自己离日本的夏天又近了一点。”: Watching the fireworks, Lin thought, "I feel like I've gotten a little closer to summer in Japan."
一到8月，镇上的公园和学校操场就会举办盂兰盆舞会。: In August, Bon dances are held in town parks and on school sports grounds.
据说盂兰盆舞原本是为了迎接、送别在盂兰盆节回家的祖先而跳的舞。: It is said that Bon dancing was originally a dance to welcome the ancestors who return home during Obon and then send them off again.
会场正中间有一个叫“矢仓”的高台，上面有人在打太鼓。: In the middle of the venue there is a tall stage called a 「やぐら」 (yagura), and someone on top of it beats a taiko drum.
四周挂着很多灯笼，一到晚上非常漂亮。: Lots of paper lanterns hang all around, and at night it is very beautiful.
人们在矢仓周围围成一个大圆圈，大家朝同一个方向边走边跳。: People form a big circle around the yagura and dance while all moving in the same direction.
舞步不太难，只要跟着前面的人做一样的动作，很快就能学会。: The dance isn't very difficult, so if you move the same way as the person in front of you, you'll learn it quickly.
也有《炭坑节》《东京音头》等自古以来常用的曲子。: There are also songs that have been used since long ago, such as "Tanko Bushi" and "Tokyo Ondo."
不要只是看，中途加入圆圈一起跳，才是盂兰盆舞的乐趣所在。: The way to enjoy Bon dancing is not just to watch, but to join the circle partway through and dance together.
从穿着浴衣的小孩子到老爷爷，大家跳着同样的舞，光是看着就很开心。: Seeing everyone, from small children in yukata to old men, dancing the same dance is fun even just to watch.
送，送走: to send off, to see off
山之日要早起: Get up early on Mountain Day
8月11日是叫做“山之日”的节日，是亲近大山、感谢大山恩惠的日子。: August 11 is a national holiday called Mountain Day, designated as a day to get to know the mountains and be thankful for their blessings.
在各个节日里它算是比较新的，把它和盂兰盆假期连起来休长假的人也不少。: It is one of the newer holidays, and quite a few people combine it with the Obon holidays to take a long break.
这个时候，即使是高山，登山道和山间小屋也都准备就绪，正是夏季登山的好时节。: At this time of year, even on high mountains the trails and huts are ready, making it just the right season for summer climbing.
夏季登山要特别注意的是下午的天气变化。: What you especially need to watch out for in the summer mountains is changes in the weather in the afternoon.
即使早上是晴天，过了中午也常常会突然起云，下起暴雨、打起雷来。: Even if the morning is clear, it often happens that clouds suddenly appear in the early afternoon, bringing heavy rain or thunder.
所以在山里，“早出发、早到达”被认为是基本原则。: That is why, in the mountains, "start early, arrive early" is said to be the basic rule.
住在山上小屋里的人，常常天还黑着就起床，在日出前就开始赶路。: People who stay at huts up on the mountain often get up while it is still dark and start walking before the sun comes up.
另外，山上的气温比平地低得多，所以即使是夏天也应该准备外套。: Also, temperatures up on the mountain are much lower than on flat land, so you should bring a jacket even in summer.
为应对天气变化准备好水和雨具，定一个不勉强的计划，这才是享受登山的最好捷径。: Preparing water and rain gear for changes in the weather and making a plan that doesn't push you too hard is, above all, the surest way to enjoy the mountains.
八月中旬的盂兰盆假期，回故乡的人会变得特别多。: During the Obon holidays in mid-August, a great many people go back to their hometowns in the countryside.
像这样回到家乡的父母家，日语叫作“帰省”。: Going back like this to your parents' home in the town where you were born is called 「帰省」 (kisei).
假期开始的那天，新干线和飞机都会满员，高速公路上的车也一直排到很远，迟迟走不动。: On the day the holidays start, shinkansen and planes fill up, and on the expressways, cars are lined up far into the distance and barely move.
每年电视新闻都会报道这种“回乡高峰”的情况。: Every year, the TV news reports on this 「帰省ラッシュ」 (kisei rasshu, "homecoming rush").
一到父母家，爷爷奶奶已经满脸高兴地在等了。: When they arrive at their parents' home, Grandpa and Grandma are waiting with happy faces.
孩子们在河里玩、捉虫子，享受在大城市里体验不到的夏天。: The children play in the river and catch insects, enjoying a summer they can't experience in a big city.
晚上亲戚们聚在一起，大家边吃饭边聊到很晚。: At night, the relatives get together and talk until late while eating dinner together.
假期快结束时，道路和车站又会挤满返回大城市的人。: Around the end of the holidays, roads and stations get crowded again, this time with people heading back to the big cities.
这被称为“返程高峰”（U-turn rush）。: This is called the 「Uターンラッシュ」 (U-turn rasshu, "U-turn rush").
回去的时候，父母常常会让他们带上很多蔬菜和大米。: When they leave, the parents often send them home with lots of vegetables and rice.
提着沉甸甸的行李回去很辛苦，但这也是回乡的回忆之一。: Carrying heavy bags home is hard work, but that, too, is one of the memories of going home.
日本小学的暑假，在很多地方是从七月底左右到八月底左右。: In many areas, summer vacation at Japanese elementary schools runs from around the end of July to around the end of August.
放假期间也会布置很多作业。: Lots of homework is given even during the vacation.
有算术和汉字练习、图画日记、写读书感想的作文等等。: There are math and kanji drills, picture diaries, essays about what you thought of a book you read, and so on.
其中让孩子们头疼的是“自由研究”。: The one that gives children the most trouble is the 「自由研究」 (jiyu kenkyu, "independent research project").
自由研究要自己决定调查什么，把调查的内容或做好的东西交到学校。: For the independent research project, you decide for yourself what to investigate and hand in what you found out or what you made to the school.
比如每天观察牵牛花并画下来、做昆虫标本、试着做各种尝试看怎样让冰化得更快。: For example, children look at morning glory flowers every day and draw them, make insect specimens, or try various things to see how to make ice melt faster.
也有很多孩子定不下来做什么，就去找父母商量。: Many children can't decide what to do and ask their parents for advice.
每年一到八月的最后一周，作业还没写完的孩子们就开始慌了。: Every year, when the last week of August comes, children who haven't finished their homework start to panic.
图画日记要写当天的天气，事后一口气补写好几天的特别费劲。: The picture diary, in which you have to write the weather for each day, is especially hard to fill in later for many days at once.
长大以后，回想起“作业要是第一周就写完就好了”的人也不少。: Quite a few people look back after they grow up and think, "I should have finished my homework in the first week."
因为1923年的这一天发生了关东大地震，所以定在了这一天。: This day was chosen because on this day in 1923, a huge earthquake called the Great Kanto Earthquake struck.
这个时期台风也多，正适合思考地震、台风来时该怎么办。: There are also many typhoons at this time of year, so it's a good time to think about what to do in an earthquake or typhoon.
防灾日前后，很多学校都会举行避难演练。: Around Disaster Prevention Day, evacuation drills are held at many schools.
一听到地震广播，孩子们马上钻到桌子底下，保护好头部。: When they hear the earthquake announcement, the children immediately get under their desks and protect their heads.
摇晃停止后，好好听老师的指示，排好队走到操场。: When the shaking stops, they listen carefully to what the teacher says, line up, and go out to the schoolyard.
这时很重要的是一个叫“おかしも”的约定。: What is important at this time is a promise called 「おかしも」 (okashimo).
它是取“不推挤、不奔跑、不说话、不返回”这四句话的第一个音组成的。: It is a word made from the first sounds of 「押さない・かけない・しゃべらない・もどらない」 (osanai, kakenai, shaberanai, modoranai: "don't push, don't run, don't talk, don't go back").
有些地方还会练习戴上一种塞了棉花的“防灾头巾”逃生。: In some places, children also practice escaping while wearing a bosai zukin (disaster prevention hood), a hood padded with cotton.
也有学校会进行家人到学校接孩子的“交接演练”。: Some schools also hold "handover drills," in which family members come to the school to pick up the children.
演练虽然看起来每年都一样，但要反复练习，直到真正遇到地震时身体能马上行动起来，这: The drills may look the same every year, but it is important to practice them many times, until your body moves right away when a real earthquake comes.
一到九月，超市和米店里就开始摆出写着“新米”的大米。: In September, rice labeled 「新米」 (shinmai, "new rice") starts appearing in supermarkets and rice shops.
新米是指当年秋天刚收获的大米。: Shinmai means rice that has just been harvested in the autumn of that year.
早的地方从八月开始，多数地方在九月到十月左右收割稻子。: The rice harvest takes place from August in early areas, and from around September to October in most places.
新米水分多，煮出来的饭亮晶晶的，又软又甜。: New rice contains a lot of water, so when it is cooked, it is beautifully glossy, soft, and sweet.
所以，人们常说煮的时候水要比平时稍微少放一点。: That's why it's said that you should use just a little less water than usual when cooking it.
即使没有别的菜，光是盐饭团或生鸡蛋拌饭这样简单的东西也非常好吃。: Even with nothing else, simple things like shio-musubi (salted rice balls) or tamago kake gohan (rice with raw egg) are delicious enough on their own.
在日本，“越光米”等许多品种的大米在各地都有种植。: In Japan, many varieties of rice, such as Koshihikari, are grown in various places.
即使同样是白米饭，品种不同，软硬和甜度也会略有不同。: Even though it's all white rice, different varieties differ slightly in firmness and sweetness.
把各种新米比较着尝一尝，也是秋天的乐趣之一。: Trying different kinds of new rice and comparing them is one of the pleasures of autumn.
进行，举行: to carry out, to hold (an event)
敬老日的礼物: Presents for Respect for the Aged Day
九月的第三个星期一是“敬老日”。: The third Monday of September is Respect for the Aged Day.
这是敬重老人、祝贺长寿的日子，是国家的法定假日。: It is a day to honor elderly people and celebrate their long lives, and it is a national holiday.
这一天，孙辈常常会给爷爷奶奶、外公外婆送礼物。: On this day, grandchildren often give presents to their grandparents.
除了鲜花和点心，小孩子还会画爷爷奶奶的肖像画、写信送给他们。: Besides flowers and sweets, small children draw portraits or write letters and give them.
也有孩子会做一张“捶肩券”，之后给老人捶肩。: Some children make a "shoulder massage coupon" and later give a shoulder massage by tapping.
日本还有到了特定年龄时举行的长寿庆祝。: In Japan, there are also celebrations of long life held when people reach certain ages.
六十岁的“还历”，按老习惯要穿上红色的无袖棉坎肩来庆祝。: For 「還暦」 (kanreki), the 60th birthday, it is a long-standing custom to celebrate by wearing a red chanchanko (padded sleeveless vest).
因为把“米”字拆开，看起来就像“八十八”。: This is because when the character 「米」 (rice) is split apart, it looks like 「八十八」 (eighty-eight).
像这样每个庆祝的年龄都有一个名称，大概是因为长寿是件格外值得高兴的事吧。: The reason each celebrated age has its own name like this is probably that living a long life was something to be especially happy about.
决定，规定: to be decided, to be set
九月二十三日前后是“秋分日”，白天和黑夜的长度几乎相同。: Around September 23 is Autumnal Equinox Day, when day and night are almost the same length.
以秋分日为中心，前后各三天，一共七天叫作“彼岸”。: The seven days centered on Autumnal Equinox Day, three days before and three days after, are called 「お彼岸」 (Ohigan).
彼岸期间，很多人会全家一起去扫墓。: During Ohigan, many people go with their families to visit their family graves.
把墓碑仔细洗干净后，在周围摆上鲜花，点上线香，向祖先祈祷。: After carefully washing the grave, people place flowers around it, light incense sticks, and pray to their ancestors.
彼岸期间特别常吃的是“萩饼”。: A food eaten especially often during Ohigan is 「おはぎ」 (ohagi).
这是把糯米煮熟后轻轻捣一捣，揉成团再裹上豆沙的甜点心。: It is a sweet made by cooking glutinous rice, lightly mashing it, shaping it into balls, and wrapping them in sweet red bean paste.
春天的彼岸也吃类似的点心，不过春天多叫它“牡丹饼”。: A similar sweet is also eaten during the spring Ohigan, but in spring it is often called 「ぼたもち」 (botamochi).
据说“牡丹饼”的名字来自春天开的牡丹花，“萩饼”的名字来自秋天开的胡枝子花。: It is said that the name 「ぼたもち」 came from the peony (botan), which blooms in spring, and the name 「おはぎ」 from the bush clover (hagi), which blooms in autumn.
有句老话叫“热到秋彼岸，冷到春彼岸”。: There is an old saying, 「暑さ寒さも彼岸まで」 (atsusa samusa mo higan made, "heat and cold last only until Higan").
意思是夏天的炎热持续到秋彼岸前后，冬天的寒冷持续到春彼岸前后，之后就会变成舒适宜: It means that summer heat lasts until around the autumn Ohigan and winter cold lasts until around the spring Ohigan, and after that comes a season that is easier to live in.
秋天被称为“读书之秋”，是适合读书的季节。: Autumn is called 「読書の秋」 (dokusho no aki, "autumn, the season for reading"), and it is a good time to read books.
夜晚变长、天气凉爽，所以在家里慢慢享受读书的人多了起来。: The nights get longer and it is cool, so more people enjoy reading books at home at their leisure.
在日本，又小又轻的“文库本”特别受欢迎。: In Japan, small, light 「文庫本」 (bunkobon, pocket paperbacks) are especially widely read.
文库本很容易放进包里，所以很多人在坐电车上班上学的路上读。: Bunkobon fit easily in a bag, so many people read them on the train while commuting to work or school.
在书店买书时，收银台的店员有时会问：“需要给您包上书皮吗？”: When you buy a book at a bookstore, the clerk at the register may ask you, "Would you like a cover on it?"
回答“好的”，店员就会用纸书皮帮你仔细包好。: If you answer "Yes," the clerk carefully puts a paper cover on it for you.
有了书皮，书不容易弄脏，周围的人也看不到你在读什么。: With a cover, the book won't get dirty, and the people around you can't see what you're reading.
每家书店书皮的颜色和图案都不一样，所以还有人专门收集。: Each bookstore has its own cover colors and designs, so some people collect the covers.
今年秋天，你打算读什么书呢？: What kinds of books are you planning to read this autumn?
来往，上学/上班: to commute, to go regularly (to school or work)
红队和白队的运动会: Sports day: the red team and the white team
在日本的小学，运动会是非常重要的活动之一。: At Japanese elementary schools, sports day is one of the most important events.
很多学校在秋天举办，不过最近在春天举办的学校也多了起来。: Many schools hold it in autumn, but recently more and more schools are holding it in spring.
孩子们被分成红队和白队，比赛哪一边得分多。: The children are divided into a red team and a white team and compete to see which side scores more points.
在“投球入篮”比赛中，大家把红色或白色的小球扔进高处的篮子里。: In tamaire (ball toss), the children throw red or white balls into a basket placed high up.
拔河时，大家一起用尽全力拉一根长长的绳子。: In tug-of-war, everyone pulls on one long rope with all their might.
最后的接力赛是气氛最热烈的项目。: The final relay is the liveliest event.
家人们一大早就来，铺开垫子占好位置。: Families come early in the morning and spread out sheets to claim good spots.
有的学校午饭时间让孩子和家人一起吃便当。: At some schools, the children eat bento with their families at lunchtime.
装着饭团、玉子烧和炸鸡块的便当，是运动会的乐趣之一。: A bento with onigiri, tamagoyaki (rolled omelet), and karaage (fried chicken) is one of the pleasures of sports day.
栃木县的日光一到秋天，就挤满了来赏红叶的游客。: In autumn, Nikko in Tochigi Prefecture fills up with tourists who come to see the autumn leaves.
其中作为红叶美景地特别受欢迎的，是通往山上中禅寺湖的“伊吕波坂”。: One place that is especially popular for its beautiful autumn leaves is the 「いろは坂」 (Irohazaka), which leads up the mountain to Lake Chuzenji.
伊吕波坂分为上山和下山两条路，有许多急弯。: Irohazaka is divided into two roads, one going up the mountain and one going down, and it has many sharp curves.
据说弯道一共有48个，人们把这个数字比作“伊吕波歌”的假名，于是称它为“伊吕波坂: There are 48 curves in all, and it is said that the number was likened to the characters of the 「いろは歌」 (Iroha poem), which is how it came to be called Irohazaka.
每个弯道旁都立着一块牌子，上面依次写着“い”“ろ”“は”等一个假名。: At each curve there is a sign with a single character written on it: 「い」, 「ろ」, 「は」, and so on.
红叶季的周末道路拥挤，所以上坡有时要花好几个小时。: On weekends during autumn leaf season, the roads are congested, so it can take hours to get up the slope.
所以也有很多人一大早出发，或者改坐公交车。: That's why many people set out early in the morning or take the bus.
红叶从山顶开始变色，然后一点点地向山下蔓延。: The autumn colors start near the mountaintop and gradually work their way down.
爬完这段坡，等待你的是华严瀑布壮观的水流。: When you reach the top of the slope, the magnificent cascade of Kegon Falls awaits you.
享受化装的日本万圣节: Halloween in Japan, a time for dressing up
一到10月，日本的商店里就装饰着很多南瓜和小鬼。: In October, shops in Japan are decorated with lots of pumpkins and ghosts.
超市和便利店的柜台上也常常卖橙色和紫色的点心。: Orange and purple sweets are also often sold in supermarkets and convenience stores.
在日本的万圣节，最多人喜欢的是化装。: What the most people enjoy about Halloween in Japan is dressing up in costumes.
大家穿上动漫角色、女巫、僵尸等的样子，和朋友一起拍照玩。: People dress up as anime characters, witches, zombies, and so on, and have fun taking photos with friends.
在大城市，还有化了装的年轻人大批聚集的地方。: In big cities, there are also places where lots of young people in costumes gather.
孩子挨家挨户去要糖果，在国外很普通，但在日本很少见。: Children going from house to house to get candy is common in other countries, but rare in Japan.
不过，也有些地方会举办活动，让孩子们在镇上的店铺一家家转着拿糖果。: However, some places hold events in which children go around to the shops in town and get candy.
小朋友们上的幼儿园等地方，有时也会开化装派对。: Costume parties are also sometimes held at kindergartens and other places that small children attend.
一家一家，挨家挨户: house by house, door to door
天气一冷，很多家庭就会把被炉准备好。: As it gets colder, more households set up their kotatsu.
被炉就是在底下装有加热器的矮桌上，盖上一床厚被子。: A kotatsu is a low table with a heater underneath, covered with a thick futon.
把脚伸进去，全身都会暖和起来。: When you put your feet inside, your whole body warms up.
被炉上常常放着橘子。: Mandarin oranges are often placed on top of the kotatsu.
一家人边看电视节目边吃橘子，是日本冬天常见的普通生活情景。: Eating mandarin oranges with the family while watching TV is an ordinary scene of daily life often seen in Japanese winters.
猫也特别喜欢被炉，有时会钻到里面睡觉。: Cats love kotatsu too, and sometimes they crawl inside and fall asleep.
不过，被炉也有让人头疼的地方。: But kotatsu have a troublesome side, too.
一旦钻进去就太舒服了，怎么也出不来。: Once you get in, it feels so good that you can hardly get out.
在被炉里睡着的话可能会感冒，要注意哦。: If you fall asleep in a kotatsu, you may catch a cold, so be careful.
